book.notes: Old Testament original is the Hebrew Masoretic text; New Testament original is the SBL Greek text. Transliteration is automatic and flagged. Hebrew verse numbering can differ from KJV numbering in a few psalms.

verses.original: Ὡς δὲ ἐκρίθη τοῦ ἀποπλεῖν ἡμᾶς εἰς τὴν Ἰταλίαν, παρεδίδουν τόν τε Παῦλον καί τινας ἑτέρους δεσμώτας ἑκατοντάρχῃ ὀνόματι Ἰουλίῳ σπείρης Σεβαστῆς.
verses.translit: Os de ekrithi tou apoplein emas eis ten Italian, paredidoyn ton te Paulon kai tinas eteroys desmotas ekatontarhe onomati Ioylio speiris Sevastes.
verses.translation: And when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners unto one named Julius, a centurion of Augustus’ band.

verses.original: ἐπιβάντες δὲ πλοίῳ Ἀδραμυττηνῷ ⸀μέλλοντι πλεῖν ⸀εἰς τοὺς κατὰ τὴν Ἀσίαν τόπους ἀνήχθημεν ὄντος σὺν ἡμῖν Ἀριστάρχου Μακεδόνος Θεσσαλονικέως·
verses.translit: epivantes de ploio Adramyttino mellonti plein eis tous kata ten Asian topoys anihthimen ontos sun emin Aristarhoy Makedonos Thessalonikeos*
verses.translation: And entering into a ship of Adramyttium, we launched, meaning to sail by the coasts of Asia; one Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.

verses.original: τῇ τε ἑτέρᾳ κατήχθημεν εἰς Σιδῶνα, φιλανθρώπως τε ὁ Ἰούλιος τῷ Παύλῳ χρησάμενος ἐπέτρεψεν πρὸς τοὺς φίλους ⸀πορευθέντι ἐπιμελείας τυχεῖν.
verses.translit: te te etera katihthimen eis Sidona, filanthropos te o Ioylios to Paylo hrisamenos epetrepsen pros tous filoys poreythenti epimeleias tyhein.
verses.translation: And the next day we touched at Sidon. And Julius courteously entreated Paul, and gave him liberty to go unto his friends to refresh himself.

verses.original: κἀκεῖθεν ἀναχθέντες ὑπεπλεύσαμεν τὴν Κύπρον διὰ τὸ τοὺς ἀνέμους εἶναι ἐναντίους,
verses.translit: kakeithen anahthentes upepleysamen ten Kypron dia to tous anemoys einai enantioys,
verses.translation: And when we had launched from thence, we sailed under Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.

verses.original: τό τε πέλαγος τὸ κατὰ τὴν Κιλικίαν καὶ Παμφυλίαν διαπλεύσαντες κατήλθομεν εἰς Μύρα τῆς Λυκίας.
verses.translit: to te pelagos to kata ten Kilikian kai Pamfylian diapleysantes katilthomen eis Myra tes Lykias.
verses.translation: And when we had sailed over the sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.

verses.original: κἀκεῖ εὑρὼν ὁ ⸀ἑκατοντάρχης πλοῖον Ἀλεξανδρῖνον πλέον εἰς τὴν Ἰταλίαν ἐνεβίβασεν ἡμᾶς εἰς αὐτό.
verses.translit: kakei euron o ekatontarhis ploion Alexandrinon pleon eis ten Italian enevivasen emas eis auto.
verses.translation: And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy; and he put us therein.

verses.original: ἐν ἱκαναῖς δὲ ἡμέραις βραδυπλοοῦντες καὶ μόλις γενόμενοι κατὰ τὴν Κνίδον, μὴ προσεῶντος ἡμᾶς τοῦ ἀνέμου, ὑπεπλεύσαμεν τὴν Κρήτην κατὰ Σαλμώνην,
verses.translit: en ikanais de emerais vradyploountes kai molis genomenoi kata ten Knidon, me proseontos emas tou anemoy, upepleysamen ten Kritin kata Salmonin,
verses.translation: And when we had sailed slowly many days, and scarce were come over against Cnidus, the wind not suffering us, we sailed under Crete, over against Salmone;

verses.original: μόλις τε παραλεγόμενοι αὐτὴν ἤλθομεν εἰς τόπον τινὰ καλούμενον Καλοὺς Λιμένας ᾧ ἐγγὺς ⸂ἦν πόλις⸃ ⸀Λασαία.
verses.translit: molis te paralegomenoi auten elthomen eis topon tina kaloymenon Kalous Limenas o eggus en polis Lasaia.
verses.translation: And, hardly passing it, came unto a place which is called The fair havens; nigh whereunto was the city of Lasea.

verses.original: Ἱκανοῦ δὲ χρόνου διαγενομένου καὶ ὄντος ἤδη ἐπισφαλοῦς τοῦ πλοὸς διὰ τὸ καὶ τὴν νηστείαν ἤδη παρεληλυθέναι, παρῄνει ὁ Παῦλος
verses.translit: Ikanou de hronoy diagenomenoy kai ontos edi episfalous tou ploos dia to kai ten nisteian edi parelilythenai, parenei o Paulos
verses.translation: Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished them ,

verses.original: λέγων αὐτοῖς· Ἄνδρες, θεωρῶ ὅτι μετὰ ὕβρεως καὶ πολλῆς ζημίας οὐ μόνον τοῦ φορτίου καὶ τοῦ πλοίου ἀλλὰ καὶ τῶν ψυχῶν ἡμῶν μέλλειν ἔσεσθαι τὸν πλοῦν.
verses.translit: legon autois* Andres, theoro oti meta uvreos kai polles zimias ou monon tou fortioy kai tou ploioy alla kai ton psyhon emon mellein esesthai ton ploun.
verses.translation: And said unto them, Sirs, I perceive that this voyage will be with hurt and much damage, not only of the lading and ship, but also of our lives.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἑκατοντάρχης τῷ κυβερνήτῃ καὶ τῷ ναυκλήρῳ ⸂μᾶλλον ἐπείθετο⸃ ἢ τοῖς ⸀ὑπὸ Παύλου λεγομένοις.
verses.translit: o de ekatontarhis to kyvernite kai to naykliro mallon epeitheto e tois upo Payloy legomenois.
verses.translation: Nevertheless the centurion believed the master and the owner of the ship, more than those things which were spoken by Paul.

verses.original: ἀνευθέτου δὲ τοῦ λιμένος ὑπάρχοντος πρὸς παραχειμασίαν οἱ πλείονες ἔθεντο βουλὴν ἀναχθῆναι ⸀ἐκεῖθεν, εἴ πως δύναιντο καταντήσαντες εἰς Φοίνικα παραχειμάσαι, λιμένα τῆς Κρήτης βλέποντα κατὰ λίβα καὶ κατὰ χῶρον.
verses.translit: aneythetoy de tou limenos uparhontos pros paraheimasian oi pleiones ethento voylen anahthenai ekeithen, ei pos dynainto katantisantes eis Foinika paraheimasai, limena tes Kritis vleponta kata liva kai kata horon.
verses.translation: And because the haven was not commodious to winter in, the more part advised to depart thence also, if by any means they might attain to Phenice, and there to winter; which is an haven of Crete, and lieth toward the south west and north west.

verses.original: Ὑποπνεύσαντος δὲ νότου δόξαντες τῆς προθέσεως κεκρατηκέναι ἄραντες ἆσσον παρελέγοντο τὴν Κρήτην.
verses.translit: Upopneysantos de notoy doxantes tes protheseos kekratikenai arantes asson parelegonto ten Kritin.
verses.translation: And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, loosing thence , they sailed close by Crete.

verses.original: μετʼ οὐ πολὺ δὲ ἔβαλεν κατʼ αὐτῆς ἄνεμος τυφωνικὸς ὁ καλούμενος ⸀Εὐρακύλων·
verses.translit: met' ou polu de evalen kat' autes anemos tyfonikos o kaloymenos Eurakylon*
verses.translation: But not long after there arose against it a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon.

verses.original: συναρπασθέντος δὲ τοῦ πλοίου καὶ μὴ δυναμένου ἀντοφθαλμεῖν τῷ ἀνέμῳ ἐπιδόντες ἐφερόμεθα.
verses.translit: synarpasthentos de tou ploioy kai me dynamenoy antofthalmein to anemo epidontes eferometha.
verses.translation: And when the ship was caught, and could not bear up into the wind, we let her drive.

verses.original: νησίον δέ τι ὑποδραμόντες καλούμενον ⸀Καῦδα ⸂ἰσχύσαμεν μόλις⸃ περικρατεῖς γενέσθαι τῆς σκάφης,
verses.translit: nision de ti upodramontes kaloymenon Kauda ishysamen molis perikrateis genesthai tes skafis,
verses.translation: And running under a certain island which is called Clauda, we had much work to come by the boat:

verses.original: ἣν ἄραντες βοηθείαις ἐχρῶντο ὑποζωννύντες τὸ πλοῖον· φοβούμενοί τε μὴ εἰς τὴν Σύρτιν ἐκπέσωσιν, χαλάσαντες τὸ σκεῦος, οὕτως ἐφέροντο.
verses.translit: en arantes voitheiais ehronto upozonnyntes to ploion* fovoymenoi te me eis ten Syrtin ekpesosin, halasantes to skeuos, outos eferonto.
verses.translation: Which when they had taken up, they used helps, undergirding the ship; and, fearing lest they should fall into the quicksands, strake sail, and so were driven.

verses.original: σφοδρῶς δὲ χειμαζομένων ἡμῶν τῇ ἑξῆς ἐκβολὴν ἐποιοῦντο,
verses.translit: sfodros de heimazomenon emon te exes ekvolen epoiounto,
verses.translation: And we being exceedingly tossed with a tempest, the next day they lightened the ship;

verses.original: καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ αὐτόχειρες τὴν σκευὴν τοῦ πλοίου ⸀ἔρριψαν.
verses.translit: kai te trite autoheires ten skeyen tou ploioy erripsan.
verses.translation: And the third day we cast out with our own hands the tackling of the ship.

verses.original: μήτε δὲ ἡλίου μήτε ἄστρων ἐπιφαινόντων ἐπὶ πλείονας ἡμέρας, χειμῶνός τε οὐκ ὀλίγου ἐπικειμένου, λοιπὸν περιῃρεῖτο ⸂ἐλπὶς πᾶσα⸃ τοῦ σῴζεσθαι ἡμᾶς.
verses.translit: mite de elioy mite astron epifainonton epi pleionas emeras, heimonos te ouk oligoy epikeimenoy, loipon periereito elpis pasa tou sozesthai emas.
verses.translation: And when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on us , all hope that we should be saved was then taken away.

verses.original: Πολλῆς ⸀τε ἀσιτίας ὑπαρχούσης τότε σταθεὶς ὁ Παῦλος ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῶν εἶπεν· Ἔδει μέν, ὦ ἄνδρες, πειθαρχήσαντάς μοι μὴ ἀνάγεσθαι ἀπὸ τῆς Κρήτης κερδῆσαί τε τὴν ὕβριν ταύτην καὶ τὴν ζημίαν.
verses.translit: Polles te asitias uparhoysis tote statheis o Paulos en meso auton eipen* Edei men, o andres, peitharhisantas moi me anagesthai apo tes Kritis kerdesai te ten uvrin taytin kai ten zimian.
verses.translation: But after long abstinence Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Sirs, ye should have hearkened unto me, and not have loosed from Crete, and to have gained this harm and loss.

verses.original: καὶ τὰ νῦν παραινῶ ὑμᾶς εὐθυμεῖν, ἀποβολὴ γὰρ ψυχῆς οὐδεμία ἔσται ἐξ ὑμῶν πλὴν τοῦ πλοίου·
verses.translit: kai ta nun paraino umas euthymein, apovole gar psyhes oudemia estai ex umon plen tou ploioy*
verses.translation: And now I exhort you to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of any man’s life among you, but of the ship.

verses.original: παρέστη γάρ μοι ταύτῃ τῇ ⸀νυκτὶ τοῦ θεοῦ, οὗ ⸀εἰμι, ᾧ καὶ λατρεύω, ⸀ἄγγελος
verses.translit: paresti gar moi tayte te nykti tou theou, ou eimi, o kai latreyo, aggelos
verses.translation: For there stood by me this night the angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve,

verses.original: λέγων· Μὴ φοβοῦ, Παῦλε· Καίσαρί σε δεῖ παραστῆναι, καὶ ἰδοὺ κεχάρισταί σοι ὁ θεὸς πάντας τοὺς πλέοντας μετὰ σοῦ.
verses.translit: legon* Me fovou, Paule* Kaisari se dei parastenai, kai idou keharistai soi o theos pantas tous pleontas meta sou.
verses.translation: Saying, Fear not, Paul; thou must be brought before Cæsar: and, lo, God hath given thee all them that sail with thee.

verses.original: διὸ εὐθυμεῖτε, ἄνδρες· πιστεύω γὰρ τῷ θεῷ ὅτι οὕτως ἔσται καθʼ ὃν τρόπον λελάληταί μοι.
verses.translit: dio euthymeite, andres* pisteyo gar to theo oti outos estai kath' on tropon lelalitai moi.
verses.translation: Wherefore, sirs, be of good cheer: for I believe God, that it shall be even as it was told me.

verses.original: εἰς νῆσον δέ τινα δεῖ ἡμᾶς ἐκπεσεῖν.
verses.translit: eis neson de tina dei emas ekpesein.
verses.translation: Howbeit we must be cast upon a certain island.

verses.original: Ὡς δὲ τεσσαρεσκαιδεκάτη νὺξ ἐγένετο διαφερομένων ἡμῶν ἐν τῷ Ἀδρίᾳ, κατὰ μέσον τῆς νυκτὸς ὑπενόουν οἱ ναῦται προσάγειν τινὰ αὐτοῖς χώραν.
verses.translit: Os de tessareskaidekati nux egeneto diaferomenon emon en to Adria, kata meson tes nyktos upenooyn oi nautai prosagein tina autois horan.
verses.translation: But when the fourteenth night was come, as we were driven up and down in Adria, about midnight the shipmen deemed that they drew near to some country;

verses.original: καὶ βολίσαντες εὗρον ὀργυιὰς εἴκοσι, βραχὺ δὲ διαστήσαντες καὶ πάλιν βολίσαντες εὗρον ὀργυιὰς δεκαπέντε·
verses.translit: kai volisantes euron orgyias eikosi, vrahu de diastisantes kai palin volisantes euron orgyias dekapente*
verses.translation: And sounded, and found it twenty fathoms: and when they had gone a little further, they sounded again, and found it fifteen fathoms.

verses.original: φοβούμενοί τε ⸂μή που κατὰ⸃ τραχεῖς τόπους ἐκπέσωμεν ἐκ πρύμνης ῥίψαντες ἀγκύρας τέσσαρας ηὔχοντο ἡμέραν γενέσθαι.
verses.translit: fovoymenoi te mi poy kata traheis topoys ekpesomen ek prymnis Ripsantes agkyras tessaras iuhonto emeran genesthai.
verses.translation: Then fearing lest we should have fallen upon rocks, they cast four anchors out of the stern, and wished for the day.

verses.original: τῶν δὲ ναυτῶν ζητούντων φυγεῖν ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου καὶ χαλασάντων τὴν σκάφην εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν προφάσει ὡς ἐκ πρῴρης ⸂ἀγκύρας μελλόντων⸃ ἐκτείνειν,
verses.translit: ton de nayton zitoynton fygein ek tou ploioy kai halasanton ten skafin eis ten thalassan profasei os ek proris agkyras mellonton ekteinein,
verses.translation: And as the shipmen were about to flee out of the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea, under colour as though they would have cast anchors out of the foreship,

verses.original: εἶπεν ὁ Παῦλος τῷ ἑκατοντάρχῃ καὶ τοῖς στρατιώταις· Ἐὰν μὴ οὗτοι μείνωσιν ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ, ὑμεῖς σωθῆναι οὐ δύνασθε.
verses.translit: eipen o Paulos to ekatontarhe kai tois stratiotais* Ean me outoi meinosin en to ploio, umeis sothenai ou dynasthe.
verses.translation: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Except these abide in the ship, ye cannot be saved.

verses.original: τότε ⸂ἀπέκοψαν οἱ στρατιῶται⸃ τὰ σχοινία τῆς σκάφης καὶ εἴασαν αὐτὴν ἐκπεσεῖν.
verses.translit: tote apekopsan oi stratiotai ta shoinia tes skafis kai eiasan auten ekpesein.
verses.translation: Then the soldiers cut off the ropes of the boat, and let her fall off.

verses.original: Ἄχρι δὲ οὗ ⸂ἡμέρα ἤμελλεν⸃ γίνεσθαι παρεκάλει ὁ Παῦλος ἅπαντας μεταλαβεῖν τροφῆς λέγων· Τεσσαρεσκαιδεκάτην σήμερον ἡμέραν προσδοκῶντες ἄσιτοι διατελεῖτε, μηθὲν προσλαβόμενοι·
verses.translit: Ahri de ou emera emellen ginesthai parekalei o Paulos apantas metalavein trofes legon* Tessareskaidekatin simeron emeran prosdokontes asitoi diateleite, mithen proslavomenoi*
verses.translation: And while the day was coming on, Paul besought them all to take meat, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that ye have tarried and continued fasting, having taken nothing.

verses.original: διὸ παρακαλῶ ὑμᾶς ⸀μεταλαβεῖν τροφῆς, τοῦτο γὰρ πρὸς τῆς ὑμετέρας σωτηρίας ὑπάρχει· οὐδενὸς γὰρ ὑμῶν θρὶξ ⸀ἀπὸ τῆς κεφαλῆς ⸀ἀπολεῖται.
verses.translit: dio parakalo umas metalavein trofes, touto gar pros tes umeteras sotirias uparhei* oudenos gar umon thrix apo tes kefales apoleitai.
verses.translation: Wherefore I pray you to take some meat: for this is for your health: for there shall not an hair fall from the head of any of you.

verses.original: ⸀εἴπας δὲ ταῦτα καὶ λαβὼν ἄρτον εὐχαρίστησεν τῷ θεῷ ἐνώπιον πάντων καὶ κλάσας ἤρξατο ἐσθίειν.
verses.translit: eipas de tauta kai lavon arton euharistisen to theo enopion panton kai klasas erxato esthiein.
verses.translation: And when he had thus spoken, he took bread, and gave thanks to God in presence of them all: and when he had broken it , he began to eat.

verses.original: εὔθυμοι δὲ γενόμενοι πάντες καὶ αὐτοὶ προσελάβοντο τροφῆς.
verses.translit: euthymoi de genomenoi pantes kai autoi proselavonto trofes.
verses.translation: Then were they all of good cheer, and they also took some meat.

verses.original: ἤμεθα δὲ ⸂αἱ πᾶσαι ψυχαὶ ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ⸃ ⸀διακόσιαι ἑβδομήκοντα ἕξ.
verses.translit: emetha de ai pasai psyhai en to ploio diakosiai evdomikonta ex.
verses.translation: And we were in all in the ship two hundred threescore and sixteen souls.

verses.original: κορεσθέντες ⸀δὲ τροφῆς ἐκούφιζον τὸ πλοῖον ἐκβαλλόμενοι τὸν σῖτον εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν.
verses.translit: koresthentes de trofes ekoyfizon to ploion ekvallomenoi ton siton eis ten thalassan.
verses.translation: And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, and cast out the wheat into the sea.

verses.original: Ὅτε δὲ ἡμέρα ἐγένετο, τὴν γῆν οὐκ ἐπεγίνωσκον, κόλπον δέ τινα κατενόουν ἔχοντα αἰγιαλὸν εἰς ὃν ⸀ἐβουλεύοντο εἰ ⸀δύναιντο ⸀ἐξῶσαι τὸ πλοῖον.
verses.translit: Ote de emera egeneto, ten gen ouk epeginoskon, kolpon de tina katenooyn ehonta aigialon eis on evoyleyonto ei dynainto exosai to ploion.
verses.translation: And when it was day, they knew not the land: but they discovered a certain creek with a shore, into the which they were minded, if it were possible, to thrust in the ship.

verses.original: καὶ τὰς ἀγκύρας περιελόντες εἴων εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν, ἅμα ἀνέντες τὰς ζευκτηρίας τῶν πηδαλίων, καὶ ἐπάραντες τὸν ἀρτέμωνα τῇ πνεούσῃ κατεῖχον εἰς τὸν αἰγιαλόν.
verses.translit: kai tas agkyras perielontes eion eis ten thalassan, ama anentes tas zeyktirias ton pidalion, kai eparantes ton artemona te pneoyse kateihon eis ton aigialon.
verses.translation: And when they had taken up the anchors, they committed themselves unto the sea, and loosed the rudder bands, and hoised up the mainsail to the wind, and made toward shore.

verses.original: περιπεσόντες δὲ εἰς τόπον διθάλασσον ⸀ἐπέκειλαν τὴν ναῦν, καὶ ἡ μὲν πρῷρα ἐρείσασα ἔμεινεν ἀσάλευτος, ἡ δὲ πρύμνα ἐλύετο ὑπὸ τῆς ⸀βίας.
verses.translit: peripesontes de eis topon dithalasson epekeilan ten naun, kai e men prora ereisasa emeinen asaleytos, e de prymna elyeto upo tes vias.
verses.translation: And falling into a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and the forepart stuck fast, and remained unmoveable, but the hinder part was broken with the violence of the waves.

verses.original: τῶν δὲ στρατιωτῶν βουλὴ ἐγένετο ἵνα τοὺς δεσμώτας ἀποκτείνωσιν, μή τις ἐκκολυμβήσας διαφύγῃ·
verses.translit: ton de stratioton voyle egeneto ina tous desmotas apokteinosin, mi tis ekkolymvisas diafyge*
verses.translation: And the soldiers’ counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ⸀ἑκατοντάρχης βουλόμενος διασῶσαι τὸν Παῦλον ἐκώλυσεν αὐτοὺς τοῦ βουλήματος, ἐκέλευσέν τε τοὺς δυναμένους κολυμβᾶν ἀπορίψαντας πρώτους ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἐξιέναι,
verses.translit: o de ekatontarhis voylomenos diasosai ton Paulon ekolysen autous tou voylimatos, ekeleysen te tous dynamenoys kolymvan aporipsantas protoys epi ten gen exienai,
verses.translation: But the centurion, willing to save Paul, kept them from their purpose; and commanded that they which could swim should cast themselves first into the sea , and get to land:

verses.original: καὶ τοὺς λοιποὺς οὓς μὲν ἐπὶ σανίσιν οὓς δὲ ἐπί τινων τῶν ἀπὸ τοῦ πλοίου· καὶ οὕτως ἐγένετο πάντας διασωθῆναι ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν.
verses.translit: kai tous loipous ous men epi sanisin ous de epi tinon ton apo tou ploioy* kai outos egeneto pantas diasothenai epi ten gen.
verses.translation: And the rest, some on boards, and some on broken pieces of the ship. And so it came to pass, that they escaped all safe to land.

verses.original: Καὶ διασωθέντες τότε ⸀ἐπέγνωμεν ὅτι ⸀Μελίτη ἡ νῆσος καλεῖται.
verses.translit: Kai diasothentes tote epegnomen oti Meliti e nesos kaleitai.
verses.translation: And when they were escaped, then they knew that the island was called Melita.

verses.original: οἵ ⸀τε βάρβαροι παρεῖχον οὐ τὴν τυχοῦσαν φιλανθρωπίαν ἡμῖν, ⸀ἅψαντες γὰρ πυρὰν προσελάβοντο πάντας ἡμᾶς διὰ τὸν ὑετὸν τὸν ἐφεστῶτα καὶ διὰ τὸ ψῦχος.
verses.translit: oi te varvaroi pareihon ou ten tyhousan filanthropian emin, apsantes gar pyran proselavonto pantas emas dia ton ueton ton efestota kai dia to psuhos.
verses.translation: And the barbarous people shewed us no little kindness: for they kindled a fire, and received us every one, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.

verses.original: συστρέψαντος δὲ τοῦ Παύλου φρυγάνων ⸀τι πλῆθος καὶ ἐπιθέντος ἐπὶ τὴν πυράν, ἔχιδνα ⸀ἀπὸ τῆς θέρμης ⸀ἐξελθοῦσα καθῆψε τῆς χειρὸς αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: systrepsantos de tou Payloy fryganon ti plethos kai epithentos epi ten pyran, ehidna apo tes thermis exelthousa kathepse tes heiros autou.
verses.translation: And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid them on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand.

verses.original: ὡς δὲ εἶδον οἱ βάρβαροι κρεμάμενον τὸ θηρίον ἐκ τῆς χειρὸς αὐτοῦ, ⸂πρὸς ἀλλήλους ἔλεγον⸃· Πάντως φονεύς ἐστιν ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος ὃν διασωθέντα ἐκ τῆς θαλάσσης ἡ δίκη ζῆν οὐκ εἴασεν.
verses.translit: os de eidon oi varvaroi kremamenon to thirion ek tes heiros autou, pros alliloys elegon* Pantos foneys estin o anthropos outos on diasothenta ek tes thalassis e diki zen ouk eiasen.
verses.translation: And when the barbarians saw the venomous beast hang on his hand, they said among themselves, No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he hath escaped the sea, yet vengeance suffereth not to live.

verses.original: ὁ μὲν οὖν ἀποτινάξας τὸ θηρίον εἰς τὸ πῦρ ἔπαθεν οὐδὲν κακόν·
verses.translit: o men oun apotinaxas to thirion eis to pur epathen ouden kakon*
verses.translation: And he shook off the beast into the fire, and felt no harm.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ προσεδόκων αὐτὸν μέλλειν πίμπρασθαι ἢ καταπίπτειν ἄφνω νεκρόν. ἐπὶ πολὺ δὲ αὐτῶν προσδοκώντων καὶ θεωρούντων μηδὲν ἄτοπον εἰς αὐτὸν γινόμενον, ⸀μεταβαλόμενοι ἔλεγον ⸂αὐτὸν εἶναι θεόν⸃.
verses.translit: oi de prosedokon auton mellein pimprasthai e katapiptein afno nekron. epi polu de auton prosdokonton kai theoroynton miden atopon eis auton ginomenon, metavalomenoi elegon auton einai theon.
verses.translation: Howbeit they looked when he should have swollen, or fallen down dead suddenly: but after they had looked a great while, and saw no harm come to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god.

verses.original: Ἐν δὲ τοῖς περὶ τὸν τόπον ἐκεῖνον ὑπῆρχεν χωρία τῷ πρώτῳ τῆς νήσου ὀνόματι Ποπλίῳ, ὃς ἀναδεξάμενος ἡμᾶς ⸂τρεῖς ἡμέρας⸃ φιλοφρόνως ἐξένισεν.
verses.translit: En de tois peri ton topon ekeinon uperhen horia to proto tes nisoy onomati Poplio, os anadexamenos emas treis emeras filofronos exenisen.
verses.translation: In the same quarters were possessions of the chief man of the island, whose name was Publius; who received us, and lodged us three days courteously.

verses.original: ἐγένετο δὲ τὸν πατέρα τοῦ Ποπλίου πυρετοῖς καὶ ⸀δυσεντερίῳ συνεχόμενον κατακεῖσθαι, πρὸς ὃν ὁ Παῦλος εἰσελθὼν καὶ προσευξάμενος ἐπιθεὶς τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῷ ἰάσατο αὐτόν.
verses.translit: egeneto de ton patera tou Poplioy pyretois kai dysenterio synehomenon katakeisthai, pros on o Paulos eiselthon kai proseyxamenos epitheis tas heiras auto iasato auton.
verses.translation: And it came to pass, that the father of Publius lay sick of a fever and of a bloody flux: to whom Paul entered in, and prayed, and laid his hands on him, and healed him.

verses.original: τούτου ⸀δὲ γενομένου καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ οἱ ⸂ἐν τῇ νήσῳ ἔχοντες ἀσθενείας⸃ προσήρχοντο καὶ ἐθεραπεύοντο,
verses.translit: toytoy de genomenoy kai oi loipoi oi en te niso ehontes astheneias prosirhonto kai etherapeyonto,
verses.translation: So when this was done, others also, which had diseases in the island, came, and were healed:

verses.original: οἳ καὶ πολλαῖς τιμαῖς ἐτίμησαν ἡμᾶς καὶ ἀναγομένοις ἐπέθεντο τὰ πρὸς ⸂τὰς χρείας⸃.
verses.translit: oi kai pollais timais etimisan emas kai anagomenois epethento ta pros tas hreias.
verses.translation: Who also honoured us with many honours; and when we departed, they laded us with such things as were necessary.

verses.original: Μετὰ δὲ τρεῖς μῆνας ⸀ἀνήχθημεν ἐν πλοίῳ παρακεχειμακότι ἐν τῇ νήσῳ Ἀλεξανδρίνῳ, παρασήμῳ Διοσκούροις.
verses.translit: Meta de treis menas anihthimen en ploio parakeheimakoti en te niso Alexandrino, parasimo Dioskoyrois.
verses.translation: And after three months we departed in a ship of Alexandria, which had wintered in the isle, whose sign was Castor and Pollux.

verses.original: καὶ καταχθέντες εἰς Συρακούσας ἐπεμείναμεν ἡμέρας τρεῖς,
verses.translit: kai katahthentes eis Syrakoysas epemeinamen emeras treis,
verses.translation: And landing at Syracuse, we tarried there three days.

verses.original: ὅθεν ⸀περιελόντες κατηντήσαμεν εἰς Ῥήγιον. καὶ μετὰ μίαν ἡμέραν ἐπιγενομένου νότου δευτεραῖοι ἤλθομεν εἰς Ποτιόλους,
verses.translit: othen perielontes katintisamen eis Rigion. kai meta mian emeran epigenomenoy notoy deyteraioi elthomen eis Potioloys,
verses.translation: And from thence we fetched a compass, and came to Rhegium: and after one day the south wind blew, and we came the next day to Puteoli:

verses.original: οὗ εὑρόντες ἀδελφοὺς παρεκλήθημεν ⸀παρʼ αὐτοῖς ἐπιμεῖναι ἡμέρας ἑπτά· καὶ οὕτως εἰς τὴν Ῥώμην ἤλθαμεν.
verses.translit: ou eurontes adelfous pareklithimen par' autois epimeinai emeras epta* kai outos eis ten Romin elthamen.
verses.translation: Where we found brethren, and were desired to tarry with them seven days: and so we went toward Rome.

verses.original: κἀκεῖθεν οἱ ἀδελφοὶ ἀκούσαντες τὰ περὶ ἡμῶν ⸀ἦλθαν εἰς ἀπάντησιν ἡμῖν ἄχρι Ἀππίου Φόρου καὶ Τριῶν Ταβερνῶν, οὓς ἰδὼν ὁ Παῦλος εὐχαριστήσας τῷ θεῷ ἔλαβε θάρσος.
verses.translit: kakeithen oi adelfoi akoysantes ta peri emon elthan eis apantisin emin ahri Appioy Foroy kai Trion Tavernon, ous idon o Paulos euharistisas to theo elave tharsos.
verses.translation: And from thence, when the brethren heard of us, they came to meet us as far as Appii forum, and The three taverns: whom when Paul saw, he thanked God, and took courage.

verses.original: Ὅτε δὲ ⸀εἰσήλθομεν εἰς Ῥώμην, ⸂ἐπετράπη τῷ Παύλῳ⸃ μένειν καθʼ ἑαυτὸν σὺν τῷ φυλάσσοντι αὐτὸν στρατιώτῃ.
verses.translit: Ote de eisilthomen eis Romin, epetrapi to Paylo menein kath' eayton sun to fylassonti auton stratiote.
verses.translation: And when we came to Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard: but Paul was suffered to dwell by himself with a soldier that kept him.

verses.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ μετὰ ἡμέρας τρεῖς συγκαλέσασθαι ⸀αὐτὸν τοὺς ὄντας τῶν Ἰουδαίων πρώτους· συνελθόντων δὲ αὐτῶν ἔλεγεν πρὸς αὐτούς· ⸂Ἐγώ, ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί⸃, οὐδὲν ἐναντίον ποιήσας τῷ λαῷ ἢ τοῖς ἔθεσι τοῖς πατρῴοις δέσμιος ἐξ Ἱεροσολύμων παρεδόθην εἰς τὰς χεῖρας τῶν Ῥωμαίων,
verses.translit: Egeneto de meta emeras treis sygkalesasthai auton tous ontas ton Ioydaion protoys* synelthonton de auton elegen pros autoys* Ego, andres adelfoi, ouden enantion poiisas to lao e tois ethesi tois patroois desmios ex Ierosolymon paredothin eis tas heiras ton Romaion,
verses.translation: And it came to pass, that after three days Paul called the chief of the Jews together: and when they were come together, he said unto them, Men and brethren, though I have committed nothing against the people, or customs of our fathers, yet was I delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans.

verses.original: οἵτινες ἀνακρίναντές με ἐβούλοντο ἀπολῦσαι διὰ τὸ μηδεμίαν αἰτίαν θανάτου ὑπάρχειν ἐν ἐμοί·
verses.translit: oitines anakrinantes me evoylonto apolusai dia to midemian aitian thanatoy uparhein en emoi*
verses.translation: Who, when they had examined me, would have let me go, because there was no cause of death in me.

verses.original: ἀντιλεγόντων δὲ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἠναγκάσθην ἐπικαλέσασθαι Καίσαρα, οὐχ ὡς τοῦ ἔθνους μου ἔχων τι ⸀κατηγορεῖν.
verses.translit: antilegonton de ton Ioydaion enagkasthin epikalesasthai Kaisara, ouh os tou ethnoys moy ehon ti katigorein.
verses.translation: But when the Jews spake against it , I was constrained to appeal unto Cæsar; not that I had ought to accuse my nation of.

verses.original: διὰ ταύτην οὖν τὴν αἰτίαν παρεκάλεσα ὑμᾶς ἰδεῖν καὶ προσλαλῆσαι, ἕνεκεν γὰρ τῆς ἐλπίδος τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ τὴν ἅλυσιν ταύτην περίκειμαι.
verses.translit: dia taytin oun ten aitian parekalesa umas idein kai proslalesai, eneken gar tes elpidos tou Israel ten alysin taytin perikeimai.
verses.translation: For this cause therefore have I called for you, to see you , and to speak with you : because that for the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν εἶπαν· Ἡμεῖς οὔτε γράμματα περὶ σοῦ ἐδεξάμεθα ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰουδαίας, οὔτε παραγενόμενός τις τῶν ἀδελφῶν ἀπήγγειλεν ἢ ἐλάλησέν τι περὶ σοῦ πονηρόν.
verses.translit: oi de pros auton eipan* Emeis oute grammata peri sou edexametha apo tes Ioydaias, oute paragenomenos tis ton adelfon apiggeilen e elalisen ti peri sou poniron.
verses.translation: And they said unto him, We neither received letters out of Judæa concerning thee, neither any of the brethren that came shewed or spake any harm of thee.

verses.original: ἀξιοῦμεν δὲ παρὰ σοῦ ἀκοῦσαι ἃ φρονεῖς, περὶ μὲν γὰρ τῆς αἱρέσεως ταύτης γνωστὸν ⸂ἡμῖν ἐστιν⸃ ὅτι πανταχοῦ ἀντιλέγεται.
verses.translit: axioumen de para sou akousai a froneis, peri men gar tes aireseos taytis gnoston emin estin oti pantahou antilegetai.
verses.translation: But we desire to hear of thee what thou thinkest: for as concerning this sect, we know that every where it is spoken against.

verses.original: Ταξάμενοι δὲ αὐτῷ ἡμέραν ⸀ἧκον πρὸς αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν ξενίαν πλείονες, οἷς ἐξετίθετο διαμαρτυρόμενος τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ πείθων τε ⸀αὐτοὺς περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἀπό τε τοῦ νόμου Μωϋσέως καὶ τῶν προφητῶν ἀπὸ πρωῒ ἕως ἑσπέρας.
verses.translit: Taxamenoi de auto emeran ekon pros auton eis ten xenian pleiones, ois exetitheto diamartyromenos ten vasileian tou theou peithon te autous peri tou Iisou apo te tou nomoy Moyseos kai ton profiton apo proi eos esperas.
verses.translation: And when they had appointed him a day, there came many to him into his lodging; to whom he expounded and testified the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus, both out of the law of Moses, and out of the prophets, from morning till evening.

verses.original: καὶ οἱ μὲν ἐπείθοντο τοῖς λεγομένοις οἱ δὲ ἠπίστουν,
verses.translit: kai oi men epeithonto tois legomenois oi de epistoyn,
verses.translation: And some believed the things which were spoken, and some believed not.

verses.original: ἀσύμφωνοι δὲ ὄντες πρὸς ἀλλήλους ἀπελύοντο, εἰπόντος τοῦ Παύλου ῥῆμα ἓν ὅτι Καλῶς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἐλάλησεν διὰ Ἠσαΐου τοῦ προφήτου πρὸς τοὺς πατέρας ⸀ὑμῶν
verses.translit: asymfonoi de ontes pros alliloys apelyonto, eipontos tou Payloy Rema en oti Kalos to pneuma to agion elalisen dia EsaIoy tou profitoy pros tous pateras umon
verses.translation: And when they agreed not among themselves, they departed, after that Paul had spoken one word, Well spake the Holy Ghost by Esaias the prophet unto our fathers,

verses.original: ⸀λέγων· Πορεύθητι πρὸς τὸν λαὸν τοῦτον καὶ εἰπόν· Ἀκοῇ ἀκούσετε καὶ οὐ μὴ συνῆτε, καὶ βλέποντες βλέψετε καὶ οὐ μὴ ἴδητε·
verses.translit: legon* Poreythiti pros ton laon touton kai eipon* Akoe akoysete kai ou me synete, kai vlepontes vlepsete kai ou me idite*
verses.translation: Saying, Go unto this people, and say, Hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and not perceive:

verses.original: ἐπαχύνθη γὰρ ἡ καρδία τοῦ λαοῦ τούτου, καὶ τοῖς ὠσὶν βαρέως ἤκουσαν, καὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν ἐκάμμυσαν· μήποτε ἴδωσιν τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς καὶ τοῖς ὠσὶν ἀκούσωσιν καὶ τῇ καρδίᾳ συνῶσιν καὶ ἐπιστρέψωσιν, καὶ ἰάσομαι αὐτούς.
verses.translit: epahynthi gar e kardia tou laou toytoy, kai tois osin vareos ekoysan, kai tous ofthalmous auton ekammysan* mipote idosin tois ofthalmois kai tois osin akoysosin kai te kardia synosin kai epistrepsosin, kai iasomai autoys.
verses.translation: For the heart of this people is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes have they closed; lest they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.

verses.original: γνωστὸν οὖν ⸂ἔστω ὑμῖν⸃ ὅτι τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ἀπεστάλη ⸀τοῦτο τὸ σωτήριον τοῦ θεοῦ· αὐτοὶ καὶ ⸀ἀκούσονται.
verses.translit: gnoston oun esto umin oti tois ethnesin apestali touto to sotirion tou theou* autoi kai akoysontai.
verses.translation: Be it known therefore unto you, that the salvation of God is sent unto the Gentiles, and that they will hear it.
And when he had said these words, the Jews departed, and had great reasoning among themselves.

verses.original: ⸀Ἐνέμεινεν ⸀δὲ διετίαν ὅλην ἐν ἰδίῳ μισθώματι, καὶ ἀπεδέχετο πάντας τοὺς εἰσπορευομένους πρὸς αὐτόν,
verses.translit: Enemeinen de dietian olin en idio misthomati, kai apedeheto pantas tous eisporeyomenoys pros auton,
verses.translation: And Paul dwelt two whole years in his own hired house, and received all that came in unto him,

verses.original: κηρύσσων τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ διδάσκων τὰ περὶ τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ μετὰ πάσης παρρησίας ἀκωλύτως.
verses.translit: kirysson ten vasileian tou theou kai didaskon ta peri tou kyrioy Iisou Hristou meta pasis parrisias akolytos.
verses.translation: Preaching the kingdom of God, and teaching those things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ, with all confidence, no man forbidding him.

verses.original: Παῦλος δοῦλος ⸂Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ⸃, κλητὸς ἀπόστολος, ἀφωρισμένος εἰς εὐαγγέλιον θεοῦ
verses.translit: Paulos doulos Hristou Iisou, klitos apostolos, aforismenos eis euaggelion theou
verses.translation: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, separated unto the gospel of God,

verses.original: ὃ προεπηγγείλατο διὰ τῶν προφητῶν αὐτοῦ ἐν γραφαῖς ἁγίαις
verses.translit: o proepiggeilato dia ton profiton autou en grafais agiais
verses.translation: (Which he had promised afore by his prophets in the holy scriptures,)

verses.original: περὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, τοῦ γενομένου ἐκ σπέρματος Δαυὶδ κατὰ σάρκα,
verses.translit: peri tou yiou autou, tou genomenoy ek spermatos Dayid kata sarka,
verses.translation: Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;

verses.original: τοῦ ὁρισθέντος υἱοῦ θεοῦ ἐν δυνάμει κατὰ πνεῦμα ἁγιωσύνης ἐξ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν, Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν,
verses.translit: tou oristhentos yiou theou en dynamei kata pneuma agiosynis ex anastaseos nekron, Iisou Hristou tou kyrioy emon,
verses.translation: And declared to be the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead:

verses.original: διʼ οὗ ἐλάβομεν χάριν καὶ ἀποστολὴν εἰς ὑπακοὴν πίστεως ἐν πᾶσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ,
verses.translit: di' ou elavomen harin kai apostolen eis upakoen pisteos en pasin tois ethnesin uper tou onomatos autou,
verses.translation: By whom we have received grace and apostleship, for obedience to the faith among all nations, for his name:

verses.original: ἐν οἷς ἐστε καὶ ὑμεῖς κλητοὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ,
verses.translit: en ois este kai umeis klitoi Iisou Hristou,
verses.translation: Among whom are ye also the called of Jesus Christ:

verses.original: πᾶσιν τοῖς οὖσιν ἐν Ῥώμῃ ἀγαπητοῖς θεοῦ, κλητοῖς ἁγίοις· χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν καὶ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
verses.translit: pasin tois ousin en Rome agapitois theou, klitois agiois* haris umin kai eirini apo theou patros emon kai kyrioy Iisou Hristou.
verses.translation: To all that be in Rome, beloved of God, called to be saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.original: Πρῶτον μὲν εὐχαριστῶ τῷ θεῷ μου διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ⸀περὶ πάντων ὑμῶν, ὅτι ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν καταγγέλλεται ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ κόσμῳ.
verses.translit: Proton men euharisto to theo moy dia Iisou Hristou peri panton umon, oti e pistis umon kataggelletai en olo to kosmo.
verses.translation: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for you all, that your faith is spoken of throughout the whole world.

verses.original: μάρτυς γάρ μού ἐστιν ὁ θεός, ᾧ λατρεύω ἐν τῷ πνεύματί μου ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, ὡς ἀδιαλείπτως μνείαν ὑμῶν ποιοῦμαι
verses.translit: martys gar moy estin o theos, o latreyo en to pneymati moy en to euaggelio tou yiou autou, os adialeiptos mneian umon poioumai
verses.translation: For God is my witness, whom I serve with my spirit in the gospel of his Son, that without ceasing I make mention of you always in my prayers;

verses.original: πάντοτε ἐπὶ τῶν προσευχῶν μου, δεόμενος εἴ πως ἤδη ποτὲ εὐοδωθήσομαι ἐν τῷ θελήματι τοῦ θεοῦ ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς.
verses.translit: pantote epi ton proseyhon moy, deomenos ei pos edi pote euodothisomai en to thelimati tou theou elthein pros umas.
verses.translation: Making request, if by any means now at length I might have a prosperous journey by the will of God to come unto you.

verses.original: ἐπιποθῶ γὰρ ἰδεῖν ὑμᾶς, ἵνα τι μεταδῶ χάρισμα ὑμῖν πνευματικὸν εἰς τὸ στηριχθῆναι ὑμᾶς,
verses.translit: epipotho gar idein umas, ina ti metado harisma umin pneymatikon eis to stirihthenai umas,
verses.translation: For I long to see you, that I may impart unto you some spiritual gift, to the end ye may be established;

verses.original: τοῦτο δέ ἐστιν συμπαρακληθῆναι ἐν ὑμῖν διὰ τῆς ἐν ἀλλήλοις πίστεως ὑμῶν τε καὶ ἐμοῦ.
verses.translit: touto de estin symparaklithenai en umin dia tes en allilois pisteos umon te kai emou.
verses.translation: That is, that I may be comforted together with you by the mutual faith both of you and me.

verses.original: οὐ θέλω δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν, ἀδελφοί, ὅτι πολλάκις προεθέμην ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς, καὶ ἐκωλύθην ἄχρι τοῦ δεῦρο, ἵνα τινὰ καρπὸν σχῶ καὶ ἐν ὑμῖν καθὼς καὶ ἐν τοῖς λοιποῖς ἔθνεσιν.
verses.translit: ou thelo de umas agnoein, adelfoi, oti pollakis proethemin elthein pros umas, kai ekolythin ahri tou deuro, ina tina karpon sho kai en umin kathos kai en tois loipois ethnesin.
verses.translation: Now I would not have you ignorant, brethren, that oftentimes I purposed to come unto you, (but was let hitherto,) that I might have some fruit among you also, even as among other Gentiles.

verses.original: Ἕλλησίν τε καὶ βαρβάροις, σοφοῖς τε καὶ ἀνοήτοις ὀφειλέτης εἰμί·
verses.translit: Ellisin te kai varvarois, sofois te kai anoitois ofeiletis eimi*
verses.translation: I am debtor both to the Greeks, and to the Barbarians; both to the wise, and to the unwise.

verses.original: οὕτως τὸ κατʼ ἐμὲ πρόθυμον καὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς ἐν Ῥώμῃ εὐαγγελίσασθαι.
verses.translit: outos to kat' eme prothymon kai umin tois en Rome euaggelisasthai.
verses.translation: So, as much as in me is, I am ready to preach the gospel to you that are at Rome also.

verses.original: Οὐ γὰρ ἐπαισχύνομαι τὸ ⸀εὐαγγέλιον, δύναμις γὰρ θεοῦ ἐστιν εἰς σωτηρίαν παντὶ τῷ πιστεύοντι, Ἰουδαίῳ τε πρῶτον καὶ Ἕλληνι·
verses.translit: Ou gar epaishynomai to euaggelion, dynamis gar theou estin eis sotirian panti to pisteyonti, Ioydaio te proton kai Ellini*
verses.translation: For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.

verses.original: δικαιοσύνη γὰρ θεοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ ἀποκαλύπτεται ἐκ πίστεως εἰς πίστιν, καθὼς γέγραπται· Ὁ δὲ δίκαιος ἐκ πίστεως ζήσεται.
verses.translit: dikaiosyni gar theou en auto apokalyptetai ek pisteos eis pistin, kathos gegraptai* O de dikaios ek pisteos zisetai.
verses.translation: For therein is the righteousness of God revealed from faith to faith: as it is written, The just shall live by faith.

verses.original: Ἀποκαλύπτεται γὰρ ὀργὴ θεοῦ ἀπʼ οὐρανοῦ ἐπὶ πᾶσαν ἀσέβειαν καὶ ἀδικίαν ἀνθρώπων τῶν τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἐν ἀδικίᾳ κατεχόντων,
verses.translit: Apokalyptetai gar orge theou ap' ouranou epi pasan aseveian kai adikian anthropon ton ten alitheian en adikia katehonton,
verses.translation: For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness;

verses.original: διότι τὸ γνωστὸν τοῦ θεοῦ φανερόν ἐστιν ἐν αὐτοῖς, ὁ ⸂θεὸς γὰρ⸃ αὐτοῖς ἐφανέρωσεν.
verses.translit: dioti to gnoston tou theou faneron estin en autois, o theos gar autois efanerosen.
verses.translation: Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them.

verses.original: τὰ γὰρ ἀόρατα αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ κτίσεως κόσμου τοῖς ποιήμασιν νοούμενα καθορᾶται, ἥ τε ἀΐδιος αὐτοῦ δύναμις καὶ θειότης, εἰς τὸ εἶναι αὐτοὺς ἀναπολογήτους,
verses.translit: ta gar aorata autou apo ktiseos kosmoy tois poiimasin nooymena kathoratai, e te aIdios autou dynamis kai theiotis, eis to einai autous anapologitoys,
verses.translation: For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse:

verses.original: διότι γνόντες τὸν θεὸν οὐχ ὡς θεὸν ἐδόξασαν ἢ ηὐχαρίστησαν, ἀλλὰ ἐματαιώθησαν ἐν τοῖς διαλογισμοῖς αὐτῶν καὶ ἐσκοτίσθη ἡ ἀσύνετος αὐτῶν καρδία·
verses.translit: dioti gnontes ton theon ouh os theon edoxasan e iuharistisan, alla emataiothisan en tois dialogismois auton kai eskotisthi e asynetos auton kardia*
verses.translation: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened.

verses.original: φάσκοντες εἶναι σοφοὶ ἐμωράνθησαν,
verses.translit: faskontes einai sofoi emoranthisan,
verses.translation: Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,

verses.original: καὶ ἤλλαξαν τὴν δόξαν τοῦ ἀφθάρτου θεοῦ ἐν ὁμοιώματι εἰκόνος φθαρτοῦ ἀνθρώπου καὶ πετεινῶν καὶ τετραπόδων καὶ ἑρπετῶν.
verses.translit: kai ellaxan ten doxan tou afthartoy theou en omoiomati eikonos fthartou anthropoy kai peteinon kai tetrapodon kai erpeton.
verses.translation: And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.

verses.original: ⸀Διὸ παρέδωκεν αὐτοὺς ὁ θεὸς ἐν ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις τῶν καρδιῶν αὐτῶν εἰς ἀκαθαρσίαν τοῦ ἀτιμάζεσθαι τὰ σώματα αὐτῶν ἐν ⸀αὐτοῖς,
verses.translit: Dio paredoken autous o theos en tais epithymiais ton kardion auton eis akatharsian tou atimazesthai ta somata auton en autois,
verses.translation: Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves:

verses.original: οἵτινες μετήλλαξαν τὴν ἀλήθειαν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν τῷ ψεύδει, καὶ ἐσεβάσθησαν καὶ ἐλάτρευσαν τῇ κτίσει παρὰ τὸν κτίσαντα, ὅς ἐστιν εὐλογητὸς εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας· ἀμήν.
verses.translit: oitines metillaxan ten alitheian tou theou en to pseydei, kai esevasthisan kai elatreysan te ktisei para ton ktisanta, os estin eulogitos eis tous aionas* amin.
verses.translation: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.

verses.original: Διὰ τοῦτο παρέδωκεν αὐτοὺς ὁ θεὸς εἰς πάθη ἀτιμίας· αἵ τε γὰρ θήλειαι αὐτῶν μετήλλαξαν τὴν φυσικὴν χρῆσιν εἰς τὴν παρὰ φύσιν,
verses.translit: Dia touto paredoken autous o theos eis pathi atimias* ai te gar thileiai auton metillaxan ten fysiken hresin eis ten para fysin,
verses.translation: For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature:

verses.original: ὁμοίως τε καὶ οἱ ἄρσενες ἀφέντες τὴν φυσικὴν χρῆσιν τῆς θηλείας ἐξεκαύθησαν ἐν τῇ ὀρέξει αὐτῶν εἰς ἀλλήλους, ἄρσενες ἐν ἄρσεσιν τὴν ἀσχημοσύνην κατεργαζόμενοι καὶ τὴν ἀντιμισθίαν ἣν ἔδει τῆς πλάνης αὐτῶν ἐν ⸀ἑαυτοῖς ἀπολαμβάνοντες.
verses.translit: omoios te kai oi arsenes afentes ten fysiken hresin tes thileias exekaythisan en te orexei auton eis alliloys, arsenes en arsesin ten ashimosynin katergazomenoi kai ten antimisthian en edei tes planis auton en eaytois apolamvanontes.
verses.translation: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet.

verses.original: Καὶ καθὼς οὐκ ἐδοκίμασαν τὸν θεὸν ἔχειν ἐν ἐπιγνώσει, παρέδωκεν αὐτοὺς ὁ θεὸς εἰς ἀδόκιμον νοῦν, ποιεῖν τὰ μὴ καθήκοντα,
verses.translit: Kai kathos ouk edokimasan ton theon ehein en epignosei, paredoken autous o theos eis adokimon noun, poiein ta me kathikonta,
verses.translation: And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient;

verses.original: πεπληρωμένους πάσῃ ⸀ἀδικίᾳ πονηρίᾳ πλεονεξίᾳ κακίᾳ, μεστοὺς φθόνου φόνου ἔριδος δόλου κακοηθείας, ψιθυριστάς,
verses.translit: pepliromenoys pase adikia poniria pleonexia kakia, mestous fthonoy fonoy eridos doloy kakoitheias, psithyristas,
verses.translation: Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers,

verses.original: καταλάλους, θεοστυγεῖς, ὑβριστάς, ὑπερηφάνους, ἀλαζόνας, ἐφευρετὰς κακῶν, γονεῦσιν ἀπειθεῖς,
verses.translit: katalaloys, theostygeis, uvristas, uperifanoys, alazonas, efeyretas kakon, goneusin apeitheis,
verses.translation: Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents,

verses.original: ἀσυνέτους, ἀσυνθέτους, ⸀ἀστόργους, ἀνελεήμονας·
verses.translit: asynetoys, asynthetoys, astorgoys, aneleimonas*
verses.translation: Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful:

verses.original: οἵτινες τὸ δικαίωμα τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπιγνόντες, ὅτι οἱ τὰ τοιαῦτα πράσσοντες ἄξιοι θανάτου εἰσίν, οὐ μόνον αὐτὰ ποιοῦσιν ἀλλὰ καὶ συνευδοκοῦσιν τοῖς πράσσουσιν.
verses.translit: oitines to dikaioma tou theou epignontes, oti oi ta toiauta prassontes axioi thanatoy eisin, ou monon auta poiousin alla kai syneydokousin tois prassoysin.
verses.translation: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.

verses.original: Διὸ ἀναπολόγητος εἶ, ὦ ἄνθρωπε πᾶς ὁ κρίνων· ἐν ᾧ γὰρ κρίνεις τὸν ἕτερον, σεαυτὸν κατακρίνεις, τὰ γὰρ αὐτὰ πράσσεις ὁ κρίνων·
verses.translit: Dio anapologitos ei, o anthrope pas o krinon* en o gar krineis ton eteron, seayton katakrineis, ta gar auta prasseis o krinon*
verses.translation: Therefore thou art inexcusable, O man, whosoever thou art that judgest: for wherein thou judgest another, thou condemnest thyself; for thou that judgest doest the same things.

verses.original: οἴδαμεν δὲ ὅτι τὸ κρίμα τοῦ θεοῦ ἐστιν κατὰ ἀλήθειαν ἐπὶ τοὺς τὰ τοιαῦτα πράσσοντας.
verses.translit: oidamen de oti to krima tou theou estin kata alitheian epi tous ta toiauta prassontas.
verses.translation: But we are sure that the judgment of God is according to truth against them which commit such things.

verses.original: λογίζῃ δὲ τοῦτο, ὦ ἄνθρωπε ὁ κρίνων τοὺς τὰ τοιαῦτα πράσσοντας καὶ ποιῶν αὐτά, ὅτι σὺ ἐκφεύξῃ τὸ κρίμα τοῦ θεοῦ;
verses.translit: logize de touto, o anthrope o krinon tous ta toiauta prassontas kai poion auta, oti su ekfeyxe to krima tou theou;
verses.translation: And thinkest thou this, O man, that judgest them which do such things, and doest the same, that thou shalt escape the judgment of God?

verses.original: ἢ τοῦ πλούτου τῆς χρηστότητος αὐτοῦ καὶ τῆς ἀνοχῆς καὶ τῆς μακροθυμίας καταφρονεῖς, ἀγνοῶν ὅτι τὸ χρηστὸν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς μετάνοιάν σε ἄγει;
verses.translit: e tou ploytoy tes hristotitos autou kai tes anohes kai tes makrothymias katafroneis, agnoon oti to hriston tou theou eis metanoian se agei;
verses.translation: Or despisest thou the riches of his goodness and forbearance and longsuffering; not knowing that the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance?

verses.original: κατὰ δὲ τὴν σκληρότητά σου καὶ ἀμετανόητον καρδίαν θησαυρίζεις σεαυτῷ ὀργὴν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ὀργῆς καὶ ⸀ἀποκαλύψεως δικαιοκρισίας τοῦ θεοῦ,
verses.translit: kata de ten sklirotita soy kai ametanoiton kardian thisayrizeis seayto orgen en emera orges kai apokalypseos dikaiokrisias tou theou,
verses.translation: But after thy hardness and impenitent heart treasurest up unto thyself wrath against the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God;

verses.original: ὃς ἀποδώσει ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ·
verses.translit: os apodosei ekasto kata ta erga autou*
verses.translation: Who will render to every man according to his deeds:

verses.original: τοῖς μὲν καθʼ ὑπομονὴν ἔργου ἀγαθοῦ δόξαν καὶ τιμὴν καὶ ἀφθαρσίαν ζητοῦσιν ζωὴν αἰώνιον·
verses.translit: tois men kath' upomonen ergoy agathou doxan kai timen kai aftharsian zitousin zoen aionion*
verses.translation: To them who by patient continuance in well doing seek for glory and honour and immortality, eternal life:

verses.original: τοῖς δὲ ἐξ ἐριθείας καὶ ⸀ἀπειθοῦσι τῇ ἀληθείᾳ πειθομένοις δὲ τῇ ἀδικίᾳ ⸂ὀργὴ καὶ θυμός⸃,
verses.translit: tois de ex eritheias kai apeithousi te alitheia peithomenois de te adikia orge kai thymos,
verses.translation: But unto them that are contentious, and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness, indignation and wrath,

verses.original: θλῖψις καὶ στενοχωρία, ἐπὶ πᾶσαν ψυχὴν ἀνθρώπου τοῦ κατεργαζομένου τὸ κακόν, Ἰουδαίου τε πρῶτον καὶ Ἕλληνος·
verses.translit: thlipsis kai stenohoria, epi pasan psyhen anthropoy tou katergazomenoy to kakon, Ioydaioy te proton kai Ellinos*
verses.translation: Tribulation and anguish, upon every soul of man that doeth evil, of the Jew first, and also of the Gentile;

verses.original: δόξα δὲ καὶ τιμὴ καὶ εἰρήνη παντὶ τῷ ἐργαζομένῳ τὸ ἀγαθόν, Ἰουδαίῳ τε πρῶτον καὶ Ἕλληνι·
verses.translit: doxa de kai time kai eirini panti to ergazomeno to agathon, Ioydaio te proton kai Ellini*
verses.translation: But glory, honour, and peace, to every man that worketh good, to the Jew first, and also to the Gentile:

verses.original: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν προσωπολημψία παρὰ τῷ θεῷ.
verses.translit: ou gar estin prosopolimpsia para to theo.
verses.translation: For there is no respect of persons with God.

verses.original: Ὅσοι γὰρ ἀνόμως ἥμαρτον, ἀνόμως καὶ ἀπολοῦνται· καὶ ὅσοι ἐν νόμῳ ἥμαρτον, διὰ νόμου κριθήσονται·
verses.translit: Osoi gar anomos emarton, anomos kai apolountai* kai osoi en nomo emarton, dia nomoy krithisontai*
verses.translation: For as many as have sinned without law shall also perish without law: and as many as have sinned in the law shall be judged by the law;

verses.original: οὐ γὰρ οἱ ἀκροαταὶ ⸀νόμου δίκαιοι παρὰ ⸀τῷ θεῷ, ἀλλʼ οἱ ποιηταὶ ⸁νόμου δικαιωθήσονται.
verses.translit: ou gar oi akroatai nomoy dikaioi para to theo, all' oi poiitai nomoy dikaiothisontai.
verses.translation: (For not the hearers of the law are just before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified.

verses.original: ὅταν γὰρ ἔθνη τὰ μὴ νόμον ἔχοντα φύσει τὰ τοῦ νόμου ⸀ποιῶσιν, οὗτοι νόμον μὴ ἔχοντες ἑαυτοῖς εἰσιν νόμος·
verses.translit: otan gar ethni ta me nomon ehonta fysei ta tou nomoy poiosin, outoi nomon me ehontes eaytois eisin nomos*
verses.translation: For when the Gentiles, which have not the law, do by nature the things contained in the law, these, having not the law, are a law unto themselves:

verses.original: οἵτινες ἐνδείκνυνται τὸ ἔργον τοῦ νόμου γραπτὸν ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν, συμμαρτυρούσης αὐτῶν τῆς συνειδήσεως καὶ μεταξὺ ἀλλήλων τῶν λογισμῶν κατηγορούντων ἢ καὶ ἀπολογουμένων,
verses.translit: oitines endeiknyntai to ergon tou nomoy grapton en tais kardiais auton, symmartyroysis auton tes syneidiseos kai metaxu allilon ton logismon katigoroynton e kai apologoymenon,
verses.translation: Which shew the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience also bearing witness, and their thoughts the mean while accusing or else excusing one another;)

verses.original: ἐν ⸂ἡμέρᾳ ὅτε⸃ ⸀κρίνει ὁ θεὸς τὰ κρυπτὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων κατὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιόν μου διὰ ⸂Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ⸃.
verses.translit: en emera ote krinei o theos ta krypta ton anthropon kata to euaggelion moy dia Hristou Iisou.
verses.translation: In the day when God shall judge the secrets of men by Jesus Christ according to my gospel.

verses.original: ⸂Εἰ δὲ⸃ σὺ Ἰουδαῖος ἐπονομάζῃ καὶ ἐπαναπαύῃ ⸀νόμῳ καὶ καυχᾶσαι ἐν θεῷ
verses.translit: Ei de su Ioydaios eponomaze kai epanapaye nomo kai kayhasai en theo
verses.translation: Behold, thou art called a Jew, and restest in the law, and makest thy boast of God,

verses.original: καὶ γινώσκεις τὸ θέλημα καὶ δοκιμάζεις τὰ διαφέροντα κατηχούμενος ἐκ τοῦ νόμου,
verses.translit: kai ginoskeis to thelima kai dokimazeis ta diaferonta katihoymenos ek tou nomoy,
verses.translation: And knowest his will, and approvest the things that are more excellent, being instructed out of the law;

verses.original: πέποιθάς τε σεαυτὸν ὁδηγὸν εἶναι τυφλῶν, φῶς τῶν ἐν σκότει,
verses.translit: pepoithas te seayton odigon einai tyflon, fos ton en skotei,
verses.translation: And art confident that thou thyself art a guide of the blind, a light of them which are in darkness,

verses.original: παιδευτὴν ἀφρόνων, διδάσκαλον νηπίων, ἔχοντα τὴν μόρφωσιν τῆς γνώσεως καὶ τῆς ἀληθείας ἐν τῷ νόμῳ—
verses.translit: paideyten afronon, didaskalon nipion, ehonta ten morfosin tes gnoseos kai tes alitheias en to nomo--
verses.translation: An instructor of the foolish, a teacher of babes, which hast the form of knowledge and of the truth in the law.

verses.original: ὁ οὖν διδάσκων ἕτερον σεαυτὸν οὐ διδάσκεις; ὁ κηρύσσων μὴ κλέπτειν κλέπτεις;
verses.translit: o oun didaskon eteron seayton ou didaskeis; o kirysson me kleptein klepteis;
verses.translation: Thou therefore which teachest another, teachest thou not thyself? thou that preachest a man should not steal, dost thou steal?

verses.original: ὁ λέγων μὴ μοιχεύειν μοιχεύεις; ὁ βδελυσσόμενος τὰ εἴδωλα ἱεροσυλεῖς;
verses.translit: o legon me moiheyein moiheyeis; o vdelyssomenos ta eidola ierosyleis;
verses.translation: Thou that sayest a man should not commit adultery, dost thou commit adultery? thou that abhorrest idols, dost thou commit sacrilege?

verses.original: ὃς ἐν νόμῳ καυχᾶσαι, διὰ τῆς παραβάσεως τοῦ νόμου τὸν θεὸν ἀτιμάζεις;
verses.translit: os en nomo kayhasai, dia tes paravaseos tou nomoy ton theon atimazeis?
verses.translation: Thou that makest thy boast of the law, through breaking the law dishonourest thou God?

verses.original: τὸ γὰρ ὄνομα τοῦ θεοῦ διʼ ὑμᾶς βλασφημεῖται ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, καθὼς γέγραπται.
verses.translit: to gar onoma tou theou di' umas vlasfimeitai en tois ethnesin, kathos gegraptai.
verses.translation: For the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles through you, as it is written.

verses.original: Περιτομὴ μὲν γὰρ ὠφελεῖ ἐὰν νόμον πράσσῃς· ἐὰν δὲ παραβάτης νόμου ᾖς, ἡ περιτομή σου ἀκροβυστία γέγονεν.
verses.translit: Peritome men gar ofelei ean nomon prasses* ean de paravatis nomoy es, e peritomi soy akrovystia gegonen.
verses.translation: For circumcision verily profiteth, if thou keep the law: but if thou be a breaker of the law, thy circumcision is made uncircumcision.

verses.original: ἐὰν οὖν ἡ ἀκροβυστία τὰ δικαιώματα τοῦ νόμου φυλάσσῃ, ⸀οὐχ ἡ ἀκροβυστία αὐτοῦ εἰς περιτομὴν λογισθήσεται;
verses.translit: ean oun e akrovystia ta dikaiomata tou nomoy fylasse, ouh e akrovystia autou eis peritomen logisthisetai;
verses.translation: Therefore if the uncircumcision keep the righteousness of the law, shall not his uncircumcision be counted for circumcision?

verses.original: καὶ κρινεῖ ἡ ἐκ φύσεως ἀκροβυστία τὸν νόμον τελοῦσα σὲ τὸν διὰ γράμματος καὶ περιτομῆς παραβάτην νόμου.
verses.translit: kai krinei e ek fyseos akrovystia ton nomon telousa se ton dia grammatos kai peritomes paravatin nomoy.
verses.translation: And shall not uncircumcision which is by nature, if it fulfil the law, judge thee, who by the letter and circumcision dost transgress the law?

verses.original: οὐ γὰρ ὁ ἐν τῷ φανερῷ Ἰουδαῖός ἐστιν, οὐδὲ ἡ ἐν τῷ φανερῷ ἐν σαρκὶ περιτομή·
verses.translit: ou gar o en to fanero Ioydaios estin, oude e en to fanero en sarki peritomi*
verses.translation: For he is not a Jew, which is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision, which is outward in the flesh:

verses.original: ἀλλʼ ὁ ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ Ἰουδαῖος, καὶ περιτομὴ καρδίας ἐν πνεύματι οὐ γράμματι, οὗ ὁ ἔπαινος οὐκ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων ἀλλʼ ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: all' o en to krypto Ioydaios, kai peritome kardias en pneymati ou grammati, ou o epainos ouk ex anthropon all' ek tou theou.
verses.translation: But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God.

verses.original: Τί οὖν τὸ περισσὸν τοῦ Ἰουδαίου, ἢ τίς ἡ ὠφέλεια τῆς περιτομῆς;
verses.translit: Ti oun to perisson tou Ioydaioy, e tis e ofeleia tes peritomes;
verses.translation: What advantage then hath the Jew? or what profit is there of circumcision?

verses.original: πολὺ κατὰ πάντα τρόπον. πρῶτον μὲν ⸀γὰρ ὅτι ἐπιστεύθησαν τὰ λόγια τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: polu kata panta tropon. proton men gar oti episteythisan ta logia tou theou.
verses.translation: Much every way: chiefly, because that unto them were committed the oracles of God.

verses.original: τί γάρ; εἰ ἠπίστησάν τινες, μὴ ἡ ἀπιστία αὐτῶν τὴν πίστιν τοῦ θεοῦ καταργήσει;
verses.translit: ti gar; ei epistisan tines, me e apistia auton ten pistin tou theou katargisei;
verses.translation: For what if some did not believe? shall their unbelief make the faith of God without effect?

verses.original: μὴ γένοιτο· γινέσθω δὲ ὁ θεὸς ἀληθής, πᾶς δὲ ἄνθρωπος ψεύστης, ⸀καθὼς γέγραπται· Ὅπως ἂν δικαιωθῇς ἐν τοῖς λόγοις σου καὶ ⸀νικήσεις ἐν τῷ κρίνεσθαί σε.
verses.translit: me genoito* ginestho de o theos alithis, pas de anthropos pseystis, kathos gegraptai* Opos an dikaiothes en tois logois soy kai nikiseis en to krinesthai se.
verses.translation: God forbid: yea, let God be true, but every man a liar; as it is written, That thou mightest be justified in thy sayings, and mightest overcome when thou art judged.

verses.original: εἰ δὲ ἡ ἀδικία ἡμῶν θεοῦ δικαιοσύνην συνίστησιν, τί ἐροῦμεν; μὴ ἄδικος ὁ θεὸς ὁ ἐπιφέρων τὴν ὀργήν; κατὰ ἄνθρωπον λέγω.
verses.translit: ei de e adikia emon theou dikaiosynin synistisin, ti eroumen; me adikos o theos o epiferon ten orgin; kata anthropon lego.
verses.translation: But if our unrighteousness commend the righteousness of God, what shall we say? Is God unrighteous who taketh vengeance? (I speak as a man)

verses.original: μὴ γένοιτο· ἐπεὶ πῶς κρινεῖ ὁ θεὸς τὸν κόσμον;
verses.translit: me genoito* epei pos krinei o theos ton kosmon;
verses.translation: God forbid: for then how shall God judge the world?

verses.original: εἰ ⸀δὲ ἡ ἀλήθεια τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν τῷ ἐμῷ ψεύσματι ἐπερίσσευσεν εἰς τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ, τί ἔτι κἀγὼ ὡς ἁμαρτωλὸς κρίνομαι,
verses.translit: ei de e alitheia tou theou en to emo pseysmati eperisseysen eis ten doxan autou, ti eti kago os amartolos krinomai,
verses.translation: For if the truth of God hath more abounded through my lie unto his glory; why yet am I also judged as a sinner?

verses.original: καὶ μὴ καθὼς βλασφημούμεθα καὶ καθώς φασίν τινες ἡμᾶς λέγειν ὅτι Ποιήσωμεν τὰ κακὰ ἵνα ἔλθῃ τὰ ἀγαθά; ὧν τὸ κρίμα ἔνδικόν ἐστιν.
verses.translit: kai me kathos vlasfimoymetha kai kathos fasin tines emas legein oti Poiisomen ta kaka ina elthe ta agatha; on to krima endikon estin.
verses.translation: And not rather , (as we be slanderously reported, and as some affirm that we say,) Let us do evil, that good may come? whose damnation is just.

verses.original: Τί οὖν; προεχόμεθα; οὐ πάντως, προῃτιασάμεθα γὰρ Ἰουδαίους τε καὶ Ἕλληνας πάντας ὑφʼ ἁμαρτίαν εἶναι,
verses.translit: Ti oun; proehometha; ou pantos, proetiasametha gar Ioydaioys te kai Ellinas pantas uf' amartian einai,
verses.translation: What then? are we better than they ? No, in no wise: for we have before proved both Jews and Gentiles, that they are all under sin;

verses.original: καθὼς γέγραπται ὅτι Οὐκ ἔστιν δίκαιος οὐδὲ εἷς,
verses.translit: kathos gegraptai oti Ouk estin dikaios oude eis,
verses.translation: As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one:

verses.original: οὐκ ἔστιν ⸀ὁ συνίων, οὐκ ἔστιν ⸁ὁ ἐκζητῶν τὸν θεόν·
verses.translit: ouk estin o synion, ouk estin o ekziton ton theon*
verses.translation: There is none that understandeth, there is none that seeketh after God.

verses.original: πάντες ἐξέκλιναν, ἅμα ἠχρεώθησαν· οὐκ ⸀ἔστιν ποιῶν χρηστότητα, οὐκ ἔστιν ἕως ἑνός.
verses.translit: pantes exeklinan, ama ehreothisan* ouk estin poion hristotita, ouk estin eos enos.
verses.translation: They are all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable; there is none that doeth good, no, not one.

verses.original: τάφος ἀνεῳγμένος ὁ λάρυγξ αὐτῶν, ταῖς γλώσσαις αὐτῶν ἐδολιοῦσαν, ἰὸς ἀσπίδων ὑπὸ τὰ χείλη αὐτῶν,
verses.translit: tafos aneogmenos o larygx auton, tais glossais auton edoliousan, ios aspidon upo ta heili auton,
verses.translation: Their throat is an open sepulchre; with their tongues they have used deceit; the poison of asps is under their lips:

verses.original: ὧν τὸ στόμα ἀρᾶς καὶ πικρίας γέμει·
verses.translit: on to stoma aras kai pikrias gemei*
verses.translation: Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness:

verses.original: ὀξεῖς οἱ πόδες αὐτῶν ἐκχέαι αἷμα,
verses.translit: oxeis oi podes auton ekheai aima,
verses.translation: Their feet are swift to shed blood:

verses.original: σύντριμμα καὶ ταλαιπωρία ἐν ταῖς ὁδοῖς αὐτῶν,
verses.translit: syntrimma kai talaiporia en tais odois auton,
verses.translation: Destruction and misery are in their ways:

verses.original: καὶ ὁδὸν εἰρήνης οὐκ ἔγνωσαν.
verses.translit: kai odon eirinis ouk egnosan.
verses.translation: And the way of peace have they not known:

verses.original: οὐκ ἔστιν φόβος θεοῦ ἀπέναντι τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: ouk estin fovos theou apenanti ton ofthalmon auton.
verses.translation: There is no fear of God before their eyes.

verses.original: Οἴδαμεν δὲ ὅτι ὅσα ὁ νόμος λέγει τοῖς ἐν τῷ νόμῳ λαλεῖ, ἵνα πᾶν στόμα φραγῇ καὶ ὑπόδικος γένηται πᾶς ὁ κόσμος τῷ θεῷ·
verses.translit: Oidamen de oti osa o nomos legei tois en to nomo lalei, ina pan stoma frage kai upodikos genitai pas o kosmos to theo*
verses.translation: Now we know that what things soever the law saith, it saith to them who are under the law: that every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty before God.

verses.original: διότι ἐξ ἔργων νόμου οὐ δικαιωθήσεται πᾶσα σὰρξ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ, διὰ γὰρ νόμου ἐπίγνωσις ἁμαρτίας.
verses.translit: dioti ex ergon nomoy ou dikaiothisetai pasa sarx enopion autou, dia gar nomoy epignosis amartias.
verses.translation: Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law is the knowledge of sin.

verses.original: Νυνὶ δὲ χωρὶς νόμου δικαιοσύνη θεοῦ πεφανέρωται, μαρτυρουμένη ὑπὸ τοῦ νόμου καὶ τῶν προφητῶν,
verses.translit: Nyni de horis nomoy dikaiosyni theou pefanerotai, martyroymeni upo tou nomoy kai ton profiton,
verses.translation: But now the righteousness of God without the law is manifested, being witnessed by the law and the prophets;

verses.original: δικαιοσύνη δὲ θεοῦ διὰ πίστεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, εἰς ⸀πάντας τοὺς πιστεύοντας, οὐ γάρ ἐστιν διαστολή.
verses.translit: dikaiosyni de theou dia pisteos Iisou Hristou, eis pantas tous pisteyontas, ou gar estin diastoli.
verses.translation: Even the righteousness of God which is by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe: for there is no difference:

verses.original: πάντες γὰρ ἥμαρτον καὶ ὑστεροῦνται τῆς δόξης τοῦ θεοῦ,
verses.translit: pantes gar emarton kai usterountai tes doxis tou theou,
verses.translation: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God;

verses.original: δικαιούμενοι δωρεὰν τῇ αὐτοῦ χάριτι διὰ τῆς ἀπολυτρώσεως τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ·
verses.translit: dikaioymenoi dorean te autou hariti dia tes apolytroseos tes en Hristo Iisou*
verses.translation: Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus:

verses.original: ὃν προέθετο ὁ θεὸς ἱλαστήριον ⸀διὰ πίστεως ἐν τῷ αὐτοῦ αἵματι εἰς ἔνδειξιν τῆς δικαιοσύνης αὐτοῦ διὰ τὴν πάρεσιν τῶν προγεγονότων ἁμαρτημάτων
verses.translit: on proetheto o theos ilastirion dia pisteos en to autou aimati eis endeixin tes dikaiosynis autou dia ten paresin ton progegonoton amartimaton
verses.translation: Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God;

verses.original: ἐν τῇ ἀνοχῇ τοῦ θεοῦ, πρὸς ⸀τὴν ἔνδειξιν τῆς δικαιοσύνης αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ νῦν καιρῷ, εἰς τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν δίκαιον καὶ δικαιοῦντα τὸν ἐκ πίστεως Ἰησοῦ.
verses.translit: en te anohe tou theou, pros ten endeixin tes dikaiosynis autou en to nun kairo, eis to einai auton dikaion kai dikaiounta ton ek pisteos Iisou.
verses.translation: To declare, I say , at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus.

verses.original: Ποῦ οὖν ἡ καύχησις; ἐξεκλείσθη. διὰ ποίου νόμου; τῶν ἔργων; οὐχί, ἀλλὰ διὰ νόμου πίστεως.
verses.translit: Pou oun e kayhisis; exekleisthi. dia poioy nomoy; ton ergon; ouhi, alla dia nomoy pisteos.
verses.translation: Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith.

verses.original: λογιζόμεθα ⸀γὰρ ⸂δικαιοῦσθαι πίστει⸃ ἄνθρωπον χωρὶς ἔργων νόμου.
verses.translit: logizometha gar dikaiousthai pistei anthropon horis ergon nomoy.
verses.translation: Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.

verses.original: ἢ Ἰουδαίων ὁ θεὸς μόνον; ⸀οὐχὶ καὶ ἐθνῶν; ναὶ καὶ ἐθνῶν,
verses.translit: e Ioydaion o theos monon; ouhi kai ethnon; nai kai ethnon,
verses.translation: Is he the God of the Jews only? is he not also of the Gentiles? Yes, of the Gentiles also:

verses.original: ⸀εἴπερ εἷς ὁ θεός, ὃς δικαιώσει περιτομὴν ἐκ πίστεως καὶ ἀκροβυστίαν διὰ τῆς πίστεως.
verses.translit: eiper eis o theos, os dikaiosei peritomen ek pisteos kai akrovystian dia tes pisteos.
verses.translation: Seeing it is one God, which shall justify the circumcision by faith, and uncircumcision through faith.

verses.original: νόμον οὖν καταργοῦμεν διὰ τῆς πίστεως; μὴ γένοιτο, ἀλλὰ νόμον ⸀ἱστάνομεν.
verses.translit: nomon oun katargoumen dia tes pisteos; me genoito, alla nomon istanomen.
verses.translation: Do we then make void the law through faith? God forbid: yea, we establish the law.

verses.original: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν ⸀εὑρηκέναι Ἀβραὰμ τὸν ⸀προπάτορα ⸀ἡμῶν κατὰ σάρκα;
verses.translit: Ti oun eroumen eurikenai Avraam ton propatora emon kata sarka;
verses.translation: What shall we say then that Abraham our father, as pertaining to the flesh, hath found?

verses.original: εἰ γὰρ Ἀβραὰμ ἐξ ἔργων ἐδικαιώθη, ἔχει καύχημα· ἀλλʼ οὐ ⸀πρὸς θεόν,
verses.translit: ei gar Avraam ex ergon edikaiothi, ehei kayhima* all' ou pros theon,
verses.translation: For if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory; but not before God.

verses.original: τί γὰρ ἡ γραφὴ λέγει; Ἐπίστευσεν δὲ Ἀβραὰμ τῷ θεῷ καὶ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην.
verses.translit: ti gar e grafe legei; Episteysen de Avraam to theo kai elogisthi auto eis dikaiosynin.
verses.translation: For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness.

verses.original: τῷ δὲ ἐργαζομένῳ ὁ μισθὸς οὐ λογίζεται κατὰ χάριν ἀλλὰ κατὰ ὀφείλημα·
verses.translit: to de ergazomeno o misthos ou logizetai kata harin alla kata ofeilima*
verses.translation: Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt.

verses.original: τῷ δὲ μὴ ἐργαζομένῳ, πιστεύοντι δὲ ἐπὶ τὸν δικαιοῦντα τὸν ἀσεβῆ, λογίζεται ἡ πίστις αὐτοῦ εἰς δικαιοσύνην,
verses.translit: to de me ergazomeno, pisteyonti de epi ton dikaiounta ton aseve, logizetai e pistis autou eis dikaiosynin,
verses.translation: But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness.

verses.original: καθάπερ καὶ Δαυὶδ λέγει τὸν μακαρισμὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ᾧ ὁ θεὸς λογίζεται δικαιοσύνην χωρὶς ἔργων·
verses.translit: kathaper kai Dayid legei ton makarismon tou anthropoy o o theos logizetai dikaiosynin horis ergon*
verses.translation: Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works,

verses.original: Μακάριοι ὧν ἀφέθησαν αἱ ἀνομίαι καὶ ὧν ἐπεκαλύφθησαν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι,
verses.translit: Makarioi on afethisan ai anomiai kai on epekalyfthisan ai amartiai,
verses.translation: Saying , Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered.

verses.original: μακάριος ἀνὴρ ⸀οὗ οὐ μὴ λογίσηται κύριος ἁμαρτίαν.
verses.translit: makarios aner ou ou me logisitai kyrios amartian.
verses.translation: Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin.

verses.original: Ὁ μακαρισμὸς οὖν οὗτος ἐπὶ τὴν περιτομὴν ἢ καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν ἀκροβυστίαν; λέγομεν ⸀γάρ· Ἐλογίσθη τῷ Ἀβραὰμ ἡ πίστις εἰς δικαιοσύνην.
verses.translit: O makarismos oun outos epi ten peritomen e kai epi ten akrovystian; legomen gar* Elogisthi to Avraam e pistis eis dikaiosynin.
verses.translation: Cometh this blessedness then upon the circumcision only , or upon the uncircumcision also? for we say that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness.

verses.original: πῶς οὖν ἐλογίσθη; ἐν περιτομῇ ὄντι ἢ ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ; οὐκ ἐν περιτομῇ ἀλλʼ ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ·
verses.translit: pos oun elogisthi; en peritome onti e en akrovystia; ouk en peritome all' en akrovystia*
verses.translation: How was it then reckoned? when he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.

verses.original: καὶ σημεῖον ἔλαβεν περιτομῆς, σφραγῖδα τῆς δικαιοσύνης τῆς πίστεως τῆς ἐν τῇ ἀκροβυστίᾳ, εἰς τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν πατέρα πάντων τῶν πιστευόντων διʼ ἀκροβυστίας, εἰς τὸ ⸀λογισθῆναι αὐτοῖς τὴν δικαιοσύνην,
verses.translit: kai simeion elaven peritomes, sfragida tes dikaiosynis tes pisteos tes en te akrovystia, eis to einai auton patera panton ton pisteyonton di' akrovystias, eis to logisthenai autois ten dikaiosynin,
verses.translation: And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had yet being uncircumcised: that he might be the father of all them that believe, though they be not circumcised; that righteousness might be imputed unto them also:

verses.original: καὶ πατέρα περιτομῆς τοῖς οὐκ ἐκ περιτομῆς μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῖς στοιχοῦσιν τοῖς ἴχνεσιν τῆς ⸂ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ πίστεως⸃ τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν Ἀβραάμ.
verses.translit: kai patera peritomes tois ouk ek peritomes monon alla kai tois stoihousin tois ihnesin tes en akrovystia pisteos tou patros emon Avraam.
verses.translation: And the father of circumcision to them who are not of the circumcision only, but who also walk in the steps of that faith of our father Abraham, which he had being yet uncircumcised.

verses.original: Οὐ γὰρ διὰ νόμου ἡ ἐπαγγελία τῷ Ἀβραὰμ ἢ τῷ σπέρματι αὐτοῦ, τὸ κληρονόμον αὐτὸν ⸀εἶναι κόσμου, ἀλλὰ διὰ δικαιοσύνης πίστεως·
verses.translit: Ou gar dia nomoy e epaggelia to Avraam e to spermati autou, to klironomon auton einai kosmoy, alla dia dikaiosynis pisteos*
verses.translation: For the promise, that he should be the heir of the world, was not to Abraham, or to his seed, through the law, but through the righteousness of faith.

verses.original: εἰ γὰρ οἱ ἐκ νόμου κληρονόμοι, κεκένωται ἡ πίστις καὶ κατήργηται ἡ ἐπαγγελία·
verses.translit: ei gar oi ek nomoy klironomoi, kekenotai e pistis kai katirgitai e epaggelia*
verses.translation: For if they which are of the law be heirs, faith is made void, and the promise made of none effect:

verses.original: ὁ γὰρ νόμος ὀργὴν κατεργάζεται, οὗ ⸀δὲ οὐκ ἔστιν νόμος, οὐδὲ παράβασις.
verses.translit: o gar nomos orgen katergazetai, ou de ouk estin nomos, oude paravasis.
verses.translation: Because the law worketh wrath: for where no law is, there is no transgression.

verses.original: Διὰ τοῦτο ἐκ πίστεως, ἵνα κατὰ χάριν, εἰς τὸ εἶναι βεβαίαν τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν παντὶ τῷ σπέρματι, οὐ τῷ ἐκ τοῦ νόμου μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ τῷ ἐκ πίστεως Ἀβραάμ (ὅς ἐστιν πατὴρ πάντων ἡμῶν,
verses.translit: Dia touto ek pisteos, ina kata harin, eis to einai vevaian ten epaggelian panti to spermati, ou to ek tou nomoy monon alla kai to ek pisteos Avraam (os estin pater panton emon,
verses.translation: Therefore it is of faith, that it might be by grace; to the end the promise might be sure to all the seed; not to that only which is of the law, but to that also which is of the faith of Abraham; who is the father of us all,

verses.original: καθὼς γέγραπται ὅτι Πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν τέθεικά σε), κατέναντι οὗ ἐπίστευσεν θεοῦ τοῦ ζῳοποιοῦντος τοὺς νεκροὺς καὶ καλοῦντος τὰ μὴ ὄντα ὡς ὄντα·
verses.translit: kathos gegraptai oti Patera pollon ethnon tetheika se), katenanti ou episteysen theou tou zoopoiountos tous nekrous kai kalountos ta me onta os onta*
verses.translation: (As it is written, I have made thee a father of many nations,) before him whom he believed, even God, who quickeneth the dead, and calleth those things which be not as though they were.

verses.original: ὃς παρʼ ἐλπίδα ἐπʼ ἐλπίδι ἐπίστευσεν εἰς τὸ γενέσθαι αὐτὸν πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν κατὰ τὸ εἰρημένον· Οὕτως ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα σου·
verses.translit: os par' elpida ep' elpidi episteysen eis to genesthai auton patera pollon ethnon kata to eirimenon* Outos estai to sperma soy*
verses.translation: Who against hope believed in hope, that he might become the father of many nations; according to that which was spoken, So shall thy seed be.

verses.original: καὶ μὴ ἀσθενήσας τῇ ⸀πίστει κατενόησεν τὸ ἑαυτοῦ ⸀σῶμα νενεκρωμένον, ἑκατονταετής που ὑπάρχων, καὶ τὴν νέκρωσιν τῆς μήτρας Σάρρας,
verses.translit: kai me asthenisas te pistei katenoisen to eaytou soma nenekromenon, ekatontaetis poy uparhon, kai ten nekrosin tes mitras Sarras,
verses.translation: And being not weak in faith, he considered not his own body now dead, when he was about an hundred years old, neither yet the deadness of Sara’s womb:

verses.original: εἰς δὲ τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ θεοῦ οὐ διεκρίθη τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ ἀλλὰ ἐνεδυναμώθη τῇ πίστει, δοὺς δόξαν τῷ θεῷ
verses.translit: eis de ten epaggelian tou theou ou diekrithi te apistia alla enedynamothi te pistei, dous doxan to theo
verses.translation: He staggered not at the promise of God through unbelief; but was strong in faith, giving glory to God;

verses.original: καὶ πληροφορηθεὶς ὅτι ὃ ἐπήγγελται δυνατός ἐστιν καὶ ποιῆσαι.
verses.translit: kai pliroforitheis oti o epiggeltai dynatos estin kai poiesai.
verses.translation: And being fully persuaded that, what he had promised, he was able also to perform.

verses.original: ⸀διὸ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην.
verses.translit: dio elogisthi auto eis dikaiosynin.
verses.translation: And therefore it was imputed to him for righteousness.

verses.original: Οὐκ ἐγράφη δὲ διʼ αὐτὸν μόνον ὅτι ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ,
verses.translit: Ouk egrafi de di' auton monon oti elogisthi auto,
verses.translation: Now it was not written for his sake alone, that it was imputed to him;

verses.original: ἀλλὰ καὶ διʼ ἡμᾶς οἷς μέλλει λογίζεσθαι, τοῖς πιστεύουσιν ἐπὶ τὸν ἐγείραντα Ἰησοῦν τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν ἐκ νεκρῶν,
verses.translit: alla kai di' emas ois mellei logizesthai, tois pisteyoysin epi ton egeiranta Iisoun ton kyrion emon ek nekron,
verses.translation: But for us also, to whom it shall be imputed, if we believe on him that raised up Jesus our Lord from the dead;

verses.original: ὃς παρεδόθη διὰ τὰ παραπτώματα ἡμῶν καὶ ἠγέρθη διὰ τὴν δικαίωσιν ἡμῶν.
verses.translit: os paredothi dia ta paraptomata emon kai egerthi dia ten dikaiosin emon.
verses.translation: Who was delivered for our offences, and was raised again for our justification.

verses.original: Δικαιωθέντες οὖν ἐκ πίστεως εἰρήνην ⸀ἔχομεν πρὸς τὸν θεὸν διὰ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ,
verses.translit: Dikaiothentes oun ek pisteos eirinin ehomen pros ton theon dia tou kyrioy emon Iisou Hristou,
verses.translation: Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ:

verses.original: διʼ οὗ καὶ τὴν προσαγωγὴν ἐσχήκαμεν τῇ πίστει εἰς τὴν χάριν ταύτην ἐν ᾗ ἑστήκαμεν, καὶ καυχώμεθα ἐπʼ ἐλπίδι τῆς δόξης τοῦ θεοῦ·
verses.translit: di' ou kai ten prosagogen eshikamen te pistei eis ten harin taytin en e estikamen, kai kayhometha ep' elpidi tes doxis tou theou*
verses.translation: By whom also we have access by faith into this grace wherein we stand, and rejoice in hope of the glory of God.

verses.original: οὐ μόνον δέ, ἀλλὰ καὶ ⸀καυχώμεθα ἐν ταῖς θλίψεσιν, εἰδότες ὅτι ἡ θλῖψις ὑπομονὴν κατεργάζεται,
verses.translit: ou monon de, alla kai kayhometha en tais thlipsesin, eidotes oti e thlipsis upomonen katergazetai,
verses.translation: And not only so , but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience;

verses.original: ἡ δὲ ὑπομονὴ δοκιμήν, ἡ δὲ δοκιμὴ ἐλπίδα.
verses.translit: e de upomone dokimin, e de dokime elpida.
verses.translation: And patience, experience; and experience, hope:

verses.original: ἡ δὲ ἐλπὶς οὐ καταισχύνει· ὅτι ἡ ἀγάπη τοῦ θεοῦ ἐκκέχυται ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἡμῶν διὰ πνεύματος ἁγίου τοῦ δοθέντος ἡμῖν.
verses.translit: e de elpis ou kataishynei* oti e agapi tou theou ekkehytai en tais kardiais emon dia pneymatos agioy tou dothentos emin.
verses.translation: And hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us.

verses.original: ⸂Ἔτι γὰρ⸃ Χριστὸς ὄντων ἡμῶν ἀσθενῶν ⸀ἔτι κατὰ καιρὸν ὑπὲρ ἀσεβῶν ἀπέθανεν.
verses.translit: Eti gar Hristos onton emon asthenon eti kata kairon uper asevon apethanen.
verses.translation: For when we were yet without strength, in due time Christ died for the ungodly.

verses.original: μόλις γὰρ ὑπὲρ δικαίου τις ἀποθανεῖται· ὑπὲρ γὰρ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ τάχα τις καὶ τολμᾷ ἀποθανεῖν·
verses.translit: molis gar uper dikaioy tis apothaneitai* uper gar tou agathou taha tis kai tolma apothanein*
verses.translation: For scarcely for a righteous man will one die: yet peradventure for a good man some would even dare to die.

verses.original: συνίστησιν δὲ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ἀγάπην εἰς ἡμᾶς ὁ θεὸς ὅτι ἔτι ἁμαρτωλῶν ὄντων ἡμῶν Χριστὸς ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἀπέθανεν.
verses.translit: synistisin de ten eaytou agapin eis emas o theos oti eti amartolon onton emon Hristos uper emon apethanen.
verses.translation: But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.

verses.original: πολλῷ οὖν μᾶλλον δικαιωθέντες νῦν ἐν τῷ αἵματι αὐτοῦ σωθησόμεθα διʼ αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῆς ὀργῆς.
verses.translit: pollo oun mallon dikaiothentes nun en to aimati autou sothisometha di' autou apo tes orges.
verses.translation: Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him.

verses.original: εἰ γὰρ ἐχθροὶ ὄντες κατηλλάγημεν τῷ θεῷ διὰ τοῦ θανάτου τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, πολλῷ μᾶλλον καταλλαγέντες σωθησόμεθα ἐν τῇ ζωῇ αὐτοῦ·
verses.translit: ei gar ehthroi ontes katillagimen to theo dia tou thanatoy tou yiou autou, pollo mallon katallagentes sothisometha en te zoe autou*
verses.translation: For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life.

verses.original: οὐ μόνον δέ, ἀλλὰ καὶ καυχώμενοι ἐν τῷ θεῷ διὰ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, διʼ οὗ νῦν τὴν καταλλαγὴν ἐλάβομεν.
verses.translit: ou monon de, alla kai kayhomenoi en to theo dia tou kyrioy emon Iisou Hristou, di' ou nun ten katallagen elavomen.
verses.translation: And not only so , but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement.

verses.original: Διὰ τοῦτο ὥσπερ διʼ ἑνὸς ἀνθρώπου ἡ ἁμαρτία εἰς τὸν κόσμον εἰσῆλθεν καὶ διὰ τῆς ἁμαρτίας ὁ θάνατος, καὶ οὕτως εἰς πάντας ἀνθρώπους ὁ θάνατος διῆλθεν ἐφʼ ᾧ πάντες ἥμαρτον—
verses.translit: Dia touto osper di' enos anthropoy e amartia eis ton kosmon eiselthen kai dia tes amartias o thanatos, kai outos eis pantas anthropoys o thanatos dielthen ef' o pantes emarton--
verses.translation: Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned:

verses.original: ἄχρι γὰρ νόμου ἁμαρτία ἦν ἐν κόσμῳ, ἁμαρτία δὲ οὐκ ἐλλογεῖται μὴ ὄντος νόμου,
verses.translit: ahri gar nomoy amartia en en kosmo, amartia de ouk ellogeitai me ontos nomoy,
verses.translation: (For until the law sin was in the world: but sin is not imputed when there is no law.

verses.original: ἀλλὰ ἐβασίλευσεν ὁ θάνατος ἀπὸ Ἀδὰμ μέχρι Μωϋσέως καὶ ἐπὶ τοὺς μὴ ἁμαρτήσαντας ἐπὶ τῷ ὁμοιώματι τῆς παραβάσεως Ἀδάμ, ὅς ἐστιν τύπος τοῦ μέλλοντος.
verses.translit: alla evasileysen o thanatos apo Adam mehri Moyseos kai epi tous me amartisantas epi to omoiomati tes paravaseos Adam, os estin typos tou mellontos.
verses.translation: Nevertheless death reigned from Adam to Moses, even over them that had not sinned after the similitude of Adam’s transgression, who is the figure of him that was to come.

verses.original: Ἀλλʼ οὐχ ὡς τὸ παράπτωμα, οὕτως καὶ τὸ χάρισμα· εἰ γὰρ τῷ τοῦ ἑνὸς παραπτώματι οἱ πολλοὶ ἀπέθανον, πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἡ χάρις τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἡ δωρεὰ ἐν χάριτι τῇ τοῦ ἑνὸς ἀνθρώπου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς τοὺς πολλοὺς ἐπερίσσευσεν.
verses.translit: All' ouh os to paraptoma, outos kai to harisma* ei gar to tou enos paraptomati oi polloi apethanon, pollo mallon e haris tou theou kai e dorea en hariti te tou enos anthropoy Iisou Hristou eis tous pollous eperisseysen.
