verses.translation: But not as the offence, so also is the free gift. For if through the offence of one many be dead, much more the grace of God, and the gift by grace, which is by one man, Jesus Christ, hath abounded unto many.

verses.original: καὶ οὐχ ὡς διʼ ἑνὸς ἁμαρτήσαντος τὸ δώρημα· τὸ μὲν γὰρ κρίμα ἐξ ἑνὸς εἰς κατάκριμα, τὸ δὲ χάρισμα ἐκ πολλῶν παραπτωμάτων εἰς δικαίωμα.
verses.translit: kai ouh os di' enos amartisantos to dorima* to men gar krima ex enos eis katakrima, to de harisma ek pollon paraptomaton eis dikaioma.
verses.translation: And not as it was by one that sinned, so is the gift: for the judgment was by one to condemnation, but the free gift is of many offences unto justification.

verses.original: εἰ γὰρ τῷ τοῦ ἑνὸς παραπτώματι ὁ θάνατος ἐβασίλευσεν διὰ τοῦ ἑνός, πολλῷ μᾶλλον οἱ τὴν περισσείαν τῆς χάριτος καὶ τῆς δωρεᾶς τῆς δικαιοσύνης λαμβάνοντες ἐν ζωῇ βασιλεύσουσιν διὰ τοῦ ἑνὸς Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
verses.translit: ei gar to tou enos paraptomati o thanatos evasileysen dia tou enos, pollo mallon oi ten perisseian tes haritos kai tes doreas tes dikaiosynis lamvanontes en zoe vasileysoysin dia tou enos Iisou Hristou.
verses.translation: For if by one man’s offence death reigned by one; much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ.)

verses.original: Ἄρα οὖν ὡς διʼ ἑνὸς παραπτώματος εἰς πάντας ἀνθρώπους εἰς κατάκριμα, οὕτως καὶ διʼ ἑνὸς δικαιώματος εἰς πάντας ἀνθρώπους εἰς δικαίωσιν ζωῆς·
verses.translit: Ara oun os di' enos paraptomatos eis pantas anthropoys eis katakrima, outos kai di' enos dikaiomatos eis pantas anthropoys eis dikaiosin zoes*
verses.translation: Therefore as by the offence of one judgment came upon all men to condemnation; even so by the righteousness of one the free gift came upon all men unto justification of life.

verses.original: ὥσπερ γὰρ διὰ τῆς παρακοῆς τοῦ ἑνὸς ἀνθρώπου ἁμαρτωλοὶ κατεστάθησαν οἱ πολλοί, οὕτως καὶ διὰ τῆς ὑπακοῆς τοῦ ἑνὸς δίκαιοι κατασταθήσονται οἱ πολλοί.
verses.translit: osper gar dia tes parakoes tou enos anthropoy amartoloi katestathisan oi polloi, outos kai dia tes upakoes tou enos dikaioi katastathisontai oi polloi.
verses.translation: For as by one man’s disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous.

verses.original: νόμος δὲ παρεισῆλθεν ἵνα πλεονάσῃ τὸ παράπτωμα· οὗ δὲ ἐπλεόνασεν ἡ ἁμαρτία, ὑπερεπερίσσευσεν ἡ χάρις,
verses.translit: nomos de pareiselthen ina pleonase to paraptoma* ou de epleonasen e amartia, upereperisseysen e haris,
verses.translation: Moreover the law entered, that the offence might abound. But where sin abounded, grace did much more abound:

verses.original: ἵνα ὥσπερ ἐβασίλευσεν ἡ ἁμαρτία ἐν τῷ θανάτῳ, οὕτως καὶ ἡ χάρις βασιλεύσῃ διὰ δικαιοσύνης εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν.
verses.translit: ina osper evasileysen e amartia en to thanato, outos kai e haris vasileyse dia dikaiosynis eis zoen aionion dia Iisou Hristou tou kyrioy emon.
verses.translation: That as sin hath reigned unto death, even so might grace reign through righteousness unto eternal life by Jesus Christ our Lord.

verses.original: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν; ⸀ἐπιμένωμεν τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ, ἵνα ἡ χάρις πλεονάσῃ;
verses.translit: Ti oun eroumen; epimenomen te amartia, ina e haris pleonase;
verses.translation: What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?

verses.original: μὴ γένοιτο· οἵτινες ἀπεθάνομεν τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ, πῶς ἔτι ζήσομεν ἐν αὐτῇ;
verses.translit: me genoito* oitines apethanomen te amartia, pos eti zisomen en aute;
verses.translation: God forbid. How shall we, that are dead to sin, live any longer therein?

verses.original: ἢ ἀγνοεῖτε ὅτι ὅσοι ἐβαπτίσθημεν εἰς Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν εἰς τὸν θάνατον αὐτοῦ ἐβαπτίσθημεν;
verses.translit: e agnoeite oti osoi evaptisthimen eis Hriston Iisoun eis ton thanaton autou evaptisthimen;
verses.translation: Know ye not, that so many of us as were baptized into Jesus Christ were baptized into his death?

verses.original: συνετάφημεν οὖν αὐτῷ διὰ τοῦ βαπτίσματος εἰς τὸν θάνατον, ἵνα ὥσπερ ἠγέρθη Χριστὸς ἐκ νεκρῶν διὰ τῆς δόξης τοῦ πατρός, οὕτως καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐν καινότητι ζωῆς περιπατήσωμεν.
verses.translit: synetafimen oun auto dia tou vaptismatos eis ton thanaton, ina osper egerthi Hristos ek nekron dia tes doxis tou patros, outos kai emeis en kainotiti zoes peripatisomen.
verses.translation: Therefore we are buried with him by baptism into death: that like as Christ was raised up from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life.

verses.original: Εἰ γὰρ σύμφυτοι γεγόναμεν τῷ ὁμοιώματι τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ, ἀλλὰ καὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως ἐσόμεθα·
verses.translit: Ei gar symfytoi gegonamen to omoiomati tou thanatoy autou, alla kai tes anastaseos esometha*
verses.translation: For if we have been planted together in the likeness of his death, we shall be also in the likeness of his resurrection:

verses.original: τοῦτο γινώσκοντες ὅτι ὁ παλαιὸς ἡμῶν ἄνθρωπος συνεσταυρώθη, ἵνα καταργηθῇ τὸ σῶμα τῆς ἁμαρτίας, τοῦ μηκέτι δουλεύειν ἡμᾶς τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ,
verses.translit: touto ginoskontes oti o palaios emon anthropos synestayrothi, ina katargithe to soma tes amartias, tou miketi doyleyein emas te amartia,
verses.translation: Knowing this, that our old man is crucified with him , that the body of sin might be destroyed, that henceforth we should not serve sin.

verses.original: ὁ γὰρ ἀποθανὼν δεδικαίωται ἀπὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας.
verses.translit: o gar apothanon dedikaiotai apo tes amartias.
verses.translation: For he that is dead is freed from sin.

verses.original: εἰ δὲ ἀπεθάνομεν σὺν Χριστῷ, πιστεύομεν ὅτι καὶ συζήσομεν αὐτῷ·
verses.translit: ei de apethanomen sun Hristo, pisteyomen oti kai syzisomen auto*
verses.translation: Now if we be dead with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with him:

verses.original: εἰδότες ὅτι Χριστὸς ἐγερθεὶς ἐκ νεκρῶν οὐκέτι ἀποθνῄσκει, θάνατος αὐτοῦ οὐκέτι κυριεύει·
verses.translit: eidotes oti Hristos egertheis ek nekron ouketi apothneskei, thanatos autou ouketi kyrieyei*
verses.translation: Knowing that Christ being raised from the dead dieth no more; death hath no more dominion over him.

verses.original: ὃ γὰρ ἀπέθανεν, τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ ἀπέθανεν ἐφάπαξ· ὃ δὲ ζῇ, ζῇ τῷ θεῷ.
verses.translit: o gar apethanen, te amartia apethanen efapax* o de ze, ze to theo.
verses.translation: For in that he died, he died unto sin once: but in that he liveth, he liveth unto God.

verses.original: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς λογίζεσθε ἑαυτοὺς ⸂εἶναι νεκροὺς μὲν⸃ τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ ζῶντας δὲ τῷ θεῷ ἐν Χριστῷ ⸀Ἰησοῦ.
verses.translit: outos kai umeis logizesthe eaytous einai nekrous men te amartia zontas de to theo en Hristo Iisou.
verses.translation: Likewise reckon ye also yourselves to be dead indeed unto sin, but alive unto God through Jesus Christ our Lord.

verses.original: Μὴ οὖν βασιλευέτω ἡ ἁμαρτία ἐν τῷ θνητῷ ὑμῶν σώματι εἰς τὸ ⸀ὑπακούειν ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις αὐτοῦ,
verses.translit: Me oun vasileyeto e amartia en to thnito umon somati eis to upakoyein tais epithymiais autou,
verses.translation: Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that ye should obey it in the lusts thereof.

verses.original: μηδὲ παριστάνετε τὰ μέλη ὑμῶν ὅπλα ἀδικίας τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ, ἀλλὰ παραστήσατε ἑαυτοὺς τῷ θεῷ ⸀ὡσεὶ ἐκ νεκρῶν ζῶντας καὶ τὰ μέλη ὑμῶν ὅπλα δικαιοσύνης τῷ θεῷ.
verses.translit: mide paristanete ta meli umon opla adikias te amartia, alla parastisate eaytous to theo osei ek nekron zontas kai ta meli umon opla dikaiosynis to theo.
verses.translation: Neither yield ye your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin: but yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness unto God.

verses.original: ἁμαρτία γὰρ ὑμῶν οὐ κυριεύσει, οὐ γάρ ἐστε ὑπὸ νόμον ἀλλὰ ὑπὸ χάριν.
verses.translit: amartia gar umon ou kyrieysei, ou gar este upo nomon alla upo harin.
verses.translation: For sin shall not have dominion over you: for ye are not under the law, but under grace.

verses.original: Τί οὖν; ⸀ἁμαρτήσωμεν ὅτι οὐκ ἐσμὲν ὑπὸ νόμον ἀλλὰ ὑπὸ χάριν; μὴ γένοιτο·
verses.translit: Ti oun; amartisomen oti ouk esmen upo nomon alla upo harin; me genoito*
verses.translation: What then? shall we sin, because we are not under the law, but under grace? God forbid.

verses.original: οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ᾧ παριστάνετε ἑαυτοὺς δούλους εἰς ὑπακοήν, δοῦλοί ἐστε ᾧ ὑπακούετε, ἤτοι ἁμαρτίας εἰς θάνατον ἢ ὑπακοῆς εἰς δικαιοσύνην;
verses.translit: ouk oidate oti o paristanete eaytous doyloys eis upakoin, douloi este o upakoyete, etoi amartias eis thanaton e upakoes eis dikaiosynin;
verses.translation: Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?

verses.original: χάρις δὲ τῷ θεῷ ὅτι ἦτε δοῦλοι τῆς ἁμαρτίας ὑπηκούσατε δὲ ἐκ καρδίας εἰς ὃν παρεδόθητε τύπον διδαχῆς,
verses.translit: haris de to theo oti ete douloi tes amartias upikoysate de ek kardias eis on paredothite typon didahes,
verses.translation: But God be thanked, that ye were the servants of sin, but ye have obeyed from the heart that form of doctrine which was delivered you.

verses.original: ἐλευθερωθέντες δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας ἐδουλώθητε τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ·
verses.translit: eleytherothentes de apo tes amartias edoylothite te dikaiosyne*
verses.translation: Being then made free from sin, ye became the servants of righteousness.

verses.original: ἀνθρώπινον λέγω διὰ τὴν ἀσθένειαν τῆς σαρκὸς ὑμῶν· ὥσπερ γὰρ παρεστήσατε τὰ μέλη ὑμῶν δοῦλα τῇ ἀκαθαρσίᾳ καὶ τῇ ἀνομίᾳ εἰς τὴν ἀνομίαν, οὕτως νῦν παραστήσατε τὰ μέλη ὑμῶν δοῦλα τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ εἰς ἁγιασμόν.
verses.translit: anthropinon lego dia ten astheneian tes sarkos umon* osper gar parestisate ta meli umon doula te akatharsia kai te anomia eis ten anomian, outos nun parastisate ta meli umon doula te dikaiosyne eis agiasmon.
verses.translation: I speak after the manner of men because of the infirmity of your flesh: for as ye have yielded your members servants to uncleanness and to iniquity unto iniquity; even so now yield your members servants to righteousness unto holiness.

verses.original: Ὅτε γὰρ δοῦλοι ἦτε τῆς ἁμαρτίας, ἐλεύθεροι ἦτε τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ.
verses.translit: Ote gar douloi ete tes amartias, eleytheroi ete te dikaiosyne.
verses.translation: For when ye were the servants of sin, ye were free from righteousness.

verses.original: τίνα οὖν καρπὸν εἴχετε τότε ἐφʼ οἷς νῦν ἐπαισχύνεσθε; τὸ γὰρ τέλος ἐκείνων θάνατος·
verses.translit: tina oun karpon eihete tote ef' ois nun epaishynesthe? to gar telos ekeinon thanatos*
verses.translation: What fruit had ye then in those things whereof ye are now ashamed? for the end of those things is death.

verses.original: νυνὶ δέ, ἐλευθερωθέντες ἀπὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας δουλωθέντες δὲ τῷ θεῷ, ἔχετε τὸν καρπὸν ὑμῶν εἰς ἁγιασμόν, τὸ δὲ τέλος ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
verses.translit: nyni de, eleytherothentes apo tes amartias doylothentes de to theo, ehete ton karpon umon eis agiasmon, to de telos zoen aionion.
verses.translation: But now being made free from sin, and become servants to God, ye have your fruit unto holiness, and the end everlasting life.

verses.original: τὰ γὰρ ὀψώνια τῆς ἁμαρτίας θάνατος, τὸ δὲ χάρισμα τοῦ θεοῦ ζωὴ αἰώνιος ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ κυρίῳ ἡμῶν.
verses.translit: ta gar opsonia tes amartias thanatos, to de harisma tou theou zoe aionios en Hristo Iisou to kyrio emon.
verses.translation: For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

verses.original: Ἢ ἀγνοεῖτε, ἀδελφοί, γινώσκουσιν γὰρ νόμον λαλῶ, ὅτι ὁ νόμος κυριεύει τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐφʼ ὅσον χρόνον ζῇ;
verses.translit: E agnoeite, adelfoi, ginoskoysin gar nomon lalo, oti o nomos kyrieyei tou anthropoy ef' oson hronon ze;
verses.translation: Know ye not, brethren, (for I speak to them that know the law,) how that the law hath dominion over a man as long as he liveth?

verses.original: ἡ γὰρ ὕπανδρος γυνὴ τῷ ζῶντι ἀνδρὶ δέδεται νόμῳ· ἐὰν δὲ ἀποθάνῃ ὁ ἀνήρ, κατήργηται ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου τοῦ ἀνδρός.
verses.translit: e gar upandros gyne to zonti andri dedetai nomo* ean de apothane o anir, katirgitai apo tou nomoy tou andros.
verses.translation: For the woman which hath an husband is bound by the law to her husband so long as he liveth; but if the husband be dead, she is loosed from the law of her husband.

verses.original: ἄρα οὖν ζῶντος τοῦ ἀνδρὸς μοιχαλὶς χρηματίσει ἐὰν γένηται ἀνδρὶ ἑτέρῳ· ἐὰν δὲ ἀποθάνῃ ὁ ἀνήρ, ἐλευθέρα ἐστὶν ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου, τοῦ μὴ εἶναι αὐτὴν μοιχαλίδα γενομένην ἀνδρὶ ἑτέρῳ.
verses.translit: ara oun zontos tou andros moihalis hrimatisei ean genitai andri etero* ean de apothane o anir, eleythera estin apo tou nomoy, tou me einai auten moihalida genomenin andri etero.
verses.translation: So then if, while her husband liveth, she be married to another man, she shall be called an adulteress: but if her husband be dead, she is free from that law; so that she is no adulteress, though she be married to another man.

verses.original: Ὥστε, ἀδελφοί μου, καὶ ὑμεῖς ἐθανατώθητε τῷ νόμῳ διὰ τοῦ σώματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ, εἰς τὸ γενέσθαι ὑμᾶς ἑτέρῳ, τῷ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἐγερθέντι ἵνα καρποφορήσωμεν τῷ θεῷ.
verses.translit: Oste, adelfoi moy, kai umeis ethanatothite to nomo dia tou somatos tou Hristou, eis to genesthai umas etero, to ek nekron egerthenti ina karpoforisomen to theo.
verses.translation: Wherefore, my brethren, ye also are become dead to the law by the body of Christ; that ye should be married to another, even to him who is raised from the dead, that we should bring forth fruit unto God.

verses.original: ὅτε γὰρ ἦμεν ἐν τῇ σαρκί, τὰ παθήματα τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν τὰ διὰ τοῦ νόμου ἐνηργεῖτο ἐν τοῖς μέλεσιν ἡμῶν εἰς τὸ καρποφορῆσαι τῷ θανάτῳ·
verses.translit: ote gar emen en te sarki, ta pathimata ton amartion ta dia tou nomoy enirgeito en tois melesin emon eis to karpoforesai to thanato*
verses.translation: For when we were in the flesh, the motions of sins, which were by the law, did work in our members to bring forth fruit unto death.

verses.original: νυνὶ δὲ κατηργήθημεν ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου, ἀποθανόντες ἐν ᾧ κατειχόμεθα, ὥστε δουλεύειν ἡμᾶς ἐν καινότητι πνεύματος καὶ οὐ παλαιότητι γράμματος.
verses.translit: nyni de katirgithimen apo tou nomoy, apothanontes en o kateihometha, oste doyleyein emas en kainotiti pneymatos kai ou palaiotiti grammatos.
verses.translation: But now we are delivered from the law, that being dead wherein we were held; that we should serve in newness of spirit, and not in the oldness of the letter.

verses.original: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν; ὁ νόμος ἁμαρτία; μὴ γένοιτο· ἀλλὰ τὴν ἁμαρτίαν οὐκ ἔγνων εἰ μὴ διὰ νόμου, τήν τε γὰρ ἐπιθυμίαν οὐκ ᾔδειν εἰ μὴ ὁ νόμος ἔλεγεν· Οὐκ ἐπιθυμήσεις·
verses.translit: Ti oun eroumen; o nomos amartia; me genoito* alla ten amartian ouk egnon ei me dia nomoy, tin te gar epithymian ouk edein ei me o nomos elegen* Ouk epithymiseis*
verses.translation: What shall we say then? Is the law sin? God forbid. Nay, I had not known sin, but by the law: for I had not known lust, except the law had said, Thou shalt not covet.

verses.original: ἀφορμὴν δὲ λαβοῦσα ἡ ἁμαρτία διὰ τῆς ἐντολῆς κατειργάσατο ἐν ἐμοὶ πᾶσαν ἐπιθυμίαν, χωρὶς γὰρ νόμου ἁμαρτία νεκρά.
verses.translit: aformen de lavousa e amartia dia tes entoles kateirgasato en emoi pasan epithymian, horis gar nomoy amartia nekra.
verses.translation: But sin, taking occasion by the commandment, wrought in me all manner of concupiscence. For without the law sin was dead.

verses.original: ἐγὼ δὲ ἔζων χωρὶς νόμου ποτέ· ἐλθούσης δὲ τῆς ἐντολῆς ἡ ἁμαρτία ἀνέζησεν,
verses.translit: ego de ezon horis nomoy pote* elthoysis de tes entoles e amartia anezisen,
verses.translation: For I was alive without the law once: but when the commandment came, sin revived, and I died.

verses.original: ἐγὼ δὲ ἀπέθανον, καὶ εὑρέθη μοι ἡ ἐντολὴ ἡ εἰς ζωὴν αὕτη εἰς θάνατον·
verses.translit: ego de apethanon, kai eurethi moi e entole e eis zoen auti eis thanaton*
verses.translation: And the commandment, which was ordained to life, I found to be unto death.

verses.original: ἡ γὰρ ἁμαρτία ἀφορμὴν λαβοῦσα διὰ τῆς ἐντολῆς ἐξηπάτησέν με καὶ διʼ αὐτῆς ἀπέκτεινεν.
verses.translit: e gar amartia aformen lavousa dia tes entoles exipatisen me kai di' autes apekteinen.
verses.translation: For sin, taking occasion by the commandment, deceived me, and by it slew me .

verses.original: ὥστε ὁ μὲν νόμος ἅγιος, καὶ ἡ ἐντολὴ ἁγία καὶ δικαία καὶ ἀγαθή.
verses.translit: oste o men nomos agios, kai e entole agia kai dikaia kai agathi.
verses.translation: Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.

verses.original: Τὸ οὖν ἀγαθὸν ἐμοὶ ⸀ἐγένετο θάνατος; μὴ γένοιτο· ἀλλὰ ἡ ἁμαρτία, ἵνα φανῇ ἁμαρτία διὰ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ μοι κατεργαζομένη θάνατον· ἵνα γένηται καθʼ ὑπερβολὴν ἁμαρτωλὸς ἡ ἁμαρτία διὰ τῆς ἐντολῆς.
verses.translit: To oun agathon emoi egeneto thanatos; me genoito* alla e amartia, ina fane amartia dia tou agathou moi katergazomeni thanaton* ina genitai kath' upervolen amartolos e amartia dia tes entoles.
verses.translation: Was then that which is good made death unto me? God forbid. But sin, that it might appear sin, working death in me by that which is good; that sin by the commandment might become exceeding sinful.

verses.original: Οἴδαμεν γὰρ ὅτι ὁ νόμος πνευματικός ἐστιν· ἐγὼ δὲ ⸀σάρκινός εἰμι, πεπραμένος ὑπὸ τὴν ἁμαρτίαν.
verses.translit: Oidamen gar oti o nomos pneymatikos estin* ego de sarkinos eimi, pepramenos upo ten amartian.
verses.translation: For we know that the law is spiritual: but I am carnal, sold under sin.

verses.original: ὃ γὰρ κατεργάζομαι οὐ γινώσκω· οὐ γὰρ ὃ θέλω τοῦτο πράσσω, ἀλλʼ ὃ μισῶ τοῦτο ποιῶ.
verses.translit: o gar katergazomai ou ginosko* ou gar o thelo touto prasso, all' o miso touto poio.
verses.translation: For that which I do I allow not: for what I would, that do I not; but what I hate, that do I.

verses.original: εἰ δὲ ὃ οὐ θέλω τοῦτο ποιῶ, σύμφημι τῷ νόμῳ ὅτι καλός.
verses.translit: ei de o ou thelo touto poio, symfimi to nomo oti kalos.
verses.translation: If then I do that which I would not, I consent unto the law that it is good.

verses.original: νυνὶ δὲ οὐκέτι ἐγὼ κατεργάζομαι αὐτὸ ἀλλὰ ἡ ⸀οἰκοῦσα ἐν ἐμοὶ ἁμαρτία.
verses.translit: nyni de ouketi ego katergazomai auto alla e oikousa en emoi amartia.
verses.translation: Now then it is no more I that do it, but sin that dwelleth in me.

verses.original: οἶδα γὰρ ὅτι οὐκ οἰκεῖ ἐν ἐμοί, τοῦτʼ ἔστιν ἐν τῇ σαρκί μου, ἀγαθόν· τὸ γὰρ θέλειν παράκειταί μοι, τὸ δὲ κατεργάζεσθαι τὸ καλὸν ⸀οὔ·
verses.translit: oida gar oti ouk oikei en emoi, tout' estin en te sarki moy, agathon* to gar thelein parakeitai moi, to de katergazesthai to kalon ou*
verses.translation: For I know that in me (that is, in my flesh,) dwelleth no good thing: for to will is present with me; but how to perform that which is good I find not.

verses.original: οὐ γὰρ ὃ θέλω ποιῶ ἀγαθόν, ἀλλὰ ὃ οὐ θέλω κακὸν τοῦτο πράσσω.
verses.translit: ou gar o thelo poio agathon, alla o ou thelo kakon touto prasso.
verses.translation: For the good that I would I do not: but the evil which I would not, that I do.

verses.original: εἰ δὲ ὃ οὐ ⸀θέλω τοῦτο ποιῶ, οὐκέτι ἐγὼ κατεργάζομαι αὐτὸ ἀλλὰ ἡ οἰκοῦσα ἐν ἐμοὶ ἁμαρτία.
verses.translit: ei de o ou thelo touto poio, ouketi ego katergazomai auto alla e oikousa en emoi amartia.
verses.translation: Now if I do that I would not, it is no more I that do it, but sin that dwelleth in me.

verses.original: Εὑρίσκω ἄρα τὸν νόμον τῷ θέλοντι ἐμοὶ ποιεῖν τὸ καλὸν ὅτι ἐμοὶ τὸ κακὸν παράκειται·
verses.translit: Eurisko ara ton nomon to thelonti emoi poiein to kalon oti emoi to kakon parakeitai*
verses.translation: I find then a law, that, when I would do good, evil is present with me.

verses.original: συνήδομαι γὰρ τῷ νόμῳ τοῦ θεοῦ κατὰ τὸν ἔσω ἄνθρωπον,
verses.translit: synidomai gar to nomo tou theou kata ton eso anthropon,
verses.translation: For I delight in the law of God after the inward man:

verses.original: βλέπω δὲ ἕτερον νόμον ἐν τοῖς μέλεσίν μου ἀντιστρατευόμενον τῷ νόμῳ τοῦ νοός μου καὶ αἰχμαλωτίζοντά με ⸀ἐν τῷ νόμῳ τῆς ἁμαρτίας τῷ ὄντι ἐν τοῖς μέλεσίν μου.
verses.translit: vlepo de eteron nomon en tois melesin moy antistrateyomenon to nomo tou noos moy kai aihmalotizonta me en to nomo tes amartias to onti en tois melesin moy.
verses.translation: But I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity to the law of sin which is in my members.

verses.original: ταλαίπωρος ἐγὼ ἄνθρωπος· τίς με ῥύσεται ἐκ τοῦ σώματος τοῦ θανάτου τούτου;
verses.translit: talaiporos ego anthropos* tis me Rysetai ek tou somatos tou thanatoy toytoy;
verses.translation: O wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me from the body of this death?

verses.original: ⸀χάρις τῷ θεῷ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν. Ἄρα οὖν αὐτὸς ἐγὼ τῷ μὲν νοῒ δουλεύω νόμῳ θεοῦ, τῇ δὲ σαρκὶ νόμῳ ἁμαρτίας.
verses.translit: haris to theo dia Iisou Hristou tou kyrioy emon. Ara oun autos ego to men noi doyleyo nomo theou, te de sarki nomo amartias.
verses.translation: I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord. So then with the mind I myself serve the law of God; but with the flesh the law of sin.

verses.original: Οὐδὲν ἄρα νῦν κατάκριμα τοῖς ἐν Χριστῷ ⸀Ἰησοῦ·
verses.translit: Ouden ara nun katakrima tois en Hristo Iisou*
verses.translation: There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.

verses.original: ὁ γὰρ νόμος τοῦ πνεύματος τῆς ζωῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ ἠλευθέρωσέν ⸀σε ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου τῆς ἁμαρτίας καὶ τοῦ θανάτου.
verses.translit: o gar nomos tou pneymatos tes zoes en Hristo Iisou eleytherosen se apo tou nomoy tes amartias kai tou thanatoy.
verses.translation: For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus hath made me free from the law of sin and death.

verses.original: τὸ γὰρ ἀδύνατον τοῦ νόμου, ἐν ᾧ ἠσθένει διὰ τῆς σαρκός, ὁ θεὸς τὸν ἑαυτοῦ υἱὸν πέμψας ἐν ὁμοιώματι σαρκὸς ἁμαρτίας καὶ περὶ ἁμαρτίας κατέκρινε τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ἐν τῇ σαρκί,
verses.translit: to gar adynaton tou nomoy, en o esthenei dia tes sarkos, o theos ton eaytou yion pempsas en omoiomati sarkos amartias kai peri amartias katekrine ten amartian en te sarki,
verses.translation: For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh:

verses.original: ἵνα τὸ δικαίωμα τοῦ νόμου πληρωθῇ ἐν ἡμῖν τοῖς μὴ κατὰ σάρκα περιπατοῦσιν ἀλλὰ κατὰ πνεῦμα·
verses.translit: ina to dikaioma tou nomoy plirothe en emin tois me kata sarka peripatousin alla kata pneuma*
verses.translation: That the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.

verses.original: οἱ γὰρ κατὰ σάρκα ὄντες τὰ τῆς σαρκὸς φρονοῦσιν, οἱ δὲ κατὰ πνεῦμα τὰ τοῦ πνεύματος.
verses.translit: oi gar kata sarka ontes ta tes sarkos fronousin, oi de kata pneuma ta tou pneymatos.
verses.translation: For they that are after the flesh do mind the things of the flesh; but they that are after the Spirit the things of the Spirit.

verses.original: τὸ γὰρ φρόνημα τῆς σαρκὸς θάνατος, τὸ δὲ φρόνημα τοῦ πνεύματος ζωὴ καὶ εἰρήνη·
verses.translit: to gar fronima tes sarkos thanatos, to de fronima tou pneymatos zoe kai eirini*
verses.translation: For to be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace.

verses.original: διότι τὸ φρόνημα τῆς σαρκὸς ἔχθρα εἰς θεόν, τῷ γὰρ νόμῳ τοῦ θεοῦ οὐχ ὑποτάσσεται, οὐδὲ γὰρ δύναται·
verses.translit: dioti to fronima tes sarkos ehthra eis theon, to gar nomo tou theou ouh upotassetai, oude gar dynatai*
verses.translation: Because the carnal mind is enmity against God: for it is not subject to the law of God, neither indeed can be.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἐν σαρκὶ ὄντες θεῷ ἀρέσαι οὐ δύνανται.
verses.translit: oi de en sarki ontes theo aresai ou dynantai.
verses.translation: So then they that are in the flesh cannot please God.

verses.original: Ὑμεῖς δὲ οὐκ ἐστὲ ἐν σαρκὶ ἀλλὰ ἐν πνεύματι, εἴπερ πνεῦμα θεοῦ οἰκεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν. εἰ δέ τις πνεῦμα Χριστοῦ οὐκ ἔχει, οὗτος οὐκ ἔστιν αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: Umeis de ouk este en sarki alla en pneymati, eiper pneuma theou oikei en umin. ei de tis pneuma Hristou ouk ehei, outos ouk estin autou.
verses.translation: But ye are not in the flesh, but in the Spirit, if so be that the Spirit of God dwell in you. Now if any man have not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his.

verses.original: εἰ δὲ Χριστὸς ἐν ὑμῖν, τὸ μὲν σῶμα νεκρὸν διὰ ἁμαρτίαν, τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα ζωὴ διὰ δικαιοσύνην.
verses.translit: ei de Hristos en umin, to men soma nekron dia amartian, to de pneuma zoe dia dikaiosynin.
verses.translation: And if Christ be in you, the body is dead because of sin; but the Spirit is life because of righteousness.

verses.original: εἰ δὲ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ ἐγείραντος ⸀τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐκ νεκρῶν οἰκεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν, ὁ ἐγείρας ⸂ἐκ νεκρῶν Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν⸃ ζῳοποιήσει καὶ τὰ θνητὰ σώματα ὑμῶν διὰ ⸂τὸ ἐνοικοῦν αὐτοῦ πνεῦμα⸃ ἐν ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: ei de to pneuma tou egeirantos ton Iisoun ek nekron oikei en umin, o egeiras ek nekron Hriston Iisoun zoopoiisei kai ta thnita somata umon dia to enoikoun autou pneuma en umin.
verses.translation: But if the Spirit of him that raised up Jesus from the dead dwell in you, he that raised up Christ from the dead shall also quicken your mortal bodies by his Spirit that dwelleth in you.

verses.original: Ἄρα οὖν, ἀδελφοί, ὀφειλέται ἐσμέν, οὐ τῇ σαρκὶ τοῦ κατὰ σάρκα ζῆν,
verses.translit: Ara oun, adelfoi, ofeiletai esmen, ou te sarki tou kata sarka zen,
verses.translation: Therefore, brethren, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live after the flesh.

verses.original: εἰ γὰρ κατὰ σάρκα ζῆτε μέλλετε ἀποθνῄσκειν, εἰ δὲ πνεύματι τὰς πράξεις τοῦ σώματος θανατοῦτε, ζήσεσθε.
verses.translit: ei gar kata sarka zete mellete apothneskein, ei de pneymati tas praxeis tou somatos thanatoute, zisesthe.
verses.translation: For if ye live after the flesh, ye shall die: but if ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the body, ye shall live.

verses.original: ὅσοι γὰρ πνεύματι θεοῦ ἄγονται, οὗτοι ⸂υἱοί εἰσιν θεοῦ⸃.
verses.translit: osoi gar pneymati theou agontai, outoi yioi eisin theou.
verses.translation: For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God.

verses.original: οὐ γὰρ ἐλάβετε πνεῦμα δουλείας πάλιν εἰς φόβον, ἀλλὰ ἐλάβετε πνεῦμα υἱοθεσίας ἐν ᾧ κράζομεν· Αββα ὁ πατήρ·
verses.translit: ou gar elavete pneuma doyleias palin eis fovon, alla elavete pneuma yiothesias en o krazomen* Avva o patir*
verses.translation: For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father.

verses.original: αὐτὸ τὸ πνεῦμα συμμαρτυρεῖ τῷ πνεύματι ἡμῶν ὅτι ἐσμὲν τέκνα θεοῦ.
verses.translit: auto to pneuma symmartyrei to pneymati emon oti esmen tekna theou.
verses.translation: The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God:

verses.original: εἰ δὲ τέκνα, καὶ κληρονόμοι· κληρονόμοι μὲν θεοῦ, συγκληρονόμοι δὲ Χριστοῦ, εἴπερ συμπάσχομεν ἵνα καὶ συνδοξασθῶμεν.
verses.translit: ei de tekna, kai klironomoi* klironomoi men theou, sygklironomoi de Hristou, eiper sympashomen ina kai syndoxasthomen.
verses.translation: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him , that we may be also glorified together.

verses.original: Λογίζομαι γὰρ ὅτι οὐκ ἄξια τὰ παθήματα τοῦ νῦν καιροῦ πρὸς τὴν μέλλουσαν δόξαν ἀποκαλυφθῆναι εἰς ἡμᾶς.
verses.translit: Logizomai gar oti ouk axia ta pathimata tou nun kairou pros ten melloysan doxan apokalyfthenai eis emas.
verses.translation: For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us.

verses.original: ἡ γὰρ ἀποκαραδοκία τῆς κτίσεως τὴν ἀποκάλυψιν τῶν υἱῶν τοῦ θεοῦ ἀπεκδέχεται·
verses.translit: e gar apokaradokia tes ktiseos ten apokalypsin ton yion tou theou apekdehetai*
verses.translation: For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.

verses.original: τῇ γὰρ ματαιότητι ἡ κτίσις ὑπετάγη, οὐχ ἑκοῦσα ἀλλὰ διὰ τὸν ὑποτάξαντα, ⸀ἐφʼ ἑλπίδι
verses.translit: te gar mataiotiti e ktisis upetagi, ouh ekousa alla dia ton upotaxanta, ef' elpidi
verses.translation: For the creature was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who hath subjected the same in hope,

verses.original: ὅτι καὶ αὐτὴ ἡ κτίσις ἐλευθερωθήσεται ἀπὸ τῆς δουλείας τῆς φθορᾶς εἰς τὴν ἐλευθερίαν τῆς δόξης τῶν τέκνων τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: oti kai aute e ktisis eleytherothisetai apo tes doyleias tes fthoras eis ten eleytherian tes doxis ton teknon tou theou.
verses.translation: Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God.

verses.original: οἴδαμεν γὰρ ὅτι πᾶσα ἡ κτίσις συστενάζει καὶ συνωδίνει ἄχρι τοῦ νῦν·
verses.translit: oidamen gar oti pasa e ktisis systenazei kai synodinei ahri tou nun*
verses.translation: For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now.

verses.original: οὐ μόνον δέ, ἀλλὰ ⸂καὶ αὐτοὶ⸃ τὴν ἀπαρχὴν τοῦ πνεύματος ἔχοντες ⸂ἡμεῖς καὶ⸃ αὐτοὶ ἐν ἑαυτοῖς στενάζομεν, υἱοθεσίαν ἀπεκδεχόμενοι τὴν ἀπολύτρωσιν τοῦ σώματος ἡμῶν.
verses.translit: ou monon de, alla kai autoi ten aparhen tou pneymatos ehontes emeis kai autoi en eaytois stenazomen, yiothesian apekdehomenoi ten apolytrosin tou somatos emon.
verses.translation: And not only they , but ourselves also, which have the firstfruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit , the redemption of our body.

verses.original: τῇ γὰρ ἐλπίδι ἐσώθημεν· ἐλπὶς δὲ βλεπομένη οὐκ ἔστιν ἐλπίς, ὃ γὰρ βλέπει ⸀τίς ἐλπίζει;
verses.translit: te gar elpidi esothimen* elpis de vlepomeni ouk estin elpis, o gar vlepei tis elpizei;
verses.translation: For we are saved by hope: but hope that is seen is not hope: for what a man seeth, why doth he yet hope for?

verses.original: εἰ δὲ ὃ οὐ βλέπομεν ἐλπίζομεν, διʼ ὑπομονῆς ἀπεκδεχόμεθα.
verses.translit: ei de o ou vlepomen elpizomen, di' upomones apekdehometha.
verses.translation: But if we hope for that we see not, then do we with patience wait for it .

verses.original: Ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα συναντιλαμβάνεται ⸂τῇ ἀσθενείᾳ⸃ ἡμῶν· τὸ γὰρ τί ⸀προσευξώμεθα καθὸ δεῖ οὐκ οἴδαμεν, ἀλλὰ αὐτὸ τὸ πνεῦμα ⸀ὑπερεντυγχάνει στεναγμοῖς ἀλαλήτοις,
verses.translit: Osaytos de kai to pneuma synantilamvanetai te astheneia emon* to gar ti proseyxometha katho dei ouk oidamen, alla auto to pneuma uperentyghanei stenagmois alalitois,
verses.translation: Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἐραυνῶν τὰς καρδίας οἶδεν τί τὸ φρόνημα τοῦ πνεύματος, ὅτι κατὰ θεὸν ἐντυγχάνει ὑπὲρ ἁγίων.
verses.translit: o de eraynon tas kardias oiden ti to fronima tou pneymatos, oti kata theon entyghanei uper agion.
verses.translation: And he that searcheth the hearts knoweth what is the mind of the Spirit, because he maketh intercession for the saints according to the will of God.

verses.original: Οἴδαμεν δὲ ὅτι τοῖς ἀγαπῶσι τὸν θεὸν πάντα ⸀συνεργεῖ εἰς ἀγαθόν, τοῖς κατὰ πρόθεσιν κλητοῖς οὖσιν.
verses.translit: Oidamen de oti tois agaposi ton theon panta synergei eis agathon, tois kata prothesin klitois ousin.
verses.translation: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.

verses.original: ὅτι οὓς προέγνω, καὶ προώρισεν συμμόρφους τῆς εἰκόνος τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, εἰς τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν πρωτότοκον ἐν πολλοῖς ἀδελφοῖς·
verses.translit: oti ous proegno, kai proorisen symmorfoys tes eikonos tou yiou autou, eis to einai auton prototokon en pollois adelfois*
verses.translation: For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.

verses.original: οὓς δὲ προώρισεν, τούτους καὶ ἐκάλεσεν· καὶ οὓς ἐκάλεσεν, τούτους καὶ ἐδικαίωσεν· οὓς δὲ ἐδικαίωσεν, τούτους καὶ ἐδόξασεν.
verses.translit: ous de proorisen, toytoys kai ekalesen* kai ous ekalesen, toytoys kai edikaiosen* ous de edikaiosen, toytoys kai edoxasen.
verses.translation: Moreover whom he did predestinate, them he also called: and whom he called, them he also justified: and whom he justified, them he also glorified.

verses.original: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν πρὸς ταῦτα; εἰ ὁ θεὸς ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν, τίς καθʼ ἡμῶν;
verses.translit: Ti oun eroumen pros tauta; ei o theos uper emon, tis kath' emon;
verses.translation: What shall we then say to these things? If God be for us, who can be against us?

verses.original: ὅς γε τοῦ ἰδίου υἱοῦ οὐκ ἐφείσατο, ἀλλὰ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν πάντων παρέδωκεν αὐτόν, πῶς οὐχὶ καὶ σὺν αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα ἡμῖν χαρίσεται;
verses.translit: os ge tou idioy yiou ouk efeisato, alla uper emon panton paredoken auton, pos ouhi kai sun auto ta panta emin harisetai;
verses.translation: He that spared not his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how shall he not with him also freely give us all things?

verses.original: τίς ἐγκαλέσει κατὰ ἐκλεκτῶν θεοῦ; θεὸς ὁ δικαιῶν·
verses.translit: tis egkalesei kata eklekton theou; theos o dikaion*
verses.translation: Who shall lay any thing to the charge of God’s elect? It is God that justifieth.

verses.original: τίς ὁ ⸀κατακρινῶν; ⸀Χριστὸς ὁ ἀποθανών, μᾶλλον ⸀δὲ ⸀ἐγερθείς, ὅς ⸀καί ἐστιν ἐν δεξιᾷ τοῦ θεοῦ, ὃς καὶ ἐντυγχάνει ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν·
verses.translit: tis o katakrinon; Hristos o apothanon, mallon de egertheis, os kai estin en dexia tou theou, os kai entyghanei uper emon*
verses.translation: Who is he that condemneth? It is Christ that died, yea rather, that is risen again, who is even at the right hand of God, who also maketh intercession for us.

verses.original: τίς ἡμᾶς χωρίσει ἀπὸ τῆς ἀγάπης τοῦ Χριστοῦ; θλῖψις ἢ στενοχωρία ἢ διωγμὸς ἢ λιμὸς ἢ γυμνότης ἢ κίνδυνος ἢ μάχαιρα;
verses.translit: tis emas horisei apo tes agapis tou Hristou; thlipsis e stenohoria e diogmos e limos e gymnotis e kindynos e mahaira;
verses.translation: Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword?

verses.original: καθὼς γέγραπται ὅτι Ἕνεκεν σοῦ θανατούμεθα ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν, ἐλογίσθημεν ὡς πρόβατα σφαγῆς.
verses.translit: kathos gegraptai oti Eneken sou thanatoymetha olin ten emeran, elogisthimen os provata sfages.
verses.translation: As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter.

verses.original: ἀλλʼ ἐν τούτοις πᾶσιν ὑπερνικῶμεν διὰ τοῦ ἀγαπήσαντος ἡμᾶς.
verses.translit: all' en toytois pasin upernikomen dia tou agapisantos emas.
verses.translation: Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us.

verses.original: πέπεισμαι γὰρ ὅτι οὔτε θάνατος οὔτε ζωὴ οὔτε ἄγγελοι οὔτε ἀρχαὶ οὔτε ⸂ἐνεστῶτα οὔτε μέλλοντα οὔτε δυνάμεις⸃
verses.translit: pepeismai gar oti oute thanatos oute zoe oute aggeloi oute arhai oute enestota oute mellonta oute dynameis
verses.translation: For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come,

verses.original: οὔτε ὕψωμα οὔτε βάθος οὔτε τις κτίσις ἑτέρα δυνήσεται ἡμᾶς χωρίσαι ἀπὸ τῆς ἀγάπης τοῦ θεοῦ τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ κυρίῳ ἡμῶν.
verses.translit: oute upsoma oute vathos oute tis ktisis etera dynisetai emas horisai apo tes agapis tou theou tes en Hristo Iisou to kyrio emon.
verses.translation: Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

verses.original: Ἀλήθειαν λέγω ἐν Χριστῷ, οὐ ψεύδομαι, συμμαρτυρούσης μοι τῆς συνειδήσεώς μου ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ,
verses.translit: Alitheian lego en Hristo, ou pseydomai, symmartyroysis moi tes syneidiseos moy en pneymati agio,
verses.translation: I say the truth in Christ, I lie not, my conscience also bearing me witness in the Holy Ghost,

verses.original: ὅτι λύπη μοί ἐστιν μεγάλη καὶ ἀδιάλειπτος ὀδύνη τῇ καρδίᾳ μου·
verses.translit: oti lypi moi estin megali kai adialeiptos odyni te kardia moy*
verses.translation: That I have great heaviness and continual sorrow in my heart.

verses.original: ηὐχόμην γὰρ ⸂ἀνάθεμα εἶναι αὐτὸς ἐγὼ⸃ ἀπὸ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ὑπὲρ τῶν ἀδελφῶν μου τῶν συγγενῶν μου κατὰ σάρκα,
verses.translit: iuhomin gar anathema einai autos ego apo tou Hristou uper ton adelfon moy ton syggenon moy kata sarka,
verses.translation: For I could wish that myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh:

verses.original: οἵτινές εἰσιν Ἰσραηλῖται, ὧν ἡ υἱοθεσία καὶ ἡ δόξα καὶ αἱ διαθῆκαι καὶ ἡ νομοθεσία καὶ ἡ λατρεία καὶ αἱ ἐπαγγελίαι,
verses.translit: oitines eisin Israilitai, on e yiothesia kai e doxa kai ai diathekai kai e nomothesia kai e latreia kai ai epaggeliai,
verses.translation: Who are Israelites; to whom pertaineth the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God , and the promises;

verses.original: ὧν οἱ πατέρες, καὶ ἐξ ὧν ὁ χριστὸς τὸ κατὰ σάρκα, ὁ ὢν ἐπὶ πάντων, θεὸς εὐλογητὸς εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας· ἀμήν.
verses.translit: on oi pateres, kai ex on o hristos to kata sarka, o on epi panton, theos eulogitos eis tous aionas* amin.
verses.translation: Whose are the fathers, and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came , who is over all, God blessed for ever. Amen.

verses.original: Οὐχ οἷον δὲ ὅτι ἐκπέπτωκεν ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ. οὐ γὰρ πάντες οἱ ἐξ Ἰσραήλ, οὗτοι Ἰσραήλ·
verses.translit: Ouh oion de oti ekpeptoken o logos tou theou. ou gar pantes oi ex Israil, outoi Israil*
verses.translation: Not as though the word of God hath taken none effect. For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel:

verses.original: οὐδʼ ὅτι εἰσὶν σπέρμα Ἀβραάμ, πάντες τέκνα, ἀλλʼ· Ἐν Ἰσαὰκ κληθήσεταί σοι σπέρμα.
verses.translit: oud' oti eisin sperma Avraam, pantes tekna, all'* En Isaak klithisetai soi sperma.
verses.translation: Neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children: but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called.

verses.original: τοῦτʼ ἔστιν, οὐ τὰ τέκνα τῆς σαρκὸς ταῦτα τέκνα τοῦ θεοῦ, ἀλλὰ τὰ τέκνα τῆς ἐπαγγελίας λογίζεται εἰς σπέρμα·
verses.translit: tout' estin, ou ta tekna tes sarkos tauta tekna tou theou, alla ta tekna tes epaggelias logizetai eis sperma*
verses.translation: That is, They which are the children of the flesh, these are not the children of God: but the children of the promise are counted for the seed.

verses.original: ἐπαγγελίας γὰρ ὁ λόγος οὗτος· Κατὰ τὸν καιρὸν τοῦτον ἐλεύσομαι καὶ ἔσται τῇ Σάρρᾳ υἱός.
verses.translit: epaggelias gar o logos outos* Kata ton kairon touton eleysomai kai estai te Sarra yios.
verses.translation: For this is the word of promise, At this time will I come, and Sara shall have a son.

verses.original: οὐ μόνον δέ, ἀλλὰ καὶ Ῥεβέκκα ἐξ ἑνὸς κοίτην ἔχουσα, Ἰσαὰκ τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν·
verses.translit: ou monon de, alla kai Revekka ex enos koitin ehoysa, Isaak tou patros emon*
verses.translation: And not only this ; but when Rebecca also had conceived by one, even by our father Isaac;

verses.original: μήπω γὰρ γεννηθέντων μηδὲ πραξάντων τι ἀγαθὸν ἢ ⸀φαῦλον, ἵνα ἡ κατʼ ἐκλογὴν πρόθεσις τοῦ θεοῦ μένῃ,
verses.translit: mipo gar gennithenton mide praxanton ti agathon e faulon, ina e kat' eklogen prothesis tou theou mene,
verses.translation: (For the children being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil, that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calleth;)

verses.original: οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων ἀλλʼ ἐκ τοῦ καλοῦντος, ἐρρέθη αὐτῇ ὅτι Ὁ μείζων δουλεύσει τῷ ἐλάσσονι·
verses.translit: ouk ex ergon all' ek tou kalountos, errethi aute oti O meizon doyleysei to elassoni*
verses.translation: It was said unto her, The elder shall serve the younger.

verses.original: ⸀καθὼς γέγραπται· Τὸν Ἰακὼβ ἠγάπησα, τὸν δὲ Ἠσαῦ ἐμίσησα.
verses.translit: kathos gegraptai* Ton Iakov egapisa, ton de Esau emisisa.
verses.translation: As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.

verses.original: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν; μὴ ἀδικία παρὰ τῷ θεῷ; μὴ γένοιτο·
verses.translit: Ti oun eroumen; me adikia para to theo; me genoito*
verses.translation: What shall we say then? Is there unrighteousness with God? God forbid.

verses.original: τῷ ⸂Μωϋσεῖ γὰρ⸃ λέγει· Ἐλεήσω ὃν ἂν ἐλεῶ, καὶ οἰκτιρήσω ὃν ἂν οἰκτίρω.
verses.translit: to Moysei gar legei* Eleiso on an eleo, kai oiktiriso on an oiktiro.
verses.translation: For he saith to Moses, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion.

verses.original: ἄρα οὖν οὐ τοῦ θέλοντος οὐδὲ τοῦ τρέχοντος ἀλλὰ τοῦ ἐλεῶντος θεοῦ.
verses.translit: ara oun ou tou thelontos oude tou trehontos alla tou eleontos theou.
verses.translation: So then it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy.

verses.original: λέγει γὰρ ἡ γραφὴ τῷ Φαραὼ ὅτι Εἰς αὐτὸ τοῦτο ἐξήγειρά σε ὅπως ἐνδείξωμαι ἐν σοὶ τὴν δύναμίν μου, καὶ ὅπως διαγγελῇ τὸ ὄνομά μου ἐν πάσῃ τῇ γῇ.
verses.translit: legei gar e grafe to Farao oti Eis auto touto exigeira se opos endeixomai en soi ten dynamin moy, kai opos diaggele to onoma moy en pase te ge.
verses.translation: For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might shew my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth.

verses.original: ἄρα οὖν ὃν θέλει ἐλεεῖ, ὃν δὲ θέλει σκληρύνει.
verses.translit: ara oun on thelei eleei, on de thelei sklirynei.
verses.translation: Therefore hath he mercy on whom he will have mercy , and whom he will he hardeneth.

verses.original: Ἐρεῖς ⸂μοι οὖν⸃· Τί ⸀οὖν ἔτι μέμφεται; τῷ γὰρ βουλήματι αὐτοῦ τίς ἀνθέστηκεν;
verses.translit: Ereis moi oun* Ti oun eti memfetai; to gar voylimati autou tis anthestiken;
verses.translation: Thou wilt say then unto me, Why doth he yet find fault? For who hath resisted his will?

verses.original: ⸂ὦ ἄνθρωπε, μενοῦνγε⸃ σὺ τίς εἶ ὁ ἀνταποκρινόμενος τῷ θεῷ; μὴ ἐρεῖ τὸ πλάσμα τῷ πλάσαντι Τί με ἐποίησας οὕτως;
verses.translit: o anthrope, menounge su tis ei o antapokrinomenos to theo; me erei to plasma to plasanti Ti me epoiisas outos;
verses.translation: Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it , Why hast thou made me thus?

verses.original: ἢ οὐκ ἔχει ἐξουσίαν ὁ κεραμεὺς τοῦ πηλοῦ ἐκ τοῦ αὐτοῦ φυράματος ποιῆσαι ὃ μὲν εἰς τιμὴν σκεῦος ὃ δὲ εἰς ἀτιμίαν;
verses.translit: e ouk ehei exoysian o kerameus tou pilou ek tou autou fyramatos poiesai o men eis timen skeuos o de eis atimian;
verses.translation: Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?

verses.original: εἰ δὲ θέλων ὁ θεὸς ἐνδείξασθαι τὴν ὀργὴν καὶ γνωρίσαι τὸ δυνατὸν αὐτοῦ ἤνεγκεν ἐν πολλῇ μακροθυμίᾳ σκεύη ὀργῆς κατηρτισμένα εἰς ἀπώλειαν,
verses.translit: ei de thelon o theos endeixasthai ten orgen kai gnorisai to dynaton autou enegken en polle makrothymia skeyi orges katirtismena eis apoleian,
verses.translation: What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction:

verses.original: ⸀καὶ ἵνα γνωρίσῃ τὸν πλοῦτον τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ σκεύη ἐλέους, ἃ προητοίμασεν εἰς δόξαν,
verses.translit: kai ina gnorise ton plouton tes doxis autou epi skeyi eleoys, a proitoimasen eis doxan,
verses.translation: And that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory,

verses.original: οὓς καὶ ἐκάλεσεν ἡμᾶς οὐ μόνον ἐξ Ἰουδαίων ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐξ ἐθνῶν;—
verses.translit: ous kai ekalesen emas ou monon ex Ioydaion alla kai ex ethnon;--
verses.translation: Even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles?

verses.original: ὡς καὶ ἐν τῷ Ὡσηὲ λέγει· Καλέσω τὸν οὐ λαόν μου λαόν μου καὶ τὴν οὐκ ἠγαπημένην ἠγαπημένην·
verses.translit: os kai en to Osie legei* Kaleso ton ou laon moy laon moy kai ten ouk egapimenin egapimenin*
verses.translation: As he saith also in Osee, I will call them my people, which were not my people; and her beloved, which was not beloved.

verses.original: καὶ ἔσται ἐν τῷ τόπῳ οὗ ἐρρέθη ⸀αὐτοῖς· Οὐ λαός μου ὑμεῖς, ἐκεῖ κληθήσονται υἱοὶ θεοῦ ζῶντος.
verses.translit: kai estai en to topo ou errethi autois* Ou laos moy umeis, ekei klithisontai yioi theou zontos.
verses.translation: And it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people; there shall they be called the children of the living God.

verses.original: Ἠσαΐας δὲ κράζει ὑπὲρ τοῦ Ἰσραήλ· Ἐὰν ᾖ ὁ ἀριθμὸς τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ ὡς ἡ ἄμμος τῆς θαλάσσης, τὸ ⸀ὑπόλειμμα σωθήσεται·
verses.translit: EsaIas de krazei uper tou Israil* Ean e o arithmos ton yion Israel os e ammos tes thalassis, to upoleimma sothisetai*
verses.translation: Esaias also crieth concerning Israel, Though the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant shall be saved:

verses.original: λόγον γὰρ συντελῶν καὶ ⸀συντέμνων ποιήσει κύριος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
verses.translit: logon gar syntelon kai syntemnon poiisei kyrios epi tes ges.
verses.translation: For he will finish the work, and cut it short in righteousness: because a short work will the Lord make upon the earth.

verses.original: καὶ καθὼς προείρηκεν Ἠσαΐας· Εἰ μὴ κύριος Σαβαὼθ ἐγκατέλιπεν ἡμῖν σπέρμα, ὡς Σόδομα ἂν ἐγενήθημεν καὶ ὡς Γόμορρα ἂν ὡμοιώθημεν.
verses.translit: kai kathos proeiriken EsaIas* Ei me kyrios Savaoth egkatelipen emin sperma, os Sodoma an egenithimen kai os Gomorra an omoiothimen.
verses.translation: And as Esaias said before, Except the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed, we had been as Sodoma, and been made like unto Gomorrha.

verses.original: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν; ὅτι ἔθνη τὰ μὴ διώκοντα δικαιοσύνην κατέλαβεν δικαιοσύνην, δικαιοσύνην δὲ τὴν ἐκ πίστεως·
verses.translit: Ti oun eroumen; oti ethni ta me diokonta dikaiosynin katelaven dikaiosynin, dikaiosynin de ten ek pisteos*
verses.translation: What shall we say then? That the Gentiles, which followed not after righteousness, have attained to righteousness, even the righteousness which is of faith.

verses.original: Ἰσραὴλ δὲ διώκων νόμον δικαιοσύνης εἰς ⸀νόμον οὐκ ἔφθασεν.
verses.translit: Israel de diokon nomon dikaiosynis eis nomon ouk efthasen.
verses.translation: But Israel, which followed after the law of righteousness, hath not attained to the law of righteousness.

verses.original: διὰ τί; ὅτι οὐκ ἐκ πίστεως ἀλλʼ ὡς ἐξ ⸀ἔργων· ⸀προσέκοψαν τῷ λίθῳ τοῦ προσκόμματος,
verses.translit: dia ti; oti ouk ek pisteos all' os ex ergon* prosekopsan to litho tou proskommatos,
verses.translation: Wherefore? Because they sought it not by faith, but as it were by the works of the law. For they stumbled at that stumblingstone;

verses.original: καθὼς γέγραπται· Ἰδοὺ τίθημι ἐν Σιὼν λίθον προσκόμματος καὶ πέτραν σκανδάλου, ⸀καὶ ὁ πιστεύων ἐπʼ αὐτῷ οὐ καταισχυνθήσεται.
verses.translit: kathos gegraptai* Idou tithimi en Sion lithon proskommatos kai petran skandaloy, kai o pisteyon ep' auto ou kataishynthisetai.
verses.translation: As it is written, Behold, I lay in Sion a stumblingstone and rock of offence: and whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed.

verses.original: Ἀδελφοί, ἡ μὲν εὐδοκία τῆς ἐμῆς καρδίας καὶ ἡ ⸀δέησις πρὸς τὸν θεὸν ὑπὲρ ⸀αὐτῶν εἰς σωτηρίαν.
verses.translit: Adelfoi, e men eudokia tes emes kardias kai e deisis pros ton theon uper auton eis sotirian.
verses.translation: Brethren, my heart’s desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved.

verses.original: μαρτυρῶ γὰρ αὐτοῖς ὅτι ζῆλον θεοῦ ἔχουσιν· ἀλλʼ οὐ κατʼ ἐπίγνωσιν,
verses.translit: martyro gar autois oti zelon theou ehoysin* all' ou kat' epignosin,
verses.translation: For I bear them record that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge.

verses.original: ἀγνοοῦντες γὰρ τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ δικαιοσύνην, καὶ τὴν ⸀ἰδίαν ζητοῦντες στῆσαι, τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ τοῦ θεοῦ οὐχ ὑπετάγησαν·
verses.translit: agnoountes gar ten tou theou dikaiosynin, kai ten idian zitountes stesai, te dikaiosyne tou theou ouh upetagisan*
verses.translation: For they being ignorant of God’s righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God.

verses.original: τέλος γὰρ νόμου Χριστὸς εἰς δικαιοσύνην παντὶ τῷ πιστεύοντι.
verses.translit: telos gar nomoy Hristos eis dikaiosynin panti to pisteyonti.
verses.translation: For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth.

verses.original: Μωϋσῆς γὰρ γράφει ⸂ὅτι τὴν δικαιοσύνην τὴν ἐκ ⸀τοῦ νόμου⸃ ὁ ⸀ποιήσας ἄνθρωπος ζήσεται ἐν ⸀αὐτῇ.
verses.translit: Moyses gar grafei oti ten dikaiosynin ten ek tou nomoy o poiisas anthropos zisetai en aute.
verses.translation: For Moses describeth the righteousness which is of the law, That the man which doeth those things shall live by them.

verses.original: ἡ δὲ ἐκ πίστεως δικαιοσύνη οὕτως λέγει· Μὴ εἴπῃς ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ σου· Τίς ἀναβήσεται εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν; τοῦτʼ ἔστιν Χριστὸν καταγαγεῖν·
verses.translit: e de ek pisteos dikaiosyni outos legei* Me eipes en te kardia soy* Tis anavisetai eis ton ouranon; tout' estin Hriston katagagein*
verses.translation: But the righteousness which is of faith speaketh on this wise, Say not in thine heart, Who shall ascend into heaven? (that is, to bring Christ down from above :)

verses.original: ἤ· Τίς καταβήσεται εἰς τὴν ἄβυσσον; τοῦτʼ ἔστιν Χριστὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναγαγεῖν.
verses.translit: e* Tis katavisetai eis ten avysson; tout' estin Hriston ek nekron anagagein.
verses.translation: Or, Who shall descend into the deep? (that is, to bring up Christ again from the dead.)

verses.original: ἀλλὰ τί λέγει; Ἐγγύς σου τὸ ῥῆμά ἐστιν, ἐν τῷ στόματί σου καὶ ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ σου, τοῦτʼ ἔστιν τὸ ῥῆμα τῆς πίστεως ὃ κηρύσσομεν.
verses.translit: alla ti legei; Eggys soy to Rema estin, en to stomati soy kai en te kardia soy, tout' estin to Rema tes pisteos o kiryssomen.
verses.translation: But what saith it? The word is nigh thee, even in thy mouth, and in thy heart: that is, the word of faith, which we preach;

verses.original: ὅτι ἐὰν ⸀ὁμολογήσῃς ἐν τῷ στόματί ⸀σου κύριον Ἰησοῦν, καὶ πιστεύσῃς ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ σου ὅτι ὁ θεὸς αὐτὸν ἤγειρεν ἐκ νεκρῶν, σωθήσῃ·
verses.translit: oti ean omologises en to stomati soy kyrion Iisoun, kai pisteyses en te kardia soy oti o theos auton egeiren ek nekron, sothise*
verses.translation: That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved.

verses.original: καρδίᾳ γὰρ πιστεύεται εἰς δικαιοσύνην, στόματι δὲ ὁμολογεῖται εἰς σωτηρίαν·
verses.translit: kardia gar pisteyetai eis dikaiosynin, stomati de omologeitai eis sotirian*
verses.translation: For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.

verses.original: λέγει γὰρ ἡ γραφή· Πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων ἐπʼ αὐτῷ οὐ καταισχυνθήσεται.
verses.translit: legei gar e grafi* Pas o pisteyon ep' auto ou kataishynthisetai.
verses.translation: For the scripture saith, Whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed.

verses.original: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν διαστολὴ Ἰουδαίου τε καὶ Ἕλληνος, ὁ γὰρ αὐτὸς κύριος πάντων, πλουτῶν εἰς πάντας τοὺς ἐπικαλουμένους αὐτόν·
verses.translit: ou gar estin diastole Ioydaioy te kai Ellinos, o gar autos kyrios panton, ployton eis pantas tous epikaloymenoys auton*
verses.translation: For there is no difference between the Jew and the Greek: for the same Lord over all is rich unto all that call upon him.

verses.original: Πᾶς γὰρ ὃς ἂν ἐπικαλέσηται τὸ ὄνομα κυρίου σωθήσεται.
verses.translit: Pas gar os an epikalesitai to onoma kyrioy sothisetai.
verses.translation: For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.

verses.original: Πῶς οὖν ⸀ἐπικαλέσωνται εἰς ὃν οὐκ ἐπίστευσαν; πῶς δὲ ⸀πιστεύσωσιν οὗ οὐκ ἤκουσαν; πῶς δὲ ⸀ἀκούσωσιν χωρὶς κηρύσσοντος;
verses.translit: Pos oun epikalesontai eis on ouk episteysan; pos de pisteysosin ou ouk ekoysan; pos de akoysosin horis kiryssontos;
verses.translation: How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher?

verses.original: πῶς δὲ ⸀κηρύξωσιν ἐὰν μὴ ἀποσταλῶσιν; ⸀καθὼς γέγραπται· Ὡς ὡραῖοι οἱ πόδες τῶν ⸀εὐαγγελιζομένων ⸀τὰ ἀγαθά.
verses.translit: pos de kiryxosin ean me apostalosin; kathos gegraptai* Os oraioi oi podes ton euaggelizomenon ta agatha.
verses.translation: And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!

verses.original: ἀλλʼ οὐ πάντες ὑπήκουσαν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ· Ἠσαΐας γὰρ λέγει· Κύριε, τίς ἐπίστευσεν τῇ ἀκοῇ ἡμῶν;
verses.translit: all' ou pantes upikoysan to euaggelio* EsaIas gar legei* Kyrie, tis episteysen te akoe emon;
verses.translation: But they have not all obeyed the gospel. For Esaias saith, Lord, who hath believed our report?

verses.original: ἄρα ἡ πίστις ἐξ ἀκοῆς, ἡ δὲ ἀκοὴ διὰ ῥήματος ⸀Χριστοῦ.
verses.translit: ara e pistis ex akoes, e de akoe dia Rimatos Hristou.
verses.translation: So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.

verses.original: Ἀλλὰ λέγω, μὴ οὐκ ἤκουσαν; μενοῦνγε· Εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν ἐξῆλθεν ὁ φθόγγος αὐτῶν, καὶ εἰς τὰ πέρατα τῆς οἰκουμένης τὰ ῥήματα αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: Alla lego, me ouk ekoysan; menounge* Eis pasan ten gen exelthen o fthoggos auton, kai eis ta perata tes oikoymenis ta Rimata auton.
verses.translation: But I say, Have they not heard? Yes verily, their sound went into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world.

verses.original: ἀλλὰ λέγω, μὴ ⸂Ἰσραὴλ οὐκ ἔγνω⸃; πρῶτος Μωϋσῆς λέγει· Ἐγὼ παραζηλώσω ὑμᾶς ἐπʼ οὐκ ἔθνει, ἐπʼ ἔθνει ἀσυνέτῳ παροργιῶ ὑμᾶς.
verses.translit: alla lego, me Israel ouk egno; protos Moyses legei* Ego paraziloso umas ep' ouk ethnei, ep' ethnei asyneto parorgio umas.
verses.translation: But I say, Did not Israel know? First Moses saith, I will provoke you to jealousy by them that are no people, and by a foolish nation I will anger you.

verses.original: Ἠσαΐας δὲ ἀποτολμᾷ καὶ λέγει· Εὑρέθην ⸀ἐν τοῖς ἐμὲ μὴ ζητοῦσιν, ἐμφανὴς ⸀ἐγενόμην τοῖς ἐμὲ μὴ ἐπερωτῶσιν.
verses.translit: EsaIas de apotolma kai legei* Eurethin en tois eme me zitousin, emfanes egenomin tois eme me eperotosin.
verses.translation: But Esaias is very bold, and saith, I was found of them that sought me not; I was made manifest unto them that asked not after me.

verses.original: πρὸς δὲ τὸν Ἰσραὴλ λέγει· Ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν ἐξεπέτασα τὰς χεῖράς μου πρὸς λαὸν ἀπειθοῦντα καὶ ἀντιλέγοντα.
verses.translit: pros de ton Israel legei* Olin ten emeran exepetasa tas heiras moy pros laon apeithounta kai antilegonta.
verses.translation: But to Israel he saith, All day long I have stretched forth my hands unto a disobedient and gainsaying people.

verses.original: Λέγω οὖν, μὴ ἀπώσατο ὁ θεὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ; μὴ γένοιτο· καὶ γὰρ ἐγὼ Ἰσραηλίτης εἰμί, ἐκ σπέρματος Ἀβραάμ, φυλῆς Βενιαμίν.
verses.translit: Lego oun, me aposato o theos ton laon autou; me genoito* kai gar ego Israilitis eimi, ek spermatos Avraam, fyles Veniamin.
verses.translation: I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.

verses.original: οὐκ ἀπώσατο ὁ θεὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ ὃν προέγνω. ἢ οὐκ οἴδατε ἐν Ἠλίᾳ τί λέγει ἡ γραφή, ὡς ἐντυγχάνει τῷ θεῷ κατὰ τοῦ ⸀Ἰσραήλ;
verses.translit: ouk aposato o theos ton laon autou on proegno. e ouk oidate en Elia ti legei e grafi, os entyghanei to theo kata tou Israil;
verses.translation: God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew. Wot ye not what the scripture saith of Elias? how he maketh intercession to God against Israel, saying,

verses.original: Κύριε, τοὺς προφήτας σου ἀπέκτειναν, ⸀τὰ θυσιαστήριά σου κατέσκαψαν, κἀγὼ ὑπελείφθην μόνος, καὶ ζητοῦσιν τὴν ψυχήν μου.
verses.translit: Kyrie, tous profitas soy apekteinan, ta thysiastiria soy kateskapsan, kago upeleifthin monos, kai zitousin ten psyhin moy.
verses.translation: Lord, they have killed thy prophets, and digged down thine altars; and I am left alone, and they seek my life.

verses.original: ἀλλὰ τί λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ χρηματισμός; Κατέλιπον ἐμαυτῷ ἑπτακισχιλίους ἄνδρας, οἵτινες οὐκ ἔκαμψαν γόνυ τῇ Βάαλ.
verses.translit: alla ti legei auto o hrimatismos; Katelipon emayto eptakishilioys andras, oitines ouk ekampsan gony te Vaal.
verses.translation: But what saith the answer of God unto him? I have reserved to myself seven thousand men, who have not bowed the knee to the image of Baal.

verses.original: οὕτως οὖν καὶ ἐν τῷ νῦν καιρῷ λεῖμμα κατʼ ἐκλογὴν χάριτος γέγονεν·
verses.translit: outos oun kai en to nun kairo leimma kat' eklogen haritos gegonen*
verses.translation: Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace.

verses.original: εἰ δὲ χάριτι, οὐκέτι ἐξ ἔργων, ἐπεὶ ἡ χάρις οὐκέτι γίνεται ⸀χάρις.
verses.translit: ei de hariti, ouketi ex ergon, epei e haris ouketi ginetai haris.
verses.translation: And if by grace, then is it no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace. But if it be of works, then is it no more grace: otherwise work is no more work.

verses.original: τί οὖν; ὃ ἐπιζητεῖ Ἰσραήλ, τοῦτο οὐκ ἐπέτυχεν, ἡ δὲ ἐκλογὴ ἐπέτυχεν· οἱ δὲ λοιποὶ ἐπωρώθησαν,
verses.translit: ti oun; o epizitei Israil, touto ouk epetyhen, e de ekloge epetyhen* oi de loipoi eporothisan,
verses.translation: What then? Israel hath not obtained that which he seeketh for; but the election hath obtained it, and the rest were blinded

verses.original: ⸀καθὼς γέγραπται· Ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ὁ θεὸς πνεῦμα κατανύξεως, ὀφθαλμοὺς τοῦ μὴ βλέπειν καὶ ὦτα τοῦ μὴ ἀκούειν, ἕως τῆς σήμερον ἡμέρας.
verses.translit: kathos gegraptai* Edoken autois o theos pneuma katanyxeos, ofthalmous tou me vlepein kai ota tou me akoyein, eos tes simeron emeras.
verses.translation: (According as it is written, God hath given them the spirit of slumber, eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear;) unto this day.

verses.original: καὶ Δαυὶδ λέγει· Γενηθήτω ἡ τράπεζα αὐτῶν εἰς παγίδα καὶ εἰς θήραν καὶ εἰς σκάνδαλον καὶ εἰς ἀνταπόδομα αὐτοῖς,
verses.translit: kai Dayid legei* Genithito e trapeza auton eis pagida kai eis thiran kai eis skandalon kai eis antapodoma autois,
verses.translation: And David saith, Let their table be made a snare, and a trap, and a stumblingblock, and a recompence unto them:

verses.original: σκοτισθήτωσαν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτῶν τοῦ μὴ βλέπειν, καὶ τὸν νῶτον αὐτῶν διὰ παντὸς σύγκαμψον.
verses.translit: skotisthitosan oi ofthalmoi auton tou me vlepein, kai ton noton auton dia pantos sygkampson.
verses.translation: Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see, and bow down their back alway.

verses.original: Λέγω οὖν, μὴ ἔπταισαν ἵνα πέσωσιν; μὴ γένοιτο· ἀλλὰ τῷ αὐτῶν παραπτώματι ἡ σωτηρία τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, εἰς τὸ παραζηλῶσαι αὐτούς.
verses.translit: Lego oun, me eptaisan ina pesosin; me genoito* alla to auton paraptomati e sotiria tois ethnesin, eis to parazilosai autoys.
verses.translation: I say then, Have they stumbled that they should fall? God forbid: but rather through their fall salvation is come unto the Gentiles, for to provoke them to jealousy.

verses.original: εἰ δὲ τὸ παράπτωμα αὐτῶν πλοῦτος κόσμου καὶ τὸ ἥττημα αὐτῶν πλοῦτος ἐθνῶν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: ei de to paraptoma auton ploutos kosmoy kai to ettima auton ploutos ethnon, poso mallon to pliroma auton.
verses.translation: Now if the fall of them be the riches of the world, and the diminishing of them the riches of the Gentiles; how much more their fulness?

verses.original: Ὑμῖν ⸀δὲ λέγω τοῖς ἔθνεσιν. ἐφʼ ὅσον μὲν ⸀οὖν εἰμι ἐγὼ ἐθνῶν ἀπόστολος, τὴν διακονίαν μου δοξάζω,
verses.translit: Umin de lego tois ethnesin. ef' oson men oun eimi ego ethnon apostolos, ten diakonian moy doxazo,
verses.translation: For I speak to you Gentiles, inasmuch as I am the apostle of the Gentiles, I magnify mine office:

verses.original: εἴ πως παραζηλώσω μου τὴν σάρκα καὶ σώσω τινὰς ἐξ αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: ei pos paraziloso moy ten sarka kai soso tinas ex auton.
verses.translation: If by any means I may provoke to emulation them which are my flesh, and might save some of them.

verses.original: εἰ γὰρ ἡ ἀποβολὴ αὐτῶν καταλλαγὴ κόσμου, τίς ἡ πρόσλημψις εἰ μὴ ζωὴ ἐκ νεκρῶν;
verses.translit: ei gar e apovole auton katallage kosmoy, tis e proslimpsis ei me zoe ek nekron;
verses.translation: For if the casting away of them be the reconciling of the world, what shall the receiving of them be , but life from the dead?

verses.original: εἰ δὲ ἡ ἀπαρχὴ ἁγία, καὶ τὸ φύραμα· καὶ εἰ ἡ ῥίζα ἁγία, καὶ οἱ κλάδοι.
verses.translit: ei de e aparhe agia, kai to fyrama* kai ei e Riza agia, kai oi kladoi.
verses.translation: For if the firstfruit be holy, the lump is also holy : and if the root be holy, so are the branches.

verses.original: Εἰ δέ τινες τῶν κλάδων ἐξεκλάσθησαν, σὺ δὲ ἀγριέλαιος ὢν ἐνεκεντρίσθης ἐν αὐτοῖς καὶ συγκοινωνὸς τῆς ⸀ῥίζης τῆς πιότητος τῆς ἐλαίας ἐγένου,
verses.translit: Ei de tines ton kladon exeklasthisan, su de agrielaios on enekentristhis en autois kai sygkoinonos tes Rizis tes piotitos tes elaias egenoy,
verses.translation: And if some of the branches be broken off, and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert graffed in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree;

verses.original: μὴ κατακαυχῶ τῶν κλάδων· εἰ δὲ κατακαυχᾶσαι, οὐ σὺ τὴν ῥίζαν βαστάζεις ἀλλὰ ἡ ῥίζα σέ.
verses.translit: me katakayho ton kladon* ei de katakayhasai, ou su ten Rizan vastazeis alla e Riza se.
verses.translation: Boast not against the branches. But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee.

verses.original: ἐρεῖς οὖν· Ἐξεκλάσθησαν κλάδοι ἵνα ἐγὼ ἐγκεντρισθῶ.
verses.translit: ereis oun* Exeklasthisan kladoi ina ego egkentristho.
verses.translation: Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be graffed in.

verses.original: καλῶς· τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ ἐξεκλάσθησαν, σὺ δὲ τῇ πίστει ἕστηκας. μὴ ⸂ὑψηλὰ φρόνει⸃, ἀλλὰ φοβοῦ·
verses.translit: kalos* te apistia exeklasthisan, su de te pistei estikas. me upsila fronei, alla fovou*
verses.translation: Well; because of unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear:

verses.original: εἰ γὰρ ὁ θεὸς τῶν κατὰ φύσιν κλάδων οὐκ ἐφείσατο, ⸀οὐδὲ σοῦ φείσεται.
verses.translit: ei gar o theos ton kata fysin kladon ouk efeisato, oude sou feisetai.
verses.translation: For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee.

verses.original: ἴδε οὖν χρηστότητα καὶ ἀποτομίαν θεοῦ· ἐπὶ μὲν τοὺς πεσόντας ⸀ἀποτομία, ἐπὶ δὲ σὲ ⸂χρηστότης θεοῦ⸃, ἐὰν ⸀ἐπιμένῃς τῇ χρηστότητι, ἐπεὶ καὶ σὺ ἐκκοπήσῃ.
verses.translit: ide oun hristotita kai apotomian theou* epi men tous pesontas apotomia, epi de se hristotis theou, ean epimenes te hristotiti, epei kai su ekkopise.
verses.translation: Behold therefore the goodness and severity of God: on them which fell, severity; but toward thee, goodness, if thou continue in his goodness: otherwise thou also shalt be cut off.

verses.original: κἀκεῖνοι δέ, ἐὰν μὴ ⸀ἐπιμένωσι τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ, ἐγκεντρισθήσονται· δυνατὸς γάρ ⸂ἐστιν ὁ θεὸς⸃ πάλιν ἐγκεντρίσαι αὐτούς.
verses.translit: kakeinoi de, ean me epimenosi te apistia, egkentristhisontai* dynatos gar estin o theos palin egkentrisai autoys.
verses.translation: And they also, if they abide not still in unbelief, shall be graffed in: for God is able to graff them in again.

verses.original: εἰ γὰρ σὺ ἐκ τῆς κατὰ φύσιν ἐξεκόπης ἀγριελαίου καὶ παρὰ φύσιν ἐνεκεντρίσθης εἰς καλλιέλαιον, πόσῳ μᾶλλον οὗτοι οἱ κατὰ φύσιν ἐγκεντρισθήσονται τῇ ἰδίᾳ ἐλαίᾳ.
verses.translit: ei gar su ek tes kata fysin exekopis agrielaioy kai para fysin enekentristhis eis kallielaion, poso mallon outoi oi kata fysin egkentristhisontai te idia elaia.
verses.translation: For if thou wert cut out of the olive tree which is wild by nature, and wert graffed contrary to nature into a good olive tree: how much more shall these, which be the natural branches , be graffed into their own olive tree?

verses.original: Οὐ γὰρ θέλω ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν, ἀδελφοί, τὸ μυστήριον τοῦτο, ἵνα μὴ ⸀ἦτε ἑαυτοῖς φρόνιμοι, ὅτι πώρωσις ἀπὸ μέρους τῷ Ἰσραὴλ γέγονεν ἄχρι οὗ τὸ πλήρωμα τῶν ἐθνῶν εἰσέλθῃ,
verses.translit: Ou gar thelo umas agnoein, adelfoi, to mystirion touto, ina me ete eaytois fronimoi, oti porosis apo meroys to Israel gegonen ahri ou to pliroma ton ethnon eiselthe,
verses.translation: For I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant of this mystery, lest ye should be wise in your own conceits; that blindness in part is happened to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in.

verses.original: καὶ οὕτως πᾶς Ἰσραὴλ σωθήσεται· καθὼς γέγραπται· Ἥξει ἐκ Σιὼν ὁ ⸀ῥυόμενος, ἀποστρέψει ἀσεβείας ἀπὸ Ἰακώβ.
verses.translit: kai outos pas Israel sothisetai* kathos gegraptai* Exei ek Sion o Ryomenos, apostrepsei aseveias apo Iakov.
verses.translation: And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob:

verses.original: καὶ αὕτη αὐτοῖς ἡ παρʼ ἐμοῦ διαθήκη, ὅταν ἀφέλωμαι τὰς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: kai auti autois e par' emou diathiki, otan afelomai tas amartias auton.
verses.translation: For this is my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins.

verses.original: κατὰ μὲν τὸ εὐαγγέλιον ἐχθροὶ διʼ ὑμᾶς, κατὰ δὲ τὴν ἐκλογὴν ἀγαπητοὶ διὰ τοὺς πατέρας·
verses.translit: kata men to euaggelion ehthroi di' umas, kata de ten eklogen agapitoi dia tous pateras*
verses.translation: As concerning the gospel, they are enemies for your sakes: but as touching the election, they are beloved for the fathers’ sakes.

verses.original: ἀμεταμέλητα γὰρ τὰ χαρίσματα καὶ ἡ κλῆσις τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: ametamelita gar ta harismata kai e klesis tou theou.
verses.translation: For the gifts and calling of God are without repentance.

verses.original: ὥσπερ ⸀γὰρ ὑμεῖς ποτε ἠπειθήσατε τῷ θεῷ, νῦν δὲ ἠλεήθητε τῇ τούτων ἀπειθείᾳ,
verses.translit: osper gar umeis pote epeithisate to theo, nun de eleithite te toyton apeitheia,
verses.translation: For as ye in times past have not believed God, yet have now obtained mercy through their unbelief:

verses.original: οὕτως καὶ οὗτοι νῦν ἠπείθησαν τῷ ὑμετέρῳ ἐλέει ἵνα καὶ αὐτοὶ ⸀νῦν ἐλεηθῶσιν·
verses.translit: outos kai outoi nun epeithisan to umetero eleei ina kai autoi nun eleithosin*
verses.translation: Even so have these also now not believed, that through your mercy they also may obtain mercy.

verses.original: συνέκλεισεν γὰρ ὁ θεὸς τοὺς πάντας εἰς ἀπείθειαν ἵνα τοὺς πάντας ἐλεήσῃ.
verses.translit: synekleisen gar o theos tous pantas eis apeitheian ina tous pantas eleise.
verses.translation: For God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all.

verses.original: Ὦ βάθος πλούτου καὶ σοφίας καὶ γνώσεως θεοῦ· ὡς ἀνεξεραύνητα τὰ κρίματα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀνεξιχνίαστοι αἱ ὁδοὶ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: O vathos ploytoy kai sofias kai gnoseos theou* os anexeraynita ta krimata autou kai anexihniastoi ai odoi autou.
verses.translation: O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God! how unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past finding out!

verses.original: Τίς γὰρ ἔγνω νοῦν κυρίου; ἢ τίς σύμβουλος αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο;
verses.translit: Tis gar egno noun kyrioy; e tis symvoylos autou egeneto;
verses.translation: For who hath known the mind of the Lord? or who hath been his counsellor?

verses.original: ἢ τίς προέδωκεν αὐτῷ, καὶ ἀνταποδοθήσεται αὐτῷ;
verses.translit: e tis proedoken auto, kai antapodothisetai auto;
verses.translation: Or who hath first given to him, and it shall be recompensed unto him again?

verses.original: ὅτι ἐξ αὐτοῦ καὶ διʼ αὐτοῦ καὶ εἰς αὐτὸν τὰ πάντα· αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας, ἀμήν.
verses.translit: oti ex autou kai di' autou kai eis auton ta panta* auto e doxa eis tous aionas, amin.
verses.translation: For of him, and through him, and to him, are all things: to whom be glory for ever. Amen.

verses.original: Παρακαλῶ οὖν ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί, διὰ τῶν οἰκτιρμῶν τοῦ θεοῦ παραστῆσαι τὰ σώματα ὑμῶν θυσίαν ζῶσαν ἁγίαν ⸂εὐάρεστον τῷ θεῷ⸃, τὴν λογικὴν λατρείαν ὑμῶν·
verses.translit: Parakalo oun umas, adelfoi, dia ton oiktirmon tou theou parastesai ta somata umon thysian zosan agian euareston to theo, ten logiken latreian umon*
verses.translation: I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.

verses.original: καὶ μὴ ⸀συσχηματίζεσθε τῷ αἰῶνι τούτῳ, ἀλλὰ ⸀μεταμορφοῦσθε τῇ ἀνακαινώσει τοῦ ⸀νοός, εἰς τὸ δοκιμάζειν ὑμᾶς τί τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ, τὸ ἀγαθὸν καὶ εὐάρεστον καὶ τέλειον.
verses.translit: kai me syshimatizesthe to aioni toyto, alla metamorfousthe te anakainosei tou noos, eis to dokimazein umas ti to thelima tou theou, to agathon kai euareston kai teleion.
verses.translation: And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.

verses.original: Λέγω γὰρ διὰ τῆς χάριτος τῆς δοθείσης μοι παντὶ τῷ ὄντι ἐν ὑμῖν μὴ ὑπερφρονεῖν παρʼ ὃ δεῖ φρονεῖν, ἀλλὰ φρονεῖν εἰς τὸ σωφρονεῖν, ἑκάστῳ ὡς ὁ θεὸς ἐμέρισεν μέτρον πίστεως.
verses.translit: Lego gar dia tes haritos tes dotheisis moi panti to onti en umin me uperfronein par' o dei fronein, alla fronein eis to sofronein, ekasto os o theos emerisen metron pisteos.
verses.translation: For I say, through the grace given unto me, to every man that is among you, not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith.

verses.original: καθάπερ γὰρ ἐν ἑνὶ σώματι ⸂πολλὰ μέλη⸃ ἔχομεν, τὰ δὲ μέλη πάντα οὐ τὴν αὐτὴν ἔχει πρᾶξιν,
verses.translit: kathaper gar en eni somati polla meli ehomen, ta de meli panta ou ten auten ehei praxin,
verses.translation: For as we have many members in one body, and all members have not the same office:

verses.original: οὕτως οἱ πολλοὶ ἓν σῶμά ἐσμεν ἐν Χριστῷ, ⸀τὸ δὲ καθʼ εἷς ἀλλήλων μέλη.
verses.translit: outos oi polloi en soma esmen en Hristo, to de kath' eis allilon meli.
verses.translation: So we, being many, are one body in Christ, and every one members one of another.

verses.original: ἔχοντες δὲ χαρίσματα κατὰ τὴν χάριν τὴν δοθεῖσαν ἡμῖν διάφορα, εἴτε προφητείαν κατὰ τὴν ἀναλογίαν τῆς πίστεως,
verses.translit: ehontes de harismata kata ten harin ten dotheisan emin diafora, eite profiteian kata ten analogian tes pisteos,
verses.translation: Having then gifts differing according to the grace that is given to us, whether prophecy, let us prophesy according to the proportion of faith;

verses.original: εἴτε διακονίαν ἐν τῇ διακονίᾳ, εἴτε ὁ διδάσκων ἐν τῇ διδασκαλίᾳ,
verses.translit: eite diakonian en te diakonia, eite o didaskon en te didaskalia,
verses.translation: Or ministry, let us wait on our ministering: or he that teacheth, on teaching;

verses.original: εἴτε ὁ παρακαλῶν ἐν τῇ παρακλήσει, ὁ μεταδιδοὺς ἐν ἁπλότητι, ὁ προϊστάμενος ἐν σπουδῇ, ὁ ἐλεῶν ἐν ἱλαρότητι.
verses.translit: eite o parakalon en te paraklisei, o metadidous en aplotiti, o proistamenos en spoyde, o eleon en ilarotiti.
verses.translation: Or he that exhorteth, on exhortation: he that giveth, let him do it with simplicity; he that ruleth, with diligence; he that sheweth mercy, with cheerfulness.

verses.original: Ἡ ἀγάπη ἀνυπόκριτος. ἀποστυγοῦντες τὸ πονηρόν, κολλώμενοι τῷ ἀγαθῷ·
verses.translit: E agapi anypokritos. apostygountes to poniron, kollomenoi to agatho*
verses.translation: Let love be without dissimulation. Abhor that which is evil; cleave to that which is good.

verses.original: τῇ φιλαδελφίᾳ εἰς ἀλλήλους φιλόστοργοι, τῇ τιμῇ ἀλλήλους προηγούμενοι,
verses.translit: te filadelfia eis alliloys filostorgoi, te time alliloys proigoymenoi,
verses.translation: Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another;

verses.original: τῇ σπουδῇ μὴ ὀκνηροί, τῷ πνεύματι ζέοντες, τῷ κυρίῳ δουλεύοντες,
verses.translit: te spoyde me okniroi, to pneymati zeontes, to kyrio doyleyontes,
verses.translation: Not slothful in business; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord;

verses.original: τῇ ἐλπίδι χαίροντες, τῇ θλίψει ὑπομένοντες, τῇ προσευχῇ προσκαρτεροῦντες,
verses.translit: te elpidi hairontes, te thlipsei upomenontes, te proseyhe proskarterountes,
verses.translation: Rejoicing in hope; patient in tribulation; continuing instant in prayer;

verses.original: ταῖς χρείαις τῶν ἁγίων κοινωνοῦντες, τὴν φιλοξενίαν διώκοντες.
verses.translit: tais hreiais ton agion koinonountes, ten filoxenian diokontes.
verses.translation: Distributing to the necessity of saints; given to hospitality.

verses.original: εὐλογεῖτε τοὺς ⸀διώκοντας, εὐλογεῖτε καὶ μὴ καταρᾶσθε.
verses.translit: eulogeite tous diokontas, eulogeite kai me katarasthe.
verses.translation: Bless them which persecute you: bless, and curse not.

verses.original: χαίρειν μετὰ ⸀χαιρόντων, κλαίειν μετὰ κλαιόντων.
verses.translit: hairein meta haironton, klaiein meta klaionton.
verses.translation: Rejoice with them that do rejoice, and weep with them that weep.

verses.original: τὸ αὐτὸ εἰς ἀλλήλους φρονοῦντες, μὴ τὰ ὑψηλὰ φρονοῦντες ἀλλὰ τοῖς ταπεινοῖς συναπαγόμενοι. μὴ γίνεσθε φρόνιμοι παρʼ ἑαυτοῖς.
verses.translit: to auto eis alliloys fronountes, me ta upsila fronountes alla tois tapeinois synapagomenoi. me ginesthe fronimoi par' eaytois.
verses.translation: Be of the same mind one toward another. Mind not high things, but condescend to men of low estate. Be not wise in your own conceits.

verses.original: μηδενὶ κακὸν ἀντὶ κακοῦ ἀποδιδόντες· προνοούμενοι καλὰ ἐνώπιον πάντων ἀνθρώπων·
verses.translit: mideni kakon anti kakou apodidontes* pronooymenoi kala enopion panton anthropon*
verses.translation: Recompense to no man evil for evil. Provide things honest in the sight of all men.

verses.original: εἰ δυνατόν, τὸ ἐξ ὑμῶν μετὰ πάντων ἀνθρώπων εἰρηνεύοντες·
verses.translit: ei dynaton, to ex umon meta panton anthropon eirineyontes*
verses.translation: If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.

verses.original: μὴ ἑαυτοὺς ἐκδικοῦντες, ἀγαπητοί, ἀλλὰ δότε τόπον τῇ ὀργῇ, γέγραπται γάρ· Ἐμοὶ ἐκδίκησις, ἐγὼ ἀνταποδώσω, λέγει κύριος.
verses.translit: me eaytous ekdikountes, agapitoi, alla dote topon te orge, gegraptai gar* Emoi ekdikisis, ego antapodoso, legei kyrios.
verses.translation: Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord.

verses.original: ⸂ἀλλὰ ἐὰν⸃ πεινᾷ ὁ ἐχθρός σου, ψώμιζε αὐτόν· ἐὰν διψᾷ, πότιζε αὐτόν· τοῦτο γὰρ ποιῶν ἄνθρακας πυρὸς σωρεύσεις ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: alla ean peina o ehthros soy, psomize auton* ean dipsa, potize auton* touto gar poion anthrakas pyros soreyseis epi ten kefalen autou.
verses.translation: Therefore if thine enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink: for in so doing thou shalt heap coals of fire on his head.

verses.original: μὴ νικῶ ὑπὸ τοῦ κακοῦ, ἀλλὰ νίκα ἐν τῷ ἀγαθῷ τὸ κακόν.
verses.translit: me niko upo tou kakou, alla nika en to agatho to kakon.
verses.translation: Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.

verses.original: Πᾶσα ψυχὴ ἐξουσίαις ὑπερεχούσαις ὑποτασσέσθω, οὐ γὰρ ἔστιν ἐξουσία εἰ μὴ ὑπὸ θεοῦ, αἱ δὲ ⸀οὖσαι ⸀ὑπὸ θεοῦ τεταγμέναι εἰσίν.
verses.translit: Pasa psyhe exoysiais uperehoysais upotassestho, ou gar estin exoysia ei me upo theou, ai de ousai upo theou tetagmenai eisin.
verses.translation: Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God.

verses.original: ὥστε ὁ ἀντιτασσόμενος τῇ ἐξουσίᾳ τῇ τοῦ θεοῦ διαταγῇ ἀνθέστηκεν, οἱ δὲ ἀνθεστηκότες ἑαυτοῖς κρίμα λήμψονται.
verses.translit: oste o antitassomenos te exoysia te tou theou diatage anthestiken, oi de anthestikotes eaytois krima limpsontai.
verses.translation: Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation.

verses.original: οἱ γὰρ ἄρχοντες οὐκ εἰσὶν φόβος ⸂τῷ ἀγαθῷ ἔργῳ⸃ ἀλλὰ ⸂τῷ κακῷ⸃. θέλεις δὲ μὴ φοβεῖσθαι τὴν ἐξουσίαν; τὸ ἀγαθὸν ποίει, καὶ ἕξεις ἔπαινον ἐξ αὐτῆς·
verses.translit: oi gar arhontes ouk eisin fovos to agatho ergo alla to kako. theleis de me foveisthai ten exoysian? to agathon poiei, kai exeis epainon ex autes*
verses.translation: For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil. Wilt thou then not be afraid of the power? do that which is good, and thou shalt have praise of the same:

verses.original: θεοῦ γὰρ διάκονός ἐστιν σοὶ εἰς τὸ ἀγαθόν. ἐὰν δὲ τὸ κακὸν ποιῇς, φοβοῦ· οὐ γὰρ εἰκῇ τὴν μάχαιραν φορεῖ· θεοῦ γὰρ διάκονός ἐστιν, ἔκδικος εἰς ὀργὴν τῷ τὸ κακὸν πράσσοντι.
verses.translit: theou gar diakonos estin soi eis to agathon. ean de to kakon poies, fovou* ou gar eike ten mahairan forei* theou gar diakonos estin, ekdikos eis orgen to to kakon prassonti.
verses.translation: For he is the minister of God to thee for good. But if thou do that which is evil, be afraid; for he beareth not the sword in vain: for he is the minister of God, a revenger to execute wrath upon him that doeth evil.

verses.original: διὸ ἀνάγκη ὑποτάσσεσθαι, οὐ μόνον διὰ τὴν ὀργὴν ἀλλὰ καὶ διὰ τὴν συνείδησιν,
verses.translit: dio anagki upotassesthai, ou monon dia ten orgen alla kai dia ten syneidisin,
verses.translation: Wherefore ye must needs be subject, not only for wrath, but also for conscience sake.

verses.original: διὰ τοῦτο γὰρ καὶ φόρους τελεῖτε, λειτουργοὶ γὰρ θεοῦ εἰσιν εἰς αὐτὸ τοῦτο προσκαρτεροῦντες.
verses.translit: dia touto gar kai foroys teleite, leitoyrgoi gar theou eisin eis auto touto proskarterountes.
verses.translation: For for this cause pay ye tribute also: for they are God’s ministers, attending continually upon this very thing.

verses.original: ⸀ἀπόδοτε πᾶσι τὰς ὀφειλάς, τῷ τὸν φόρον τὸν φόρον, τῷ τὸ τέλος τὸ τέλος, τῷ τὸν φόβον τὸν φόβον, τῷ τὴν τιμὴν τὴν τιμήν.
verses.translit: apodote pasi tas ofeilas, to ton foron ton foron, to to telos to telos, to ton fovon ton fovon, to ten timen ten timin.
verses.translation: Render therefore to all their dues: tribute to whom tribute is due ; custom to whom custom; fear to whom fear; honour to whom honour.

verses.original: Μηδενὶ μηδὲν ὀφείλετε, εἰ μὴ τὸ ⸂ἀλλήλους ἀγαπᾶν⸃· ὁ γὰρ ἀγαπῶν τὸν ἕτερον νόμον πεπλήρωκεν.
verses.translit: Mideni miden ofeilete, ei me to alliloys agapan* o gar agapon ton eteron nomon pepliroken.
verses.translation: Owe no man any thing, but to love one another: for he that loveth another hath fulfilled the law.

verses.original: τὸ γάρ· Οὐ μοιχεύσεις, Οὐ φονεύσεις, Οὐ κλέψεις, Οὐκ ἐπιθυμήσεις, καὶ εἴ τις ἑτέρα ἐντολή, ἐν ⸂τῷ λόγῳ τούτῳ⸃ ἀνακεφαλαιοῦται, ⸂ἐν τῷ⸃· Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν.
verses.translit: to gar* Ou moiheyseis, Ou foneyseis, Ou klepseis, Ouk epithymiseis, kai ei tis etera entoli, en to logo toyto anakefalaioutai, en to* Agapiseis ton plision soy os seayton.
verses.translation: For this, Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not kill, Thou shalt not steal, Thou shalt not bear false witness, Thou shalt not covet; and if there be any other commandment, it is briefly comprehended in this saying, namely, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.

verses.original: ἡ ἀγάπη τῷ πλησίον κακὸν οὐκ ἐργάζεται· πλήρωμα οὖν νόμου ἡ ἀγάπη.
verses.translit: e agapi to plision kakon ouk ergazetai* pliroma oun nomoy e agapi.
verses.translation: Love worketh no ill to his neighbour: therefore love is the fulfilling of the law.
