verses.original: εἰ δὲ οὐκ ἐγκρατεύονται, γαμησάτωσαν, κρεῖττον γάρ ἐστιν ⸀γαμῆσαι ἢ πυροῦσθαι.
verses.translit: ei de ouk egkrateyontai, gamisatosan, kreitton gar estin gamesai e pyrousthai.
verses.translation: But if they cannot contain, let them marry: for it is better to marry than to burn.

verses.original: Τοῖς δὲ γεγαμηκόσιν παραγγέλλω, οὐκ ἐγὼ ἀλλὰ ὁ κύριος, γυναῖκα ἀπὸ ἀνδρὸς μὴ χωρισθῆναι—
verses.translit: Tois de gegamikosin paraggello, ouk ego alla o kyrios, gynaika apo andros me horisthenai--
verses.translation: And unto the married I command, yet not I, but the Lord, Let not the wife depart from her husband:

verses.original: ἐὰν δὲ καὶ χωρισθῇ, μενέτω ἄγαμος ἢ τῷ ἀνδρὶ καταλλαγήτω— καὶ ἄνδρα γυναῖκα μὴ ἀφιέναι.
verses.translit: ean de kai horisthe, meneto agamos e to andri katallagito-- kai andra gynaika me afienai.
verses.translation: But and if she depart, let her remain unmarried, or be reconciled to her husband: and let not the husband put away his wife.

verses.original: Τοῖς δὲ λοιποῖς ⸂λέγω ἐγώ⸃, οὐχ ὁ κύριος· εἴ τις ἀδελφὸς γυναῖκα ἔχει ἄπιστον, καὶ αὕτη συνευδοκεῖ οἰκεῖν μετʼ αὐτοῦ, μὴ ἀφιέτω αὐτήν·
verses.translit: Tois de loipois lego ego, ouh o kyrios* ei tis adelfos gynaika ehei apiston, kai auti syneydokei oikein met' autou, me afieto autin*
verses.translation: But to the rest speak I, not the Lord: If any brother hath a wife that believeth not, and she be pleased to dwell with him, let him not put her away.

verses.original: καὶ γυνὴ ⸂εἴ τις⸃ ἔχει ἄνδρα ἄπιστον, καὶ ⸀οὗτος συνευδοκεῖ οἰκεῖν μετʼ αὐτῆς, μὴ ἀφιέτω ⸂τὸν ἄνδρα⸃.
verses.translit: kai gyne ei tis ehei andra apiston, kai outos syneydokei oikein met' autes, me afieto ton andra.
verses.translation: And the woman which hath an husband that believeth not, and if he be pleased to dwell with her, let her not leave him.

verses.original: ἡγίασται γὰρ ὁ ἀνὴρ ὁ ἄπιστος ἐν τῇ γυναικί, καὶ ἡγίασται ἡ γυνὴ ἡ ἄπιστος ἐν τῷ ⸀ἀδελφῷ· ἐπεὶ ἄρα τὰ τέκνα ὑμῶν ἀκάθαρτά ἐστιν, νῦν δὲ ἅγιά ἐστιν.
verses.translit: egiastai gar o aner o apistos en te gynaiki, kai egiastai e gyne e apistos en to adelfo* epei ara ta tekna umon akatharta estin, nun de agia estin.
verses.translation: For the unbelieving husband is sanctified by the wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified by the husband: else were your children unclean; but now are they holy.

verses.original: εἰ δὲ ὁ ἄπιστος χωρίζεται, χωριζέσθω· οὐ δεδούλωται ὁ ἀδελφὸς ἢ ἡ ἀδελφὴ ἐν τοῖς τοιούτοις, ἐν δὲ εἰρήνῃ κέκληκεν ⸀ἡμᾶς ὁ θεός.
verses.translit: ei de o apistos horizetai, horizestho* ou dedoylotai o adelfos e e adelfe en tois toioytois, en de eirine kekliken emas o theos.
verses.translation: But if the unbelieving depart, let him depart. A brother or a sister is not under bondage in such cases : but God hath called us to peace.

verses.original: τί γὰρ οἶδας, γύναι, εἰ τὸν ἄνδρα σώσεις; ἢ τί οἶδας, ἄνερ, εἰ τὴν γυναῖκα σώσεις;
verses.translit: ti gar oidas, gynai, ei ton andra soseis; e ti oidas, aner, ei ten gynaika soseis;
verses.translation: For what knowest thou, O wife, whether thou shalt save thy husband? or how knowest thou, O man, whether thou shalt save thy wife?

verses.original: Εἰ μὴ ἑκάστῳ ὡς ⸀ἐμέρισεν ὁ ⸀κύριος, ἕκαστον ὡς κέκληκεν ὁ ⸀θεός, οὕτως περιπατείτω· καὶ οὕτως ἐν ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις πάσαις διατάσσομαι.
verses.translit: Ei me ekasto os emerisen o kyrios, ekaston os kekliken o theos, outos peripateito* kai outos en tais ekklisiais pasais diatassomai.
verses.translation: But as God hath distributed to every man, as the Lord hath called every one, so let him walk. And so ordain I in all churches.

verses.original: περιτετμημένος τις ἐκλήθη; μὴ ἐπισπάσθω· ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ ⸂κέκληταί τις⸃; μὴ περιτεμνέσθω.
verses.translit: peritetmimenos tis eklithi? me epispastho* en akrovystia keklitai tis? me peritemnestho.
verses.translation: Is any man called being circumcised? let him not become uncircumcised. Is any called in uncircumcision? let him not be circumcised.

verses.original: ἡ περιτομὴ οὐδέν ἐστιν, καὶ ἡ ἀκροβυστία οὐδέν ἐστιν, ἀλλὰ τήρησις ἐντολῶν θεοῦ.
verses.translit: e peritome ouden estin, kai e akrovystia ouden estin, alla tirisis entolon theou.
verses.translation: Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing, but the keeping of the commandments of God.

verses.original: ἕκαστος ἐν τῇ κλήσει ᾗ ἐκλήθη ἐν ταύτῃ μενέτω.
verses.translit: ekastos en te klisei e eklithi en tayte meneto.
verses.translation: Let every man abide in the same calling wherein he was called.

verses.original: Δοῦλος ἐκλήθης; μή σοι μελέτω· ἀλλʼ εἰ καὶ δύνασαι ἐλεύθερος γενέσθαι, μᾶλλον χρῆσαι.
verses.translit: Doulos eklithis? mi soi meleto* all' ei kai dynasai eleytheros genesthai, mallon hresai.
verses.translation: Art thou called being a servant? care not for it: but if thou mayest be made free, use it rather.

verses.original: ὁ γὰρ ἐν κυρίῳ κληθεὶς δοῦλος ἀπελεύθερος κυρίου ἐστίν· ⸀ὁμοίως ὁ ἐλεύθερος κληθεὶς δοῦλός ἐστιν Χριστοῦ.
verses.translit: o gar en kyrio klitheis doulos apeleytheros kyrioy estin* omoios o eleytheros klitheis doulos estin Hristou.
verses.translation: For he that is called in the Lord, being a servant, is the Lord’s freeman: likewise also he that is called, being free, is Christ’s servant.

verses.original: τιμῆς ἠγοράσθητε· μὴ γίνεσθε δοῦλοι ἀνθρώπων.
verses.translit: times egorasthite* me ginesthe douloi anthropon.
verses.translation: Ye are bought with a price; be not ye the servants of men.

verses.original: ἕκαστος ἐν ᾧ ἐκλήθη, ἀδελφοί, ἐν τούτῳ μενέτω παρὰ θεῷ.
verses.translit: ekastos en o eklithi, adelfoi, en toyto meneto para theo.
verses.translation: Brethren, let every man, wherein he is called, therein abide with God.

verses.original: Περὶ δὲ τῶν παρθένων ἐπιταγὴν κυρίου οὐκ ἔχω, γνώμην δὲ δίδωμι ὡς ἠλεημένος ὑπὸ κυρίου πιστὸς εἶναι.
verses.translit: Peri de ton parthenon epitagen kyrioy ouk eho, gnomin de didomi os eleimenos upo kyrioy pistos einai.
verses.translation: Now concerning virgins I have no commandment of the Lord: yet I give my judgment, as one that hath obtained mercy of the Lord to be faithful.

verses.original: νομίζω οὖν τοῦτο καλὸν ὑπάρχειν διὰ τὴν ἐνεστῶσαν ἀνάγκην, ὅτι καλὸν ἀνθρώπῳ τὸ οὕτως εἶναι.
verses.translit: nomizo oun touto kalon uparhein dia ten enestosan anagkin, oti kalon anthropo to outos einai.
verses.translation: I suppose therefore that this is good for the present distress, I say , that it is good for a man so to be.

verses.original: δέδεσαι γυναικί; μὴ ζήτει λύσιν· λέλυσαι ἀπὸ γυναικός; μὴ ζήτει γυναῖκα·
verses.translit: dedesai gynaiki? me zitei lysin* lelysai apo gynaikos? me zitei gynaika*
verses.translation: Art thou bound unto a wife? seek not to be loosed. Art thou loosed from a wife? seek not a wife.

verses.original: ἐὰν δὲ καὶ ⸀γαμήσῃς, οὐχ ἥμαρτες. καὶ ἐὰν γήμῃ ἡ παρθένος, οὐχ ἥμαρτεν. θλῖψιν δὲ τῇ σαρκὶ ἕξουσιν οἱ τοιοῦτοι, ἐγὼ δὲ ὑμῶν φείδομαι.
verses.translit: ean de kai gamises, ouh emartes. kai ean gime e parthenos, ouh emarten. thlipsin de te sarki exoysin oi toioutoi, ego de umon feidomai.
verses.translation: But and if thou marry, thou hast not sinned; and if a virgin marry, she hath not sinned. Nevertheless such shall have trouble in the flesh: but I spare you.

verses.original: τοῦτο δέ φημι, ἀδελφοί, ὁ καιρὸς συνεσταλμένος ⸂ἐστίν· τὸ λοιπὸν⸃ ἵνα καὶ οἱ ἔχοντες γυναῖκας ὡς μὴ ἔχοντες ὦσιν,
verses.translit: touto de fimi, adelfoi, o kairos synestalmenos estin* to loipon ina kai oi ehontes gynaikas os me ehontes osin,
verses.translation: But this I say, brethren, the time is short: it remaineth, that both they that have wives be as though they had none;

verses.original: καὶ οἱ κλαίοντες ὡς μὴ κλαίοντες, καὶ οἱ χαίροντες ὡς μὴ χαίροντες, καὶ οἱ ἀγοράζοντες ὡς μὴ κατέχοντες,
verses.translit: kai oi klaiontes os me klaiontes, kai oi hairontes os me hairontes, kai oi agorazontes os me katehontes,
verses.translation: And they that weep, as though they wept not; and they that rejoice, as though they rejoiced not; and they that buy, as though they possessed not;

verses.original: καὶ οἱ χρώμενοι ⸂τὸν κόσμον⸃ ὡς μὴ καταχρώμενοι· παράγει γὰρ τὸ σχῆμα τοῦ κόσμου τούτου.
verses.translit: kai oi hromenoi ton kosmon os me katahromenoi* paragei gar to shema tou kosmoy toytoy.
verses.translation: And they that use this world, as not abusing it : for the fashion of this world passeth away.

verses.original: Θέλω δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀμερίμνους εἶναι. ὁ ἄγαμος μεριμνᾷ τὰ τοῦ κυρίου, πῶς ⸀ἀρέσῃ τῷ κυρίῳ·
verses.translit: Thelo de umas amerimnoys einai. o agamos merimna ta tou kyrioy, pos arese to kyrio*
verses.translation: But I would have you without carefulness. He that is unmarried careth for the things that belong to the Lord, how he may please the Lord:

verses.original: ὁ δὲ γαμήσας μεριμνᾷ τὰ τοῦ κόσμου, πῶς ⸀ἀρέσῃ τῇ γυναικί,
verses.translit: o de gamisas merimna ta tou kosmoy, pos arese te gynaiki,
verses.translation: But he that is married careth for the things that are of the world, how he may please his wife.

verses.original: ⸀καὶ μεμέρισται. καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ⸂ἡ ἄγαμος⸃ καὶ ἡ ⸀παρθένος μεριμνᾷ τὰ τοῦ κυρίου, ἵνα ᾖ ἁγία καὶ ⸀τῷ σώματι καὶ ⸁τῷ πνεύματι· ἡ δὲ γαμήσασα μεριμνᾷ τὰ τοῦ κόσμου, πῶς ⸀ἀρέσῃ τῷ ἀνδρί.
verses.translit: kai memeristai. kai e gyne e agamos kai e parthenos merimna ta tou kyrioy, ina e agia kai to somati kai to pneymati* e de gamisasa merimna ta tou kosmoy, pos arese to andri.
verses.translation: There is difference also between a wife and a virgin. The unmarried woman careth for the things of the Lord, that she may be holy both in body and in spirit: but she that is married careth for the things of the world, how she may please her husband.

verses.original: τοῦτο δὲ πρὸς τὸ ὑμῶν αὐτῶν ⸀σύμφορον λέγω, οὐχ ἵνα βρόχον ὑμῖν ἐπιβάλω, ἀλλὰ πρὸς τὸ εὔσχημον καὶ ⸀εὐπάρεδρον τῷ κυρίῳ ἀπερισπάστως.
verses.translit: touto de pros to umon auton symforon lego, ouh ina vrohon umin epivalo, alla pros to eushimon kai euparedron to kyrio aperispastos.
verses.translation: And this I speak for your own profit; not that I may cast a snare upon you, but for that which is comely, and that ye may attend upon the Lord without distraction.

verses.original: Εἰ δέ τις ἀσχημονεῖν ἐπὶ τὴν παρθένον αὐτοῦ νομίζει ἐὰν ᾖ ὑπέρακμος, καὶ οὕτως ὀφείλει γίνεσθαι, ὃ θέλει ποιείτω· οὐχ ἁμαρτάνει· γαμείτωσαν.
verses.translit: Ei de tis ashimonein epi ten parthenon autou nomizei ean e uperakmos, kai outos ofeilei ginesthai, o thelei poieito* ouh amartanei* gameitosan.
verses.translation: But if any man think that he behaveth himself uncomely toward his virgin, if she pass the flower of her age, and need so require, let him do what he will, he sinneth not: let them marry.

verses.original: ὃς δὲ ἕστηκεν ⸂ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ ἑδραῖος⸃ μὴ ἔχων ἀνάγκην, ἐξουσίαν δὲ ἔχει περὶ τοῦ ἰδίου θελήματος, καὶ τοῦτο κέκρικεν ἐν τῇ ⸂ἰδίᾳ καρδίᾳ⸃, ⸀τηρεῖν τὴν ἑαυτοῦ παρθένον, καλῶς ⸀ποιήσει·
verses.translit: os de estiken en te kardia autou edraios me ehon anagkin, exoysian de ehei peri tou idioy thelimatos, kai touto kekriken en te idia kardia, tirein ten eaytou parthenon, kalos poiisei*
verses.translation: Nevertheless he that standeth stedfast in his heart, having no necessity, but hath power over his own will, and hath so decreed in his heart that he will keep his virgin, doeth well.

verses.original: ὥστε καὶ ὁ ⸀γαμίζων ⸂τὴν παρθένον ἑαυτοῦ⸃ καλῶς ποιεῖ, ⸂καὶ ὁ⸃ μὴ ⸁γαμίζων κρεῖσσον ⸀ποιήσει.
verses.translit: oste kai o gamizon ten parthenon eaytou kalos poiei, kai o me gamizon kreisson poiisei.
verses.translation: So then he that giveth her in marriage doeth well; but he that giveth her not in marriage doeth better.

verses.original: Γυνὴ ⸀δέδεται ἐφʼ ὅσον χρόνον ζῇ ὁ ἀνὴρ αὐτῆς· ἐὰν ⸀δὲ κοιμηθῇ ὁ ἀνήρ, ἐλευθέρα ἐστὶν ᾧ θέλει γαμηθῆναι, μόνον ἐν κυρίῳ·
verses.translit: Gyne dedetai ef' oson hronon ze o aner autes* ean de koimithe o anir, eleythera estin o thelei gamithenai, monon en kyrio*
verses.translation: The wife is bound by the law as long as her husband liveth; but if her husband be dead, she is at liberty to be married to whom she will; only in the Lord.

verses.original: μακαριωτέρα δέ ἐστιν ἐὰν οὕτως μείνῃ, κατὰ τὴν ἐμὴν γνώμην, δοκῶ ⸀δὲ κἀγὼ πνεῦμα θεοῦ ἔχειν.
verses.translit: makariotera de estin ean outos meine, kata ten emen gnomin, doko de kago pneuma theou ehein.
verses.translation: But she is happier if she so abide, after my judgment: and I think also that I have the Spirit of God.

verses.original: Περὶ δὲ τῶν εἰδωλοθύτων, οἴδαμεν ὅτι πάντες γνῶσιν ἔχομεν. ἡ γνῶσις φυσιοῖ, ἡ δὲ ἀγάπη οἰκοδομεῖ.
verses.translit: Peri de ton eidolothyton, oidamen oti pantes gnosin ehomen. e gnosis fysioi, e de agapi oikodomei.
verses.translation: Now as touching things offered unto idols, we know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffeth up, but charity edifieth.

verses.original: ⸀εἴ τις δοκεῖ ⸀ἐγνωκέναι τι, ⸀οὔπω ⸀ἔγνω καθὼς δεῖ γνῶναι·
verses.translit: ei tis dokei egnokenai ti, oupo egno kathos dei gnonai*
verses.translation: And if any man think that he knoweth any thing, he knoweth nothing yet as he ought to know.

verses.original: εἰ δέ τις ἀγαπᾷ τὸν θεόν, οὗτος ἔγνωσται ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: ei de tis agapa ton theon, outos egnostai up' autou.
verses.translation: But if any man love God, the same is known of him.

verses.original: Περὶ τῆς βρώσεως οὖν τῶν εἰδωλοθύτων οἴδαμεν ὅτι οὐδὲν εἴδωλον ἐν κόσμῳ, καὶ ὅτι οὐδεὶς ⸀θεὸς εἰ μὴ εἷς.
verses.translit: Peri tes vroseos oun ton eidolothyton oidamen oti ouden eidolon en kosmo, kai oti oudeis theos ei me eis.
verses.translation: As concerning therefore the eating of those things that are offered in sacrifice unto idols, we know that an idol is nothing in the world, and that there is none other God but one.

verses.original: καὶ γὰρ εἴπερ εἰσὶν λεγόμενοι θεοὶ εἴτε ἐν οὐρανῷ εἴτε ἐπὶ γῆς, ὥσπερ εἰσὶν θεοὶ πολλοὶ καὶ κύριοι πολλοί,
verses.translit: kai gar eiper eisin legomenoi theoi eite en ourano eite epi ges, osper eisin theoi polloi kai kyrioi polloi,
verses.translation: For though there be that are called gods, whether in heaven or in earth, (as there be gods many, and lords many,)

verses.original: ἀλλʼ ἡμῖν εἷς θεὸς ὁ πατήρ, ἐξ οὗ τὰ πάντα καὶ ἡμεῖς εἰς αὐτόν, καὶ εἷς κύριος Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, διʼ οὗ τὰ πάντα καὶ ἡμεῖς διʼ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: all' emin eis theos o patir, ex ou ta panta kai emeis eis auton, kai eis kyrios Iisous Hristos, di' ou ta panta kai emeis di' autou.
verses.translation: But to us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him.

verses.original: Ἀλλʼ οὐκ ἐν πᾶσιν ἡ γνῶσις· τινὲς δὲ τῇ ⸀συνηθείᾳ ⸂ἕως ἄρτι τοῦ εἰδώλου⸃ ὡς εἰδωλόθυτον ἐσθίουσιν, καὶ ἡ συνείδησις αὐτῶν ἀσθενὴς οὖσα μολύνεται.
verses.translit: All' ouk en pasin e gnosis* tines de te synitheia eos arti tou eidoloy os eidolothyton esthioysin, kai e syneidisis auton asthenes ousa molynetai.
verses.translation: Howbeit there is not in every man that knowledge: for some with conscience of the idol unto this hour eat it as a thing offered unto an idol; and their conscience being weak is defiled.

verses.original: βρῶμα δὲ ἡμᾶς οὐ ⸀παραστήσει τῷ θεῷ· οὔτε ⸂γὰρ ἐὰν φάγωμεν, περισσεύομεν, οὔτε ἐὰν μὴ φάγωμεν, ὑστερούμεθα⸃.
verses.translit: vroma de emas ou parastisei to theo* oute gar ean fagomen, perisseyomen, oute ean me fagomen, usteroymetha.
verses.translation: But meat commendeth us not to God: for neither, if we eat, are we the better; neither, if we eat not, are we the worse.

verses.original: βλέπετε δὲ μή πως ἡ ἐξουσία ὑμῶν αὕτη πρόσκομμα γένηται τοῖς ⸀ἀσθενέσιν.
verses.translit: vlepete de mi pos e exoysia umon auti proskomma genitai tois asthenesin.
verses.translation: But take heed lest by any means this liberty of yours become a stumblingblock to them that are weak.

verses.original: ἐὰν γάρ τις ἴδῃ σὲ τὸν ἔχοντα γνῶσιν ἐν εἰδωλείῳ κατακείμενον, οὐχὶ ἡ συνείδησις αὐτοῦ ἀσθενοῦς ὄντος οἰκοδομηθήσεται εἰς τὸ τὰ εἰδωλόθυτα ἐσθίειν;
verses.translit: ean gar tis ide se ton ehonta gnosin en eidoleio katakeimenon, ouhi e syneidisis autou asthenous ontos oikodomithisetai eis to ta eidolothyta esthiein;
verses.translation: For if any man see thee which hast knowledge sit at meat in the idol’s temple, shall not the conscience of him which is weak be emboldened to eat those things which are offered to idols;

verses.original: ⸂ἀπόλλυται γὰρ⸃ ὁ ἀσθενῶν ⸀ἐν τῇ σῇ γνώσει, ⸂ὁ ἀδελφὸς⸃ διʼ ὃν Χριστὸς ἀπέθανεν.
verses.translit: apollytai gar o asthenon en te se gnosei, o adelfos di' on Hristos apethanen.
verses.translation: And through thy knowledge shall the weak brother perish, for whom Christ died?

verses.original: οὕτως δὲ ἁμαρτάνοντες εἰς τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς καὶ τύπτοντες αὐτῶν τὴν συνείδησιν ἀσθενοῦσαν εἰς Χριστὸν ἁμαρτάνετε.
verses.translit: outos de amartanontes eis tous adelfous kai typtontes auton ten syneidisin asthenousan eis Hriston amartanete.
verses.translation: But when ye sin so against the brethren, and wound their weak conscience, ye sin against Christ.

verses.original: διόπερ εἰ βρῶμα σκανδαλίζει τὸν ἀδελφόν μου, οὐ μὴ φάγω κρέα εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, ἵνα μὴ τὸν ἀδελφόν μου σκανδαλίσω.
verses.translit: dioper ei vroma skandalizei ton adelfon moy, ou me fago krea eis ton aiona, ina me ton adelfon moy skandaliso.
verses.translation: Wherefore, if meat make my brother to offend, I will eat no flesh while the world standeth, lest I make my brother to offend.

verses.original: Οὐκ εἰμὶ ⸂ἐλεύθερος; οὐκ εἰμὶ ἀπόστολος⸃; οὐχὶ ⸀Ἰησοῦν τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν ἑόρακα; οὐ τὸ ἔργον μου ὑμεῖς ἐστε ἐν κυρίῳ;
verses.translit: Ouk eimi eleytheros; ouk eimi apostolos; ouhi Iisoun ton kyrion emon eoraka; ou to ergon moy umeis este en kyrio;
verses.translation: Am I not an apostle? am I not free? have I not seen Jesus Christ our Lord? are not ye my work in the Lord?

verses.original: εἰ ἄλλοις οὐκ εἰμὶ ἀπόστολος, ἀλλά γε ὑμῖν εἰμι, ἡ γὰρ σφραγίς ⸂μου τῆς⸃ ἀποστολῆς ὑμεῖς ἐστε ἐν κυρίῳ.
verses.translit: ei allois ouk eimi apostolos, alla ge umin eimi, e gar sfragis moy tes apostoles umeis este en kyrio.
verses.translation: If I be not an apostle unto others, yet doubtless I am to you: for the seal of mine apostleship are ye in the Lord.

verses.original: Ἡ ἐμὴ ἀπολογία τοῖς ἐμὲ ἀνακρίνουσίν ⸂ἐστιν αὕτη⸃.
verses.translit: E eme apologia tois eme anakrinoysin estin auti.
verses.translation: Mine answer to them that do examine me is this,

verses.original: μὴ οὐκ ἔχομεν ἐξουσίαν φαγεῖν καὶ ⸀πεῖν;
verses.translit: me ouk ehomen exoysian fagein kai pein;
verses.translation: Have we not power to eat and to drink?

verses.original: μὴ οὐκ ἔχομεν ἐξουσίαν ἀδελφὴν γυναῖκα περιάγειν, ὡς καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ ἀπόστολοι καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ τοῦ κυρίου καὶ Κηφᾶς;
verses.translit: me ouk ehomen exoysian adelfen gynaika periagein, os kai oi loipoi apostoloi kai oi adelfoi tou kyrioy kai Kifas;
verses.translation: Have we not power to lead about a sister, a wife, as well as other apostles, and as the brethren of the Lord, and Cephas?

verses.original: ἢ μόνος ἐγὼ καὶ Βαρναβᾶς οὐκ ἔχομεν ἐξουσίαν ⸀μὴ ἐργάζεσθαι;
verses.translit: e monos ego kai Varnavas ouk ehomen exoysian me ergazesthai;
verses.translation: Or I only and Barnabas, have not we power to forbear working?

verses.original: τίς στρατεύεται ἰδίοις ὀψωνίοις ποτέ; τίς φυτεύει ἀμπελῶνα καὶ ⸂τὸν καρπὸν⸃ αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἐσθίει; ⸀τίς ποιμαίνει ποίμνην καὶ ἐκ τοῦ γάλακτος τῆς ποίμνης οὐκ ἐσθίει;
verses.translit: tis strateyetai idiois opsoniois pote; tis fyteyei ampelona kai ton karpon autou ouk esthiei; tis poimainei poimnin kai ek tou galaktos tes poimnis ouk esthiei;
verses.translation: Who goeth a warfare any time at his own charges? who planteth a vineyard, and eateth not of the fruit thereof? or who feedeth a flock, and eateth not of the milk of the flock?

verses.original: Μὴ κατὰ ἄνθρωπον ταῦτα λαλῶ ἢ ⸂καὶ ὁ νόμος ταῦτα οὐ⸃ λέγει;
verses.translit: Me kata anthropon tauta lalo e kai o nomos tauta ou legei;
verses.translation: Say I these things as a man? or saith not the law the same also?

verses.original: ἐν γὰρ τῷ Μωϋσέως νόμῳ γέγραπται· Οὐ ⸀κημώσεις βοῦν ἀλοῶντα. μὴ τῶν βοῶν μέλει τῷ θεῷ,
verses.translit: en gar to Moyseos nomo gegraptai* Ou kimoseis voun aloonta. me ton voon melei to theo,
verses.translation: For it is written in the law of Moses, Thou shalt not muzzle the mouth of the ox that treadeth out the corn. Doth God take care for oxen?

verses.original: ἢ διʼ ἡμᾶς πάντως λέγει; διʼ ἡμᾶς γὰρ ἐγράφη, ὅτι ⸂ὀφείλει ἐπʼ ἐλπίδι⸃ ὁ ἀροτριῶν ἀροτριᾶν, καὶ ὁ ἀλοῶν ⸂ἐπʼ ἐλπίδι τοῦ μετέχειν⸃.
verses.translit: e di' emas pantos legei; di' emas gar egrafi, oti ofeilei ep' elpidi o arotrion arotrian, kai o aloon ep' elpidi tou metehein.
verses.translation: Or saith he it altogether for our sakes? For our sakes, no doubt, this is written: that he that ploweth should plow in hope; and that he that thresheth in hope should be partaker of his hope.

verses.original: εἰ ἡμεῖς ὑμῖν τὰ πνευματικὰ ἐσπείραμεν, μέγα εἰ ἡμεῖς ὑμῶν τὰ σαρκικὰ θερίσομεν;
verses.translit: ei emeis umin ta pneymatika espeiramen, mega ei emeis umon ta sarkika therisomen;
verses.translation: If we have sown unto you spiritual things, is it a great thing if we shall reap your carnal things?

verses.original: εἰ ἄλλοι τῆς ⸂ὑμῶν ἐξουσίας⸃ μετέχουσιν, οὐ μᾶλλον ἡμεῖς; Ἀλλʼ οὐκ ἐχρησάμεθα τῇ ἐξουσίᾳ ταύτῃ, ἀλλὰ πάντα στέγομεν ἵνα μή ⸂τινα ἐγκοπὴν⸃ δῶμεν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ.
verses.translit: ei alloi tes umon exoysias metehoysin, ou mallon emeis; All' ouk ehrisametha te exoysia tayte, alla panta stegomen ina mi tina egkopen domen to euaggelio tou Hristou.
verses.translation: If others be partakers of this power over you, are not we rather? Nevertheless we have not used this power; but suffer all things, lest we should hinder the gospel of Christ.

verses.original: οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι οἱ τὰ ἱερὰ ἐργαζόμενοι ⸀τὰ ἐκ τοῦ ἱεροῦ ἐσθίουσιν, οἱ τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ ⸀παρεδρεύοντες τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ συμμερίζονται;
verses.translit: ouk oidate oti oi ta iera ergazomenoi ta ek tou ierou esthioysin, oi to thysiastirio paredreyontes to thysiastirio symmerizontai;
verses.translation: Do ye not know that they which minister about holy things live of the things of the temple? and they which wait at the altar are partakers with the altar?

verses.original: οὕτως καὶ ὁ κύριος διέταξεν τοῖς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον καταγγέλλουσιν ἐκ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου ζῆν.
verses.translit: outos kai o kyrios dietaxen tois to euaggelion kataggelloysin ek tou euaggelioy zen.
verses.translation: Even so hath the Lord ordained that they which preach the gospel should live of the gospel.

verses.original: Ἐγὼ δὲ ⸂οὐ κέχρημαι οὐδενὶ⸃ τούτων. οὐκ ἔγραψα δὲ ταῦτα ἵνα οὕτως γένηται ἐν ἐμοί, καλὸν γάρ μοι μᾶλλον ἀποθανεῖν ἤ— τὸ καύχημά μου ⸂οὐδεὶς κενώσει⸃.
verses.translit: Ego de ou kehrimai oudeni toyton. ouk egrapsa de tauta ina outos genitai en emoi, kalon gar moi mallon apothanein e-- to kayhima moy oudeis kenosei.
verses.translation: But I have used none of these things: neither have I written these things, that it should be so done unto me: for it were better for me to die, than that any man should make my glorying void.

verses.original: ἐὰν γὰρ εὐαγγελίζωμαι, οὐκ ἔστιν μοι καύχημα, ἀνάγκη γάρ μοι ἐπίκειται· οὐαὶ ⸀γάρ μοί ἐστιν ἐὰν μὴ ⸀εὐαγγελίσωμαι.
verses.translit: ean gar euaggelizomai, ouk estin moi kayhima, anagki gar moi epikeitai* ouai gar moi estin ean me euaggelisomai.
verses.translation: For though I preach the gospel, I have nothing to glory of: for necessity is laid upon me; yea, woe is unto me, if I preach not the gospel!

verses.original: εἰ γὰρ ἑκὼν τοῦτο πράσσω, μισθὸν ἔχω· εἰ δὲ ἄκων, οἰκονομίαν πεπίστευμαι.
verses.translit: ei gar ekon touto prasso, misthon eho* ei de akon, oikonomian pepisteymai.
verses.translation: For if I do this thing willingly, I have a reward: but if against my will, a dispensation of the gospel is committed unto me.

verses.original: τίς οὖν ⸀μού ἐστιν ὁ μισθός; ἵνα εὐαγγελιζόμενος ἀδάπανον θήσω τὸ ⸀εὐαγγέλιον, εἰς τὸ μὴ καταχρήσασθαι τῇ ἐξουσίᾳ μου ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ.
verses.translit: tis oun moy estin o misthos; ina euaggelizomenos adapanon thiso to euaggelion, eis to me katahrisasthai te exoysia moy en to euaggelio.
verses.translation: What is my reward then? Verily that, when I preach the gospel, I may make the gospel of Christ without charge, that I abuse not my power in the gospel.

verses.original: Ἐλεύθερος γὰρ ὢν ἐκ πάντων πᾶσιν ἐμαυτὸν ἐδούλωσα, ἵνα τοὺς πλείονας κερδήσω·
verses.translit: Eleytheros gar on ek panton pasin emayton edoylosa, ina tous pleionas kerdiso*
verses.translation: For though I be free from all men , yet have I made myself servant unto all, that I might gain the more.

verses.original: καὶ ἐγενόμην τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ὡς Ἰουδαῖος, ἵνα Ἰουδαίους κερδήσω· τοῖς ὑπὸ νόμον ὡς ὑπὸ νόμον, ⸂μὴ ὢν αὐτὸς ὑπὸ νόμον⸃, ἵνα τοὺς ὑπὸ νόμον κερδήσω·
verses.translit: kai egenomin tois Ioydaiois os Ioydaios, ina Ioydaioys kerdiso* tois upo nomon os upo nomon, me on autos upo nomon, ina tous upo nomon kerdiso*
verses.translation: And unto the Jews I became as a Jew, that I might gain the Jews; to them that are under the law, as under the law, that I might gain them that are under the law;

verses.original: τοῖς ἀνόμοις ὡς ἄνομος, μὴ ὢν ἄνομος ⸀θεοῦ ἀλλʼ ἔννομος ⸀Χριστοῦ, ἵνα ⸀κερδάνω ⸀τοὺς ἀνόμους·
verses.translit: tois anomois os anomos, me on anomos theou all' ennomos Hristou, ina kerdano tous anomoys*
verses.translation: To them that are without law, as without law, (being not without law to God, but under the law to Christ,) that I might gain them that are without law.

verses.original: ἐγενόμην τοῖς ⸀ἀσθενέσιν ἀσθενής, ἵνα τοὺς ἀσθενεῖς κερδήσω· τοῖς πᾶσιν ⸀γέγονα πάντα, ἵνα πάντως τινὰς σώσω.
verses.translit: egenomin tois asthenesin asthenis, ina tous astheneis kerdiso* tois pasin gegona panta, ina pantos tinas soso.
verses.translation: To the weak became I as weak, that I might gain the weak: I am made all things to all men , that I might by all means save some.

verses.original: ⸀πάντα δὲ ποιῶ διὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον, ἵνα συγκοινωνὸς αὐτοῦ γένωμαι.
verses.translit: panta de poio dia to euaggelion, ina sygkoinonos autou genomai.
verses.translation: And this I do for the gospel’s sake, that I might be partaker thereof with you .

verses.original: Οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι οἱ ἐν σταδίῳ τρέχοντες πάντες μὲν τρέχουσιν, εἷς δὲ λαμβάνει τὸ βραβεῖον; οὕτως τρέχετε ἵνα καταλάβητε.
verses.translit: Ouk oidate oti oi en stadio trehontes pantes men trehoysin, eis de lamvanei to vraveion; outos trehete ina katalavite.
verses.translation: Know ye not that they which run in a race run all, but one receiveth the prize? So run, that ye may obtain.

verses.original: πᾶς δὲ ὁ ἀγωνιζόμενος πάντα ἐγκρατεύεται, ἐκεῖνοι μὲν οὖν ἵνα φθαρτὸν στέφανον λάβωσιν, ἡμεῖς δὲ ἄφθαρτον.
verses.translit: pas de o agonizomenos panta egkrateyetai, ekeinoi men oun ina ftharton stefanon lavosin, emeis de aftharton.
verses.translation: And every man that striveth for the mastery is temperate in all things. Now they do it to obtain a corruptible crown; but we an incorruptible.

verses.original: ἐγὼ τοίνυν οὕτως τρέχω ὡς οὐκ ἀδήλως, οὕτως πυκτεύω ὡς οὐκ ἀέρα δέρων·
verses.translit: ego toinyn outos treho os ouk adilos, outos pykteyo os ouk aera deron*
verses.translation: I therefore so run, not as uncertainly; so fight I, not as one that beateth the air:

verses.original: ἀλλὰ ὑπωπιάζω μου τὸ σῶμα καὶ δουλαγωγῶ, μή πως ἄλλοις κηρύξας αὐτὸς ἀδόκιμος γένωμαι.
verses.translit: alla upopiazo moy to soma kai doylagogo, mi pos allois kiryxas autos adokimos genomai.
verses.translation: But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway.

verses.original: Οὐ θέλω ⸀γὰρ ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν, ἀδελφοί, ὅτι οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν πάντες ὑπὸ τὴν νεφέλην ἦσαν καὶ πάντες διὰ τῆς θαλάσσης διῆλθον,
verses.translit: Ou thelo gar umas agnoein, adelfoi, oti oi pateres emon pantes upo ten nefelin esan kai pantes dia tes thalassis dielthon,
verses.translation: Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea;

verses.original: καὶ πάντες εἰς τὸν Μωϋσῆν ⸀ἐβαπτίσαντο ἐν τῇ νεφέλῃ καὶ ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ,
verses.translit: kai pantes eis ton Moysen evaptisanto en te nefele kai en te thalasse,
verses.translation: And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea;

verses.original: καὶ πάντες τὸ αὐτὸ ⸂πνευματικὸν βρῶμα⸃ ἔφαγον
verses.translit: kai pantes to auto pneymatikon vroma efagon
verses.translation: And did all eat the same spiritual meat;

verses.original: καὶ πάντες τὸ αὐτὸ ⸂πνευματικὸν ἔπιον πόμα⸃, ἔπινον γὰρ ἐκ πνευματικῆς ἀκολουθούσης πέτρας, ἡ ⸂πέτρα δὲ⸃ ἦν ὁ Χριστός·
verses.translit: kai pantes to auto pneymatikon epion poma, epinon gar ek pneymatikes akoloythoysis petras, e petra de en o Hristos*
verses.translation: And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.

verses.original: ἀλλʼ οὐκ ἐν τοῖς πλείοσιν αὐτῶν ηὐδόκησεν ὁ θεός, κατεστρώθησαν γὰρ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ.
verses.translit: all' ouk en tois pleiosin auton iudokisen o theos, katestrothisan gar en te erimo.
verses.translation: But with many of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the wilderness.

verses.original: Ταῦτα δὲ τύποι ἡμῶν ἐγενήθησαν, εἰς τὸ μὴ εἶναι ἡμᾶς ἐπιθυμητὰς κακῶν, καθὼς κἀκεῖνοι ἐπεθύμησαν.
verses.translit: Tauta de typoi emon egenithisan, eis to me einai emas epithymitas kakon, kathos kakeinoi epethymisan.
verses.translation: Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted.

verses.original: μηδὲ εἰδωλολάτραι γίνεσθε, καθώς τινες αὐτῶν· ὥσπερ γέγραπται· Ἐκάθισεν ὁ λαὸς φαγεῖν καὶ πεῖν, καὶ ἀνέστησαν παίζειν.
verses.translit: mide eidololatrai ginesthe, kathos tines auton* osper gegraptai* Ekathisen o laos fagein kai pein, kai anestisan paizein.
verses.translation: Neither be ye idolaters, as were some of them; as it is written, The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.

verses.original: μηδὲ πορνεύωμεν, καθώς τινες αὐτῶν ἐπόρνευσαν, καὶ ἔπεσαν μιᾷ ἡμέρᾳ εἴκοσι τρεῖς χιλιάδες.
verses.translit: mide porneyomen, kathos tines auton eporneysan, kai epesan mia emera eikosi treis hiliades.
verses.translation: Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed, and fell in one day three and twenty thousand.

verses.original: μηδὲ ἐκπειράζωμεν τὸν ⸀Χριστόν, ⸀καθώς τινες αὐτῶν ἐπείρασαν, καὶ ὑπὸ τῶν ὄφεων ⸀ἀπώλλυντο.
verses.translit: mide ekpeirazomen ton Hriston, kathos tines auton epeirasan, kai upo ton ofeon apollynto.
verses.translation: Neither let us tempt Christ, as some of them also tempted, and were destroyed of serpents.

verses.original: μηδὲ γογγύζετε, ⸀καθάπερ τινὲς αὐτῶν ἐγόγγυσαν, καὶ ἀπώλοντο ὑπὸ τοῦ ὀλοθρευτοῦ.
verses.translit: mide goggyzete, kathaper tines auton egoggysan, kai apolonto upo tou olothreytou.
verses.translation: Neither murmur ye, as some of them also murmured, and were destroyed of the destroyer.

verses.original: ταῦτα ⸀δὲ ⸂τυπικῶς συνέβαινεν⸃ ἐκείνοις, ἐγράφη δὲ πρὸς νουθεσίαν ἡμῶν, εἰς οὓς τὰ τέλη τῶν αἰώνων ⸀κατήντηκεν.
verses.translit: tauta de typikos synevainen ekeinois, egrafi de pros noythesian emon, eis ous ta teli ton aionon katintiken.
verses.translation: Now all these things happened unto them for ensamples: and they are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come.

verses.original: ὥστε ὁ δοκῶν ἑστάναι βλεπέτω μὴ πέσῃ,
verses.translit: oste o dokon estanai vlepeto me pese,
verses.translation: Wherefore let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall.

verses.original: πειρασμὸς ὑμᾶς οὐκ εἴληφεν εἰ μὴ ἀνθρώπινος· πιστὸς δὲ ὁ θεός, ὃς οὐκ ἐάσει ὑμᾶς πειρασθῆναι ὑπὲρ ὃ δύνασθε, ἀλλὰ ποιήσει σὺν τῷ πειρασμῷ καὶ τὴν ἔκβασιν τοῦ ⸀δύνασθαι ὑπενεγκεῖν.
verses.translit: peirasmos umas ouk eilifen ei me anthropinos* pistos de o theos, os ouk easei umas peirasthenai uper o dynasthe, alla poiisei sun to peirasmo kai ten ekvasin tou dynasthai upenegkein.
verses.translation: There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.

verses.original: Διόπερ, ἀγαπητοί μου, φεύγετε ἀπὸ τῆς εἰδωλολατρίας.
verses.translit: Dioper, agapitoi moy, feygete apo tes eidololatrias.
verses.translation: Wherefore, my dearly beloved, flee from idolatry.

verses.original: ὡς φρονίμοις λέγω· κρίνατε ὑμεῖς ὅ φημι.
verses.translit: os fronimois lego* krinate umeis o fimi.
verses.translation: I speak as to wise men; judge ye what I say.

verses.original: τὸ ποτήριον τῆς εὐλογίας ὃ εὐλογοῦμεν, οὐχὶ κοινωνία ⸂ἐστὶν τοῦ αἵματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ⸃; τὸν ἄρτον ὃν κλῶμεν, οὐχὶ κοινωνία τοῦ σώματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐστιν;
verses.translit: to potirion tes eulogias o eulogoumen, ouhi koinonia estin tou aimatos tou Hristou; ton arton on klomen, ouhi koinonia tou somatos tou Hristou estin;
verses.translation: The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ?

verses.original: ὅτι εἷς ἄρτος, ἓν σῶμα οἱ πολλοί ἐσμεν, οἱ γὰρ πάντες ἐκ τοῦ ἑνὸς ἄρτου μετέχομεν.
verses.translit: oti eis artos, en soma oi polloi esmen, oi gar pantes ek tou enos artoy metehomen.
verses.translation: For we being many are one bread, and one body: for we are all partakers of that one bread.

verses.original: βλέπετε τὸν Ἰσραὴλ κατὰ σάρκα· ⸀οὐχ οἱ ἐσθίοντες τὰς θυσίας κοινωνοὶ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου εἰσίν;
verses.translit: vlepete ton Israel kata sarka* ouh oi esthiontes tas thysias koinonoi tou thysiastirioy eisin;
verses.translation: Behold Israel after the flesh: are not they which eat of the sacrifices partakers of the altar?

verses.original: τί οὖν φημι; ὅτι ⸂εἰδωλόθυτόν τί ἐστιν, ἢ ὅτι εἴδωλόν⸃ τί ἐστιν;
verses.translit: ti oun fimi; oti eidolothyton ti estin, e oti eidolon ti estin;
verses.translation: What say I then? that the idol is any thing, or that which is offered in sacrifice to idols is any thing?

verses.original: ἀλλʼ ὅτι ἃ ⸀θύουσιν, δαιμονίοις ⸂καὶ οὐ θεῷ θύουσιν⸃, οὐ θέλω δὲ ὑμᾶς κοινωνοὺς τῶν δαιμονίων γίνεσθαι.
verses.translit: all' oti a thyoysin, daimoniois kai ou theo thyoysin, ou thelo de umas koinonous ton daimonion ginesthai.
verses.translation: But I say , that the things which the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to devils, and not to God: and I would not that ye should have fellowship with devils.

verses.original: οὐ δύνασθε ποτήριον κυρίου πίνειν καὶ ποτήριον δαιμονίων· οὐ δύνασθε τραπέζης κυρίου μετέχειν καὶ τραπέζης δαιμονίων.
verses.translit: ou dynasthe potirion kyrioy pinein kai potirion daimonion* ou dynasthe trapezis kyrioy metehein kai trapezis daimonion.
verses.translation: Ye cannot drink the cup of the Lord, and the cup of devils: ye cannot be partakers of the Lord’s table, and of the table of devils.

verses.original: ἢ παραζηλοῦμεν τὸν κύριον; μὴ ἰσχυρότεροι αὐτοῦ ἐσμεν;
verses.translit: e paraziloumen ton kyrion; me ishyroteroi autou esmen;
verses.translation: Do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? are we stronger than he?

verses.original: ⸀Πάντα ἔξεστιν· ἀλλʼ οὐ πάντα συμφέρει. ⸁πάντα ἔξεστιν· ἀλλʼ οὐ πάντα οἰκοδομεῖ.
verses.translit: Panta exestin* all' ou panta symferei. panta exestin* all' ou panta oikodomei.
verses.translation: All things are lawful for me, but all things are not expedient: all things are lawful for me, but all things edify not.

verses.original: μηδεὶς τὸ ἑαυτοῦ ζητείτω ἀλλὰ τὸ τοῦ ⸀ἑτέρου.
verses.translit: mideis to eaytou ziteito alla to tou eteroy.
verses.translation: Let no man seek his own, but every man another’s wealth .

verses.original: πᾶν τὸ ἐν μακέλλῳ πωλούμενον ἐσθίετε μηδὲν ἀνακρίνοντες διὰ τὴν συνείδησιν,
verses.translit: pan to en makello poloymenon esthiete miden anakrinontes dia ten syneidisin,
verses.translation: Whatsoever is sold in the shambles, that eat, asking no question for conscience sake:

verses.original: τοῦ ⸂κυρίου γὰρ⸃ ἡ γῆ καὶ τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτῆς.
verses.translit: tou kyrioy gar e ge kai to pliroma autes.
verses.translation: For the earth is the Lord’s, and the fulness thereof.

verses.original: ⸀εἴ τις καλεῖ ὑμᾶς τῶν ἀπίστων καὶ θέλετε πορεύεσθαι, πᾶν τὸ παρατιθέμενον ὑμῖν ἐσθίετε μηδὲν ἀνακρίνοντες διὰ τὴν συνείδησιν·
verses.translit: ei tis kalei umas ton apiston kai thelete poreyesthai, pan to paratithemenon umin esthiete miden anakrinontes dia ten syneidisin*
verses.translation: If any of them that believe not bid you to a feast , and ye be disposed to go; whatsoever is set before you, eat, asking no question for conscience sake.

verses.original: ἐὰν δέ τις ὑμῖν εἴπῃ· Τοῦτο ⸀ἱερόθυτόν ἐστιν, μὴ ἐσθίετε διʼ ἐκεῖνον τὸν μηνύσαντα καὶ τὴν ⸀συνείδησιν·
verses.translit: ean de tis umin eipe* Touto ierothyton estin, me esthiete di' ekeinon ton minysanta kai ten syneidisin*
verses.translation: But if any man say unto you, This is offered in sacrifice unto idols, eat not for his sake that shewed it, and for conscience sake: for the earth is the Lord’s, and the fulness thereof:

verses.original: συνείδησιν δὲ λέγω οὐχὶ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ἀλλὰ τὴν τοῦ ἑτέρου· ἱνατί γὰρ ἡ ἐλευθερία μου κρίνεται ὑπὸ ἄλλης συνειδήσεως;
verses.translit: syneidisin de lego ouhi ten eaytou alla ten tou eteroy* inati gar e eleytheria moy krinetai upo allis syneidiseos;
verses.translation: Conscience, I say, not thine own, but of the other: for why is my liberty judged of another man’s conscience?

verses.original: εἰ ἐγὼ χάριτι μετέχω, τί βλασφημοῦμαι ὑπὲρ οὗ ἐγὼ εὐχαριστῶ;
verses.translit: ei ego hariti meteho, ti vlasfimoumai uper ou ego euharisto;
verses.translation: For if I by grace be a partaker, why am I evil spoken of for that for which I give thanks?

verses.original: Εἴτε οὖν ἐσθίετε εἴτε πίνετε εἴτε τι ποιεῖτε, πάντα εἰς δόξαν θεοῦ ποιεῖτε.
verses.translit: Eite oun esthiete eite pinete eite ti poieite, panta eis doxan theou poieite.
verses.translation: Whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God.

verses.original: ἀπρόσκοποι ⸂καὶ Ἰουδαίοις γίνεσθε⸃ καὶ Ἕλλησιν καὶ τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ,
verses.translit: aproskopoi kai Ioydaiois ginesthe kai Ellisin kai te ekklisia tou theou,
verses.translation: Give none offence, neither to the Jews, nor to the Gentiles, nor to the church of God:

verses.original: καθὼς κἀγὼ πάντα πᾶσιν ἀρέσκω, μὴ ζητῶν τὸ ἐμαυτοῦ ⸀σύμφορον ἀλλὰ τὸ τῶν πολλῶν, ἵνα σωθῶσιν.
verses.translit: kathos kago panta pasin aresko, me ziton to emaytou symforon alla to ton pollon, ina sothosin.
verses.translation: Even as I please all men in all things , not seeking mine own profit, but the profit of many, that they may be saved.

verses.original: μιμηταί μου γίνεσθε, καθὼς κἀγὼ Χριστοῦ.
verses.translit: mimitai moy ginesthe, kathos kago Hristou.
verses.translation: Be ye followers of me, even as I also am of Christ.

verses.original: Ἐπαινῶ δὲ ⸀ὑμᾶς ὅτι πάντα μου μέμνησθε καὶ καθὼς παρέδωκα ὑμῖν τὰς παραδόσεις κατέχετε.
verses.translit: Epaino de umas oti panta moy memnisthe kai kathos paredoka umin tas paradoseis katehete.
verses.translation: Now I praise you, brethren, that ye remember me in all things, and keep the ordinances, as I delivered them to you.

verses.original: θέλω δὲ ὑμᾶς εἰδέναι ὅτι παντὸς ἀνδρὸς ἡ κεφαλὴ ὁ Χριστός ἐστιν, κεφαλὴ δὲ γυναικὸς ὁ ἀνήρ, κεφαλὴ δὲ ⸀τοῦ Χριστοῦ ὁ θεός.
verses.translit: thelo de umas eidenai oti pantos andros e kefale o Hristos estin, kefale de gynaikos o anir, kefale de tou Hristou o theos.
verses.translation: But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God.

verses.original: πᾶς ἀνὴρ προσευχόμενος ἢ προφητεύων κατὰ κεφαλῆς ἔχων καταισχύνει τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ·
verses.translit: pas aner proseyhomenos e profiteyon kata kefales ehon kataishynei ten kefalen autou*
verses.translation: Every man praying or prophesying, having his head covered, dishonoureth his head.

verses.original: πᾶσα δὲ γυνὴ προσευχομένη ἢ προφητεύουσα ἀκατακαλύπτῳ τῇ κεφαλῇ καταισχύνει τὴν κεφαλὴν ⸀αὐτῆς, ἓν γάρ ἐστιν καὶ τὸ αὐτὸ τῇ ἐξυρημένῃ.
verses.translit: pasa de gyne proseyhomeni e profiteyoysa akatakalypto te kefale kataishynei ten kefalen autes, en gar estin kai to auto te exyrimene.
verses.translation: But every woman that prayeth or prophesieth with her head uncovered dishonoureth her head: for that is even all one as if she were shaven.

verses.original: εἰ γὰρ οὐ κατακαλύπτεται γυνή, καὶ κειράσθω· εἰ δὲ αἰσχρὸν γυναικὶ τὸ κείρασθαι ἢ ξυρᾶσθαι, κατακαλυπτέσθω.
verses.translit: ei gar ou katakalyptetai gyni, kai keirastho* ei de aishron gynaiki to keirasthai e xyrasthai, katakalyptestho.
verses.translation: For if the woman be not covered, let her also be shorn: but if it be a shame for a woman to be shorn or shaven, let her be covered.

verses.original: ἀνὴρ μὲν γὰρ οὐκ ὀφείλει κατακαλύπτεσθαι τὴν κεφαλήν, εἰκὼν καὶ δόξα θεοῦ ὑπάρχων· ⸀ἡ γυνὴ δὲ δόξα ἀνδρός ἐστιν.
verses.translit: aner men gar ouk ofeilei katakalyptesthai ten kefalin, eikon kai doxa theou uparhon* e gyne de doxa andros estin.
verses.translation: For a man indeed ought not to cover his head, forasmuch as he is the image and glory of God: but the woman is the glory of the man.

verses.original: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν ἀνὴρ ἐκ γυναικός, ἀλλὰ γυνὴ ἐξ ἀνδρός·
verses.translit: ou gar estin aner ek gynaikos, alla gyne ex andros*
verses.translation: For the man is not of the woman; but the woman of the man.

verses.original: καὶ γὰρ οὐκ ἐκτίσθη ἀνὴρ διὰ τὴν γυναῖκα, ἀλλὰ γυνὴ διὰ τὸν ἄνδρα.
verses.translit: kai gar ouk ektisthi aner dia ten gynaika, alla gyne dia ton andra.
verses.translation: Neither was the man created for the woman; but the woman for the man.

verses.original: διὰ τοῦτο ὀφείλει ἡ γυνὴ ἐξουσίαν ἔχειν ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς διὰ τοὺς ἀγγέλους.
verses.translit: dia touto ofeilei e gyne exoysian ehein epi tes kefales dia tous aggeloys.
verses.translation: For this cause ought the woman to have power on her head because of the angels.

verses.original: πλὴν οὔτε ⸂γυνὴ χωρὶς ἀνδρὸς οὔτε ἀνὴρ χωρὶς γυναικὸς⸃ ἐν κυρίῳ·
verses.translit: plen oute gyne horis andros oute aner horis gynaikos en kyrio*
verses.translation: Nevertheless neither is the man without the woman, neither the woman without the man, in the Lord.

verses.original: ὥσπερ γὰρ ἡ γυνὴ ἐκ τοῦ ἀνδρός, οὕτως καὶ ὁ ἀνὴρ διὰ τῆς γυναικός· τὰ δὲ πάντα ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: osper gar e gyne ek tou andros, outos kai o aner dia tes gynaikos* ta de panta ek tou theou.
verses.translation: For as the woman is of the man, even so is the man also by the woman; but all things of God.

verses.original: ἐν ὑμῖν αὐτοῖς κρίνατε· πρέπον ἐστὶν γυναῖκα ἀκατακάλυπτον τῷ θεῷ προσεύχεσθαι;
verses.translit: en umin autois krinate* prepon estin gynaika akatakalypton to theo proseyhesthai;
verses.translation: Judge in yourselves: is it comely that a woman pray unto God uncovered?

verses.original: ⸀οὐδὲ ⸂ἡ φύσις αὐτὴ⸃ διδάσκει ὑμᾶς ὅτι ἀνὴρ μὲν ἐὰν κομᾷ, ἀτιμία αὐτῷ ἐστιν,
verses.translit: oude e fysis aute didaskei umas oti aner men ean koma, atimia auto estin,
verses.translation: Doth not even nature itself teach you, that, if a man have long hair, it is a shame unto him?

verses.original: γυνὴ δὲ ἐὰν κομᾷ, δόξα αὐτῇ ἐστιν; ὅτι ἡ κόμη ἀντὶ περιβολαίου ⸀δέδοται.
verses.translit: gyne de ean koma, doxa aute estin; oti e komi anti perivolaioy dedotai.
verses.translation: But if a woman have long hair, it is a glory to her: for her hair is given her for a covering.

verses.original: εἰ δέ τις δοκεῖ φιλόνεικος εἶναι, ἡμεῖς τοιαύτην συνήθειαν οὐκ ἔχομεν, οὐδὲ αἱ ἐκκλησίαι τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: ei de tis dokei filoneikos einai, emeis toiaytin synitheian ouk ehomen, oude ai ekklisiai tou theou.
verses.translation: But if any man seem to be contentious, we have no such custom, neither the churches of God.

verses.original: Τοῦτο δὲ ⸂παραγγέλλων οὐκ ἐπαινῶ⸃ ὅτι οὐκ εἰς τὸ κρεῖσσον ἀλλὰ εἰς τὸ ἧσσον συνέρχεσθε.
verses.translit: Touto de paraggellon ouk epaino oti ouk eis to kreisson alla eis to esson synerhesthe.
verses.translation: Now in this that I declare unto you I praise you not, that ye come together not for the better, but for the worse.

verses.original: πρῶτον μὲν γὰρ συνερχομένων ὑμῶν ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ ἀκούω σχίσματα ἐν ὑμῖν ὑπάρχειν, καὶ μέρος τι πιστεύω.
verses.translit: proton men gar synerhomenon umon en ekklisia akoyo shismata en umin uparhein, kai meros ti pisteyo.
verses.translation: For first of all, when ye come together in the church, I hear that there be divisions among you; and I partly believe it.

verses.original: δεῖ γὰρ καὶ αἱρέσεις ἐν ὑμῖν εἶναι, ἵνα ⸀καὶ οἱ δόκιμοι φανεροὶ γένωνται ἐν ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: dei gar kai aireseis en umin einai, ina kai oi dokimoi faneroi genontai en umin.
verses.translation: For there must be also heresies among you, that they which are approved may be made manifest among you.

verses.original: συνερχομένων οὖν ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ οὐκ ἔστιν κυριακὸν δεῖπνον φαγεῖν,
verses.translit: synerhomenon oun umon epi to auto ouk estin kyriakon deipnon fagein,
verses.translation: When ye come together therefore into one place, this is not to eat the Lord’s supper.

verses.original: ἕκαστος γὰρ τὸ ἴδιον δεῖπνον προλαμβάνει ἐν τῷ φαγεῖν, καὶ ὃς μὲν πεινᾷ, ὃς δὲ μεθύει.
verses.translit: ekastos gar to idion deipnon prolamvanei en to fagein, kai os men peina, os de methyei.
verses.translation: For in eating every one taketh before other his own supper: and one is hungry, and another is drunken.

verses.original: μὴ γὰρ οἰκίας οὐκ ἔχετε εἰς τὸ ἐσθίειν καὶ πίνειν; ἢ τῆς ἐκκλησίας τοῦ θεοῦ καταφρονεῖτε, καὶ καταισχύνετε τοὺς μὴ ἔχοντας; τί ⸂εἴπω ὑμῖν⸃; ἐπαινέσω ὑμᾶς; ἐν τούτῳ οὐκ ἐπαινῶ.
verses.translit: me gar oikias ouk ehete eis to esthiein kai pinein; e tes ekklisias tou theou katafroneite, kai kataishynete tous me ehontas; ti eipo umin; epaineso umas; en toyto ouk epaino.
verses.translation: What? have ye not houses to eat and to drink in? or despise ye the church of God, and shame them that have not? What shall I say to you? shall I praise you in this? I praise you not.

verses.original: Ἐγὼ γὰρ παρέλαβον ἀπὸ τοῦ κυρίου, ὃ καὶ παρέδωκα ὑμῖν, ὅτι ὁ κύριος Ἰησοῦς ἐν τῇ νυκτὶ ᾗ ⸀παρεδίδετο ἔλαβεν ἄρτον
verses.translit: Ego gar parelavon apo tou kyrioy, o kai paredoka umin, oti o kyrios Iisous en te nykti e paredideto elaven arton
verses.translation: For I have received of the Lord that which also I delivered unto you, That the Lord Jesus the same night in which he was betrayed took bread:

verses.original: καὶ εὐχαριστήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ ⸀εἶπεν· Τοῦτό μού ἐστιν τὸ σῶμα τὸ ὑπὲρ ⸀ὑμῶν· τοῦτο ποιεῖτε εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν ἀνάμνησιν.
verses.translit: kai euharistisas eklasen kai eipen* Touto moy estin to soma to uper umon* touto poieite eis ten emen anamnisin.
verses.translation: And when he had given thanks, he brake it , and said, Take, eat: this is my body, which is broken for you: this do in remembrance of me.

verses.original: ὡσαύτως καὶ τὸ ποτήριον μετὰ τὸ δειπνῆσαι, λέγων· Τοῦτο τὸ ποτήριον ἡ καινὴ διαθήκη ἐστὶν ἐν τῷ ἐμῷ αἵματι· τοῦτο ποιεῖτε, ὁσάκις ⸀ἐὰν πίνητε, εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν ἀνάμνησιν.
verses.translit: osaytos kai to potirion meta to deipnesai, legon* Touto to potirion e kaine diathiki estin en to emo aimati* touto poieite, osakis ean pinite, eis ten emen anamnisin.
verses.translation: After the same manner also he took the cup, when he had supped, saying, This cup is the new testament in my blood: this do ye, as oft as ye drink it , in remembrance of me.

verses.original: ὁσάκις γὰρ ⸀ἐὰν ἐσθίητε τὸν ἄρτον τοῦτον καὶ τὸ ⸀ποτήριον πίνητε, τὸν θάνατον τοῦ κυρίου καταγγέλλετε, ἄχρι ⸀οὗ ἔλθῃ.
verses.translit: osakis gar ean esthiite ton arton touton kai to potirion pinite, ton thanaton tou kyrioy kataggellete, ahri ou elthe.
verses.translation: For as often as ye eat this bread, and drink this cup, ye do shew the Lord’s death till he come.

verses.original: Ὥστε ὃς ἂν ἐσθίῃ τὸν ⸀ἄρτον ἢ πίνῃ τὸ ποτήριον τοῦ κυρίου ⸀ἀναξίως, ἔνοχος ἔσται τοῦ σώματος καὶ τοῦ αἵματος τοῦ κυρίου.
verses.translit: Oste os an esthie ton arton e pine to potirion tou kyrioy anaxios, enohos estai tou somatos kai tou aimatos tou kyrioy.
verses.translation: Wherefore whosoever shall eat this bread, and drink this cup of the Lord, unworthily, shall be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord.

verses.original: δοκιμαζέτω δὲ ἄνθρωπος ἑαυτόν, καὶ οὕτως ἐκ τοῦ ἄρτου ἐσθιέτω καὶ ἐκ τοῦ ποτηρίου πινέτω·
verses.translit: dokimazeto de anthropos eayton, kai outos ek tou artoy esthieto kai ek tou potirioy pineto*
verses.translation: But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of that bread, and drink of that cup.

verses.original: ὁ γὰρ ἐσθίων καὶ ⸀πίνων κρίμα ἑαυτῷ ἐσθίει καὶ πίνει μὴ διακρίνων τὸ ⸀σῶμα.
verses.translit: o gar esthion kai pinon krima eayto esthiei kai pinei me diakrinon to soma.
verses.translation: For he that eateth and drinketh unworthily, eateth and drinketh damnation to himself, not discerning the Lord’s body.

verses.original: διὰ τοῦτο ἐν ὑμῖν πολλοὶ ἀσθενεῖς καὶ ἄρρωστοι καὶ κοιμῶνται ἱκανοί.
verses.translit: dia touto en umin polloi astheneis kai arrostoi kai koimontai ikanoi.
verses.translation: For this cause many are weak and sickly among you, and many sleep.

verses.original: εἰ ⸀δὲ ἑαυτοὺς διεκρίνομεν, οὐκ ἂν ἐκρινόμεθα·
verses.translit: ei de eaytous diekrinomen, ouk an ekrinometha*
verses.translation: For if we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged.

verses.original: κρινόμενοι δὲ ⸀ὑπὸ κυρίου παιδευόμεθα, ἵνα μὴ σὺν τῷ κόσμῳ κατακριθῶμεν.
verses.translit: krinomenoi de upo kyrioy paideyometha, ina me sun to kosmo katakrithomen.
verses.translation: But when we are judged, we are chastened of the Lord, that we should not be condemned with the world.

verses.original: Ὥστε, ἀδελφοί μου, συνερχόμενοι εἰς τὸ φαγεῖν ἀλλήλους ἐκδέχεσθε.
verses.translit: Oste, adelfoi moy, synerhomenoi eis to fagein alliloys ekdehesthe.
verses.translation: Wherefore, my brethren, when ye come together to eat, tarry one for another.

verses.original: ⸀εἴ τις πεινᾷ, ἐν οἴκῳ ἐσθιέτω, ἵνα μὴ εἰς κρίμα συνέρχησθε. Τὰ δὲ λοιπὰ ὡς ἂν ἔλθω διατάξομαι.
verses.translit: ei tis peina, en oiko esthieto, ina me eis krima synerhisthe. Ta de loipa os an eltho diataxomai.
verses.translation: And if any man hunger, let him eat at home; that ye come not together unto condemnation. And the rest will I set in order when I come.

verses.original: Περὶ δὲ τῶν πνευματικῶν, ἀδελφοί, οὐ θέλω ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν.
verses.translit: Peri de ton pneymatikon, adelfoi, ou thelo umas agnoein.
verses.translation: Now concerning spiritual gifts , brethren, I would not have you ignorant.

verses.original: οἴδατε ὅτι ὅτε ἔθνη ἦτε πρὸς τὰ εἴδωλα τὰ ἄφωνα ὡς ἂν ἤγεσθε ἀπαγόμενοι.
verses.translit: oidate oti ote ethni ete pros ta eidola ta afona os an egesthe apagomenoi.
verses.translation: Ye know that ye were Gentiles, carried away unto these dumb idols, even as ye were led.

verses.original: διὸ γνωρίζω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδεὶς ἐν πνεύματι θεοῦ λαλῶν λέγει· Ἀνάθεμα ⸀Ἰησοῦς, καὶ οὐδεὶς δύναται εἰπεῖν· ⸂Κύριος Ἰησοῦς⸃ εἰ μὴ ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ.
verses.translit: dio gnorizo umin oti oudeis en pneymati theou lalon legei* Anathema Iisous, kai oudeis dynatai eipein* Kyrios Iisous ei me en pneymati agio.
verses.translation: Wherefore I give you to understand, that no man speaking by the Spirit of God calleth Jesus accursed: and that no man can say that Jesus is the Lord, but by the Holy Ghost.

verses.original: Διαιρέσεις δὲ χαρισμάτων εἰσίν, τὸ δὲ αὐτὸ πνεῦμα·
verses.translit: Diaireseis de harismaton eisin, to de auto pneuma*
verses.translation: Now there are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit.

verses.original: καὶ διαιρέσεις διακονιῶν εἰσιν, καὶ ὁ αὐτὸς κύριος·
verses.translit: kai diaireseis diakonion eisin, kai o autos kyrios*
verses.translation: And there are differences of administrations, but the same Lord.

verses.original: καὶ διαιρέσεις ἐνεργημάτων εἰσίν, ⸂ὁ δὲ⸃ ⸀αὐτὸς θεός, ὁ ἐνεργῶν τὰ πάντα ἐν πᾶσιν.
verses.translit: kai diaireseis energimaton eisin, o de autos theos, o energon ta panta en pasin.
verses.translation: And there are diversities of operations, but it is the same God which worketh all in all.

verses.original: ἑκάστῳ δὲ δίδοται ἡ φανέρωσις τοῦ πνεύματος πρὸς τὸ συμφέρον.
verses.translit: ekasto de didotai e fanerosis tou pneymatos pros to symferon.
verses.translation: But the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal.

verses.original: ᾧ μὲν γὰρ διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος δίδοται λόγος σοφίας, ἄλλῳ δὲ λόγος γνώσεως κατὰ τὸ αὐτὸ πνεῦμα,
verses.translit: o men gar dia tou pneymatos didotai logos sofias, allo de logos gnoseos kata to auto pneuma,
verses.translation: For to one is given by the Spirit the word of wisdom; to another the word of knowledge by the same Spirit;

verses.original: ⸀ἑτέρῳ πίστις ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ πνεύματι, ⸀ἄλλῳ χαρίσματα ἰαμάτων ἐν τῷ ⸀ἑνὶ πνεύματι,
verses.translit: etero pistis en to auto pneymati, allo harismata iamaton en to eni pneymati,
verses.translation: To another faith by the same Spirit; to another the gifts of healing by the same Spirit;

verses.original: ⸀ἄλλῳ ἐνεργήματα δυνάμεων, ⸁ἄλλῳ προφητεία, ⸀1ἄλλῳ διακρίσεις πνευμάτων, ⸀ἑτέρῳ γένη γλωσσῶν, ⸀2ἄλλῳ ἑρμηνεία γλωσσῶν·
verses.translit: allo energimata dynameon, allo profiteia, 1allo diakriseis pneymaton, etero geni glosson, 2allo ermineia glosson*
verses.translation: To another the working of miracles; to another prophecy; to another discerning of spirits; to another divers kinds of tongues; to another the interpretation of tongues:

verses.original: πάντα δὲ ταῦτα ἐνεργεῖ τὸ ἓν καὶ τὸ αὐτὸ πνεῦμα, διαιροῦν ἰδίᾳ ἑκάστῳ καθὼς βούλεται.
verses.translit: panta de tauta energei to en kai to auto pneuma, diairoun idia ekasto kathos voyletai.
verses.translation: But all these worketh that one and the selfsame Spirit, dividing to every man severally as he will.

verses.original: Καθάπερ γὰρ τὸ σῶμα ἕν ἐστιν καὶ μέλη ⸂πολλὰ ἔχει⸃, πάντα δὲ τὰ μέλη τοῦ ⸀σώματος πολλὰ ὄντα ἕν ἐστιν σῶμα, οὕτως καὶ ὁ Χριστός·
verses.translit: Kathaper gar to soma en estin kai meli polla ehei, panta de ta meli tou somatos polla onta en estin soma, outos kai o Hristos*
verses.translation: For as the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body: so also is Christ.

verses.original: καὶ γὰρ ἐν ἑνὶ πνεύματι ἡμεῖς πάντες εἰς ἓν σῶμα ἐβαπτίσθημεν, εἴτε Ἰουδαῖοι εἴτε Ἕλληνες, εἴτε δοῦλοι εἴτε ἐλεύθεροι, καὶ ⸀πάντες ἓν πνεῦμα ἐποτίσθημεν.
verses.translit: kai gar en eni pneymati emeis pantes eis en soma evaptisthimen, eite Ioydaioi eite Ellines, eite douloi eite eleytheroi, kai pantes en pneuma epotisthimen.
verses.translation: For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body, whether we be Jews or Gentiles, whether we be bond or free; and have been all made to drink into one Spirit.

verses.original: Καὶ γὰρ τὸ σῶμα οὐκ ἔστιν ἓν μέλος ἀλλὰ πολλά.
verses.translit: Kai gar to soma ouk estin en melos alla polla.
verses.translation: For the body is not one member, but many.

verses.original: ἐὰν εἴπῃ ὁ πούς· Ὅτι οὐκ εἰμὶ χείρ, οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐκ τοῦ σώματος, οὐ παρὰ τοῦτο οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ τοῦ σώματος;
verses.translit: ean eipe o poys* Oti ouk eimi heir, ouk eimi ek tou somatos, ou para touto ouk estin ek tou somatos;
verses.translation: If the foot shall say, Because I am not the hand, I am not of the body; is it therefore not of the body?

verses.original: καὶ ἐὰν εἴπῃ τὸ οὖς· Ὅτι οὐκ εἰμὶ ὀφθαλμός, οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐκ τοῦ σώματος, οὐ παρὰ τοῦτο οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ τοῦ σώματος·
verses.translit: kai ean eipe to ous* Oti ouk eimi ofthalmos, ouk eimi ek tou somatos, ou para touto ouk estin ek tou somatos*
verses.translation: And if the ear shall say, Because I am not the eye, I am not of the body; is it therefore not of the body?

verses.original: εἰ ὅλον τὸ σῶμα ὀφθαλμός, ποῦ ἡ ἀκοή; εἰ ὅλον ἀκοή, ποῦ ἡ ὄσφρησις;
verses.translit: ei olon to soma ofthalmos, pou e akoi; ei olon akoi, pou e osfrisis;
verses.translation: If the whole body were an eye, where were the hearing? If the whole were hearing, where were the smelling?

verses.original: ⸀νυνὶ δὲ ὁ θεὸς ἔθετο τὰ μέλη, ἓν ἕκαστον αὐτῶν, ἐν τῷ σώματι καθὼς ἠθέλησεν.
verses.translit: nyni de o theos etheto ta meli, en ekaston auton, en to somati kathos ethelisen.
verses.translation: But now hath God set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him.

verses.original: εἰ δὲ ἦν τὰ πάντα ἓν μέλος, ποῦ τὸ σῶμα;
verses.translit: ei de en ta panta en melos, pou to soma;
verses.translation: And if they were all one member, where were the body?

verses.original: νῦν δὲ πολλὰ ⸀μὲν μέλη, ἓν δὲ σῶμα.
verses.translit: nun de polla men meli, en de soma.
verses.translation: But now are they many members, yet but one body.

verses.original: οὐ δύναται δὲ ὁ ὀφθαλμὸς εἰπεῖν τῇ χειρί· Χρείαν σου οὐκ ἔχω, ἢ πάλιν ἡ κεφαλὴ τοῖς ποσίν· Χρείαν ὑμῶν οὐκ ἔχω·
verses.translit: ou dynatai de o ofthalmos eipein te heiri* Hreian soy ouk eho, e palin e kefale tois posin* Hreian umon ouk eho*
verses.translation: And the eye cannot say unto the hand, I have no need of thee: nor again the head to the feet, I have no need of you.

verses.original: ἀλλὰ πολλῷ μᾶλλον τὰ δοκοῦντα μέλη τοῦ σώματος ἀσθενέστερα ὑπάρχειν ἀναγκαῖά ἐστιν,
verses.translit: alla pollo mallon ta dokounta meli tou somatos asthenestera uparhein anagkaia estin,
verses.translation: Nay, much more those members of the body, which seem to be more feeble, are necessary:

verses.original: καὶ ἃ δοκοῦμεν ἀτιμότερα εἶναι τοῦ σώματος, τούτοις τιμὴν περισσοτέραν περιτίθεμεν, καὶ τὰ ἀσχήμονα ἡμῶν εὐσχημοσύνην περισσοτέραν ἔχει,
verses.translit: kai a dokoumen atimotera einai tou somatos, toytois timen perissoteran peritithemen, kai ta ashimona emon eushimosynin perissoteran ehei,
verses.translation: And those members of the body, which we think to be less honourable, upon these we bestow more abundant honour; and our uncomely parts have more abundant comeliness.

verses.original: τὰ δὲ εὐσχήμονα ἡμῶν οὐ χρείαν ⸀ἔχει. ἀλλὰ ὁ θεὸς συνεκέρασεν τὸ σῶμα, τῷ ⸀ὑστεροῦντι περισσοτέραν δοὺς τιμήν,
verses.translit: ta de eushimona emon ou hreian ehei. alla o theos synekerasen to soma, to usterounti perissoteran dous timin,
verses.translation: For our comely parts have no need: but God hath tempered the body together, having given more abundant honour to that part which lacked:

verses.original: ἵνα μὴ ᾖ ⸀σχίσμα ἐν τῷ σώματι, ἀλλὰ τὸ αὐτὸ ὑπὲρ ἀλλήλων μεριμνῶσι τὰ μέλη.
verses.translit: ina me e shisma en to somati, alla to auto uper allilon merimnosi ta meli.
verses.translation: That there should be no schism in the body; but that the members should have the same care one for another.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀εἴτε πάσχει ἓν μέλος, συμπάσχει πάντα τὰ μέλη· εἴτε δοξάζεται ⸀μέλος, συγχαίρει πάντα τὰ μέλη.
verses.translit: kai eite pashei en melos, sympashei panta ta meli* eite doxazetai melos, syghairei panta ta meli.
verses.translation: And whether one member suffer, all the members suffer with it; or one member be honoured, all the members rejoice with it.

verses.original: Ὑμεῖς δέ ἐστε σῶμα Χριστοῦ καὶ μέλη ἐκ μέρους.
verses.translit: Umeis de este soma Hristou kai meli ek meroys.
verses.translation: Now ye are the body of Christ, and members in particular.

verses.original: καὶ οὓς μὲν ἔθετο ὁ θεὸς ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ πρῶτον ἀποστόλους, δεύτερον προφήτας, τρίτον διδασκάλους, ἔπειτα δυνάμεις, ⸀ἔπειτα χαρίσματα ἰαμάτων, ἀντιλήμψεις, κυβερνήσεις, γένη γλωσσῶν.
verses.translit: kai ous men etheto o theos en te ekklisia proton apostoloys, deyteron profitas, triton didaskaloys, epeita dynameis, epeita harismata iamaton, antilimpseis, kyverniseis, geni glosson.
verses.translation: And God hath set some in the church, first apostles, secondarily prophets, thirdly teachers, after that miracles, then gifts of healings, helps, governments, diversities of tongues.

verses.original: μὴ πάντες ἀπόστολοι; μὴ πάντες προφῆται; μὴ πάντες διδάσκαλοι; μὴ πάντες δυνάμεις;
verses.translit: me pantes apostoloi; me pantes profetai; me pantes didaskaloi; me pantes dynameis;
verses.translation: Are all apostles? are all prophets? are all teachers? are all workers of miracles?

verses.original: μὴ πάντες χαρίσματα ἔχουσιν ἰαμάτων; μὴ πάντες γλώσσαις λαλοῦσιν; μὴ πάντες διερμηνεύουσιν;
verses.translit: me pantes harismata ehoysin iamaton; me pantes glossais lalousin; me pantes diermineyoysin;
verses.translation: Have all the gifts of healing? do all speak with tongues? do all interpret?

verses.original: ζηλοῦτε δὲ τὰ χαρίσματα τὰ ⸀μείζονα. καὶ ἔτι καθʼ ὑπερβολὴν ὁδὸν ὑμῖν δείκνυμι.
verses.translit: ziloute de ta harismata ta meizona. kai eti kath' upervolen odon umin deiknymi.
verses.translation: But covet earnestly the best gifts: and yet shew I unto you a more excellent way.

verses.original: Ἐὰν ταῖς γλώσσαις τῶν ἀνθρώπων λαλῶ καὶ τῶν ἀγγέλων, ἀγάπην δὲ μὴ ἔχω, γέγονα χαλκὸς ἠχῶν ἢ κύμβαλον ἀλαλάζον.
verses.translit: Ean tais glossais ton anthropon lalo kai ton aggelon, agapin de me eho, gegona halkos ehon e kymvalon alalazon.
verses.translation: Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal.

verses.original: ⸂καὶ ἐὰν⸃ ἔχω προφητείαν καὶ εἰδῶ τὰ μυστήρια πάντα καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γνῶσιν, ⸄καὶ ἐὰν⸅ ἔχω πᾶσαν τὴν πίστιν ὥστε ὄρη ⸀μεθιστάναι, ἀγάπην δὲ μὴ ἔχω, οὐθέν εἰμι.
verses.translit: kai ean eho profiteian kai eido ta mystiria panta kai pasan ten gnosin, kai ean eho pasan ten pistin oste ori methistanai, agapin de me eho, outhen eimi.
verses.translation: And though I have the gift of prophecy, and understand all mysteries, and all knowledge; and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, and have not charity, I am nothing.

verses.original: ⸂καὶ ἐὰν⸃ ψωμίσω πάντα τὰ ὑπάρχοντά μου, ⸄καὶ ἐὰν⸅ παραδῶ τὸ σῶμά μου, ἵνα ⸀καυθήσομαι, ἀγάπην δὲ μὴ ἔχω, οὐδὲν ὠφελοῦμαι.
verses.translit: kai ean psomiso panta ta uparhonta moy, kai ean parado to soma moy, ina kaythisomai, agapin de me eho, ouden ofeloumai.
verses.translation: And though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor , and though I give my body to be burned, and have not charity, it profiteth me nothing.

verses.original: Ἡ ἀγάπη μακροθυμεῖ, χρηστεύεται ἡ ἀγάπη, οὐ ζηλοῖ ⸂ἡ ἀγάπη⸃, οὐ περπερεύεται, οὐ φυσιοῦται,
verses.translit: E agapi makrothymei, hristeyetai e agapi, ou ziloi e agapi, ou perpereyetai, ou fysioutai,
verses.translation: Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up,

verses.original: οὐκ ἀσχημονεῖ, οὐ ζητεῖ τὰ ἑαυτῆς, οὐ παροξύνεται, οὐ λογίζεται τὸ κακόν,
verses.translit: ouk ashimonei, ou zitei ta eaytes, ou paroxynetai, ou logizetai to kakon,
verses.translation: Doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil;

verses.original: οὐ χαίρει ἐπὶ τῇ ἀδικίᾳ, συγχαίρει δὲ τῇ ἀληθείᾳ·
verses.translit: ou hairei epi te adikia, syghairei de te alitheia*
verses.translation: Rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth;

verses.original: πάντα στέγει, πάντα πιστεύει, πάντα ἐλπίζει, πάντα ὑπομένει.
verses.translit: panta stegei, panta pisteyei, panta elpizei, panta upomenei.
verses.translation: Beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things.

verses.original: Ἡ ἀγάπη οὐδέποτε ⸀πίπτει. εἴτε δὲ προφητεῖαι, καταργηθήσονται· εἴτε γλῶσσαι, παύσονται· εἴτε γνῶσις, καταργηθήσεται.
verses.translit: E agapi oudepote piptei. eite de profiteiai, katargithisontai* eite glossai, paysontai* eite gnosis, katargithisetai.
verses.translation: Charity never faileth: but whether there be prophecies, they shall fail; whether there be tongues, they shall cease; whether there be knowledge, it shall vanish away.

verses.original: ἐκ μέρους ⸀γὰρ γινώσκομεν καὶ ἐκ μέρους προφητεύομεν·
verses.translit: ek meroys gar ginoskomen kai ek meroys profiteyomen*
verses.translation: For we know in part, and we prophesy in part.

verses.original: ὅταν δὲ ἔλθῃ τὸ τέλειον, ⸀τὸ ἐκ μέρους καταργηθήσεται.
verses.translit: otan de elthe to teleion, to ek meroys katargithisetai.
verses.translation: But when that which is perfect is come, then that which is in part shall be done away.

verses.original: ὅτε ἤμην νήπιος, ⸂ἐλάλουν ὡς νήπιος, ἐφρόνουν ὡς νήπιος, ἐλογιζόμην ὡς νήπιος⸃· ⸀ὅτε γέγονα ἀνήρ, κατήργηκα τὰ τοῦ νηπίου.
verses.translit: ote emin nipios, elaloyn os nipios, efronoyn os nipios, elogizomin os nipios* ote gegona anir, katirgika ta tou nipioy.
verses.translation: When I was a child, I spake as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child: but when I became a man, I put away childish things.

verses.original: βλέπομεν γὰρ ἄρτι διʼ ἐσόπτρου ἐν αἰνίγματι, τότε δὲ πρόσωπον πρὸς πρόσωπον· ἄρτι γινώσκω ἐκ μέρους, τότε δὲ ἐπιγνώσομαι καθὼς καὶ ἐπεγνώσθην.
verses.translit: vlepomen gar arti di' esoptroy en ainigmati, tote de prosopon pros prosopon* arti ginosko ek meroys, tote de epignosomai kathos kai epegnosthin.
verses.translation: For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known.

verses.original: νυνὶ δὲ μένει πίστις, ἐλπίς, ἀγάπη· τὰ τρία ταῦτα, μείζων δὲ τούτων ἡ ἀγάπη.
verses.translit: nyni de menei pistis, elpis, agapi* ta tria tauta, meizon de toyton e agapi.
verses.translation: And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.

verses.original: Διώκετε τὴν ἀγάπην, ζηλοῦτε δὲ τὰ πνευματικά, μᾶλλον δὲ ἵνα προφητεύητε.
verses.translit: Diokete ten agapin, ziloute de ta pneymatika, mallon de ina profiteyite.
verses.translation: Follow after charity, and desire spiritual gifts , but rather that ye may prophesy.

verses.original: ὁ γὰρ λαλῶν γλώσσῃ οὐκ ἀνθρώποις λαλεῖ ⸀ἀλλὰ θεῷ, οὐδεὶς γὰρ ἀκούει, πνεύματι δὲ λαλεῖ μυστήρια·
verses.translit: o gar lalon glosse ouk anthropois lalei alla theo, oudeis gar akoyei, pneymati de lalei mystiria*
verses.translation: For he that speaketh in an unknown tongue speaketh not unto men, but unto God: for no man understandeth him ; howbeit in the spirit he speaketh mysteries.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ προφητεύων ἀνθρώποις λαλεῖ οἰκοδομὴν καὶ παράκλησιν καὶ παραμυθίαν.
verses.translit: o de profiteyon anthropois lalei oikodomen kai paraklisin kai paramythian.
verses.translation: But he that prophesieth speaketh unto men to edification, and exhortation, and comfort.

verses.original: ὁ λαλῶν γλώσσῃ ἑαυτὸν οἰκοδομεῖ· ὁ δὲ προφητεύων ἐκκλησίαν οἰκοδομεῖ.
verses.translit: o lalon glosse eayton oikodomei* o de profiteyon ekklisian oikodomei.
verses.translation: He that speaketh in an unknown tongue edifieth himself; but he that prophesieth edifieth the church.

verses.original: θέλω δὲ πάντας ὑμᾶς λαλεῖν γλώσσαις, μᾶλλον δὲ ἵνα προφητεύητε· μείζων ⸀δὲ ὁ προφητεύων ἢ ὁ λαλῶν γλώσσαις, ἐκτὸς εἰ μὴ ⸀διερμηνεύῃ, ἵνα ἡ ἐκκλησία οἰκοδομὴν λάβῃ.
verses.translit: thelo de pantas umas lalein glossais, mallon de ina profiteyite* meizon de o profiteyon e o lalon glossais, ektos ei me diermineye, ina e ekklisia oikodomen lave.
verses.translation: I would that ye all spake with tongues, but rather that ye prophesied: for greater is he that prophesieth than he that speaketh with tongues, except he interpret, that the church may receive edifying.

verses.original: ⸀Νῦν δέ, ἀδελφοί, ἐὰν ἔλθω πρὸς ὑμᾶς γλώσσαις λαλῶν, τί ὑμᾶς ὠφελήσω, ἐὰν μὴ ὑμῖν λαλήσω ἢ ἐν ἀποκαλύψει ἢ ἐν γνώσει ἢ ἐν προφητείᾳ ἢ ἐν διδαχῇ;
verses.translit: Nun de, adelfoi, ean eltho pros umas glossais lalon, ti umas ofeliso, ean me umin laliso e en apokalypsei e en gnosei e en profiteia e en didahe;
verses.translation: Now, brethren, if I come unto you speaking with tongues, what shall I profit you, except I shall speak to you either by revelation, or by knowledge, or by prophesying, or by doctrine?

verses.original: ὅμως τὰ ἄψυχα φωνὴν διδόντα, εἴτε αὐλὸς εἴτε κιθάρα, ἐὰν διαστολὴν τοῖς φθόγγοις μὴ ⸀δῷ, πῶς γνωσθήσεται τὸ αὐλούμενον ἢ τὸ κιθαριζόμενον;
verses.translit: omos ta apsyha fonen didonta, eite aulos eite kithara, ean diastolen tois fthoggois me do, pos gnosthisetai to auloymenon e to kitharizomenon;
verses.translation: And even things without life giving sound, whether pipe or harp, except they give a distinction in the sounds, how shall it be known what is piped or harped?

verses.original: καὶ γὰρ ἐὰν ἄδηλον ⸂φωνὴν σάλπιγξ⸃ δῷ, τίς παρασκευάσεται εἰς πόλεμον;
verses.translit: kai gar ean adilon fonen salpigx do, tis paraskeyasetai eis polemon;
verses.translation: For if the trumpet give an uncertain sound, who shall prepare himself to the battle?

verses.original: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς διὰ τῆς γλώσσης ἐὰν μὴ εὔσημον λόγον δῶτε, πῶς γνωσθήσεται τὸ λαλούμενον; ἔσεσθε γὰρ εἰς ἀέρα λαλοῦντες.
verses.translit: outos kai umeis dia tes glossis ean me eusimon logon dote, pos gnosthisetai to laloymenon; esesthe gar eis aera lalountes.
verses.translation: So likewise ye, except ye utter by the tongue words easy to be understood, how shall it be known what is spoken? for ye shall speak into the air.

verses.original: τοσαῦτα εἰ τύχοι γένη φωνῶν ⸀εἰσιν ἐν κόσμῳ, καὶ ⸀οὐδὲν ἄφωνον·
verses.translit: tosauta ei tyhoi geni fonon eisin en kosmo, kai ouden afonon*
verses.translation: There are, it may be, so many kinds of voices in the world, and none of them is without signification.

verses.original: ἐὰν οὖν μὴ εἰδῶ τὴν δύναμιν τῆς φωνῆς, ἔσομαι τῷ λαλοῦντι βάρβαρος καὶ ὁ λαλῶν ἐν ἐμοὶ βάρβαρος.
verses.translit: ean oun me eido ten dynamin tes fones, esomai to lalounti varvaros kai o lalon en emoi varvaros.
verses.translation: Therefore if I know not the meaning of the voice, I shall be unto him that speaketh a barbarian, and he that speaketh shall be a barbarian unto me.

verses.original: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς, ἐπεὶ ζηλωταί ἐστε πνευμάτων, πρὸς τὴν οἰκοδομὴν τῆς ἐκκλησίας ζητεῖτε ἵνα περισσεύητε.
verses.translit: outos kai umeis, epei zilotai este pneymaton, pros ten oikodomen tes ekklisias ziteite ina perisseyite.
verses.translation: Even so ye, forasmuch as ye are zealous of spiritual gifts , seek that ye may excel to the edifying of the church.

verses.original: ⸀Διὸ ὁ λαλῶν γλώσσῃ προσευχέσθω ἵνα διερμηνεύῃ.
verses.translit: Dio o lalon glosse proseyhestho ina diermineye.
verses.translation: Wherefore let him that speaketh in an unknown tongue pray that he may interpret.

verses.original: ἐὰν γὰρ προσεύχωμαι γλώσσῃ, τὸ πνεῦμά μου προσεύχεται, ὁ δὲ νοῦς μου ἄκαρπός ἐστιν.
verses.translit: ean gar proseyhomai glosse, to pneuma moy proseyhetai, o de nous moy akarpos estin.
verses.translation: For if I pray in an unknown tongue, my spirit prayeth, but my understanding is unfruitful.

verses.original: τί οὖν ἐστιν; προσεύξομαι τῷ πνεύματι, προσεύξομαι δὲ καὶ τῷ νοΐ· ψαλῶ τῷ πνεύματι, ψαλῶ δὲ καὶ τῷ νοΐ·
verses.translit: ti oun estin; proseyxomai to pneymati, proseyxomai de kai to noI* psalo to pneymati, psalo de kai to noI*
verses.translation: What is it then? I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray with the understanding also: I will sing with the spirit, and I will sing with the understanding also.

verses.original: ἐπεὶ ἐὰν ⸀εὐλογῇς ⸀πνεύματι, ὁ ἀναπληρῶν τὸν τόπον τοῦ ἰδιώτου πῶς ἐρεῖ τὸ Ἀμήν ἐπὶ τῇ σῇ εὐχαριστίᾳ; ἐπειδὴ τί λέγεις οὐκ οἶδεν·
verses.translit: epei ean euloges pneymati, o anapliron ton topon tou idiotoy pos erei to Amin epi te se euharistia; epeide ti legeis ouk oiden*
verses.translation: Else when thou shalt bless with the spirit, how shall he that occupieth the room of the unlearned say Amen at thy giving of thanks, seeing he understandeth not what thou sayest?

verses.original: σὺ μὲν γὰρ καλῶς εὐχαριστεῖς, ἀλλʼ ὁ ἕτερος οὐκ οἰκοδομεῖται.
verses.translit: su men gar kalos euharisteis, all' o eteros ouk oikodomeitai.
verses.translation: For thou verily givest thanks well, but the other is not edified.

verses.original: εὐχαριστῶ τῷ ⸀θεῷ, πάντων ὑμῶν μᾶλλον ⸀γλώσσαις ⸀λαλῶ·
verses.translit: euharisto to theo, panton umon mallon glossais lalo*
verses.translation: I thank my God, I speak with tongues more than ye all:

verses.original: ἀλλὰ ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ θέλω πέντε λόγους ⸂τῷ νοΐ⸃ μου λαλῆσαι, ἵνα καὶ ἄλλους κατηχήσω, ἢ μυρίους λόγους ἐν γλώσσῃ.
verses.translit: alla en ekklisia thelo pente logoys to noI moy lalesai, ina kai alloys katihiso, e myrioys logoys en glosse.
verses.translation: Yet in the church I had rather speak five words with my understanding, that by my voice I might teach others also, than ten thousand words in an unknown tongue.

verses.original: Ἀδελφοί, μὴ παιδία γίνεσθε ταῖς φρεσίν, ἀλλὰ τῇ κακίᾳ νηπιάζετε, ταῖς δὲ φρεσὶν τέλειοι γίνεσθε.
verses.translit: Adelfoi, me paidia ginesthe tais fresin, alla te kakia nipiazete, tais de fresin teleioi ginesthe.
verses.translation: Brethren, be not children in understanding: howbeit in malice be ye children, but in understanding be men.

verses.original: ἐν τῷ νόμῳ γέγραπται ὅτι Ἐν ἑτερογλώσσοις καὶ ἐν χείλεσιν ⸀ἑτέρων λαλήσω τῷ λαῷ τούτῳ, καὶ οὐδʼ οὕτως εἰσακούσονταί μου, λέγει κύριος.
verses.translit: en to nomo gegraptai oti En eteroglossois kai en heilesin eteron laliso to lao toyto, kai oud' outos eisakoysontai moy, legei kyrios.
verses.translation: In the law it is written, With men of other tongues and other lips will I speak unto this people; and yet for all that will they not hear me, saith the Lord.

verses.original: ὥστε αἱ γλῶσσαι εἰς σημεῖόν εἰσιν οὐ τοῖς πιστεύουσιν ἀλλὰ τοῖς ἀπίστοις, ἡ δὲ προφητεία οὐ τοῖς ἀπίστοις ἀλλὰ τοῖς πιστεύουσιν.
verses.translit: oste ai glossai eis simeion eisin ou tois pisteyoysin alla tois apistois, e de profiteia ou tois apistois alla tois pisteyoysin.
verses.translation: Wherefore tongues are for a sign, not to them that believe, but to them that believe not: but prophesying serveth not for them that believe not, but for them which believe.

verses.original: ἐὰν οὖν συνέλθῃ ἡ ἐκκλησία ὅλη ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ καὶ πάντες ⸂λαλῶσιν γλώσσαις⸃, εἰσέλθωσιν δὲ ἰδιῶται ἢ ἄπιστοι, οὐκ ἐροῦσιν ὅτι μαίνεσθε;
verses.translit: ean oun synelthe e ekklisia oli epi to auto kai pantes lalosin glossais, eiselthosin de idiotai e apistoi, ouk erousin oti mainesthe;
verses.translation: If therefore the whole church be come together into one place, and all speak with tongues, and there come in those that are unlearned, or unbelievers, will they not say that ye are mad?

verses.original: ἐὰν δὲ πάντες προφητεύωσιν, εἰσέλθῃ δέ τις ἄπιστος ἢ ἰδιώτης, ἐλέγχεται ὑπὸ πάντων, ἀνακρίνεται ὑπὸ πάντων,
verses.translit: ean de pantes profiteyosin, eiselthe de tis apistos e idiotis, eleghetai upo panton, anakrinetai upo panton,
verses.translation: But if all prophesy, and there come in one that believeth not, or one unlearned, he is convinced of all, he is judged of all:

verses.original: ⸀τὰ κρυπτὰ τῆς καρδίας αὐτοῦ φανερὰ γίνεται, καὶ οὕτως πεσὼν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον προσκυνήσει τῷ θεῷ, ἀπαγγέλλων ὅτι ⸂Ὄντως ὁ θεὸς⸃ ἐν ὑμῖν ἐστιν.
verses.translit: ta krypta tes kardias autou fanera ginetai, kai outos peson epi prosopon proskynisei to theo, apaggellon oti Ontos o theos en umin estin.
verses.translation: And thus are the secrets of his heart made manifest; and so falling down on his face he will worship God, and report that God is in you of a truth.

verses.original: Τί οὖν ἐστιν, ἀδελφοί; ὅταν συνέρχησθε, ⸀ἕκαστος ψαλμὸν ἔχει, διδαχὴν ἔχει, ⸂ἀποκάλυψιν ἔχει, γλῶσσαν⸃ ἔχει, ἑρμηνείαν ἔχει· πάντα πρὸς οἰκοδομὴν γινέσθω.
verses.translit: Ti oun estin, adelfoi; otan synerhisthe, ekastos psalmon ehei, didahen ehei, apokalypsin ehei, glossan ehei, ermineian ehei* panta pros oikodomen ginestho.
verses.translation: How is it then, brethren? when ye come together, every one of you hath a psalm, hath a doctrine, hath a tongue, hath a revelation, hath an interpretation. Let all things be done unto edifying.

verses.original: εἴτε γλώσσῃ τις λαλεῖ, κατὰ δύο ἢ τὸ πλεῖστον τρεῖς, καὶ ἀνὰ μέρος, καὶ εἷς διερμηνευέτω·
verses.translit: eite glosse tis lalei, kata dyo e to pleiston treis, kai ana meros, kai eis diermineyeto*
verses.translation: If any man speak in an unknown tongue, let it be by two, or at the most by three, and that by course; and let one interpret.

verses.original: ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ᾖ ⸀διερμηνευτής, σιγάτω ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ, ἑαυτῷ δὲ λαλείτω καὶ τῷ θεῷ.
verses.translit: ean de me e diermineytis, sigato en ekklisia, eayto de laleito kai to theo.
verses.translation: But if there be no interpreter, let him keep silence in the church; and let him speak to himself, and to God.

verses.original: προφῆται δὲ δύο ἢ τρεῖς λαλείτωσαν, καὶ οἱ ἄλλοι διακρινέτωσαν·
verses.translit: profetai de dyo e treis laleitosan, kai oi alloi diakrinetosan*
verses.translation: Let the prophets speak two or three, and let the other judge.

verses.original: ἐὰν δὲ ἄλλῳ ἀποκαλυφθῇ καθημένῳ, ὁ πρῶτος σιγάτω.
verses.translit: ean de allo apokalyfthe kathimeno, o protos sigato.
verses.translation: If any thing be revealed to another that sitteth by, let the first hold his peace.

verses.original: δύνασθε γὰρ καθʼ ἕνα πάντες προφητεύειν, ἵνα πάντες μανθάνωσιν καὶ πάντες παρακαλῶνται
verses.translit: dynasthe gar kath' ena pantes profiteyein, ina pantes manthanosin kai pantes parakalontai
verses.translation: For ye may all prophesy one by one, that all may learn, and all may be comforted.

verses.original: (καὶ πνεύματα προφητῶν προφήταις ὑποτάσσεται,
verses.translit: (kai pneymata profiton profitais upotassetai,
verses.translation: And the spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets.

verses.original: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν ἀκαταστασίας ὁ θεὸς ἀλλὰ εἰρήνης), ὡς ἐν πάσαις ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τῶν ἁγίων.
verses.translit: ou gar estin akatastasias o theos alla eirinis), os en pasais tais ekklisiais ton agion.
verses.translation: For God is not the author of confusion, but of peace, as in all churches of the saints.

verses.original: Αἱ ⸀γυναῖκες ἐν ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις σιγάτωσαν, οὐ γὰρ ⸀ἐπιτρέπεται αὐταῖς λαλεῖν· ἀλλὰ ⸀ὑποτασσέσθωσαν, καθὼς καὶ ὁ νόμος λέγει.
verses.translit: Ai gynaikes en tais ekklisiais sigatosan, ou gar epitrepetai autais lalein* alla upotassesthosan, kathos kai o nomos legei.
verses.translation: Let your women keep silence in the churches: for it is not permitted unto them to speak; but they are commanded to be under obedience, as also saith the law.

verses.original: εἰ δέ τι ⸀μαθεῖν θέλουσιν, ἐν οἴκῳ τοὺς ἰδίους ἄνδρας ἐπερωτάτωσαν, αἰσχρὸν γάρ ἐστιν γυναικὶ ⸂λαλεῖν ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ⸃.
verses.translit: ei de ti mathein theloysin, en oiko tous idioys andras eperotatosan, aishron gar estin gynaiki lalein en ekklisia.
verses.translation: And if they will learn any thing, let them ask their husbands at home: for it is a shame for women to speak in the church.

verses.original: ἢ ἀφʼ ὑμῶν ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ ἐξῆλθεν, ἢ εἰς ὑμᾶς μόνους κατήντησεν;
verses.translit: e af' umon o logos tou theou exelthen, e eis umas monoys katintisen;
verses.translation: What? came the word of God out from you? or came it unto you only?

verses.original: Εἴ τις δοκεῖ προφήτης εἶναι ἢ πνευματικός, ἐπιγινωσκέτω ἃ γράφω ὑμῖν ὅτι κυρίου ⸀ἐστίν·
verses.translit: Ei tis dokei profitis einai e pneymatikos, epiginosketo a grafo umin oti kyrioy estin*
verses.translation: If any man think himself to be a prophet, or spiritual, let him acknowledge that the things that I write unto you are the commandments of the Lord.

verses.original: εἰ δέ τις ἀγνοεῖ, ⸀ἀγνοεῖται.
verses.translit: ei de tis agnoei, agnoeitai.
verses.translation: But if any man be ignorant, let him be ignorant.

verses.original: ὥστε, ἀδελφοί ⸀μου, ζηλοῦτε τὸ προφητεύειν, καὶ τὸ λαλεῖν ⸂μὴ κωλύετε γλώσσαις⸃·
verses.translit: oste, adelfoi moy, ziloute to profiteyein, kai to lalein me kolyete glossais*
verses.translation: Wherefore, brethren, covet to prophesy, and forbid not to speak with tongues.

verses.original: πάντα ⸀δὲ εὐσχημόνως καὶ κατὰ τάξιν γινέσθω.
verses.translit: panta de eushimonos kai kata taxin ginestho.
verses.translation: Let all things be done decently and in order.
