verses.original: Γνωρίζω δὲ ὑμῖν, ἀδελφοί, τὸ εὐαγγέλιον ὃ εὐηγγελισάμην ὑμῖν, ὃ καὶ παρελάβετε, ἐν ᾧ καὶ ἑστήκατε,
verses.translit: Gnorizo de umin, adelfoi, to euaggelion o euiggelisamin umin, o kai parelavete, en o kai estikate,
verses.translation: Moreover, brethren, I declare unto you the gospel which I preached unto you, which also ye have received, and wherein ye stand;

verses.original: διʼ οὗ καὶ σῴζεσθε, τίνι λόγῳ εὐηγγελισάμην ὑμῖν, εἰ κατέχετε, ἐκτὸς εἰ μὴ εἰκῇ ἐπιστεύσατε.
verses.translit: di' ou kai sozesthe, tini logo euiggelisamin umin, ei katehete, ektos ei me eike episteysate.
verses.translation: By which also ye are saved, if ye keep in memory what I preached unto you, unless ye have believed in vain.

verses.original: Παρέδωκα γὰρ ὑμῖν ἐν πρώτοις, ὃ καὶ παρέλαβον, ὅτι Χριστὸς ἀπέθανεν ὑπὲρ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν κατὰ τὰς γραφάς,
verses.translit: Paredoka gar umin en protois, o kai parelavon, oti Hristos apethanen uper ton amartion emon kata tas grafas,
verses.translation: For I delivered unto you first of all that which I also received, how that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures;

verses.original: καὶ ὅτι ἐτάφη, καὶ ὅτι ἐγήγερται τῇ ⸂ἡμέρᾳ τῇ τρίτῃ⸃ κατὰ τὰς γραφάς,
verses.translit: kai oti etafi, kai oti egigertai te emera te trite kata tas grafas,
verses.translation: And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures:

verses.original: καὶ ὅτι ὤφθη Κηφᾷ, εἶτα τοῖς δώδεκα·
verses.translit: kai oti ofthi Kifa, eita tois dodeka*
verses.translation: And that he was seen of Cephas, then of the twelve:

verses.original: ἔπειτα ὤφθη ἐπάνω πεντακοσίοις ἀδελφοῖς ἐφάπαξ, ἐξ ὧν οἱ ⸀πλείονες μένουσιν ἕως ἄρτι, τινὲς ⸀δὲ ἐκοιμήθησαν·
verses.translit: epeita ofthi epano pentakosiois adelfois efapax, ex on oi pleiones menoysin eos arti, tines de ekoimithisan*
verses.translation: After that, he was seen of above five hundred brethren at once; of whom the greater part remain unto this present, but some are fallen asleep.

verses.original: ἔπειτα ὤφθη Ἰακώβῳ, εἶτα τοῖς ἀποστόλοις πᾶσιν·
verses.translit: epeita ofthi Iakovo, eita tois apostolois pasin*
verses.translation: After that, he was seen of James; then of all the apostles.

verses.original: ἔσχατον δὲ πάντων ὡσπερεὶ τῷ ἐκτρώματι ὤφθη κἀμοί.
verses.translit: eshaton de panton osperei to ektromati ofthi kamoi.
verses.translation: And last of all he was seen of me also, as of one born out of due time.

verses.original: ἐγὼ γάρ εἰμι ὁ ἐλάχιστος τῶν ἀποστόλων, ὃς οὐκ εἰμὶ ἱκανὸς καλεῖσθαι ἀπόστολος, διότι ἐδίωξα τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τοῦ θεοῦ·
verses.translit: ego gar eimi o elahistos ton apostolon, os ouk eimi ikanos kaleisthai apostolos, dioti edioxa ten ekklisian tou theou*
verses.translation: For I am the least of the apostles, that am not meet to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.

verses.original: χάριτι δὲ θεοῦ εἰμι ὅ εἰμι, καὶ ἡ χάρις αὐτοῦ ἡ εἰς ἐμὲ οὐ κενὴ ἐγενήθη, ἀλλὰ περισσότερον αὐτῶν πάντων ἐκοπίασα, οὐκ ἐγὼ δὲ ἀλλὰ ἡ χάρις τοῦ θεοῦ ⸀ἡ σὺν ἐμοί.
verses.translit: hariti de theou eimi o eimi, kai e haris autou e eis eme ou kene egenithi, alla perissoteron auton panton ekopiasa, ouk ego de alla e haris tou theou e sun emoi.
verses.translation: But by the grace of God I am what I am: and his grace which was bestowed upon me was not in vain; but I laboured more abundantly than they all: yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me.

verses.original: εἴτε οὖν ἐγὼ εἴτε ἐκεῖνοι, οὕτως κηρύσσομεν καὶ οὕτως ἐπιστεύσατε.
verses.translit: eite oun ego eite ekeinoi, outos kiryssomen kai outos episteysate.
verses.translation: Therefore whether it were I or they, so we preach, and so ye believed.

verses.original: Εἰ δὲ Χριστὸς κηρύσσεται ὅτι ἐκ νεκρῶν ἐγήγερται, πῶς λέγουσιν ⸂ἐν ὑμῖν τινες⸃ ὅτι ἀνάστασις νεκρῶν οὐκ ἔστιν;
verses.translit: Ei de Hristos kiryssetai oti ek nekron egigertai, pos legoysin en umin tines oti anastasis nekron ouk estin;
verses.translation: Now if Christ be preached that he rose from the dead, how say some among you that there is no resurrection of the dead?

verses.original: εἰ δὲ ἀνάστασις νεκρῶν οὐκ ἔστιν, οὐδὲ Χριστὸς ἐγήγερται·
verses.translit: ei de anastasis nekron ouk estin, oude Hristos egigertai*
verses.translation: But if there be no resurrection of the dead, then is Christ not risen:

verses.original: εἰ δὲ Χριστὸς οὐκ ἐγήγερται, κενὸν ⸀ἄρα τὸ κήρυγμα ἡμῶν, ⸀κενὴ καὶ ἡ πίστις ⸀ὑμῶν,
verses.translit: ei de Hristos ouk egigertai, kenon ara to kirygma emon, kene kai e pistis umon,
verses.translation: And if Christ be not risen, then is our preaching vain, and your faith is also vain.

verses.original: εὑρισκόμεθα δὲ καὶ ψευδομάρτυρες τοῦ θεοῦ, ὅτι ἐμαρτυρήσαμεν κατὰ τοῦ θεοῦ ὅτι ἤγειρεν τὸν Χριστόν, ὃν οὐκ ἤγειρεν εἴπερ ἄρα νεκροὶ οὐκ ἐγείρονται.
verses.translit: euriskometha de kai pseydomartyres tou theou, oti emartyrisamen kata tou theou oti egeiren ton Hriston, on ouk egeiren eiper ara nekroi ouk egeirontai.
verses.translation: Yea, and we are found false witnesses of God; because we have testified of God that he raised up Christ: whom he raised not up, if so be that the dead rise not.

verses.original: εἰ γὰρ νεκροὶ οὐκ ἐγείρονται, οὐδὲ Χριστὸς ἐγήγερται·
verses.translit: ei gar nekroi ouk egeirontai, oude Hristos egigertai*
verses.translation: For if the dead rise not, then is not Christ raised:

verses.original: εἰ δὲ Χριστὸς οὐκ ἐγήγερται, ματαία ἡ πίστις ⸀ὑμῶν, ἔτι ἐστὲ ἐν ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις ὑμῶν.
verses.translit: ei de Hristos ouk egigertai, mataia e pistis umon, eti este en tais amartiais umon.
verses.translation: And if Christ be not raised, your faith is vain; ye are yet in your sins.

verses.original: ἄρα καὶ οἱ κοιμηθέντες ἐν Χριστῷ ἀπώλοντο.
verses.translit: ara kai oi koimithentes en Hristo apolonto.
verses.translation: Then they also which are fallen asleep in Christ are perished.

verses.original: εἰ ἐν τῇ ζωῇ ταύτῃ ⸂ἐν Χριστῷ ἠλπικότες ἐσμὲν⸃ μόνον, ἐλεεινότεροι πάντων ἀνθρώπων ἐσμέν.
verses.translit: ei en te zoe tayte en Hristo elpikotes esmen monon, eleeinoteroi panton anthropon esmen.
verses.translation: If in this life only we have hope in Christ, we are of all men most miserable.

verses.original: Νυνὶ δὲ Χριστὸς ἐγήγερται ἐκ νεκρῶν, ἀπαρχὴ τῶν ⸀κεκοιμημένων.
verses.translit: Nyni de Hristos egigertai ek nekron, aparhe ton kekoimimenon.
verses.translation: But now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept.

verses.original: ἐπειδὴ γὰρ διʼ ἀνθρώπου ⸀θάνατος, καὶ διʼ ἀνθρώπου ἀνάστασις νεκρῶν·
verses.translit: epeide gar di' anthropoy thanatos, kai di' anthropoy anastasis nekron*
verses.translation: For since by man came death, by man came also the resurrection of the dead.

verses.original: ὥσπερ γὰρ ἐν τῷ Ἀδὰμ πάντες ἀποθνῄσκουσιν, οὕτως καὶ ἐν τῷ Χριστῷ πάντες ζῳοποιηθήσονται.
verses.translit: osper gar en to Adam pantes apothneskoysin, outos kai en to Hristo pantes zoopoiithisontai.
verses.translation: For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive.

verses.original: ἕκαστος δὲ ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ τάγματι· ἀπαρχὴ Χριστός, ἔπειτα οἱ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ αὐτοῦ·
verses.translit: ekastos de en to idio tagmati* aparhe Hristos, epeita oi tou Hristou en te paroysia autou*
verses.translation: But every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ’s at his coming.

verses.original: εἶτα τὸ τέλος, ὅταν ⸀παραδιδῷ τὴν βασιλείαν τῷ θεῷ καὶ πατρί, ὅταν καταργήσῃ πᾶσαν ἀρχὴν καὶ πᾶσαν ἐξουσίαν καὶ δύναμιν,
verses.translit: eita to telos, otan paradido ten vasileian to theo kai patri, otan katargise pasan arhen kai pasan exoysian kai dynamin,
verses.translation: Then cometh the end, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God, even the Father; when he shall have put down all rule and all authority and power.

verses.original: δεῖ γὰρ αὐτὸν βασιλεύειν ἄχρι ⸀οὗ θῇ πάντας τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑπὸ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: dei gar auton vasileyein ahri ou the pantas tous ehthrous upo tous podas autou.
verses.translation: For he must reign, till he hath put all enemies under his feet.

verses.original: ἔσχατος ἐχθρὸς καταργεῖται ὁ θάνατος,
verses.translit: eshatos ehthros katargeitai o thanatos,
verses.translation: The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death.

verses.original: πάντα γὰρ ὑπέταξεν ὑπὸ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ. ὅταν δὲ εἴπῃ ὅτι πάντα ὑποτέτακται, δῆλον ὅτι ἐκτὸς τοῦ ὑποτάξαντος αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα.
verses.translit: panta gar upetaxen upo tous podas autou. otan de eipe oti panta upotetaktai, delon oti ektos tou upotaxantos auto ta panta.
verses.translation: For he hath put all things under his feet. But when he saith all things are put under him, it is manifest that he is excepted, which did put all things under him.

verses.original: ὅταν δὲ ὑποταγῇ αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα, ⸀τότε αὐτὸς ὁ υἱὸς ὑποταγήσεται τῷ ὑποτάξαντι αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα, ἵνα ᾖ ὁ θεὸς ⸀πάντα ἐν πᾶσιν.
verses.translit: otan de upotage auto ta panta, tote autos o yios upotagisetai to upotaxanti auto ta panta, ina e o theos panta en pasin.
verses.translation: And when all things shall be subdued unto him, then shall the Son also himself be subject unto him that put all things under him, that God may be all in all.

verses.original: Ἐπεὶ τί ποιήσουσιν οἱ βαπτιζόμενοι ὑπὲρ τῶν νεκρῶν; εἰ ὅλως νεκροὶ οὐκ ἐγείρονται, τί καὶ βαπτίζονται ὑπὲρ ⸀αὐτῶν;
verses.translit: Epei ti poiisoysin oi vaptizomenoi uper ton nekron; ei olos nekroi ouk egeirontai, ti kai vaptizontai uper auton;
verses.translation: Else what shall they do which are baptized for the dead, if the dead rise not at all? why are they then baptized for the dead?

verses.original: τί καὶ ἡμεῖς κινδυνεύομεν πᾶσαν ὥραν;
verses.translit: ti kai emeis kindyneyomen pasan oran;
verses.translation: And why stand we in jeopardy every hour?

verses.original: καθʼ ἡμέραν ἀποθνῄσκω, νὴ τὴν ὑμετέραν ⸀καύχησιν, ἣν ἔχω ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ κυρίῳ ἡμῶν.
verses.translit: kath' emeran apothnesko, ne ten umeteran kayhisin, en eho en Hristo Iisou to kyrio emon.
verses.translation: I protest by your rejoicing which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily.

verses.original: εἰ κατὰ ἄνθρωπον ἐθηριομάχησα ἐν Ἐφέσῳ, τί μοι τὸ ὄφελος; εἰ νεκροὶ οὐκ ἐγείρονται, Φάγωμεν καὶ πίωμεν, αὔριον γὰρ ἀποθνῄσκομεν.
verses.translit: ei kata anthropon ethiriomahisa en Efeso, ti moi to ofelos; ei nekroi ouk egeirontai, Fagomen kai piomen, aurion gar apothneskomen.
verses.translation: If after the manner of men I have fought with beasts at Ephesus, what advantageth it me, if the dead rise not? let us eat and drink; for to morrow we die.

verses.original: μὴ πλανᾶσθε· φθείρουσιν ἤθη χρηστὰ ὁμιλίαι κακαί.
verses.translit: me planasthe* ftheiroysin ethi hrista omiliai kakai.
verses.translation: Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners.

verses.original: ἐκνήψατε δικαίως καὶ μὴ ἁμαρτάνετε, ἀγνωσίαν γὰρ θεοῦ τινες ἔχουσιν· πρὸς ἐντροπὴν ὑμῖν ⸀λαλῶ.
verses.translit: eknipsate dikaios kai me amartanete, agnosian gar theou tines ehoysin* pros entropen umin lalo.
verses.translation: Awake to righteousness, and sin not; for some have not the knowledge of God: I speak this to your shame.

verses.original: Ἀλλὰ ἐρεῖ τις· Πῶς ἐγείρονται οἱ νεκροί, ποίῳ δὲ σώματι ἔρχονται;
verses.translit: Alla erei tis* Pos egeirontai oi nekroi, poio de somati erhontai;
verses.translation: But some man will say, How are the dead raised up? and with what body do they come?

verses.original: ⸀ἄφρων, σὺ ὃ σπείρεις, οὐ ζῳοποιεῖται ἐὰν μὴ ἀποθάνῃ·
verses.translit: afron, su o speireis, ou zoopoieitai ean me apothane*
verses.translation: Thou fool, that which thou sowest is not quickened, except it die:

verses.original: καὶ ὃ σπείρεις, οὐ τὸ σῶμα τὸ γενησόμενον σπείρεις ἀλλὰ γυμνὸν κόκκον εἰ τύχοι σίτου ἤ τινος τῶν λοιπῶν·
verses.translit: kai o speireis, ou to soma to genisomenon speireis alla gymnon kokkon ei tyhoi sitoy e tinos ton loipon*
verses.translation: And that which thou sowest, thou sowest not that body that shall be, but bare grain, it may chance of wheat, or of some other grain :

verses.original: ὁ δὲ θεὸς ⸂δίδωσιν αὐτῷ⸃ σῶμα καθὼς ἠθέλησεν, καὶ ἑκάστῳ τῶν σπερμάτων ⸀ἴδιον σῶμα.
verses.translit: o de theos didosin auto soma kathos ethelisen, kai ekasto ton spermaton idion soma.
verses.translation: But God giveth it a body as it hath pleased him, and to every seed his own body.

verses.original: οὐ πᾶσα σὰρξ ἡ αὐτὴ σάρξ, ἀλλὰ ἄλλη μὲν ἀνθρώπων, ἄλλη δὲ σὰρξ κτηνῶν, ἄλλη δὲ ⸂σὰρξ πτηνῶν⸃, ἄλλη δὲ ⸀ἰχθύων.
verses.translit: ou pasa sarx e aute sarx, alla alli men anthropon, alli de sarx ktinon, alli de sarx ptinon, alli de ihthyon.
verses.translation: All flesh is not the same flesh: but there is one kind of flesh of men, another flesh of beasts, another of fishes, and another of birds.

verses.original: καὶ σώματα ἐπουράνια, καὶ σώματα ἐπίγεια· ἀλλὰ ἑτέρα μὲν ἡ τῶν ἐπουρανίων δόξα, ἑτέρα δὲ ἡ τῶν ἐπιγείων.
verses.translit: kai somata epoyrania, kai somata epigeia* alla etera men e ton epoyranion doxa, etera de e ton epigeion.
verses.translation: There are also celestial bodies, and bodies terrestrial: but the glory of the celestial is one, and the glory of the terrestrial is another.

verses.original: ἄλλη δόξα ἡλίου, καὶ ἄλλη δόξα σελήνης, καὶ ἄλλη δόξα ἀστέρων, ἀστὴρ γὰρ ἀστέρος διαφέρει ἐν δόξῃ.
verses.translit: alli doxa elioy, kai alli doxa selinis, kai alli doxa asteron, aster gar asteros diaferei en doxe.
verses.translation: There is one glory of the sun, and another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars: for one star differeth from another star in glory.

verses.original: Οὕτως καὶ ἡ ἀνάστασις τῶν νεκρῶν. σπείρεται ἐν φθορᾷ, ἐγείρεται ἐν ἀφθαρσίᾳ·
verses.translit: Outos kai e anastasis ton nekron. speiretai en fthora, egeiretai en aftharsia*
verses.translation: So also is the resurrection of the dead. It is sown in corruption; it is raised in incorruption:

verses.original: σπείρεται ἐν ἀτιμίᾳ, ἐγείρεται ἐν δόξῃ· σπείρεται ἐν ἀσθενείᾳ, ἐγείρεται ἐν δυνάμει·
verses.translit: speiretai en atimia, egeiretai en doxe* speiretai en astheneia, egeiretai en dynamei*
verses.translation: It is sown in dishonour; it is raised in glory: it is sown in weakness; it is raised in power:

verses.original: σπείρεται σῶμα ψυχικόν, ἐγείρεται σῶμα πνευματικόν. ⸀Εἰ ἔστιν σῶμα ψυχικόν, ⸂ἔστιν καὶ⸃ πνευματικόν.
verses.translit: speiretai soma psyhikon, egeiretai soma pneymatikon. Ei estin soma psyhikon, estin kai pneymatikon.
verses.translation: It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body. There is a natural body, and there is a spiritual body.

verses.original: οὕτως καὶ γέγραπται· Ἐγένετο ὁ πρῶτος ἄνθρωπος Ἀδὰμ εἰς ψυχὴν ζῶσαν· ὁ ἔσχατος Ἀδὰμ εἰς πνεῦμα ζῳοποιοῦν.
verses.translit: outos kai gegraptai* Egeneto o protos anthropos Adam eis psyhen zosan* o eshatos Adam eis pneuma zoopoioun.
verses.translation: And so it is written, The first man Adam was made a living soul; the last Adam was made a quickening spirit.

verses.original: ἀλλʼ οὐ πρῶτον τὸ πνευματικὸν ἀλλὰ τὸ ψυχικόν, ἔπειτα τὸ πνευματικόν.
verses.translit: all' ou proton to pneymatikon alla to psyhikon, epeita to pneymatikon.
verses.translation: Howbeit that was not first which is spiritual, but that which is natural; and afterward that which is spiritual.

verses.original: ὁ πρῶτος ἄνθρωπος ἐκ γῆς χοϊκός, ὁ δεύτερος ⸀ἄνθρωπος ἐξ οὐρανοῦ.
verses.translit: o protos anthropos ek ges hoikos, o deyteros anthropos ex ouranou.
verses.translation: The first man is of the earth, earthy: the second man is the Lord from heaven.

verses.original: οἷος ὁ χοϊκός, τοιοῦτοι καὶ οἱ χοϊκοί, καὶ οἷος ὁ ἐπουράνιος, τοιοῦτοι καὶ οἱ ἐπουράνιοι·
verses.translit: oios o hoikos, toioutoi kai oi hoikoi, kai oios o epoyranios, toioutoi kai oi epoyranioi*
verses.translation: As is the earthy, such are they also that are earthy: and as is the heavenly, such are they also that are heavenly.

verses.original: καὶ καθὼς ἐφορέσαμεν τὴν εἰκόνα τοῦ χοϊκοῦ, ⸀φορέσομεν καὶ τὴν εἰκόνα τοῦ ἐπουρανίου.
verses.translit: kai kathos eforesamen ten eikona tou hoikou, foresomen kai ten eikona tou epoyranioy.
verses.translation: And as we have borne the image of the earthy, we shall also bear the image of the heavenly.

verses.original: Τοῦτο δέ φημι, ἀδελφοί, ὅτι σὰρξ καὶ αἷμα βασιλείαν θεοῦ κληρονομῆσαι οὐ ⸀δύναται, οὐδὲ ἡ φθορὰ τὴν ἀφθαρσίαν κληρονομεῖ.
verses.translit: Touto de fimi, adelfoi, oti sarx kai aima vasileian theou klironomesai ou dynatai, oude e fthora ten aftharsian klironomei.
verses.translation: Now this I say, brethren, that flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God; neither doth corruption inherit incorruption.

verses.original: ἰδοὺ μυστήριον ὑμῖν λέγω· ⸀πάντες οὐ κοιμηθησόμεθα πάντες δὲ ἀλλαγησόμεθα,
verses.translit: idou mystirion umin lego* pantes ou koimithisometha pantes de allagisometha,
verses.translation: Behold, I shew you a mystery; We shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed,

verses.original: ἐν ἀτόμῳ, ἐν ῥιπῇ ὀφθαλμοῦ, ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ σάλπιγγι· σαλπίσει γάρ, καὶ οἱ νεκροὶ ἐγερθήσονται ἄφθαρτοι, καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀλλαγησόμεθα.
verses.translit: en atomo, en Ripe ofthalmou, en te eshate salpiggi* salpisei gar, kai oi nekroi egerthisontai afthartoi, kai emeis allagisometha.
verses.translation: In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump: for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed.

verses.original: δεῖ γὰρ τὸ φθαρτὸν τοῦτο ἐνδύσασθαι ἀφθαρσίαν καὶ τὸ θνητὸν τοῦτο ἐνδύσασθαι ἀθανασίαν.
verses.translit: dei gar to ftharton touto endysasthai aftharsian kai to thniton touto endysasthai athanasian.
verses.translation: For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality.

verses.original: ὅταν δὲ τὸ ⸂φθαρτὸν τοῦτο ἐνδύσηται ἀφθαρσίαν καὶ τὸ⸃ θνητὸν τοῦτο ἐνδύσηται ⸀ἀθανασίαν, τότε γενήσεται ὁ λόγος ὁ γεγραμμένος· Κατεπόθη ὁ θάνατος εἰς νῖκος.
verses.translit: otan de to ftharton touto endysitai aftharsian kai to thniton touto endysitai athanasian, tote genisetai o logos o gegrammenos* Katepothi o thanatos eis nikos.
verses.translation: So when this corruptible shall have put on incorruption, and this mortal shall have put on immortality, then shall be brought to pass the saying that is written, Death is swallowed up in victory.

verses.original: ποῦ σου, θάνατε, τὸ ⸂νῖκος; ποῦ σου, θάνατε, τὸ κέντρον⸃;
verses.translit: pou soy, thanate, to nikos; pou soy, thanate, to kentron;
verses.translation: O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory?

verses.original: τὸ δὲ κέντρον τοῦ θανάτου ἡ ἁμαρτία, ἡ δὲ δύναμις τῆς ἁμαρτίας ὁ νόμος·
verses.translit: to de kentron tou thanatoy e amartia, e de dynamis tes amartias o nomos*
verses.translation: The sting of death is sin; and the strength of sin is the law.

verses.original: τῷ δὲ θεῷ χάρις τῷ διδόντι ἡμῖν τὸ νῖκος διὰ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
verses.translit: to de theo haris to didonti emin to nikos dia tou kyrioy emon Iisou Hristou.
verses.translation: But thanks be to God, which giveth us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.original: Ὥστε, ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί, ἑδραῖοι γίνεσθε, ἀμετακίνητοι, περισσεύοντες ἐν τῷ ἔργῳ τοῦ κυρίου πάντοτε, εἰδότες ὅτι ὁ κόπος ὑμῶν οὐκ ἔστιν κενὸς ἐν κυρίῳ.
verses.translit: Oste, adelfoi moy agapitoi, edraioi ginesthe, ametakinitoi, perisseyontes en to ergo tou kyrioy pantote, eidotes oti o kopos umon ouk estin kenos en kyrio.
verses.translation: Therefore, my beloved brethren, be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, forasmuch as ye know that your labour is not in vain in the Lord.

verses.original: Περὶ δὲ τῆς λογείας τῆς εἰς τοὺς ἁγίους, ὥσπερ διέταξα ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τῆς Γαλατίας, οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ποιήσατε.
verses.translit: Peri de tes logeias tes eis tous agioys, osper dietaxa tais ekklisiais tes Galatias, outos kai umeis poiisate.
verses.translation: Now concerning the collection for the saints, as I have given order to the churches of Galatia, even so do ye.

verses.original: κατὰ μίαν ⸀σαββάτου ἕκαστος ὑμῶν παρʼ ἑαυτῷ τιθέτω θησαυρίζων ὅ τι ⸀ἐὰν εὐοδῶται, ἵνα μὴ ὅταν ἔλθω τότε λογεῖαι γίνωνται.
verses.translit: kata mian savvatoy ekastos umon par' eayto titheto thisayrizon o ti ean euodotai, ina me otan eltho tote logeiai ginontai.
verses.translation: Upon the first day of the week let every one of you lay by him in store, as God hath prospered him, that there be no gatherings when I come.

verses.original: ὅταν δὲ παραγένωμαι, οὓς ⸀ἐὰν δοκιμάσητε διʼ ἐπιστολῶν, τούτους πέμψω ἀπενεγκεῖν τὴν χάριν ὑμῶν εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ·
verses.translit: otan de paragenomai, ous ean dokimasite di' epistolon, toytoys pempso apenegkein ten harin umon eis Ieroysalim*
verses.translation: And when I come, whomsoever ye shall approve by your letters, them will I send to bring your liberality unto Jerusalem.

verses.original: ἐὰν δὲ ⸂ἄξιον ᾖ⸃ τοῦ κἀμὲ πορεύεσθαι, σὺν ἐμοὶ πορεύσονται.
verses.translit: ean de axion e tou kame poreyesthai, sun emoi poreysontai.
verses.translation: And if it be meet that I go also, they shall go with me.

verses.original: Ἐλεύσομαι δὲ πρὸς ὑμᾶς ὅταν Μακεδονίαν διέλθω, Μακεδονίαν γὰρ διέρχομαι,
verses.translit: Eleysomai de pros umas otan Makedonian dieltho, Makedonian gar dierhomai,
verses.translation: Now I will come unto you, when I shall pass through Macedonia: for I do pass through Macedonia.

verses.original: πρὸς ὑμᾶς δὲ τυχὸν ⸀παραμενῶ ἢ ⸀καὶ παραχειμάσω, ἵνα ὑμεῖς με προπέμψητε οὗ ἐὰν πορεύωμαι.
verses.translit: pros umas de tyhon parameno e kai paraheimaso, ina umeis me propempsite ou ean poreyomai.
verses.translation: And it may be that I will abide, yea, and winter with you, that ye may bring me on my journey whithersoever I go.

verses.original: οὐ θέλω γὰρ ὑμᾶς ἄρτι ἐν παρόδῳ ἰδεῖν, ἐλπίζω ⸀γὰρ χρόνον τινὰ ἐπιμεῖναι πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἐὰν ὁ κύριος ⸀ἐπιτρέψῃ.
verses.translit: ou thelo gar umas arti en parodo idein, elpizo gar hronon tina epimeinai pros umas, ean o kyrios epitrepse.
verses.translation: For I will not see you now by the way; but I trust to tarry a while with you, if the Lord permit.

verses.original: ⸀ἐπιμενῶ δὲ ἐν Ἐφέσῳ ἕως τῆς πεντηκοστῆς·
verses.translit: epimeno de en Efeso eos tes pentikostes*
verses.translation: But I will tarry at Ephesus until Pentecost.

verses.original: θύρα γάρ μοι ἀνέῳγεν μεγάλη καὶ ἐνεργής, καὶ ἀντικείμενοι πολλοί.
verses.translit: thyra gar moi aneogen megali kai energis, kai antikeimenoi polloi.
verses.translation: For a great door and effectual is opened unto me, and there are many adversaries.

verses.original: Ἐὰν δὲ ἔλθῃ Τιμόθεος, βλέπετε ἵνα ἀφόβως γένηται πρὸς ὑμᾶς, τὸ γὰρ ἔργον κυρίου ἐργάζεται ὡς ⸀κἀγώ·
verses.translit: Ean de elthe Timotheos, vlepete ina afovos genitai pros umas, to gar ergon kyrioy ergazetai os kago*
verses.translation: Now if Timotheus come, see that he may be with you without fear: for he worketh the work of the Lord, as I also do .

verses.original: μή τις οὖν αὐτὸν ἐξουθενήσῃ. προπέμψατε δὲ αὐτὸν ἐν εἰρήνῃ, ἵνα ἔλθῃ πρός ⸀με, ἐκδέχομαι γὰρ αὐτὸν μετὰ τῶν ἀδελφῶν.
verses.translit: mi tis oun auton exoythenise. propempsate de auton en eirine, ina elthe pros me, ekdehomai gar auton meta ton adelfon.
verses.translation: Let no man therefore despise him: but conduct him forth in peace, that he may come unto me: for I look for him with the brethren.

verses.original: Περὶ δὲ Ἀπολλῶ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ, πολλὰ παρεκάλεσα αὐτὸν ἵνα ἔλθῃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς μετὰ τῶν ἀδελφῶν· καὶ πάντως οὐκ ἦν θέλημα ἵνα νῦν ἔλθῃ, ἐλεύσεται δὲ ὅταν εὐκαιρήσῃ.
verses.translit: Peri de Apollo tou adelfou, polla parekalesa auton ina elthe pros umas meta ton adelfon* kai pantos ouk en thelima ina nun elthe, eleysetai de otan eukairise.
verses.translation: As touching our brother Apollos, I greatly desired him to come unto you with the brethren: but his will was not at all to come at this time; but he will come when he shall have convenient time.

verses.original: Γρηγορεῖτε, στήκετε ἐν τῇ πίστει, ἀνδρίζεσθε, κραταιοῦσθε.
verses.translit: Grigoreite, stikete en te pistei, andrizesthe, krataiousthe.
verses.translation: Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong.

verses.original: πάντα ὑμῶν ἐν ἀγάπῃ γινέσθω.
verses.translit: panta umon en agape ginestho.
verses.translation: Let all your things be done with charity.

verses.original: Παρακαλῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί· οἴδατε τὴν οἰκίαν Στεφανᾶ, ὅτι ἐστὶν ἀπαρχὴ τῆς Ἀχαΐας καὶ εἰς διακονίαν τοῖς ἁγίοις ἔταξαν ἑαυτούς·
verses.translit: Parakalo de umas, adelfoi* oidate ten oikian Stefana, oti estin aparhe tes AhaIas kai eis diakonian tois agiois etaxan eaytoys*
verses.translation: I beseech you, brethren, (ye know the house of Stephanas, that it is the firstfruits of Achaia, and that they have addicted themselves to the ministry of the saints,)

verses.original: ἵνα καὶ ὑμεῖς ὑποτάσσησθε τοῖς τοιούτοις καὶ παντὶ τῷ συνεργοῦντι καὶ κοπιῶντι.
verses.translit: ina kai umeis upotassisthe tois toioytois kai panti to synergounti kai kopionti.
verses.translation: That ye submit yourselves unto such, and to every one that helpeth with us , and laboureth.

verses.original: χαίρω δὲ ἐπὶ τῇ παρουσίᾳ Στεφανᾶ καὶ Φορτουνάτου καὶ Ἀχαϊκοῦ, ὅτι τὸ ⸀ὑμέτερον ὑστέρημα οὗτοι ἀνεπλήρωσαν,
verses.translit: hairo de epi te paroysia Stefana kai Fortoynatoy kai Ahaikou, oti to umeteron usterima outoi aneplirosan,
verses.translation: I am glad of the coming of Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus: for that which was lacking on your part they have supplied.

verses.original: ἀνέπαυσαν γὰρ τὸ ἐμὸν πνεῦμα καὶ τὸ ὑμῶν. ἐπιγινώσκετε οὖν τοὺς τοιούτους.
verses.translit: anepaysan gar to emon pneuma kai to umon. epiginoskete oun tous toioytoys.
verses.translation: For they have refreshed my spirit and yours: therefore acknowledge ye them that are such.

verses.original: Ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς αἱ ἐκκλησίαι τῆς Ἀσίας. ⸀ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς ἐν κυρίῳ πολλὰ Ἀκύλας καὶ ⸀Πρίσκα σὺν τῇ κατʼ οἶκον αὐτῶν ἐκκλησίᾳ.
verses.translit: Aspazontai umas ai ekklisiai tes Asias. aspazetai umas en kyrio polla Akylas kai Priska sun te kat' oikon auton ekklisia.
verses.translation: The churches of Asia salute you. Aquila and Priscilla salute you much in the Lord, with the church that is in their house.

verses.original: ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς οἱ ἀδελφοὶ πάντες. ἀσπάσασθε ἀλλήλους ἐν φιλήματι ἁγίῳ.
verses.translit: aspazontai umas oi adelfoi pantes. aspasasthe alliloys en filimati agio.
verses.translation: All the brethren greet you. Greet ye one another with an holy kiss.

verses.original: Ὁ ἀσπασμὸς τῇ ἐμῇ χειρὶ Παύλου.
verses.translit: O aspasmos te eme heiri Payloy.
verses.translation: The salutation of me Paul with mine own hand.

verses.original: εἴ τις οὐ φιλεῖ τὸν ⸀κύριον, ἤτω ἀνάθεμα. ⸂Μαράνα θά⸃.
verses.translit: ei tis ou filei ton kyrion, eto anathema. Marana tha.
verses.translation: If any man love not the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be Anathema Maranatha.

verses.original: ἡ χάρις τοῦ κυρίου ⸀Ἰησοῦ μεθʼ ὑμῶν.
verses.translit: e haris tou kyrioy Iisou meth' umon.
verses.translation: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.

verses.original: ἡ ἀγάπη μου μετὰ πάντων ὑμῶν ἐν Χριστῷ ⸀Ἰησοῦ.
verses.translit: e agapi moy meta panton umon en Hristo Iisou.
verses.translation: My love be with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen.

verses.original: Παῦλος ἀπόστολος ⸂Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ⸃ διὰ θελήματος θεοῦ καὶ Τιμόθεος ὁ ἀδελφὸς τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ τῇ οὔσῃ ἐν Κορίνθῳ, σὺν τοῖς ἁγίοις πᾶσιν τοῖς οὖσιν ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ Ἀχαΐᾳ·
verses.translit: Paulos apostolos Hristou Iisou dia thelimatos theou kai Timotheos o adelfos te ekklisia tou theou te ouse en Korintho, sun tois agiois pasin tois ousin en ole te AhaIa*
verses.translation: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy our brother, unto the church of God which is at Corinth, with all the saints which are in all Achaia:

verses.original: χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν καὶ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
verses.translit: haris umin kai eirini apo theou patros emon kai kyrioy Iisou Hristou.
verses.translation: Grace be to you and peace from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.original: Εὐλογητὸς ὁ θεὸς καὶ πατὴρ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὁ πατὴρ τῶν οἰκτιρμῶν καὶ θεὸς πάσης παρακλήσεως,
verses.translit: Eulogitos o theos kai pater tou kyrioy emon Iisou Hristou, o pater ton oiktirmon kai theos pasis parakliseos,
verses.translation: Blessed be God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort;

verses.original: ὁ παρακαλῶν ἡμᾶς ἐπὶ πάσῃ τῇ θλίψει ἡμῶν, εἰς τὸ δύνασθαι ἡμᾶς παρακαλεῖν τοὺς ἐν πάσῃ θλίψει διὰ τῆς παρακλήσεως ἧς παρακαλούμεθα αὐτοὶ ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: o parakalon emas epi pase te thlipsei emon, eis to dynasthai emas parakalein tous en pase thlipsei dia tes parakliseos es parakaloymetha autoi upo tou theou.
verses.translation: Who comforteth us in all our tribulation, that we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble, by the comfort wherewith we ourselves are comforted of God.

verses.original: ὅτι καθὼς περισσεύει τὰ παθήματα τοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς ἡμᾶς, οὕτως διὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ περισσεύει καὶ ἡ παράκλησις ἡμῶν.
verses.translit: oti kathos perisseyei ta pathimata tou Hristou eis emas, outos dia tou Hristou perisseyei kai e paraklisis emon.
verses.translation: For as the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so our consolation also aboundeth by Christ.

verses.original: εἴτε δὲ θλιβόμεθα, ὑπὲρ τῆς ὑμῶν παρακλήσεως καὶ σωτηρίας· ⸂εἴτε παρακαλούμεθα, ὑπὲρ τῆς ὑμῶν παρακλήσεως⸃ τῆς ἐνεργουμένης ἐν ὑπομονῇ τῶν αὐτῶν παθημάτων ὧν καὶ ἡμεῖς πάσχομεν,
verses.translit: eite de thlivometha, uper tes umon parakliseos kai sotirias* eite parakaloymetha, uper tes umon parakliseos tes energoymenis en upomone ton auton pathimaton on kai emeis pashomen,
verses.translation: And whether we be afflicted, it is for your consolation and salvation, which is effectual in the enduring of the same sufferings which we also suffer: or whether we be comforted, it is for your consolation and salvation.

verses.original: καὶ ἡ ἐλπὶς ἡμῶν βεβαία ὑπὲρ ⸀ὑμῶν· εἰδότες ὅτι ⸀ὡς κοινωνοί ἐστε τῶν παθημάτων, οὕτως καὶ τῆς παρακλήσεως.
verses.translit: kai e elpis emon vevaia uper umon* eidotes oti os koinonoi este ton pathimaton, outos kai tes parakliseos.
verses.translation: And our hope of you is stedfast, knowing, that as ye are partakers of the sufferings, so shall ye be also of the consolation.

verses.original: Οὐ γὰρ θέλομεν ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν, ἀδελφοί, ⸀ὑπὲρ τῆς θλίψεως ἡμῶν τῆς ⸀γενομένης ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ, ὅτι καθʼ ὑπερβολὴν ⸂ὑπὲρ δύναμιν ἐβαρήθημεν⸃, ὥστε ἐξαπορηθῆναι ἡμᾶς καὶ τοῦ ζῆν·
verses.translit: Ou gar thelomen umas agnoein, adelfoi, uper tes thlipseos emon tes genomenis en te Asia, oti kath' upervolen uper dynamin evarithimen, oste exaporithenai emas kai tou zen*
verses.translation: For we would not, brethren, have you ignorant of our trouble which came to us in Asia, that we were pressed out of measure, above strength, insomuch that we despaired even of life:

verses.original: ἀλλὰ αὐτοὶ ἐν ἑαυτοῖς τὸ ἀπόκριμα τοῦ θανάτου ἐσχήκαμεν, ἵνα μὴ πεποιθότες ὦμεν ἐφʼ ἑαυτοῖς ἀλλʼ ἐπὶ τῷ θεῷ τῷ ἐγείροντι τοὺς νεκρούς·
verses.translit: alla autoi en eaytois to apokrima tou thanatoy eshikamen, ina me pepoithotes omen ef' eaytois all' epi to theo to egeironti tous nekroys*
verses.translation: But we had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead:

verses.original: ὃς ἐκ τηλικούτου θανάτου ἐρρύσατο ἡμᾶς καὶ ⸀ῥύσεται, εἰς ὃν ἠλπίκαμεν ὅτι καὶ ἔτι ῥύσεται,
verses.translit: os ek tilikoytoy thanatoy errysato emas kai Rysetai, eis on elpikamen oti kai eti Rysetai,
verses.translation: Who delivered us from so great a death, and doth deliver: in whom we trust that he will yet deliver us ;

verses.original: συνυπουργούντων καὶ ὑμῶν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν τῇ δεήσει, ἵνα ἐκ πολλῶν προσώπων τὸ εἰς ἡμᾶς χάρισμα διὰ πολλῶν εὐχαριστηθῇ ὑπὲρ ⸀ἡμῶν.
verses.translit: synypoyrgoynton kai umon uper emon te deisei, ina ek pollon prosopon to eis emas harisma dia pollon euharistithe uper emon.
verses.translation: Ye also helping together by prayer for us, that for the gift bestowed upon us by the means of many persons thanks may be given by many on our behalf.

verses.original: Ἡ γὰρ καύχησις ἡμῶν αὕτη ἐστίν, τὸ μαρτύριον τῆς συνειδήσεως ἡμῶν, ὅτι ἐν ⸀ἁγιότητι καὶ εἰλικρινείᾳ ⸀τοῦ θεοῦ, ⸀οὐκ ἐν σοφίᾳ σαρκικῇ ἀλλʼ ἐν χάριτι θεοῦ, ἀνεστράφημεν ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ, περισσοτέρως δὲ πρὸς ὑμᾶς·
verses.translit: E gar kayhisis emon auti estin, to martyrion tes syneidiseos emon, oti en agiotiti kai eilikrineia tou theou, ouk en sofia sarkike all' en hariti theou, anestrafimen en to kosmo, perissoteros de pros umas*
verses.translation: For our rejoicing is this, the testimony of our conscience, that in simplicity and godly sincerity, not with fleshly wisdom, but by the grace of God, we have had our conversation in the world, and more abundantly to you-ward.

verses.original: οὐ γὰρ ἄλλα γράφομεν ὑμῖν ἀλλʼ ἢ ἃ ἀναγινώσκετε ἢ καὶ ἐπιγινώσκετε, ἐλπίζω δὲ ⸀ὅτι ἕως τέλους ἐπιγνώσεσθε,
verses.translit: ou gar alla grafomen umin all' e a anaginoskete e kai epiginoskete, elpizo de oti eos teloys epignosesthe,
verses.translation: For we write none other things unto you, than what ye read or acknowledge; and I trust ye shall acknowledge even to the end;

verses.original: καθὼς καὶ ἐπέγνωτε ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ μέρους, ὅτι καύχημα ὑμῶν ἐσμεν καθάπερ καὶ ὑμεῖς ἡμῶν ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ κυρίου ⸀ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ.
verses.translit: kathos kai epegnote emas apo meroys, oti kayhima umon esmen kathaper kai umeis emon en te emera tou kyrioy emon Iisou.
verses.translation: As also ye have acknowledged us in part, that we are your rejoicing, even as ye also are ours in the day of the Lord Jesus.

verses.original: Καὶ ταύτῃ τῇ πεποιθήσει ἐβουλόμην ⸂πρότερον πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐλθεῖν⸃, ἵνα δευτέραν ⸀χάριν ⸀σχῆτε,
verses.translit: Kai tayte te pepoithisei evoylomin proteron pros umas elthein, ina deyteran harin shete,
verses.translation: And in this confidence I was minded to come unto you before, that ye might have a second benefit;

verses.original: καὶ διʼ ὑμῶν διελθεῖν εἰς Μακεδονίαν, καὶ πάλιν ἀπὸ Μακεδονίας ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς καὶ ὑφʼ ὑμῶν προπεμφθῆναι εἰς τὴν Ἰουδαίαν.
verses.translit: kai di' umon dielthein eis Makedonian, kai palin apo Makedonias elthein pros umas kai uf' umon propemfthenai eis ten Ioydaian.
verses.translation: And to pass by you into Macedonia, and to come again out of Macedonia unto you, and of you to be brought on my way toward Judaea.

verses.original: τοῦτο οὖν ⸀βουλόμενος μήτι ἄρα τῇ ἐλαφρίᾳ ἐχρησάμην; ἢ ἃ βουλεύομαι κατὰ σάρκα βουλεύομαι, ἵνα ᾖ παρʼ ἐμοὶ τὸ Ναὶ ναὶ καὶ τὸ Οὒ οὔ;
verses.translit: touto oun voylomenos miti ara te elafria ehrisamin; e a voyleyomai kata sarka voyleyomai, ina e par' emoi to Nai nai kai to Ou ou;
verses.translation: When I therefore was thus minded, did I use lightness? or the things that I purpose, do I purpose according to the flesh, that with me there should be yea yea, and nay nay?

verses.original: πιστὸς δὲ ὁ θεὸς ὅτι ὁ λόγος ἡμῶν ὁ πρὸς ὑμᾶς οὐκ ⸀ἔστιν Ναὶ καὶ Οὔ.
verses.translit: pistos de o theos oti o logos emon o pros umas ouk estin Nai kai Ou.
verses.translation: But as God is true, our word toward you was not yea and nay.

verses.original: ὁ ⸂τοῦ θεοῦ γὰρ⸃ υἱὸς ⸂Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς⸃ ὁ ἐν ὑμῖν διʼ ἡμῶν κηρυχθείς, διʼ ἐμοῦ καὶ Σιλουανοῦ καὶ Τιμοθέου, οὐκ ἐγένετο Ναὶ καὶ Οὒ, ἀλλὰ Ναὶ ἐν αὐτῷ γέγονεν·
verses.translit: o tou theou gar yios Iisous Hristos o en umin di' emon kiryhtheis, di' emou kai Siloyanou kai Timotheoy, ouk egeneto Nai kai Ou, alla Nai en auto gegonen*
verses.translation: For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us, even by me and Silvanus and Timotheus, was not yea and nay, but in him was yea.

verses.original: ὅσαι γὰρ ἐπαγγελίαι θεοῦ, ἐν αὐτῷ τὸ Ναί· ⸀διὸ καὶ ⸂διʼ αὐτοῦ⸃ τὸ Ἀμὴν τῷ θεῷ πρὸς δόξαν διʼ ἡμῶν.
verses.translit: osai gar epaggeliai theou, en auto to Nai* dio kai di' autou to Amen to theo pros doxan di' emon.
verses.translation: For all the promises of God in him are yea, and in him Amen, unto the glory of God by us.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ βεβαιῶν ἡμᾶς σὺν ὑμῖν εἰς Χριστὸν καὶ χρίσας ἡμᾶς θεός,
verses.translit: o de vevaion emas sun umin eis Hriston kai hrisas emas theos,
verses.translation: Now he which stablisheth us with you in Christ, and hath anointed us, is God;

verses.original: ὁ καὶ σφραγισάμενος ἡμᾶς καὶ δοὺς τὸν ἀρραβῶνα τοῦ πνεύματος ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἡμῶν.
verses.translit: o kai sfragisamenos emas kai dous ton arravona tou pneymatos en tais kardiais emon.
verses.translation: Who hath also sealed us, and given the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts.

verses.original: Ἐγὼ δὲ μάρτυρα τὸν θεὸν ἐπικαλοῦμαι ἐπὶ τὴν ἐμὴν ψυχήν, ὅτι φειδόμενος ὑμῶν οὐκέτι ἦλθον εἰς Κόρινθον.
verses.translit: Ego de martyra ton theon epikaloumai epi ten emen psyhin, oti feidomenos umon ouketi elthon eis Korinthon.
verses.translation: Moreover I call God for a record upon my soul, that to spare you I came not as yet unto Corinth.

verses.original: οὐχ ὅτι κυριεύομεν ὑμῶν τῆς πίστεως, ἀλλὰ συνεργοί ἐσμεν τῆς χαρᾶς ὑμῶν, τῇ γὰρ πίστει ἑστήκατε.
verses.translit: ouh oti kyrieyomen umon tes pisteos, alla synergoi esmen tes haras umon, te gar pistei estikate.
verses.translation: Not for that we have dominion over your faith, but are helpers of your joy: for by faith ye stand.

verses.original: ἔκρινα ⸀γὰρ ἐμαυτῷ τοῦτο, τὸ μὴ πάλιν ἐν λύπῃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐλθεῖν·
verses.translit: ekrina gar emayto touto, to me palin en lype pros umas elthein*
verses.translation: But I determined this with myself, that I would not come again to you in heaviness.

verses.original: εἰ γὰρ ἐγὼ λυπῶ ὑμᾶς, καὶ ⸀τίς ὁ εὐφραίνων με εἰ μὴ ὁ λυπούμενος ἐξ ἐμοῦ;
verses.translit: ei gar ego lypo umas, kai tis o eufrainon me ei me o lypoymenos ex emou;
verses.translation: For if I make you sorry, who is he then that maketh me glad, but the same which is made sorry by me?

verses.original: καὶ ⸀ἔγραψα τοῦτο αὐτὸ ἵνα μὴ ἐλθὼν λύπην ⸀σχῶ ἀφʼ ὧν ἔδει με χαίρειν, πεποιθὼς ἐπὶ πάντας ὑμᾶς ὅτι ἡ ἐμὴ χαρὰ πάντων ὑμῶν ἐστιν.
verses.translit: kai egrapsa touto auto ina me elthon lypin sho af' on edei me hairein, pepoithos epi pantas umas oti e eme hara panton umon estin.
verses.translation: And I wrote this same unto you, lest, when I came, I should have sorrow from them of whom I ought to rejoice; having confidence in you all, that my joy is the joy of you all.

verses.original: ἐκ γὰρ πολλῆς θλίψεως καὶ συνοχῆς καρδίας ἔγραψα ὑμῖν διὰ πολλῶν δακρύων, οὐχ ἵνα λυπηθῆτε, ἀλλὰ τὴν ἀγάπην ἵνα γνῶτε ἣν ἔχω περισσοτέρως εἰς ὑμᾶς.
verses.translit: ek gar polles thlipseos kai synohes kardias egrapsa umin dia pollon dakryon, ouh ina lypithete, alla ten agapin ina gnote en eho perissoteros eis umas.
verses.translation: For out of much affliction and anguish of heart I wrote unto you with many tears; not that ye should be grieved, but that ye might know the love which I have more abundantly unto you.

verses.original: Εἰ δέ τις λελύπηκεν, οὐκ ἐμὲ λελύπηκεν, ἀλλὰ ἀπὸ μέρους ἵνα μὴ ἐπιβαρῶ πάντας ὑμᾶς.
verses.translit: Ei de tis lelypiken, ouk eme lelypiken, alla apo meroys ina me epivaro pantas umas.
verses.translation: But if any have caused grief, he hath not grieved me, but in part: that I may not overcharge you all.

verses.original: ἱκανὸν τῷ τοιούτῳ ἡ ἐπιτιμία αὕτη ἡ ὑπὸ τῶν πλειόνων,
verses.translit: ikanon to toioyto e epitimia auti e upo ton pleionon,
verses.translation: Sufficient to such a man is this punishment, which was inflicted of many.

verses.original: ὥστε τοὐναντίον ⸀μᾶλλον ὑμᾶς χαρίσασθαι καὶ παρακαλέσαι, μή πως τῇ περισσοτέρᾳ λύπῃ καταποθῇ ὁ τοιοῦτος.
verses.translit: oste tounantion mallon umas harisasthai kai parakalesai, mi pos te perissotera lype katapothe o toioutos.
verses.translation: So that contrariwise ye ought rather to forgive him , and comfort him , lest perhaps such a one should be swallowed up with overmuch sorrow.

verses.original: διὸ παρακαλῶ ὑμᾶς κυρῶσαι εἰς αὐτὸν ἀγάπην·
verses.translit: dio parakalo umas kyrosai eis auton agapin*
verses.translation: Wherefore I beseech you that ye would confirm your love toward him.

verses.original: εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ καὶ ἔγραψα ἵνα γνῶ τὴν δοκιμὴν ὑμῶν, εἰ εἰς πάντα ὑπήκοοί ἐστε.
verses.translit: eis touto gar kai egrapsa ina gno ten dokimen umon, ei eis panta upikooi este.
verses.translation: For to this end also did I write, that I might know the proof of you, whether ye be obedient in all things.

verses.original: ᾧ δέ τι χαρίζεσθε, κἀγώ· καὶ γὰρ ἐγὼ ⸂ὃ κεχάρισμαι, εἴ τι⸃ κεχάρισμαι, διʼ ὑμᾶς ἐν προσώπῳ Χριστοῦ,
verses.translit: o de ti harizesthe, kago* kai gar ego o keharismai, ei ti keharismai, di' umas en prosopo Hristou,
verses.translation: To whom ye forgive any thing, I forgive also: for if I forgave any thing, to whom I forgave it , for your sakes forgave I it in the person of Christ;

verses.original: ἵνα μὴ πλεονεκτηθῶμεν ὑπὸ τοῦ Σατανᾶ, οὐ γὰρ αὐτοῦ τὰ νοήματα ἀγνοοῦμεν.
verses.translit: ina me pleonektithomen upo tou Satana, ou gar autou ta noimata agnooumen.
verses.translation: Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices.

verses.original: Ἐλθὼν δὲ εἰς τὴν Τρῳάδα εἰς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ θύρας μοι ἀνεῳγμένης ἐν κυρίῳ,
verses.translit: Elthon de eis ten Troada eis to euaggelion tou Hristou kai thyras moi aneogmenis en kyrio,
verses.translation: Furthermore, when I came to Troas to preach Christ’s gospel, and a door was opened unto me of the Lord,

verses.original: οὐκ ἔσχηκα ἄνεσιν τῷ πνεύματί μου τῷ μὴ εὑρεῖν με Τίτον τὸν ἀδελφόν μου, ἀλλὰ ἀποταξάμενος αὐτοῖς ἐξῆλθον εἰς Μακεδονίαν.
verses.translit: ouk eshika anesin to pneymati moy to me eurein me Titon ton adelfon moy, alla apotaxamenos autois exelthon eis Makedonian.
verses.translation: I had no rest in my spirit, because I found not Titus my brother: but taking my leave of them, I went from thence into Macedonia.

verses.original: Τῷ δὲ θεῷ χάρις τῷ πάντοτε θριαμβεύοντι ἡμᾶς ἐν τῷ Χριστῷ καὶ τὴν ὀσμὴν τῆς γνώσεως αὐτοῦ φανεροῦντι διʼ ἡμῶν ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ·
verses.translit: To de theo haris to pantote thriamveyonti emas en to Hristo kai ten osmen tes gnoseos autou fanerounti di' emon en panti topo*
verses.translation: Now thanks be unto God, which always causeth us to triumph in Christ, and maketh manifest the savour of his knowledge by us in every place.

verses.original: ὅτι Χριστοῦ εὐωδία ἐσμὲν τῷ θεῷ ἐν τοῖς σῳζομένοις καὶ ἐν τοῖς ἀπολλυμένοις,
verses.translit: oti Hristou euodia esmen to theo en tois sozomenois kai en tois apollymenois,
verses.translation: For we are unto God a sweet savour of Christ, in them that are saved, and in them that perish:

verses.original: οἷς μὲν ὀσμὴ ⸀ἐκ θανάτου εἰς θάνατον, οἷς δὲ ὀσμὴ ⸁ἐκ ζωῆς εἰς ζωήν. καὶ πρὸς ταῦτα τίς ἱκανός;
verses.translit: ois men osme ek thanatoy eis thanaton, ois de osme ek zoes eis zoin. kai pros tauta tis ikanos;
verses.translation: To the one we are the savour of death unto death; and to the other the savour of life unto life. And who is sufficient for these things?

verses.original: οὐ γάρ ἐσμεν ὡς οἱ ⸀πολλοὶ καπηλεύοντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ, ἀλλʼ ὡς ἐξ εἰλικρινείας, ἀλλʼ ὡς ἐκ θεοῦ ⸀κατέναντι θεοῦ ἐν Χριστῷ λαλοῦμεν.
verses.translit: ou gar esmen os oi polloi kapileyontes ton logon tou theou, all' os ex eilikrineias, all' os ek theou katenanti theou en Hristo laloumen.
verses.translation: For we are not as many, which corrupt the word of God: but as of sincerity, but as of God, in the sight of God speak we in Christ.

verses.original: Ἀρχόμεθα πάλιν ἑαυτοὺς ⸀συνιστάνειν; ⸀ἢ μὴ χρῄζομεν ὥς τινες συστατικῶν ἐπιστολῶν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἢ ἐξ ⸀ὑμῶν;
verses.translit: Arhometha palin eaytous synistanein; e me hrezomen os tines systatikon epistolon pros umas e ex umon;
verses.translation: Do we begin again to commend ourselves? or need we, as some others , epistles of commendation to you, or letters of commendation from you?

verses.original: ἡ ἐπιστολὴ ἡμῶν ὑμεῖς ἐστε, ἐγγεγραμμένη ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἡμῶν, γινωσκομένη καὶ ἀναγινωσκομένη ὑπὸ πάντων ἀνθρώπων·
verses.translit: e epistole emon umeis este, eggegrammeni en tais kardiais emon, ginoskomeni kai anaginoskomeni upo panton anthropon*
verses.translation: Ye are our epistle written in our hearts, known and read of all men:

verses.original: φανερούμενοι ὅτι ἐστὲ ἐπιστολὴ Χριστοῦ διακονηθεῖσα ὑφʼ ἡμῶν, ἐγγεγραμμένη οὐ μέλανι ἀλλὰ πνεύματι θεοῦ ζῶντος, οὐκ ἐν πλαξὶν λιθίναις ἀλλʼ ἐν πλαξὶν καρδίαις σαρκίναις.
verses.translit: faneroymenoi oti este epistole Hristou diakonitheisa uf' emon, eggegrammeni ou melani alla pneymati theou zontos, ouk en plaxin lithinais all' en plaxin kardiais sarkinais.
verses.translation: Forasmuch as ye are manifestly declared to be the epistle of Christ ministered by us, written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God; not in tables of stone, but in fleshy tables of the heart.

verses.original: Πεποίθησιν δὲ τοιαύτην ἔχομεν διὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ πρὸς τὸν θεόν.
verses.translit: Pepoithisin de toiaytin ehomen dia tou Hristou pros ton theon.
verses.translation: And such trust have we through Christ to God-ward:

verses.original: οὐχ ὅτι ⸂ἀφʼ ἑαυτῶν ἱκανοί ἐσμεν⸃ λογίσασθαί τι ὡς ἐξ ⸀αὑτῶν, ἀλλʼ ἡ ἱκανότης ἡμῶν ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ,
verses.translit: ouh oti af' eayton ikanoi esmen logisasthai ti os ex auton, all' e ikanotis emon ek tou theou,
verses.translation: Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think any thing as of ourselves; but our sufficiency is of God;

verses.original: ὃς καὶ ἱκάνωσεν ἡμᾶς διακόνους καινῆς διαθήκης, οὐ γράμματος ἀλλὰ πνεύματος, τὸ γὰρ γράμμα ἀποκτέννει, τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα ζῳοποιεῖ.
verses.translit: os kai ikanosen emas diakonoys kaines diathikis, ou grammatos alla pneymatos, to gar gramma apoktennei, to de pneuma zoopoiei.
verses.translation: Who also hath made us able ministers of the new testament; not of the letter, but of the spirit: for the letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life.

verses.original: Εἰ δὲ ἡ διακονία τοῦ θανάτου ἐν ⸀γράμμασιν ⸀ἐντετυπωμένη λίθοις ἐγενήθη ἐν δόξῃ, ὥστε μὴ δύνασθαι ἀτενίσαι τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραὴλ εἰς τὸ πρόσωπον Μωϋσέως διὰ τὴν δόξαν τοῦ προσώπου αὐτοῦ τὴν καταργουμένην,
verses.translit: Ei de e diakonia tou thanatoy en grammasin entetypomeni lithois egenithi en doxe, oste me dynasthai atenisai tous yious Israel eis to prosopon Moyseos dia ten doxan tou prosopoy autou ten katargoymenin,
verses.translation: But if the ministration of death, written and engraven in stones, was glorious, so that the children of Israel could not stedfastly behold the face of Moses for the glory of his countenance; which glory was to be done away:

verses.original: πῶς οὐχὶ μᾶλλον ἡ διακονία τοῦ πνεύματος ἔσται ἐν δόξῃ;
verses.translit: pos ouhi mallon e diakonia tou pneymatos estai en doxe;
verses.translation: How shall not the ministration of the spirit be rather glorious?

verses.original: εἰ γὰρ ⸂τῇ διακονίᾳ⸃ τῆς κατακρίσεως δόξα, πολλῷ μᾶλλον περισσεύει ἡ διακονία τῆς ⸀δικαιοσύνης δόξῃ.
verses.translit: ei gar te diakonia tes katakriseos doxa, pollo mallon perisseyei e diakonia tes dikaiosynis doxe.
verses.translation: For if the ministration of condemnation be glory, much more doth the ministration of righteousness exceed in glory.

verses.original: καὶ γὰρ οὐ δεδόξασται τὸ δεδοξασμένον ἐν τούτῳ τῷ μέρει ⸀εἵνεκεν τῆς ὑπερβαλλούσης δόξης·
verses.translit: kai gar ou dedoxastai to dedoxasmenon en toyto to merei eineken tes upervalloysis doxis*
verses.translation: For even that which was made glorious had no glory in this respect, by reason of the glory that excelleth.

verses.original: εἰ γὰρ τὸ καταργούμενον διὰ δόξης, πολλῷ μᾶλλον τὸ μένον ἐν δόξῃ.
verses.translit: ei gar to katargoymenon dia doxis, pollo mallon to menon en doxe.
verses.translation: For if that which is done away was glorious, much more that which remaineth is glorious.

verses.original: Ἔχοντες οὖν τοιαύτην ἐλπίδα πολλῇ παρρησίᾳ χρώμεθα,
verses.translit: Ehontes oun toiaytin elpida polle parrisia hrometha,
verses.translation: Seeing then that we have such hope, we use great plainness of speech:

verses.original: καὶ οὐ καθάπερ Μωϋσῆς ἐτίθει κάλυμμα ἐπὶ τὸ πρόσωπον ⸀αὐτοῦ, πρὸς τὸ μὴ ἀτενίσαι τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραὴλ εἰς τὸ τέλος τοῦ καταργουμένου.
verses.translit: kai ou kathaper Moyses etithei kalymma epi to prosopon autou, pros to me atenisai tous yious Israel eis to telos tou katargoymenoy.
verses.translation: And not as Moses, which put a vail over his face, that the children of Israel could not stedfastly look to the end of that which is abolished:

verses.original: ἀλλὰ ἐπωρώθη τὰ νοήματα αὐτῶν. ἄχρι γὰρ τῆς σήμερον ⸀ἡμέρας τὸ αὐτὸ κάλυμμα ἐπὶ τῇ ἀναγνώσει τῆς παλαιᾶς διαθήκης μένει μὴ ἀνακαλυπτόμενον, ⸀ὅτι ἐν Χριστῷ καταργεῖται,
verses.translit: alla eporothi ta noimata auton. ahri gar tes simeron emeras to auto kalymma epi te anagnosei tes palaias diathikis menei me anakalyptomenon, oti en Hristo katargeitai,
verses.translation: But their minds were blinded: for until this day remaineth the same vail untaken away in the reading of the old testament; which vail is done away in Christ.

verses.original: ἀλλʼ ἕως σήμερον ἡνίκα ⸂ἂν ἀναγινώσκηται⸃ Μωϋσῆς κάλυμμα ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτῶν κεῖται·
verses.translit: all' eos simeron enika an anaginoskitai Moyses kalymma epi ten kardian auton keitai*
verses.translation: But even unto this day, when Moses is read, the vail is upon their heart.

verses.original: ἡνίκα ⸂δὲ ἐὰν⸃ ἐπιστρέψῃ πρὸς κύριον, περιαιρεῖται τὸ κάλυμμα.
verses.translit: enika de ean epistrepse pros kyrion, periaireitai to kalymma.
verses.translation: Nevertheless when it shall turn to the Lord, the vail shall be taken away.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ κύριος τὸ πνεῦμά ἐστιν· οὗ δὲ τὸ πνεῦμα ⸀κυρίου, ἐλευθερία.
verses.translit: o de kyrios to pneuma estin* ou de to pneuma kyrioy, eleytheria.
verses.translation: Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is , there is liberty.

verses.original: ἡμεῖς δὲ πάντες ἀνακεκαλυμμένῳ προσώπῳ τὴν δόξαν κυρίου κατοπτριζόμενοι τὴν αὐτὴν εἰκόνα μεταμορφούμεθα ἀπὸ δόξης εἰς δόξαν, καθάπερ ἀπὸ κυρίου πνεύματος.
verses.translit: emeis de pantes anakekalymmeno prosopo ten doxan kyrioy katoptrizomenoi ten auten eikona metamorfoymetha apo doxis eis doxan, kathaper apo kyrioy pneymatos.
verses.translation: But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord.

verses.original: Διὰ τοῦτο, ἔχοντες τὴν διακονίαν ταύτην καθὼς ἠλεήθημεν, οὐκ ⸀ἐγκακοῦμεν,
verses.translit: Dia touto, ehontes ten diakonian taytin kathos eleithimen, ouk egkakoumen,
verses.translation: Therefore seeing we have this ministry, as we have received mercy, we faint not;

verses.original: ἀλλὰ ἀπειπάμεθα τὰ κρυπτὰ τῆς αἰσχύνης, μὴ περιπατοῦντες ἐν πανουργίᾳ μηδὲ δολοῦντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ, ἀλλὰ τῇ φανερώσει τῆς ἀληθείας ⸀συνιστάνοντες ἑαυτοὺς πρὸς πᾶσαν συνείδησιν ἀνθρώπων ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: alla apeipametha ta krypta tes aishynis, me peripatountes en panoyrgia mide dolountes ton logon tou theou, alla te fanerosei tes alitheias synistanontes eaytous pros pasan syneidisin anthropon enopion tou theou.
verses.translation: But have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty, not walking in craftiness, nor handling the word of God deceitfully; but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God.

verses.original: εἰ δὲ καὶ ἔστιν κεκαλυμμένον τὸ εὐαγγέλιον ἡμῶν, ἐν τοῖς ἀπολλυμένοις ἐστὶν κεκαλυμμένον,
verses.translit: ei de kai estin kekalymmenon to euaggelion emon, en tois apollymenois estin kekalymmenon,
verses.translation: But if our gospel be hid, it is hid to them that are lost:

verses.original: ἐν οἷς ὁ θεὸς τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου ἐτύφλωσεν τὰ νοήματα τῶν ἀπίστων εἰς τὸ μὴ ⸀αὐγάσαι τὸν φωτισμὸν τοῦ εὐαγγελίου τῆς δόξης τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὅς ἐστιν εἰκὼν τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: en ois o theos tou aionos toytoy etyflosen ta noimata ton apiston eis to me augasai ton fotismon tou euaggelioy tes doxis tou Hristou, os estin eikon tou theou.
verses.translation: In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them.

verses.original: οὐ γὰρ ἑαυτοὺς κηρύσσομεν ἀλλὰ ⸂Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν⸃ κύριον, ἑαυτοὺς δὲ δούλους ὑμῶν διὰ Ἰησοῦν.
verses.translit: ou gar eaytous kiryssomen alla Hriston Iisoun kyrion, eaytous de doyloys umon dia Iisoun.
verses.translation: For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus’ sake.

verses.original: ὅτι ὁ θεὸς ὁ εἰπών· Ἐκ σκότους φῶς ⸀λάμψει, ὃς ἔλαμψεν ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἡμῶν πρὸς φωτισμὸν τῆς γνώσεως τῆς δόξης τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν προσώπῳ ⸀Χριστοῦ.
verses.translit: oti o theos o eipon* Ek skotoys fos lampsei, os elampsen en tais kardiais emon pros fotismon tes gnoseos tes doxis tou theou en prosopo Hristou.
verses.translation: For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.

verses.original: Ἔχομεν δὲ τὸν θησαυρὸν τοῦτον ἐν ὀστρακίνοις σκεύεσιν, ἵνα ἡ ὑπερβολὴ τῆς δυνάμεως ᾖ τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ μὴ ἐξ ἡμῶν·
verses.translit: Ehomen de ton thisayron touton en ostrakinois skeyesin, ina e upervole tes dynameos e tou theou kai me ex emon*
verses.translation: But we have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the excellency of the power may be of God, and not of us.

verses.original: ἐν παντὶ θλιβόμενοι ἀλλʼ οὐ στενοχωρούμενοι, ἀπορούμενοι ἀλλʼ οὐκ ἐξαπορούμενοι,
verses.translit: en panti thlivomenoi all' ou stenohoroymenoi, aporoymenoi all' ouk exaporoymenoi,
verses.translation: We are troubled on every side, yet not distressed; we are perplexed, but not in despair;

verses.original: διωκόμενοι ἀλλʼ οὐκ ἐγκαταλειπόμενοι, καταβαλλόμενοι ἀλλʼ οὐκ ἀπολλύμενοι,
verses.translit: diokomenoi all' ouk egkataleipomenoi, katavallomenoi all' ouk apollymenoi,
verses.translation: Persecuted, but not forsaken; cast down, but not destroyed;

verses.original: πάντοτε τὴν νέκρωσιν ⸀τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐν τῷ σώματι περιφέροντες, ἵνα καὶ ἡ ζωὴ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐν τῷ σώματι ἡμῶν φανερωθῇ·
verses.translit: pantote ten nekrosin tou Iisou en to somati periferontes, ina kai e zoe tou Iisou en to somati emon fanerothe*
verses.translation: Always bearing about in the body the dying of the Lord Jesus, that the life also of Jesus might be made manifest in our body.

verses.original: ἀεὶ γὰρ ἡμεῖς οἱ ζῶντες εἰς θάνατον παραδιδόμεθα διὰ Ἰησοῦν, ἵνα καὶ ἡ ζωὴ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ φανερωθῇ ἐν τῇ θνητῇ σαρκὶ ἡμῶν.
verses.translit: aei gar emeis oi zontes eis thanaton paradidometha dia Iisoun, ina kai e zoe tou Iisou fanerothe en te thnite sarki emon.
verses.translation: For we which live are alway delivered unto death for Jesus’ sake, that the life also of Jesus might be made manifest in our mortal flesh.

verses.original: ὥστε ⸀ὁ θάνατος ἐν ἡμῖν ἐνεργεῖται, ἡ δὲ ζωὴ ἐν ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: oste o thanatos en emin energeitai, e de zoe en umin.
verses.translation: So then death worketh in us, but life in you.

verses.original: Ἔχοντες δὲ τὸ αὐτὸ πνεῦμα τῆς πίστεως, κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον· Ἐπίστευσα, διὸ ἐλάλησα, καὶ ἡμεῖς πιστεύομεν, διὸ καὶ λαλοῦμεν,
verses.translit: Ehontes de to auto pneuma tes pisteos, kata to gegrammenon* Episteysa, dio elalisa, kai emeis pisteyomen, dio kai laloumen,
verses.translation: We having the same spirit of faith, according as it is written, I believed, and therefore have I spoken; we also believe, and therefore speak;

verses.original: εἰδότες ὅτι ὁ ἐγείρας ⸀τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἡμᾶς ⸀σὺν Ἰησοῦ ἐγερεῖ καὶ παραστήσει σὺν ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: eidotes oti o egeiras ton Iisoun kai emas sun Iisou egerei kai parastisei sun umin.
verses.translation: Knowing that he which raised up the Lord Jesus shall raise up us also by Jesus, and shall present us with you.

verses.original: τὰ γὰρ πάντα διʼ ὑμᾶς, ἵνα ἡ χάρις πλεονάσασα διὰ τῶν πλειόνων τὴν εὐχαριστίαν περισσεύσῃ εἰς τὴν δόξαν τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: ta gar panta di' umas, ina e haris pleonasasa dia ton pleionon ten euharistian perisseyse eis ten doxan tou theou.
verses.translation: For all things are for your sakes, that the abundant grace might through the thanksgiving of many redound to the glory of God.

verses.original: Διὸ οὐκ ⸀ἐγκακοῦμεν, ἀλλʼ εἰ καὶ ὁ ἔξω ἡμῶν ἄνθρωπος διαφθείρεται, ἀλλʼ ὁ ⸂ἔσω ἡμῶν⸃ ἀνακαινοῦται ἡμέρᾳ καὶ ἡμέρᾳ.
verses.translit: Dio ouk egkakoumen, all' ei kai o exo emon anthropos diaftheiretai, all' o eso emon anakainoutai emera kai emera.
verses.translation: For which cause we faint not; but though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day.

verses.original: τὸ γὰρ παραυτίκα ἐλαφρὸν τῆς θλίψεως ⸀ἡμῶν καθʼ ὑπερβολὴν εἰς ὑπερβολὴν αἰώνιον βάρος δόξης κατεργάζεται ἡμῖν,
verses.translit: to gar paraytika elafron tes thlipseos emon kath' upervolen eis upervolen aionion varos doxis katergazetai emin,
verses.translation: For our light affliction, which is but for a moment, worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory;

verses.original: μὴ σκοπούντων ἡμῶν τὰ βλεπόμενα ἀλλὰ τὰ μὴ βλεπόμενα, τὰ γὰρ βλεπόμενα πρόσκαιρα, τὰ δὲ μὴ βλεπόμενα αἰώνια.
verses.translit: me skopoynton emon ta vlepomena alla ta me vlepomena, ta gar vlepomena proskaira, ta de me vlepomena aionia.
verses.translation: While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen are temporal; but the things which are not seen are eternal.

verses.original: Οἴδαμεν γὰρ ὅτι ἐὰν ἡ ἐπίγειος ἡμῶν οἰκία τοῦ σκήνους καταλυθῇ, οἰκοδομὴν ἐκ θεοῦ ἔχομεν οἰκίαν ἀχειροποίητον αἰώνιον ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.
verses.translit: Oidamen gar oti ean e epigeios emon oikia tou skinoys katalythe, oikodomen ek theou ehomen oikian aheiropoiiton aionion en tois ouranois.
verses.translation: For we know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved, we have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.

verses.original: καὶ γὰρ ἐν τούτῳ στενάζομεν, τὸ οἰκητήριον ἡμῶν τὸ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐπενδύσασθαι ἐπιποθοῦντες,
verses.translit: kai gar en toyto stenazomen, to oikitirion emon to ex ouranou ependysasthai epipothountes,
verses.translation: For in this we groan, earnestly desiring to be clothed upon with our house which is from heaven:

verses.original: ⸂εἴ γε⸃ καὶ ⸀ἐνδυσάμενοι οὐ γυμνοὶ εὑρεθησόμεθα.
verses.translit: ei ge kai endysamenoi ou gymnoi eurethisometha.
verses.translation: If so be that being clothed we shall not be found naked.

verses.original: καὶ γὰρ οἱ ὄντες ἐν τῷ σκήνει στενάζομεν βαρούμενοι ἐφʼ ᾧ οὐ θέλομεν ἐκδύσασθαι ἀλλʼ ἐπενδύσασθαι, ἵνα καταποθῇ τὸ θνητὸν ὑπὸ τῆς ζωῆς.
verses.translit: kai gar oi ontes en to skinei stenazomen varoymenoi ef' o ou thelomen ekdysasthai all' ependysasthai, ina katapothe to thniton upo tes zoes.
verses.translation: For we that are in this tabernacle do groan, being burdened: not for that we would be unclothed, but clothed upon, that mortality might be swallowed up of life.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ κατεργασάμενος ἡμᾶς εἰς αὐτὸ τοῦτο θεός, ⸀ὁ δοὺς ἡμῖν τὸν ἀρραβῶνα τοῦ πνεύματος.
verses.translit: o de katergasamenos emas eis auto touto theos, o dous emin ton arravona tou pneymatos.
verses.translation: Now he that hath wrought us for the selfsame thing is God, who also hath given unto us the earnest of the Spirit.

verses.original: Θαρροῦντες οὖν πάντοτε καὶ εἰδότες ὅτι ἐνδημοῦντες ἐν τῷ σώματι ἐκδημοῦμεν ἀπὸ τοῦ κυρίου,
verses.translit: Tharrountes oun pantote kai eidotes oti endimountes en to somati ekdimoumen apo tou kyrioy,
verses.translation: Therefore we are always confident, knowing that, whilst we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord:

verses.original: διὰ πίστεως γὰρ περιπατοῦμεν, οὐ διὰ εἴδους—
verses.translit: dia pisteos gar peripatoumen, ou dia eidoys--
verses.translation: (For we walk by faith, not by sight:)

verses.original: θαρροῦμεν δὲ καὶ εὐδοκοῦμεν μᾶλλον ἐκδημῆσαι ἐκ τοῦ σώματος καὶ ἐνδημῆσαι πρὸς τὸν κύριον·
verses.translit: tharroumen de kai eudokoumen mallon ekdimesai ek tou somatos kai endimesai pros ton kyrion*
verses.translation: We are confident, I say , and willing rather to be absent from the body, and to be present with the Lord.

verses.original: διὸ καὶ φιλοτιμούμεθα, εἴτε ἐνδημοῦντες εἴτε ἐκδημοῦντες, εὐάρεστοι αὐτῷ εἶναι.
verses.translit: dio kai filotimoymetha, eite endimountes eite ekdimountes, euarestoi auto einai.
verses.translation: Wherefore we labour, that, whether present or absent, we may be accepted of him.

verses.original: τοὺς γὰρ πάντας ἡμᾶς φανερωθῆναι δεῖ ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ βήματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἵνα κομίσηται ἕκαστος τὰ διὰ τοῦ σώματος πρὸς ἃ ἔπραξεν, εἴτε ἀγαθὸν εἴτε ⸀φαῦλον.
verses.translit: tous gar pantas emas fanerothenai dei emprosthen tou vimatos tou Hristou, ina komisitai ekastos ta dia tou somatos pros a epraxen, eite agathon eite faulon.
verses.translation: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad.

verses.original: Εἰδότες οὖν τὸν φόβον τοῦ κυρίου ἀνθρώπους πείθομεν, θεῷ δὲ πεφανερώμεθα· ἐλπίζω δὲ καὶ ἐν ταῖς συνειδήσεσιν ὑμῶν πεφανερῶσθαι.
verses.translit: Eidotes oun ton fovon tou kyrioy anthropoys peithomen, theo de pefanerometha* elpizo de kai en tais syneidisesin umon pefanerosthai.
verses.translation: Knowing therefore the terror of the Lord, we persuade men; but we are made manifest unto God; and I trust also are made manifest in your consciences.

verses.original: ⸀οὐ πάλιν ἑαυτοὺς συνιστάνομεν ὑμῖν, ἀλλὰ ἀφορμὴν διδόντες ὑμῖν καυχήματος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν, ἵνα ἔχητε πρὸς τοὺς ἐν προσώπῳ καυχωμένους καὶ ⸂μὴ ἐν⸃ καρδίᾳ.
verses.translit: ou palin eaytous synistanomen umin, alla aformen didontes umin kayhimatos uper emon, ina ehite pros tous en prosopo kayhomenoys kai me en kardia.
verses.translation: For we commend not ourselves again unto you, but give you occasion to glory on our behalf, that ye may have somewhat to answer them which glory in appearance, and not in heart.

verses.original: εἴτε γὰρ ἐξέστημεν, θεῷ· εἴτε σωφρονοῦμεν, ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: eite gar exestimen, theo* eite sofronoumen, umin.
verses.translation: For whether we be beside ourselves, it is to God: or whether we be sober, it is for your cause.

verses.original: ἡ γὰρ ἀγάπη τοῦ Χριστοῦ συνέχει ἡμᾶς, κρίναντας τοῦτο ⸀ὅτι εἷς ὑπὲρ πάντων ἀπέθανεν· ἄρα οἱ πάντες ἀπέθανον·
verses.translit: e gar agapi tou Hristou synehei emas, krinantas touto oti eis uper panton apethanen* ara oi pantes apethanon*
verses.translation: For the love of Christ constraineth us; because we thus judge, that if one died for all, then were all dead:

verses.original: καὶ ὑπὲρ πάντων ἀπέθανεν ἵνα οἱ ζῶντες μηκέτι ἑαυτοῖς ζῶσιν ἀλλὰ τῷ ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν ἀποθανόντι καὶ ἐγερθέντι.
verses.translit: kai uper panton apethanen ina oi zontes miketi eaytois zosin alla to uper auton apothanonti kai egerthenti.
verses.translation: And that he died for all, that they which live should not henceforth live unto themselves, but unto him which died for them, and rose again.

verses.original: Ὥστε ἡμεῖς ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν οὐδένα οἴδαμεν κατὰ σάρκα· ⸀εἰ καὶ ἐγνώκαμεν κατὰ σάρκα Χριστόν, ἀλλὰ νῦν οὐκέτι γινώσκομεν.
verses.translit: Oste emeis apo tou nun oudena oidamen kata sarka* ei kai egnokamen kata sarka Hriston, alla nun ouketi ginoskomen.
verses.translation: Wherefore henceforth know we no man after the flesh: yea, though we have known Christ after the flesh, yet now henceforth know we him no more.

verses.original: ὥστε εἴ τις ἐν Χριστῷ, καινὴ κτίσις· τὰ ἀρχαῖα παρῆλθεν, ἰδοὺ γέγονεν ⸀καινά·
verses.translit: oste ei tis en Hristo, kaine ktisis* ta arhaia parelthen, idou gegonen kaina*
verses.translation: Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.

verses.original: τὰ δὲ πάντα ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ καταλλάξαντος ἡμᾶς ἑαυτῷ ⸀διὰ Χριστοῦ καὶ δόντος ἡμῖν τὴν διακονίαν τῆς καταλλαγῆς,
verses.translit: ta de panta ek tou theou tou katallaxantos emas eayto dia Hristou kai dontos emin ten diakonian tes katallages,
verses.translation: And all things are of God, who hath reconciled us to himself by Jesus Christ, and hath given to us the ministry of reconciliation;

verses.original: ὡς ὅτι θεὸς ἦν ἐν Χριστῷ κόσμον καταλλάσσων ἑαυτῷ, μὴ λογιζόμενος αὐτοῖς τὰ παραπτώματα αὐτῶν, καὶ θέμενος ἐν ἡμῖν τὸν λόγον τῆς καταλλαγῆς.
verses.translit: os oti theos en en Hristo kosmon katallasson eayto, me logizomenos autois ta paraptomata auton, kai themenos en emin ton logon tes katallages.
verses.translation: To wit, that God was in Christ, reconciling the world unto himself, not imputing their trespasses unto them; and hath committed unto us the word of reconciliation.

verses.original: ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ οὖν πρεσβεύομεν ὡς τοῦ θεοῦ παρακαλοῦντος διʼ ἡμῶν· δεόμεθα ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ, καταλλάγητε τῷ θεῷ.
verses.translit: uper Hristou oun presveyomen os tou theou parakalountos di' emon* deometha uper Hristou, katallagite to theo.
verses.translation: Now then we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God did beseech you by us: we pray you in Christ’s stead, be ye reconciled to God.

verses.original: ⸀τὸν μὴ γνόντα ἁμαρτίαν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἁμαρτίαν ἐποίησεν, ἵνα ἡμεῖς γενώμεθα δικαιοσύνη θεοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: ton me gnonta amartian uper emon amartian epoiisen, ina emeis genometha dikaiosyni theou en auto.
verses.translation: For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.

verses.original: Συνεργοῦντες δὲ καὶ παρακαλοῦμεν μὴ εἰς κενὸν τὴν χάριν τοῦ θεοῦ δέξασθαι ὑμᾶς·
verses.translit: Synergountes de kai parakaloumen me eis kenon ten harin tou theou dexasthai umas*
verses.translation: We then, as workers together with him , beseech you also that ye receive not the grace of God in vain.

verses.original: λέγει γάρ· Καιρῷ δεκτῷ ἐπήκουσά σου καὶ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ σωτηρίας ἐβοήθησά σοι· ἰδοὺ νῦν καιρὸς εὐπρόσδεκτος, ἰδοὺ νῦν ἡμέρα σωτηρίας·
verses.translit: legei gar* Kairo dekto epikoysa soy kai en emera sotirias evoithisa soi* idou nun kairos euprosdektos, idou nun emera sotirias*
verses.translation: (For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.)

verses.original: μηδεμίαν ἐν μηδενὶ διδόντες προσκοπήν, ἵνα μὴ μωμηθῇ ἡ διακονία,
verses.translit: midemian en mideni didontes proskopin, ina me momithe e diakonia,
verses.translation: Giving no offence in any thing, that the ministry be not blamed:

verses.original: ἀλλʼ ἐν παντὶ ⸀συνιστάνοντες ἑαυτοὺς ὡς θεοῦ διάκονοι· ἐν ὑπομονῇ πολλῇ, ἐν θλίψεσιν, ἐν ἀνάγκαις, ἐν στενοχωρίαις,
verses.translit: all' en panti synistanontes eaytous os theou diakonoi* en upomone polle, en thlipsesin, en anagkais, en stenohoriais,
verses.translation: But in all things approving ourselves as the ministers of God, in much patience, in afflictions, in necessities, in distresses,

verses.original: ἐν πληγαῖς, ἐν φυλακαῖς, ἐν ἀκαταστασίαις, ἐν κόποις, ἐν ἀγρυπνίαις, ἐν νηστείαις,
verses.translit: en pligais, en fylakais, en akatastasiais, en kopois, en agrypniais, en nisteiais,
verses.translation: In stripes, in imprisonments, in tumults, in labours, in watchings, in fastings;

verses.original: ἐν ἁγνότητι, ἐν γνώσει, ἐν μακροθυμίᾳ, ἐν χρηστότητι, ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ, ἐν ἀγάπῃ ἀνυποκρίτῳ,
verses.translit: en agnotiti, en gnosei, en makrothymia, en hristotiti, en pneymati agio, en agape anypokrito,
verses.translation: By pureness, by knowledge, by longsuffering, by kindness, by the Holy Ghost, by love unfeigned,

verses.original: ἐν λόγῳ ἀληθείας, ἐν δυνάμει θεοῦ· διὰ τῶν ὅπλων τῆς δικαιοσύνης τῶν δεξιῶν καὶ ἀριστερῶν,
verses.translit: en logo alitheias, en dynamei theou* dia ton oplon tes dikaiosynis ton dexion kai aristeron,
verses.translation: By the word of truth, by the power of God, by the armour of righteousness on the right hand and on the left,

verses.original: διὰ δόξης καὶ ἀτιμίας, διὰ δυσφημίας καὶ εὐφημίας· ὡς πλάνοι καὶ ἀληθεῖς,
verses.translit: dia doxis kai atimias, dia dysfimias kai eufimias* os planoi kai alitheis,
verses.translation: By honour and dishonour, by evil report and good report: as deceivers, and yet true;

verses.original: ὡς ἀγνοούμενοι καὶ ἐπιγινωσκόμενοι, ὡς ἀποθνῄσκοντες καὶ ἰδοὺ ζῶμεν, ὡς παιδευόμενοι καὶ μὴ θανατούμενοι,
verses.translit: os agnooymenoi kai epiginoskomenoi, os apothneskontes kai idou zomen, os paideyomenoi kai me thanatoymenoi,
verses.translation: As unknown, and yet well known; as dying, and, behold, we live; as chastened, and not killed;

verses.original: ὡς λυπούμενοι ἀεὶ δὲ χαίροντες, ὡς πτωχοὶ πολλοὺς δὲ πλουτίζοντες, ὡς μηδὲν ἔχοντες καὶ πάντα κατέχοντες.
verses.translit: os lypoymenoi aei de hairontes, os ptohoi pollous de ploytizontes, os miden ehontes kai panta katehontes.
verses.translation: As sorrowful, yet alway rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing all things.

verses.original: Τὸ στόμα ἡμῶν ἀνέῳγεν πρὸς ὑμᾶς, Κορίνθιοι, ἡ καρδία ἡμῶν πεπλάτυνται·
verses.translit: To stoma emon aneogen pros umas, Korinthioi, e kardia emon peplatyntai*
verses.translation: O ye Corinthians, our mouth is open unto you, our heart is enlarged.

verses.original: οὐ στενοχωρεῖσθε ἐν ἡμῖν, στενοχωρεῖσθε δὲ ἐν τοῖς σπλάγχνοις ὑμῶν·
verses.translit: ou stenohoreisthe en emin, stenohoreisthe de en tois splaghnois umon*
verses.translation: Ye are not straitened in us, but ye are straitened in your own bowels.

verses.original: τὴν δὲ αὐτὴν ἀντιμισθίαν, ὡς τέκνοις λέγω, πλατύνθητε καὶ ὑμεῖς.
verses.translit: ten de auten antimisthian, os teknois lego, platynthite kai umeis.
verses.translation: Now for a recompence in the same, (I speak as unto my children,) be ye also enlarged.

verses.original: Μὴ γίνεσθε ἑτεροζυγοῦντες ἀπίστοις· τίς γὰρ μετοχὴ δικαιοσύνῃ καὶ ἀνομίᾳ, ⸂ἢ τίς⸃ κοινωνία φωτὶ πρὸς σκότος;
verses.translit: Me ginesthe eterozygountes apistois* tis gar metohe dikaiosyne kai anomia, e tis koinonia foti pros skotos;
verses.translation: Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness?

verses.original: τίς δὲ συμφώνησις ⸀Χριστοῦ πρὸς Βελιάρ, ἢ τίς μερὶς πιστῷ μετὰ ἀπίστου;
verses.translit: tis de symfonisis Hristou pros Veliar, e tis meris pisto meta apistoy;
verses.translation: And what concord hath Christ with Belial? or what part hath he that believeth with an infidel?

verses.original: τίς δὲ συγκατάθεσις ναῷ θεοῦ μετὰ εἰδώλων; ⸂ἡμεῖς γὰρ ναὸς θεοῦ ἐσμεν⸃ ζῶντος· καθὼς εἶπεν ὁ θεὸς ὅτι Ἐνοικήσω ἐν αὐτοῖς καὶ ἐμπεριπατήσω, καὶ ἔσομαι αὐτῶν θεός, καὶ αὐτοὶ ἔσονταί ⸀μου λαός.
verses.translit: tis de sygkatathesis nao theou meta eidolon; emeis gar naos theou esmen zontos* kathos eipen o theos oti Enoikiso en autois kai emperipatiso, kai esomai auton theos, kai autoi esontai moy laos.
verses.translation: And what agreement hath the temple of God with idols? for ye are the temple of the living God; as God hath said, I will dwell in them, and walk in them ; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.

verses.original: διὸ ἐξέλθατε ἐκ μέσου αὐτῶν, καὶ ἀφορίσθητε, λέγει κύριος, καὶ ἀκαθάρτου μὴ ἅπτεσθε· κἀγὼ εἰσδέξομαι ὑμᾶς·
verses.translit: dio exelthate ek mesoy auton, kai aforisthite, legei kyrios, kai akathartoy me aptesthe* kago eisdexomai umas*
verses.translation: Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing ; and I will receive you,

verses.original: καὶ ἔσομαι ὑμῖν εἰς πατέρα, καὶ ὑμεῖς ἔσεσθέ μοι εἰς υἱοὺς καὶ θυγατέρας, λέγει κύριος παντοκράτωρ.
verses.translit: kai esomai umin eis patera, kai umeis esesthe moi eis yious kai thygateras, legei kyrios pantokrator.
verses.translation: And will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters, saith the Lord Almighty.

verses.original: ταύτας οὖν ἔχοντες τὰς ἐπαγγελίας, ἀγαπητοί, καθαρίσωμεν ἑαυτοὺς ἀπὸ παντὸς μολυσμοῦ σαρκὸς καὶ πνεύματος, ἐπιτελοῦντες ἁγιωσύνην ἐν φόβῳ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: taytas oun ehontes tas epaggelias, agapitoi, katharisomen eaytous apo pantos molysmou sarkos kai pneymatos, epitelountes agiosynin en fovo theou.
verses.translation: Having therefore these promises, dearly beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all filthiness of the flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.

verses.original: Χωρήσατε ἡμᾶς· οὐδένα ἠδικήσαμεν, οὐδένα ἐφθείραμεν, οὐδένα ἐπλεονεκτήσαμεν.
verses.translit: Horisate emas* oudena edikisamen, oudena eftheiramen, oudena epleonektisamen.
verses.translation: Receive us; we have wronged no man, we have corrupted no man, we have defrauded no man.

verses.original: ⸂πρὸς κατάκρισιν οὐ⸃ λέγω, προείρηκα γὰρ ὅτι ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἡμῶν ἐστε εἰς τὸ συναποθανεῖν καὶ συζῆν.
verses.translit: pros katakrisin ou lego, proeirika gar oti en tais kardiais emon este eis to synapothanein kai syzen.
verses.translation: I speak not this to condemn you : for I have said before, that ye are in our hearts to die and live with you .

verses.original: πολλή μοι παρρησία πρὸς ὑμᾶς, πολλή μοι καύχησις ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν· πεπλήρωμαι τῇ παρακλήσει, ὑπερπερισσεύομαι τῇ χαρᾷ ἐπὶ πάσῃ τῇ θλίψει ἡμῶν.
verses.translit: polli moi parrisia pros umas, polli moi kayhisis uper umon* pepliromai te paraklisei, uperperisseyomai te hara epi pase te thlipsei emon.
verses.translation: Great is my boldness of speech toward you, great is my glorying of you: I am filled with comfort, I am exceeding joyful in all our tribulation.

verses.original: Καὶ γὰρ ἐλθόντων ἡμῶν εἰς Μακεδονίαν οὐδεμίαν ⸀ἔσχηκεν ἄνεσιν ἡ σὰρξ ἡμῶν, ἀλλʼ ἐν παντὶ θλιβόμενοι— ἔξωθεν μάχαι, ἔσωθεν φόβοι—
verses.translit: Kai gar elthonton emon eis Makedonian oudemian eshiken anesin e sarx emon, all' en panti thlivomenoi-- exothen mahai, esothen fovoi--
verses.translation: For, when we were come into Macedonia, our flesh had no rest, but we were troubled on every side; without were fightings, within were fears.

verses.original: ἀλλʼ ὁ παρακαλῶν τοὺς ταπεινοὺς παρεκάλεσεν ἡμᾶς ὁ θεὸς ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ Τίτου·
verses.translit: all' o parakalon tous tapeinous parekalesen emas o theos en te paroysia Titoy*
verses.translation: Nevertheless God, that comforteth those that are cast down, comforted us by the coming of Titus;

verses.original: οὐ μόνον δὲ ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ αὐτοῦ, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν τῇ παρακλήσει ᾗ παρεκλήθη ἐφʼ ὑμῖν, ἀναγγέλλων ἡμῖν τὴν ὑμῶν ἐπιπόθησιν, τὸν ὑμῶν ὀδυρμόν, τὸν ὑμῶν ζῆλον ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ, ὥστε με μᾶλλον χαρῆναι.
verses.translit: ou monon de en te paroysia autou, alla kai en te paraklisei e pareklithi ef' umin, anaggellon emin ten umon epipothisin, ton umon odyrmon, ton umon zelon uper emou, oste me mallon harenai.
verses.translation: And not by his coming only, but by the consolation wherewith he was comforted in you, when he told us your earnest desire, your mourning, your fervent mind toward me; so that I rejoiced the more.

verses.original: ὅτι εἰ καὶ ἐλύπησα ὑμᾶς ἐν τῇ ἐπιστολῇ, οὐ μεταμέλομαι· εἰ καὶ μετεμελόμην (⸀βλέπω ὅτι ἡ ἐπιστολὴ ἐκείνη εἰ καὶ πρὸς ὥραν ἐλύπησεν ὑμᾶς),
verses.translit: oti ei kai elypisa umas en te epistole, ou metamelomai* ei kai metemelomin (vlepo oti e epistole ekeini ei kai pros oran elypisen umas),
verses.translation: For though I made you sorry with a letter, I do not repent, though I did repent: for I perceive that the same epistle hath made you sorry, though it were but for a season.

verses.original: νῦν χαίρω, οὐχ ὅτι ἐλυπήθητε, ἀλλʼ ὅτι ἐλυπήθητε εἰς μετάνοιαν, ἐλυπήθητε γὰρ κατὰ θεόν, ἵνα ἐν μηδενὶ ζημιωθῆτε ἐξ ἡμῶν.
verses.translit: nun hairo, ouh oti elypithite, all' oti elypithite eis metanoian, elypithite gar kata theon, ina en mideni zimiothete ex emon.
verses.translation: Now I rejoice, not that ye were made sorry, but that ye sorrowed to repentance: for ye were made sorry after a godly manner, that ye might receive damage by us in nothing.

verses.original: ἡ γὰρ κατὰ θεὸν λύπη μετάνοιαν εἰς σωτηρίαν ἀμεταμέλητον ⸀ἐργάζεται· ἡ δὲ τοῦ κόσμου λύπη θάνατον κατεργάζεται.
verses.translit: e gar kata theon lypi metanoian eis sotirian ametameliton ergazetai* e de tou kosmoy lypi thanaton katergazetai.
verses.translation: For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.

verses.original: ἰδοὺ γὰρ αὐτὸ τοῦτο τὸ κατὰ θεὸν ⸀λυπηθῆναι πόσην κατειργάσατο ὑμῖν σπουδήν, ἀλλὰ ἀπολογίαν, ἀλλὰ ἀγανάκτησιν, ἀλλὰ φόβον, ἀλλὰ ἐπιπόθησιν, ἀλλὰ ζῆλον, ἀλλὰ ἐκδίκησιν· ἐν παντὶ συνεστήσατε ἑαυτοὺς ἁγνοὺς ⸀εἶναι τῷ πράγματι.
verses.translit: idou gar auto touto to kata theon lypithenai posin kateirgasato umin spoydin, alla apologian, alla aganaktisin, alla fovon, alla epipothisin, alla zelon, alla ekdikisin* en panti synestisate eaytous agnous einai to pragmati.
verses.translation: For behold this selfsame thing, that ye sorrowed after a godly sort, what carefulness it wrought in you, yea, what clearing of yourselves, yea, what indignation, yea, what fear, yea, what vehement desire, yea, what zeal, yea, what revenge! In all things ye have approved yourselves to be clear in this matter.

verses.original: ἄρα εἰ καὶ ἔγραψα ὑμῖν, οὐχ ⸀ἕνεκεν τοῦ ἀδικήσαντος, ⸀οὐδὲ ⸁ἕνεκεν τοῦ ἀδικηθέντος, ἀλλʼ ⸀1ἕνεκεν τοῦ φανερωθῆναι τὴν σπουδὴν ὑμῶν τὴν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: ara ei kai egrapsa umin, ouh eneken tou adikisantos, oude eneken tou adikithentos, all' 1eneken tou fanerothenai ten spoyden umon ten uper emon pros umas enopion tou theou.
verses.translation: Wherefore, though I wrote unto you, I did it not for his cause that had done the wrong, nor for his cause that suffered wrong, but that our care for you in the sight of God might appear unto you.

verses.original: διὰ τοῦτο παρακεκλήμεθα. Ἐπὶ δὲ τῇ παρακλήσει ⸀ἡμῶν περισσοτέρως μᾶλλον ἐχάρημεν ἐπὶ τῇ χαρᾷ Τίτου, ὅτι ἀναπέπαυται τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ πάντων ὑμῶν·
verses.translit: dia touto parakeklimetha. Epi de te paraklisei emon perissoteros mallon eharimen epi te hara Titoy, oti anapepaytai to pneuma autou apo panton umon*
verses.translation: Therefore we were comforted in your comfort: yea, and exceedingly the more joyed we for the joy of Titus, because his spirit was refreshed by you all.

verses.original: ὅτι εἴ τι αὐτῷ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν κεκαύχημαι, οὐ κατῃσχύνθην, ἀλλʼ ὡς πάντα ἐν ἀληθείᾳ ἐλαλήσαμεν ὑμῖν, οὕτως καὶ ἡ καύχησις ἡμῶν ⸀ἡ ἐπὶ Τίτου ἀλήθεια ἐγενήθη.
verses.translit: oti ei ti auto uper umon kekayhimai, ou kateshynthin, all' os panta en alitheia elalisamen umin, outos kai e kayhisis emon e epi Titoy alitheia egenithi.
verses.translation: For if I have boasted any thing to him of you, I am not ashamed; but as we spake all things to you in truth, even so our boasting, which I made before Titus, is found a truth.

verses.original: καὶ τὰ σπλάγχνα αὐτοῦ περισσοτέρως εἰς ὑμᾶς ἐστιν ἀναμιμνῃσκομένου τὴν πάντων ὑμῶν ὑπακοήν, ὡς μετὰ φόβου καὶ τρόμου ἐδέξασθε αὐτόν.
verses.translit: kai ta splaghna autou perissoteros eis umas estin anamimneskomenoy ten panton umon upakoin, os meta fovoy kai tromoy edexasthe auton.
verses.translation: And his inward affection is more abundant toward you, whilst he remembereth the obedience of you all, how with fear and trembling ye received him.

verses.original: χαίρω ὅτι ἐν παντὶ θαρρῶ ἐν ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: hairo oti en panti tharro en umin.
verses.translation: I rejoice therefore that I have confidence in you in all things.

verses.original: Γνωρίζομεν δὲ ὑμῖν, ἀδελφοί, τὴν χάριν τοῦ θεοῦ τὴν δεδομένην ἐν ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τῆς Μακεδονίας,
verses.translit: Gnorizomen de umin, adelfoi, ten harin tou theou ten dedomenin en tais ekklisiais tes Makedonias,
verses.translation: Moreover, brethren, we do you to wit of the grace of God bestowed on the churches of Macedonia;

verses.original: ὅτι ἐν πολλῇ δοκιμῇ θλίψεως ἡ περισσεία τῆς χαρᾶς αὐτῶν καὶ ἡ κατὰ βάθους πτωχεία αὐτῶν ἐπερίσσευσεν εἰς ⸂τὸ πλοῦτος⸃ τῆς ἁπλότητος αὐτῶν·
