verses.translit: oti en polle dokime thlipseos e perisseia tes haras auton kai e kata vathoys ptoheia auton eperisseysen eis to ploutos tes aplotitos auton*
verses.translation: How that in a great trial of affliction the abundance of their joy and their deep poverty abounded unto the riches of their liberality.

verses.original: ὅτι κατὰ δύναμιν, μαρτυρῶ, καὶ ⸀παρὰ δύναμιν, αὐθαίρετοι
verses.translit: oti kata dynamin, martyro, kai para dynamin, authairetoi
verses.translation: For to their power, I bear record, yea, and beyond their power they were willing of themselves;

verses.original: μετὰ πολλῆς παρακλήσεως δεόμενοι ἡμῶν, τὴν χάριν καὶ τὴν κοινωνίαν τῆς διακονίας τῆς εἰς τοὺς ἁγίους—
verses.translit: meta polles parakliseos deomenoi emon, ten harin kai ten koinonian tes diakonias tes eis tous agioys--
verses.translation: Praying us with much intreaty that we would receive the gift, and take upon us the fellowship of the ministering to the saints.

verses.original: καὶ οὐ καθὼς ἠλπίσαμεν ἀλλʼ ἑαυτοὺς ἔδωκαν πρῶτον τῷ κυρίῳ καὶ ἡμῖν διὰ θελήματος θεοῦ,
verses.translit: kai ou kathos elpisamen all' eaytous edokan proton to kyrio kai emin dia thelimatos theou,
verses.translation: And this they did , not as we hoped, but first gave their own selves to the Lord, and unto us by the will of God.

verses.original: εἰς τὸ παρακαλέσαι ἡμᾶς Τίτον ἵνα καθὼς προενήρξατο οὕτως καὶ ἐπιτελέσῃ εἰς ὑμᾶς καὶ τὴν χάριν ταύτην·
verses.translit: eis to parakalesai emas Titon ina kathos proenirxato outos kai epitelese eis umas kai ten harin taytin*
verses.translation: Insomuch that we desired Titus, that as he had begun, so he would also finish in you the same grace also.

verses.original: ἀλλʼ ὥσπερ ἐν παντὶ περισσεύετε, πίστει καὶ λόγῳ καὶ γνώσει καὶ πάσῃ σπουδῇ καὶ τῇ ἐξ ⸂ἡμῶν ἐν ὑμῖν⸃ ἀγάπῃ, ἵνα καὶ ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ χάριτι περισσεύητε.
verses.translit: all' osper en panti perisseyete, pistei kai logo kai gnosei kai pase spoyde kai te ex emon en umin agape, ina kai en tayte te hariti perisseyite.
verses.translation: Therefore, as ye abound in every thing, in faith, and utterance, and knowledge, and in all diligence, and in your love to us, see that ye abound in this grace also.

verses.original: Οὐ κατʼ ἐπιταγὴν λέγω ἀλλὰ διὰ τῆς ἑτέρων σπουδῆς καὶ τὸ τῆς ὑμετέρας ἀγάπης γνήσιον δοκιμάζων·
verses.translit: Ou kat' epitagen lego alla dia tes eteron spoydes kai to tes umeteras agapis gnision dokimazon*
verses.translation: I speak not by commandment, but by occasion of the forwardness of others, and to prove the sincerity of your love.

verses.original: γινώσκετε γὰρ τὴν χάριν τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὅτι διʼ ὑμᾶς ἐπτώχευσεν πλούσιος ὤν, ἵνα ὑμεῖς τῇ ἐκείνου πτωχείᾳ πλουτήσητε.
verses.translit: ginoskete gar ten harin tou kyrioy emon Iisou Hristou, oti di' umas eptoheysen ploysios on, ina umeis te ekeinoy ptoheia ploytisite.
verses.translation: For ye know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that, though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, that ye through his poverty might be rich.

verses.original: καὶ γνώμην ἐν τούτῳ δίδωμι· τοῦτο γὰρ ὑμῖν συμφέρει, οἵτινες οὐ μόνον τὸ ποιῆσαι ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ θέλειν προενήρξασθε ἀπὸ πέρυσι·
verses.translit: kai gnomin en toyto didomi* touto gar umin symferei, oitines ou monon to poiesai alla kai to thelein proenirxasthe apo perysi*
verses.translation: And herein I give my advice: for this is expedient for you, who have begun before, not only to do, but also to be forward a year ago.

verses.original: νυνὶ δὲ καὶ τὸ ποιῆσαι ἐπιτελέσατε, ὅπως καθάπερ ἡ προθυμία τοῦ θέλειν οὕτως καὶ τὸ ἐπιτελέσαι ἐκ τοῦ ἔχειν.
verses.translit: nyni de kai to poiesai epitelesate, opos kathaper e prothymia tou thelein outos kai to epitelesai ek tou ehein.
verses.translation: Now therefore perform the doing of it ; that as there was a readiness to will, so there may be a performance also out of that which ye have.

verses.original: εἰ γὰρ ἡ προθυμία πρόκειται, καθὸ ἐὰν ⸀ἔχῃ εὐπρόσδεκτος, οὐ καθὸ οὐκ ἔχει.
verses.translit: ei gar e prothymia prokeitai, katho ean ehe euprosdektos, ou katho ouk ehei.
verses.translation: For if there be first a willing mind, it is accepted according to that a man hath, and not according to that he hath not.

verses.original: οὐ γὰρ ἵνα ἄλλοις ἄνεσις, ⸀ὑμῖν θλῖψις· ἀλλʼ ἐξ ἰσότητος
verses.translit: ou gar ina allois anesis, umin thlipsis* all' ex isotitos
verses.translation: For I mean not that other men be eased, and ye burdened:

verses.original: ἐν τῷ νῦν καιρῷ τὸ ὑμῶν περίσσευμα εἰς τὸ ἐκείνων ὑστέρημα, ἵνα καὶ τὸ ἐκείνων περίσσευμα γένηται εἰς τὸ ὑμῶν ὑστέρημα, ὅπως γένηται ἰσότης·
verses.translit: en to nun kairo to umon perisseyma eis to ekeinon usterima, ina kai to ekeinon perisseyma genitai eis to umon usterima, opos genitai isotis*
verses.translation: But by an equality, that now at this time your abundance may be a supply for their want, that their abundance also may be a supply for your want: that there may be equality:

verses.original: καθὼς γέγραπται· Ὁ τὸ πολὺ οὐκ ἐπλεόνασεν, καὶ ὁ τὸ ὀλίγον οὐκ ἠλαττόνησεν.
verses.translit: kathos gegraptai* O to polu ouk epleonasen, kai o to oligon ouk elattonisen.
verses.translation: As it is written, He that had gathered much had nothing over; and he that had gathered little had no lack.

verses.original: Χάρις δὲ τῷ θεῷ τῷ ⸀διδόντι τὴν αὐτὴν σπουδὴν ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ Τίτου,
verses.translit: Haris de to theo to didonti ten auten spoyden uper umon en te kardia Titoy,
verses.translation: But thanks be to God, which put the same earnest care into the heart of Titus for you.

verses.original: ὅτι τὴν μὲν παράκλησιν ἐδέξατο, σπουδαιότερος δὲ ὑπάρχων αὐθαίρετος ἐξῆλθεν πρὸς ὑμᾶς.
verses.translit: oti ten men paraklisin edexato, spoydaioteros de uparhon authairetos exelthen pros umas.
verses.translation: For indeed he accepted the exhortation; but being more forward, of his own accord he went unto you.

verses.original: συνεπέμψαμεν δὲ μετʼ αὐτοῦ τὸν ἀδελφὸν οὗ ὁ ἔπαινος ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ διὰ πασῶν τῶν ἐκκλησιῶν—
verses.translit: synepempsamen de met' autou ton adelfon ou o epainos en to euaggelio dia pason ton ekklision--
verses.translation: And we have sent with him the brother, whose praise is in the gospel throughout all the churches;

verses.original: οὐ μόνον δὲ ἀλλὰ καὶ χειροτονηθεὶς ὑπὸ τῶν ἐκκλησιῶν συνέκδημος ἡμῶν ⸀σὺν τῇ χάριτι ταύτῃ τῇ διακονουμένῃ ὑφʼ ἡμῶν πρὸς τὴν ⸀αὐτοῦ τοῦ κυρίου δόξαν καὶ προθυμίαν ἡμῶν—
verses.translit: ou monon de alla kai heirotonitheis upo ton ekklision synekdimos emon sun te hariti tayte te diakonoymene uf' emon pros ten autou tou kyrioy doxan kai prothymian emon--
verses.translation: And not that only, but who was also chosen of the churches to travel with us with this grace, which is administered by us to the glory of the same Lord, and declaration of your ready mind:

verses.original: στελλόμενοι τοῦτο μή τις ἡμᾶς μωμήσηται ἐν τῇ ἁδρότητι ταύτῃ τῇ διακονουμένῃ ὑφʼ ἡμῶν,
verses.translit: stellomenoi touto mi tis emas momisitai en te adrotiti tayte te diakonoymene uf' emon,
verses.translation: Avoiding this, that no man should blame us in this abundance which is administered by us:

verses.original: ⸂προνοοῦμεν γὰρ⸃ καλὰ οὐ μόνον ἐνώπιον κυρίου ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐνώπιον ἀνθρώπων.
verses.translit: pronooumen gar kala ou monon enopion kyrioy alla kai enopion anthropon.
verses.translation: Providing for honest things, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men.

verses.original: συνεπέμψαμεν δὲ αὐτοῖς τὸν ἀδελφὸν ἡμῶν ὃν ἐδοκιμάσαμεν ἐν πολλοῖς πολλάκις σπουδαῖον ὄντα, νυνὶ δὲ πολὺ σπουδαιότερον πεποιθήσει πολλῇ τῇ εἰς ὑμᾶς.
verses.translit: synepempsamen de autois ton adelfon emon on edokimasamen en pollois pollakis spoydaion onta, nyni de polu spoydaioteron pepoithisei polle te eis umas.
verses.translation: And we have sent with them our brother, whom we have oftentimes proved diligent in many things, but now much more diligent, upon the great confidence which I have in you.

verses.original: εἴτε ὑπὲρ Τίτου, κοινωνὸς ἐμὸς καὶ εἰς ὑμᾶς συνεργός· εἴτε ἀδελφοὶ ἡμῶν, ἀπόστολοι ἐκκλησιῶν, δόξα Χριστοῦ.
verses.translit: eite uper Titoy, koinonos emos kai eis umas synergos* eite adelfoi emon, apostoloi ekklision, doxa Hristou.
verses.translation: Whether any do enquire of Titus, he is my partner and fellowhelper concerning you: or our brethren be enquired of, they are the messengers of the churches, and the glory of Christ.

verses.original: τὴν οὖν ἔνδειξιν τῆς ἀγάπης ὑμῶν καὶ ἡμῶν καυχήσεως ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν εἰς αὐτοὺς ⸀ἐνδεικνύμενοι εἰς πρόσωπον τῶν ἐκκλησιῶν.
verses.translit: ten oun endeixin tes agapis umon kai emon kayhiseos uper umon eis autous endeiknymenoi eis prosopon ton ekklision.
verses.translation: Wherefore shew ye to them, and before the churches, the proof of your love, and of our boasting on your behalf.

verses.original: Περὶ μὲν γὰρ τῆς διακονίας τῆς εἰς τοὺς ἁγίους περισσόν μοί ἐστιν τὸ γράφειν ὑμῖν,
verses.translit: Peri men gar tes diakonias tes eis tous agioys perisson moi estin to grafein umin,
verses.translation: For as touching the ministering to the saints, it is superfluous for me to write to you:

verses.original: οἶδα γὰρ τὴν προθυμίαν ὑμῶν ἣν ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν καυχῶμαι Μακεδόσιν ὅτι Ἀχαΐα παρεσκεύασται ἀπὸ πέρυσι, καὶ ⸀τὸ ὑμῶν ζῆλος ἠρέθισε τοὺς πλείονας.
verses.translit: oida gar ten prothymian umon en uper umon kayhomai Makedosin oti AhaIa pareskeyastai apo perysi, kai to umon zelos erethise tous pleionas.
verses.translation: For I know the forwardness of your mind, for which I boast of you to them of Macedonia, that Achaia was ready a year ago; and your zeal hath provoked very many.

verses.original: ἔπεμψα δὲ τοὺς ἀδελφούς, ἵνα μὴ τὸ καύχημα ἡμῶν τὸ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν κενωθῇ ἐν τῷ μέρει τούτῳ, ἵνα καθὼς ἔλεγον παρεσκευασμένοι ἦτε,
verses.translit: epempsa de tous adelfoys, ina me to kayhima emon to uper umon kenothe en to merei toyto, ina kathos elegon pareskeyasmenoi ete,
verses.translation: Yet have I sent the brethren, lest our boasting of you should be in vain in this behalf; that, as I said, ye may be ready:

verses.original: μή πως ἐὰν ἔλθωσιν σὺν ἐμοὶ Μακεδόνες καὶ εὕρωσιν ὑμᾶς ἀπαρασκευάστους καταισχυνθῶμεν ἡμεῖς, ἵνα μὴ ⸀λέγωμεν ὑμεῖς, ἐν τῇ ὑποστάσει ⸀ταύτῃ.
verses.translit: mi pos ean elthosin sun emoi Makedones kai eurosin umas aparaskeyastoys kataishynthomen emeis, ina me legomen umeis, en te upostasei tayte.
verses.translation: Lest haply if they of Macedonia come with me, and find you unprepared, we (that we say not, ye) should be ashamed in this same confident boasting.

verses.original: ἀναγκαῖον οὖν ἡγησάμην παρακαλέσαι τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ἵνα προέλθωσιν ⸀εἰς ὑμᾶς καὶ προκαταρτίσωσι τὴν ⸀προεπηγγελμένην εὐλογίαν ὑμῶν, ταύτην ἑτοίμην εἶναι οὕτως ὡς εὐλογίαν καὶ μὴ ὡς πλεονεξίαν.
verses.translit: anagkaion oun egisamin parakalesai tous adelfous ina proelthosin eis umas kai prokatartisosi ten proepiggelmenin eulogian umon, taytin etoimin einai outos os eulogian kai me os pleonexian.
verses.translation: Therefore I thought it necessary to exhort the brethren, that they would go before unto you, and make up beforehand your bounty, whereof ye had notice before, that the same might be ready, as a matter of bounty, and not as of covetousness.

verses.original: Τοῦτο δέ, ὁ σπείρων φειδομένως φειδομένως καὶ θερίσει, καὶ ὁ σπείρων ἐπʼ εὐλογίαις ἐπʼ εὐλογίαις καὶ θερίσει.
verses.translit: Touto de, o speiron feidomenos feidomenos kai therisei, kai o speiron ep' eulogiais ep' eulogiais kai therisei.
verses.translation: But this I say , He which soweth sparingly shall reap also sparingly; and he which soweth bountifully shall reap also bountifully.

verses.original: ἕκαστος καθὼς ⸀προῄρηται τῇ καρδίᾳ, μὴ ἐκ λύπης ἢ ἐξ ἀνάγκης· ἱλαρὸν γὰρ δότην ἀγαπᾷ ὁ θεός.
verses.translit: ekastos kathos proeritai te kardia, me ek lypis e ex anagkis* ilaron gar dotin agapa o theos.
verses.translation: Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give ; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver.

verses.original: ⸀δυνατεῖ δὲ ὁ θεὸς πᾶσαν χάριν περισσεῦσαι εἰς ὑμᾶς, ἵνα ἐν παντὶ πάντοτε πᾶσαν αὐτάρκειαν ἔχοντες περισσεύητε εἰς πᾶν ἔργον ἀγαθόν·
verses.translit: dynatei de o theos pasan harin perisseusai eis umas, ina en panti pantote pasan autarkeian ehontes perisseyite eis pan ergon agathon*
verses.translation: And God is able to make all grace abound toward you; that ye, always having all sufficiency in all things , may abound to every good work:

verses.original: (καθὼς γέγραπται· Ἐσκόρπισεν, ἔδωκεν τοῖς πένησιν, ἡ δικαιοσύνη αὐτοῦ μένει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα·
verses.translit: (kathos gegraptai* Eskorpisen, edoken tois penisin, e dikaiosyni autou menei eis ton aiona*
verses.translation: (As it is written, He hath dispersed abroad; he hath given to the poor: his righteousness remaineth for ever.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἐπιχορηγῶν ⸀σπόρον τῷ σπείροντι καὶ ἄρτον εἰς βρῶσιν ⸀χορηγήσει καὶ ⸀πληθυνεῖ τὸν σπόρον ὑμῶν καὶ ⸀αὐξήσει τὰ γενήματα τῆς δικαιοσύνης ὑμῶν·)
verses.translit: o de epihorigon sporon to speironti kai arton eis vrosin horigisei kai plithynei ton sporon umon kai auxisei ta genimata tes dikaiosynis umon*)
verses.translation: Now he that ministereth seed to the sower both minister bread for your food, and multiply your seed sown, and increase the fruits of your righteousness;)

verses.original: ἐν παντὶ πλουτιζόμενοι εἰς πᾶσαν ἁπλότητα, ἥτις κατεργάζεται διʼ ἡμῶν εὐχαριστίαν τῷ θεῷ—
verses.translit: en panti ploytizomenoi eis pasan aplotita, etis katergazetai di' emon euharistian to theo--
verses.translation: Being enriched in every thing to all bountifulness, which causeth through us thanksgiving to God.

verses.original: ὅτι ἡ διακονία τῆς λειτουργίας ταύτης οὐ μόνον ἐστὶν προσαναπληροῦσα τὰ ὑστερήματα τῶν ἁγίων, ἀλλὰ καὶ περισσεύουσα διὰ πολλῶν εὐχαριστιῶν τῷ θεῷ—
verses.translit: oti e diakonia tes leitoyrgias taytis ou monon estin prosanaplirousa ta usterimata ton agion, alla kai perisseyoysa dia pollon euharistion to theo--
verses.translation: For the administration of this service not only supplieth the want of the saints, but is abundant also by many thanksgivings unto God;

verses.original: διὰ τῆς δοκιμῆς τῆς διακονίας ταύτης δοξάζοντες τὸν θεὸν ἐπὶ τῇ ὑποταγῇ τῆς ὁμολογίας ὑμῶν εἰς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἁπλότητι τῆς κοινωνίας εἰς αὐτοὺς καὶ εἰς πάντας,
verses.translit: dia tes dokimes tes diakonias taytis doxazontes ton theon epi te upotage tes omologias umon eis to euaggelion tou Hristou kai aplotiti tes koinonias eis autous kai eis pantas,
verses.translation: Whiles by the experiment of this ministration they glorify God for your professed subjection unto the gospel of Christ, and for your liberal distribution unto them, and unto all men ;

verses.original: καὶ αὐτῶν δεήσει ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν ἐπιποθούντων ὑμᾶς διὰ τὴν ὑπερβάλλουσαν χάριν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐφʼ ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: kai auton deisei uper umon epipothoynton umas dia ten upervalloysan harin tou theou ef' umin.
verses.translation: And by their prayer for you, which long after you for the exceeding grace of God in you.

verses.original: ⸀χάρις τῷ θεῷ ἐπὶ τῇ ἀνεκδιηγήτῳ αὐτοῦ δωρεᾷ.
verses.translit: haris to theo epi te anekdiigito autou dorea.
verses.translation: Thanks be unto God for his unspeakable gift.

verses.original: Αὐτὸς δὲ ἐγὼ Παῦλος παρακαλῶ ὑμᾶς διὰ τῆς πραΰτητος καὶ ἐπιεικείας τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὃς κατὰ πρόσωπον μὲν ταπεινὸς ἐν ὑμῖν, ἀπὼν δὲ θαρρῶ εἰς ὑμᾶς·
verses.translit: Autos de ego Paulos parakalo umas dia tes praytitos kai epieikeias tou Hristou, os kata prosopon men tapeinos en umin, apon de tharro eis umas*
verses.translation: Now I Paul myself beseech you by the meekness and gentleness of Christ, who in presence am base among you, but being absent am bold toward you:

verses.original: δέομαι δὲ τὸ μὴ παρὼν θαρρῆσαι τῇ πεποιθήσει ᾗ λογίζομαι τολμῆσαι ἐπί τινας τοὺς λογιζομένους ἡμᾶς ὡς κατὰ σάρκα περιπατοῦντας.
verses.translit: deomai de to me paron tharresai te pepoithisei e logizomai tolmesai epi tinas tous logizomenoys emas os kata sarka peripatountas.
verses.translation: But I beseech you , that I may not be bold when I am present with that confidence, wherewith I think to be bold against some, which think of us as if we walked according to the flesh.

verses.original: ἐν σαρκὶ γὰρ περιπατοῦντες οὐ κατὰ σάρκα στρατευόμεθα—
verses.translit: en sarki gar peripatountes ou kata sarka strateyometha--
verses.translation: For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh:

verses.original: τὰ γὰρ ὅπλα τῆς στρατείας ἡμῶν οὐ σαρκικὰ ἀλλὰ δυνατὰ τῷ θεῷ πρὸς καθαίρεσιν ὀχυρωμάτων— λογισμοὺς καθαιροῦντες
verses.translit: ta gar opla tes strateias emon ou sarkika alla dynata to theo pros kathairesin ohyromaton-- logismous kathairountes
verses.translation: (For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds;)

verses.original: καὶ πᾶν ὕψωμα ἐπαιρόμενον κατὰ τῆς γνώσεως τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ αἰχμαλωτίζοντες πᾶν νόημα εἰς τὴν ὑπακοὴν τοῦ Χριστοῦ,
verses.translit: kai pan upsoma epairomenon kata tes gnoseos tou theou, kai aihmalotizontes pan noima eis ten upakoen tou Hristou,
verses.translation: Casting down imaginations, and every high thing that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God, and bringing into captivity every thought to the obedience of Christ;

verses.original: καὶ ἐν ἑτοίμῳ ἔχοντες ἐκδικῆσαι πᾶσαν παρακοήν, ὅταν πληρωθῇ ὑμῶν ἡ ὑπακοή.
verses.translit: kai en etoimo ehontes ekdikesai pasan parakoin, otan plirothe umon e upakoi.
verses.translation: And having in a readiness to revenge all disobedience, when your obedience is fulfilled.

verses.original: Τὰ κατὰ πρόσωπον βλέπετε. εἴ τις πέποιθεν ἑαυτῷ Χριστοῦ εἶναι, τοῦτο λογιζέσθω πάλιν ⸀ἐφʼ ἑαυτοῦ ὅτι καθὼς αὐτὸς Χριστοῦ οὕτως καὶ ⸀ἡμεῖς.
verses.translit: Ta kata prosopon vlepete. ei tis pepoithen eayto Hristou einai, touto logizestho palin ef' eaytou oti kathos autos Hristou outos kai emeis.
verses.translation: Do ye look on things after the outward appearance? If any man trust to himself that he is Christ’s, let him of himself think this again, that, as he is Christ’s, even so are we Christ’s.

verses.original: ἐάν ⸀τε ⸀γὰρ περισσότερόν τι καυχήσωμαι περὶ τῆς ἐξουσίας ἡμῶν, ἧς ἔδωκεν ὁ ⸀κύριος εἰς οἰκοδομὴν καὶ οὐκ εἰς καθαίρεσιν ὑμῶν, οὐκ αἰσχυνθήσομαι,
verses.translit: ean te gar perissoteron ti kayhisomai peri tes exoysias emon, es edoken o kyrios eis oikodomen kai ouk eis kathairesin umon, ouk aishynthisomai,
verses.translation: For though I should boast somewhat more of our authority, which the Lord hath given us for edification, and not for your destruction, I should not be ashamed:

verses.original: ἵνα μὴ δόξω ὡς ἂν ἐκφοβεῖν ὑμᾶς διὰ τῶν ἐπιστολῶν·
verses.translit: ina me doxo os an ekfovein umas dia ton epistolon*
verses.translation: That I may not seem as if I would terrify you by letters.

verses.original: ὅτι Αἱ ⸂ἐπιστολαὶ μέν⸃, φησίν, βαρεῖαι καὶ ἰσχυραί, ἡ δὲ παρουσία τοῦ σώματος ἀσθενὴς καὶ ὁ λόγος ἐξουθενημένος.
verses.translit: oti Ai epistolai men, fisin, vareiai kai ishyrai, e de paroysia tou somatos asthenes kai o logos exoythenimenos.
verses.translation: For his letters, say they, are weighty and powerful; but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech contemptible.

verses.original: τοῦτο λογιζέσθω ὁ τοιοῦτος, ὅτι οἷοί ἐσμεν τῷ λόγῳ διʼ ἐπιστολῶν ἀπόντες, τοιοῦτοι καὶ παρόντες τῷ ἔργῳ.
verses.translit: touto logizestho o toioutos, oti oioi esmen to logo di' epistolon apontes, toioutoi kai parontes to ergo.
verses.translation: Let such an one think this, that, such as we are in word by letters when we are absent, such will we be also in deed when we are present.

verses.original: Οὐ γὰρ τολμῶμεν ἐγκρῖναι ἢ συγκρῖναι ἑαυτούς τισιν τῶν ἑαυτοὺς συνιστανόντων· ἀλλὰ αὐτοὶ ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἑαυτοὺς μετροῦντες καὶ συγκρίνοντες ἑαυτοὺς ἑαυτοῖς οὐ συνιᾶσιν.
verses.translit: Ou gar tolmomen egkrinai e sygkrinai eaytoys tisin ton eaytous synistanonton* alla autoi en eaytois eaytous metrountes kai sygkrinontes eaytous eaytois ou syniasin.
verses.translation: For we dare not make ourselves of the number, or compare ourselves with some that commend themselves: but they measuring themselves by themselves, and comparing themselves among themselves, are not wise.

verses.original: ἡμεῖς δὲ ⸀οὐκ εἰς τὰ ἄμετρα καυχησόμεθα, ἀλλὰ κατὰ τὸ μέτρον τοῦ κανόνος οὗ ἐμέρισεν ἡμῖν ὁ θεὸς μέτρου, ἐφικέσθαι ἄχρι καὶ ὑμῶν—
verses.translit: emeis de ouk eis ta ametra kayhisometha, alla kata to metron tou kanonos ou emerisen emin o theos metroy, efikesthai ahri kai umon--
verses.translation: But we will not boast of things without our measure, but according to the measure of the rule which God hath distributed to us, a measure to reach even unto you.

verses.original: οὐ γὰρ ὡς μὴ ἐφικνούμενοι εἰς ὑμᾶς ὑπερεκτείνομεν ἑαυτούς, ἄχρι γὰρ καὶ ὑμῶν ἐφθάσαμεν ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ—
verses.translit: ou gar os me efiknoymenoi eis umas uperekteinomen eaytoys, ahri gar kai umon efthasamen en to euaggelio tou Hristou--
verses.translation: For we stretch not ourselves beyond our measure , as though we reached not unto you: for we are come as far as to you also in preaching the gospel of Christ:

verses.original: οὐκ εἰς τὰ ἄμετρα καυχώμενοι ἐν ἀλλοτρίοις κόποις, ἐλπίδα δὲ ἔχοντες αὐξανομένης τῆς πίστεως ὑμῶν ἐν ὑμῖν μεγαλυνθῆναι κατὰ τὸν κανόνα ἡμῶν εἰς περισσείαν,
verses.translit: ouk eis ta ametra kayhomenoi en allotriois kopois, elpida de ehontes auxanomenis tes pisteos umon en umin megalynthenai kata ton kanona emon eis perisseian,
verses.translation: Not boasting of things without our measure, that is , of other men’s labours; but having hope, when your faith is increased, that we shall be enlarged by you according to our rule abundantly,

verses.original: εἰς τὰ ὑπερέκεινα ὑμῶν εὐαγγελίσασθαι, οὐκ ἐν ἀλλοτρίῳ κανόνι εἰς τὰ ἕτοιμα καυχήσασθαι.
verses.translit: eis ta uperekeina umon euaggelisasthai, ouk en allotrio kanoni eis ta etoima kayhisasthai.
verses.translation: To preach the gospel in the regions beyond you, and not to boast in another man’s line of things made ready to our hand.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ καυχώμενος ἐν κυρίῳ καυχάσθω·
verses.translit: O de kayhomenos en kyrio kayhastho*
verses.translation: But he that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord.

verses.original: οὐ γὰρ ὁ ἑαυτὸν ⸀συνιστάνων, ἐκεῖνός ἐστιν δόκιμος, ἀλλὰ ὃν ὁ κύριος συνίστησιν.
verses.translit: ou gar o eayton synistanon, ekeinos estin dokimos, alla on o kyrios synistisin.
verses.translation: For not he that commendeth himself is approved, but whom the Lord commendeth.

verses.original: Ὄφελον ἀνείχεσθέ μου μικρόν ⸀τι ⸀ἀφροσύνης· ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀνέχεσθέ μου.
verses.translit: Ofelon aneihesthe moy mikron ti afrosynis* alla kai anehesthe moy.
verses.translation: Would to God ye could bear with me a little in my folly: and indeed bear with me.

verses.original: ζηλῶ γὰρ ὑμᾶς θεοῦ ζήλῳ, ἡρμοσάμην γὰρ ὑμᾶς ἑνὶ ἀνδρὶ παρθένον ἁγνὴν παραστῆσαι τῷ Χριστῷ·
verses.translit: zilo gar umas theou zilo, ermosamin gar umas eni andri parthenon agnen parastesai to Hristo*
verses.translation: For I am jealous over you with godly jealousy: for I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.

verses.original: φοβοῦμαι δὲ μή πως, ὡς ὁ ὄφις ⸂ἐξηπάτησεν Εὕαν⸃ ἐν τῇ πανουργίᾳ αὐτοῦ, ⸀φθαρῇ τὰ νοήματα ὑμῶν ἀπὸ τῆς ἁπλότητος ⸂καὶ τῆς ἁγνότητος⸃ τῆς εἰς τὸν Χριστόν.
verses.translit: fovoumai de mi pos, os o ofis exipatisen Euan en te panoyrgia autou, fthare ta noimata umon apo tes aplotitos kai tes agnotitos tes eis ton Hriston.
verses.translation: But I fear, lest by any means, as the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty, so your minds should be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ.

verses.original: εἰ μὲν γὰρ ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἄλλον Ἰησοῦν κηρύσσει ὃν οὐκ ἐκηρύξαμεν, ἢ πνεῦμα ἕτερον λαμβάνετε ὃ οὐκ ἐλάβετε, ἢ εὐαγγέλιον ἕτερον ὃ οὐκ ἐδέξασθε, καλῶς ⸀ἀνέχεσθε.
verses.translit: ei men gar o erhomenos allon Iisoun kiryssei on ouk ekiryxamen, e pneuma eteron lamvanete o ouk elavete, e euaggelion eteron o ouk edexasthe, kalos anehesthe.
verses.translation: For if he that cometh preacheth another Jesus, whom we have not preached, or if ye receive another spirit, which ye have not received, or another gospel, which ye have not accepted, ye might well bear with him .

verses.original: λογίζομαι γὰρ μηδὲν ὑστερηκέναι τῶν ὑπερλίαν ἀποστόλων·
verses.translit: logizomai gar miden usterikenai ton uperlian apostolon*
verses.translation: For I suppose I was not a whit behind the very chiefest apostles.

verses.original: εἰ δὲ καὶ ἰδιώτης τῷ λόγῳ, ἀλλʼ οὐ τῇ γνώσει, ἀλλʼ ἐν παντὶ ⸀φανερώσαντες ἐν πᾶσιν εἰς ὑμᾶς.
verses.translit: ei de kai idiotis to logo, all' ou te gnosei, all' en panti fanerosantes en pasin eis umas.
verses.translation: But though I be rude in speech, yet not in knowledge; but we have been throughly made manifest among you in all things.

verses.original: Ἢ ἁμαρτίαν ἐποίησα ἐμαυτὸν ταπεινῶν ἵνα ὑμεῖς ὑψωθῆτε, ὅτι δωρεὰν τὸ τοῦ θεοῦ εὐαγγέλιον εὐηγγελισάμην ὑμῖν;
verses.translit: E amartian epoiisa emayton tapeinon ina umeis upsothete, oti dorean to tou theou euaggelion euiggelisamin umin;
verses.translation: Have I committed an offence in abasing myself that ye might be exalted, because I have preached to you the gospel of God freely?

verses.original: ἄλλας ἐκκλησίας ἐσύλησα λαβὼν ὀψώνιον πρὸς τὴν ὑμῶν διακονίαν,
verses.translit: allas ekklisias esylisa lavon opsonion pros ten umon diakonian,
verses.translation: I robbed other churches, taking wages of them , to do you service.

verses.original: καὶ παρὼν πρὸς ὑμᾶς καὶ ὑστερηθεὶς οὐ κατενάρκησα οὐθενός· τὸ γὰρ ὑστέρημά μου προσανεπλήρωσαν οἱ ἀδελφοὶ ἐλθόντες ἀπὸ Μακεδονίας· καὶ ἐν παντὶ ἀβαρῆ ⸂ἐμαυτὸν ὑμῖν⸃ ἐτήρησα καὶ τηρήσω.
verses.translit: kai paron pros umas kai usteritheis ou katenarkisa outhenos* to gar usterima moy prosaneplirosan oi adelfoi elthontes apo Makedonias* kai en panti avare emayton umin etirisa kai tiriso.
verses.translation: And when I was present with you, and wanted, I was chargeable to no man: for that which was lacking to me the brethren which came from Macedonia supplied: and in all things I have kept myself from being burdensome unto you, and so will I keep myself .

verses.original: ἔστιν ἀλήθεια Χριστοῦ ἐν ἐμοὶ ὅτι ἡ καύχησις αὕτη οὐ φραγήσεται εἰς ἐμὲ ἐν τοῖς κλίμασι τῆς Ἀχαΐας.
verses.translit: estin alitheia Hristou en emoi oti e kayhisis auti ou fragisetai eis eme en tois klimasi tes AhaIas.
verses.translation: As the truth of Christ is in me, no man shall stop me of this boasting in the regions of Achaia.

verses.original: διὰ τί; ὅτι οὐκ ἀγαπῶ ὑμᾶς; ὁ θεὸς οἶδεν.
verses.translit: dia ti; oti ouk agapo umas; o theos oiden.
verses.translation: Wherefore? because I love you not? God knoweth.

verses.original: Ὃ δὲ ποιῶ καὶ ποιήσω, ἵνα ἐκκόψω τὴν ἀφορμὴν τῶν θελόντων ἀφορμήν, ἵνα ἐν ᾧ καυχῶνται εὑρεθῶσιν καθὼς καὶ ἡμεῖς.
verses.translit: O de poio kai poiiso, ina ekkopso ten aformen ton thelonton aformin, ina en o kayhontai eurethosin kathos kai emeis.
verses.translation: But what I do, that I will do, that I may cut off occasion from them which desire occasion; that wherein they glory, they may be found even as we.

verses.original: οἱ γὰρ τοιοῦτοι ψευδαπόστολοι, ἐργάται δόλιοι, μετασχηματιζόμενοι εἰς ἀποστόλους Χριστοῦ·
verses.translit: oi gar toioutoi pseydapostoloi, ergatai dolioi, metashimatizomenoi eis apostoloys Hristou*
verses.translation: For such are false apostles, deceitful workers, transforming themselves into the apostles of Christ.

verses.original: καὶ οὐ ⸀θαῦμα, αὐτὸς γὰρ ὁ Σατανᾶς μετασχηματίζεται εἰς ἄγγελον φωτός·
verses.translit: kai ou thauma, autos gar o Satanas metashimatizetai eis aggelon fotos*
verses.translation: And no marvel; for Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light.

verses.original: οὐ μέγα οὖν εἰ καὶ οἱ διάκονοι αὐτοῦ μετασχηματίζονται ὡς διάκονοι δικαιοσύνης, ὧν τὸ τέλος ἔσται κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: ou mega oun ei kai oi diakonoi autou metashimatizontai os diakonoi dikaiosynis, on to telos estai kata ta erga auton.
verses.translation: Therefore it is no great thing if his ministers also be transformed as the ministers of righteousness; whose end shall be according to their works.

verses.original: Πάλιν λέγω, μή τίς με δόξῃ ἄφρονα εἶναι— εἰ δὲ μή γε, κἂν ὡς ἄφρονα δέξασθέ με, ἵνα κἀγὼ μικρόν τι καυχήσωμαι·
verses.translit: Palin lego, mi tis me doxe afrona einai-- ei de mi ge, kan os afrona dexasthe me, ina kago mikron ti kayhisomai*
verses.translation: I say again, Let no man think me a fool; if otherwise, yet as a fool receive me, that I may boast myself a little.

verses.original: ὃ λαλῶ οὐ ⸂κατὰ κύριον λαλῶ⸃, ἀλλʼ ὡς ἐν ἀφροσύνῃ, ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ ὑποστάσει τῆς καυχήσεως.
verses.translit: o lalo ou kata kyrion lalo, all' os en afrosyne, en tayte te upostasei tes kayhiseos.
verses.translation: That which I speak, I speak it not after the Lord, but as it were foolishly, in this confidence of boasting.

verses.original: ἐπεὶ πολλοὶ καυχῶνται ⸀κατὰ σάρκα, κἀγὼ καυχήσομαι.
verses.translit: epei polloi kayhontai kata sarka, kago kayhisomai.
verses.translation: Seeing that many glory after the flesh, I will glory also.

verses.original: ἡδέως γὰρ ἀνέχεσθε τῶν ἀφρόνων φρόνιμοι ὄντες·
verses.translit: edeos gar anehesthe ton afronon fronimoi ontes*
verses.translation: For ye suffer fools gladly, seeing ye yourselves are wise.

verses.original: ἀνέχεσθε γὰρ εἴ τις ὑμᾶς καταδουλοῖ, εἴ τις κατεσθίει, εἴ τις λαμβάνει, εἴ τις ἐπαίρεται, εἴ τις ⸂εἰς πρόσωπον ὑμᾶς⸃ δέρει.
verses.translit: anehesthe gar ei tis umas katadoyloi, ei tis katesthiei, ei tis lamvanei, ei tis epairetai, ei tis eis prosopon umas derei.
verses.translation: For ye suffer, if a man bring you into bondage, if a man devour you , if a man take of you , if a man exalt himself, if a man smite you on the face.

verses.original: κατὰ ἀτιμίαν λέγω, ὡς ὅτι ἡμεῖς ⸀ἠσθενήκαμεν· ἐν ᾧ δʼ ἄν τις τολμᾷ, ἐν ἀφροσύνῃ λέγω, τολμῶ κἀγώ.
verses.translit: kata atimian lego, os oti emeis esthenikamen* en o d' an tis tolma, en afrosyne lego, tolmo kago.
verses.translation: I speak as concerning reproach, as though we had been weak. Howbeit whereinsoever any is bold, (I speak foolishly,) I am bold also.

verses.original: Ἑβραῖοί εἰσιν; κἀγώ. Ἰσραηλῖταί εἰσιν; κἀγώ. σπέρμα Ἀβραάμ εἰσιν; κἀγώ.
verses.translit: Evraioi eisin; kago. Israilitai eisin; kago. sperma Avraam eisin; kago.
verses.translation: Are they Hebrews? so am I. Are they Israelites? so am I. Are they the seed of Abraham? so am I.

verses.original: διάκονοι Χριστοῦ εἰσιν; παραφρονῶν λαλῶ, ὑπὲρ ἐγώ· ἐν κόποις περισσοτέρως, ἐν ⸂φυλακαῖς περισσοτέρως, ἐν πληγαῖς ὑπερβαλλόντως⸃, ἐν θανάτοις πολλάκις·
verses.translit: diakonoi Hristou eisin; parafronon lalo, uper ego* en kopois perissoteros, en fylakais perissoteros, en pligais upervallontos, en thanatois pollakis*
verses.translation: Are they ministers of Christ? (I speak as a fool) I am more; in labours more abundant, in stripes above measure, in prisons more frequent, in deaths oft.

verses.original: ὑπὸ Ἰουδαίων πεντάκις τεσσεράκοντα παρὰ μίαν ἔλαβον,
verses.translit: upo Ioydaion pentakis tesserakonta para mian elavon,
verses.translation: Of the Jews five times received I forty stripes save one.

verses.original: τρὶς ἐραβδίσθην, ἅπαξ ἐλιθάσθην, τρὶς ἐναυάγησα, νυχθήμερον ἐν τῷ βυθῷ πεποίηκα·
verses.translit: tris eravdisthin, apax elithasthin, tris enayagisa, nyhthimeron en to vytho pepoiika*
verses.translation: Thrice was I beaten with rods, once was I stoned, thrice I suffered shipwreck, a night and a day I have been in the deep;

verses.original: ὁδοιπορίαις πολλάκις, κινδύνοις ποταμῶν, κινδύνοις λῃστῶν, κινδύνοις ἐκ γένους, κινδύνοις ἐξ ἐθνῶν, κινδύνοις ἐν πόλει, κινδύνοις ἐν ἐρημίᾳ, κινδύνοις ἐν θαλάσσῃ, κινδύνοις ἐν ψευδαδέλφοις,
verses.translit: odoiporiais pollakis, kindynois potamon, kindynois leston, kindynois ek genoys, kindynois ex ethnon, kindynois en polei, kindynois en erimia, kindynois en thalasse, kindynois en pseydadelfois,
verses.translation: In journeyings often, in perils of waters, in perils of robbers, in perils by mine own countrymen, in perils by the heathen, in perils in the city, in perils in the wilderness, in perils in the sea, in perils among false brethren;

verses.original: ⸀κόπῳ καὶ μόχθῳ, ἐν ἀγρυπνίαις πολλάκις, ἐν λιμῷ καὶ δίψει, ἐν νηστείαις πολλάκις, ἐν ψύχει καὶ γυμνότητι·
verses.translit: kopo kai mohtho, en agrypniais pollakis, en limo kai dipsei, en nisteiais pollakis, en psyhei kai gymnotiti*
verses.translation: In weariness and painfulness, in watchings often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness.

verses.original: χωρὶς τῶν παρεκτὸς ἡ ⸀ἐπίστασίς ⸀μοι ἡ καθʼ ἡμέραν, ἡ μέριμνα πασῶν τῶν ἐκκλησιῶν.
verses.translit: horis ton parektos e epistasis moi e kath' emeran, e merimna pason ton ekklision.
verses.translation: Beside those things that are without, that which cometh upon me daily, the care of all the churches.

verses.original: τίς ἀσθενεῖ, καὶ οὐκ ἀσθενῶ; τίς σκανδαλίζεται καὶ οὐκ ἐγὼ πυροῦμαι;
verses.translit: tis asthenei, kai ouk astheno; tis skandalizetai kai ouk ego pyroumai;
verses.translation: Who is weak, and I am not weak? who is offended, and I burn not?

verses.original: Εἰ καυχᾶσθαι δεῖ, τὰ τῆς ἀσθενείας μου καυχήσομαι.
verses.translit: Ei kayhasthai dei, ta tes astheneias moy kayhisomai.
verses.translation: If I must needs glory, I will glory of the things which concern mine infirmities.

verses.original: ὁ θεὸς καὶ πατὴρ τοῦ κυρίου ⸀Ἰησοῦ οἶδεν, ὁ ὢν εὐλογητὸς εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας, ὅτι οὐ ψεύδομαι.
verses.translit: o theos kai pater tou kyrioy Iisou oiden, o on eulogitos eis tous aionas, oti ou pseydomai.
verses.translation: The God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, which is blessed for evermore, knoweth that I lie not.

verses.original: ἐν Δαμασκῷ ὁ ἐθνάρχης Ἁρέτα τοῦ βασιλέως ἐφρούρει τὴν ⸂πόλιν Δαμασκηνῶν⸃ πιάσαι ⸀με,
verses.translit: en Damasko o ethnarhis Areta tou vasileos efroyrei ten polin Damaskinon piasai me,
verses.translation: In Damascus the governor under Aretas the king kept the city of the Damascenes with a garrison, desirous to apprehend me:

verses.original: καὶ διὰ θυρίδος ἐν σαργάνῃ ἐχαλάσθην διὰ τοῦ τείχους καὶ ἐξέφυγον τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai dia thyridos en sargane ehalasthin dia tou teihoys kai exefygon tas heiras autou.
verses.translation: And through a window in a basket was I let down by the wall, and escaped his hands.

verses.original: Καυχᾶσθαι ⸀δεῖ· οὐ ⸂συμφέρον μέν⸃, ἐλεύσομαι ⸀δὲ εἰς ὀπτασίας καὶ ἀποκαλύψεις κυρίου.
verses.translit: Kayhasthai dei* ou symferon men, eleysomai de eis optasias kai apokalypseis kyrioy.
verses.translation: It is not expedient for me doubtless to glory. I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord.

verses.original: οἶδα ἄνθρωπον ἐν Χριστῷ πρὸ ἐτῶν δεκατεσσάρων— εἴτε ἐν σώματι οὐκ οἶδα, εἴτε ἐκτὸς τοῦ σώματος οὐκ οἶδα, ὁ θεὸς οἶδεν— ἁρπαγέντα τὸν τοιοῦτον ἕως τρίτου οὐρανοῦ.
verses.translit: oida anthropon en Hristo pro eton dekatessaron-- eite en somati ouk oida, eite ektos tou somatos ouk oida, o theos oiden-- arpagenta ton toiouton eos tritoy ouranou.
verses.translation: I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago, (whether in the body, I cannot tell; or whether out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth;) such an one caught up to the third heaven.

verses.original: καὶ οἶδα τὸν τοιοῦτον ἄνθρωπον— εἴτε ἐν σώματι εἴτε ⸀χωρὶς τοῦ σώματος οὐκ οἶδα, ὁ θεὸς οἶδεν—
verses.translit: kai oida ton toiouton anthropon-- eite en somati eite horis tou somatos ouk oida, o theos oiden--
verses.translation: And I knew such a man, (whether in the body, or out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth;)

verses.original: ὅτι ἡρπάγη εἰς τὸν παράδεισον καὶ ἤκουσεν ἄρρητα ῥήματα ἃ οὐκ ἐξὸν ἀνθρώπῳ λαλῆσαι.
verses.translit: oti erpagi eis ton paradeison kai ekoysen arrita Rimata a ouk exon anthropo lalesai.
verses.translation: How that he was caught up into paradise, and heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter.

verses.original: ὑπὲρ τοῦ τοιούτου καυχήσομαι, ὑπὲρ δὲ ἐμαυτοῦ οὐ καυχήσομαι εἰ μὴ ἐν ταῖς ⸀ἀσθενείαις.
verses.translit: uper tou toioytoy kayhisomai, uper de emaytou ou kayhisomai ei me en tais astheneiais.
verses.translation: Of such an one will I glory: yet of myself I will not glory, but in mine infirmities.

verses.original: ἐὰν γὰρ θελήσω καυχήσασθαι, οὐκ ἔσομαι ἄφρων, ἀλήθειαν γὰρ ἐρῶ· φείδομαι δέ, μή τις εἰς ἐμὲ λογίσηται ὑπὲρ ὃ βλέπει με ἢ ἀκούει ⸀τι ἐξ ἐμοῦ,
verses.translit: ean gar theliso kayhisasthai, ouk esomai afron, alitheian gar ero* feidomai de, mi tis eis eme logisitai uper o vlepei me e akoyei ti ex emou,
verses.translation: For though I would desire to glory, I shall not be a fool; for I will say the truth: but now I forbear, lest any man should think of me above that which he seeth me to be , or that he heareth of me.

verses.original: καὶ τῇ ὑπερβολῇ τῶν ἀποκαλύψεων. ⸀διὸ ἵνα μὴ ὑπεραίρωμαι, ἐδόθη μοι σκόλοψ τῇ σαρκί, ἄγγελος ⸀Σατανᾶ, ἵνα με κολαφίζῃ, ⸂ἵνα μὴ ὑπεραίρωμαι⸃.
verses.translit: kai te upervole ton apokalypseon. dio ina me uperairomai, edothi moi skolops te sarki, aggelos Satana, ina me kolafize, ina me uperairomai.
verses.translation: And lest I should be exalted above measure through the abundance of the revelations, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me, lest I should be exalted above measure.

verses.original: ὑπὲρ τούτου τρὶς τὸν κύριον παρεκάλεσα ἵνα ἀποστῇ ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ·
verses.translit: uper toytoy tris ton kyrion parekalesa ina aposte ap' emou*
verses.translation: For this thing I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me.

verses.original: καὶ εἴρηκέν μοι· Ἀρκεῖ σοι ἡ χάρις μου· ἡ γὰρ ⸀δύναμις ἐν ἀσθενείᾳ ⸀τελεῖται. ἥδιστα οὖν μᾶλλον καυχήσομαι ἐν ταῖς ἀσθενείαις ⸀μου, ἵνα ἐπισκηνώσῃ ἐπʼ ἐμὲ ἡ δύναμις τοῦ Χριστοῦ.
verses.translit: kai eiriken moi* Arkei soi e haris moy* e gar dynamis en astheneia teleitai. edista oun mallon kayhisomai en tais astheneiais moy, ina episkinose ep' eme e dynamis tou Hristou.
verses.translation: And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.

verses.original: διὸ εὐδοκῶ ἐν ἀσθενείαις, ἐν ὕβρεσιν, ἐν ἀνάγκαις, ἐν διωγμοῖς ⸀καὶ στενοχωρίαις, ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ· ὅταν γὰρ ἀσθενῶ, τότε δυνατός εἰμι.
verses.translit: dio eudoko en astheneiais, en uvresin, en anagkais, en diogmois kai stenohoriais, uper Hristou* otan gar astheno, tote dynatos eimi.
verses.translation: Therefore I take pleasure in infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses for Christ’s sake: for when I am weak, then am I strong.

verses.original: Γέγονα ⸀ἄφρων· ὑμεῖς με ἠναγκάσατε· ἐγὼ γὰρ ὤφειλον ὑφʼ ὑμῶν συνίστασθαι. οὐδὲν γὰρ ὑστέρησα τῶν ὑπερλίαν ἀποστόλων, εἰ καὶ οὐδέν εἰμι·
verses.translit: Gegona afron* umeis me enagkasate* ego gar ofeilon uf' umon synistasthai. ouden gar usterisa ton uperlian apostolon, ei kai ouden eimi*
verses.translation: I am become a fool in glorying; ye have compelled me: for I ought to have been commended of you: for in nothing am I behind the very chiefest apostles, though I be nothing.

verses.original: τὰ μὲν σημεῖα τοῦ ἀποστόλου κατειργάσθη ἐν ὑμῖν ἐν πάσῃ ⸀ὑπομονῇ, σημείοις ⸀τε καὶ τέρασιν καὶ δυνάμεσιν.
verses.translit: ta men simeia tou apostoloy kateirgasthi en umin en pase upomone, simeiois te kai terasin kai dynamesin.
verses.translation: Truly the signs of an apostle were wrought among you in all patience, in signs, and wonders, and mighty deeds.

verses.original: τί γάρ ἐστιν ὃ ⸀ἡσσώθητε ὑπὲρ τὰς λοιπὰς ἐκκλησίας, εἰ μὴ ὅτι αὐτὸς ἐγὼ οὐ κατενάρκησα ὑμῶν; χαρίσασθέ μοι τὴν ἀδικίαν ταύτην.
verses.translit: ti gar estin o essothite uper tas loipas ekklisias, ei me oti autos ego ou katenarkisa umon; harisasthe moi ten adikian taytin.
verses.translation: For what is it wherein ye were inferior to other churches, except it be that I myself was not burdensome to you? forgive me this wrong.

verses.original: Ἰδοὺ τρίτον ⸀τοῦτο ἑτοίμως ἔχω ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς, καὶ οὐ ⸀καταναρκήσω· οὐ γὰρ ζητῶ τὰ ὑμῶν ἀλλὰ ὑμᾶς, οὐ γὰρ ὀφείλει τὰ τέκνα τοῖς γονεῦσιν θησαυρίζειν, ἀλλὰ οἱ γονεῖς τοῖς τέκνοις.
verses.translit: Idou triton touto etoimos eho elthein pros umas, kai ou katanarkiso* ou gar zito ta umon alla umas, ou gar ofeilei ta tekna tois goneusin thisayrizein, alla oi goneis tois teknois.
verses.translation: Behold, the third time I am ready to come to you; and I will not be burdensome to you: for I seek not yours, but you: for the children ought not to lay up for the parents, but the parents for the children.

verses.original: ἐγὼ δὲ ἥδιστα δαπανήσω καὶ ἐκδαπανηθήσομαι ὑπὲρ τῶν ψυχῶν ὑμῶν. ⸀εἰ περισσοτέρως ὑμᾶς ⸀ἀγαπῶν, ἧσσον ἀγαπῶμαι;
verses.translit: ego de edista dapaniso kai ekdapanithisomai uper ton psyhon umon. ei perissoteros umas agapon, esson agapomai;
verses.translation: And I will very gladly spend and be spent for you; though the more abundantly I love you, the less I be loved.

verses.original: ἔστω δέ, ἐγὼ οὐ κατεβάρησα ὑμᾶς· ἀλλὰ ὑπάρχων πανοῦργος δόλῳ ὑμᾶς ἔλαβον.
verses.translit: esto de, ego ou katevarisa umas* alla uparhon panourgos dolo umas elavon.
verses.translation: But be it so, I did not burden you: nevertheless, being crafty, I caught you with guile.

verses.original: μή τινα ὧν ἀπέσταλκα πρὸς ὑμᾶς, διʼ αὐτοῦ ἐπλεονέκτησα ὑμᾶς;
verses.translit: mi tina on apestalka pros umas, di' autou epleonektisa umas;
verses.translation: Did I make a gain of you by any of them whom I sent unto you?

verses.original: παρεκάλεσα Τίτον καὶ συναπέστειλα τὸν ἀδελφόν· μήτι ἐπλεονέκτησεν ὑμᾶς Τίτος; οὐ τῷ αὐτῷ πνεύματι περιεπατήσαμεν; οὐ τοῖς αὐτοῖς ἴχνεσιν;
verses.translit: parekalesa Titon kai synapesteila ton adelfon* miti epleonektisen umas Titos; ou to auto pneymati periepatisamen; ou tois autois ihnesin;
verses.translation: I desired Titus, and with him I sent a brother. Did Titus make a gain of you? walked we not in the same spirit? walked we not in the same steps?

verses.original: ⸀Πάλαι δοκεῖτε ὅτι ὑμῖν ἀπολογούμεθα; ⸀κατέναντι θεοῦ ἐν Χριστῷ λαλοῦμεν. τὰ δὲ πάντα, ἀγαπητοί, ὑπὲρ τῆς ὑμῶν οἰκοδομῆς,
verses.translit: Palai dokeite oti umin apologoymetha? katenanti theou en Hristo laloumen. ta de panta, agapitoi, uper tes umon oikodomes,
verses.translation: Again, think ye that we excuse ourselves unto you? we speak before God in Christ: but we do all things, dearly beloved, for your edifying.

verses.original: φοβοῦμαι γὰρ μή πως ἐλθὼν οὐχ οἵους θέλω εὕρω ὑμᾶς, κἀγὼ εὑρεθῶ ὑμῖν οἷον οὐ θέλετε, μή πως ⸀ἔρις, ⸀ζῆλος, θυμοί, ἐριθεῖαι, καταλαλιαί, ψιθυρισμοί, φυσιώσεις, ἀκαταστασίαι·
verses.translit: fovoumai gar mi pos elthon ouh oioys thelo euro umas, kago euretho umin oion ou thelete, mi pos eris, zelos, thymoi, eritheiai, katalaliai, psithyrismoi, fysioseis, akatastasiai*
verses.translation: For I fear, lest, when I come, I shall not find you such as I would, and that I shall be found unto you such as ye would not: lest there be debates, envyings, wraths, strifes, backbitings, whisperings, swellings, tumults:

verses.original: μὴ πάλιν ⸂ἐλθόντος μου⸃ ⸀ταπεινώσῃ ⸀με ὁ θεός μου πρὸς ὑμᾶς, καὶ πενθήσω πολλοὺς τῶν προημαρτηκότων καὶ μὴ μετανοησάντων ἐπὶ τῇ ἀκαθαρσίᾳ καὶ πορνείᾳ καὶ ἀσελγείᾳ ᾗ ἔπραξαν.
verses.translit: me palin elthontos moy tapeinose me o theos moy pros umas, kai penthiso pollous ton proimartikoton kai me metanoisanton epi te akatharsia kai porneia kai aselgeia e epraxan.
verses.translation: And lest, when I come again, my God will humble me among you, and that I shall bewail many which have sinned already, and have not repented of the uncleanness and fornication and lasciviousness which they have committed.

verses.original: Τρίτον τοῦτο ἔρχομαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς· ἐπὶ στόματος δύο μαρτύρων καὶ τριῶν σταθήσεται πᾶν ῥῆμα.
verses.translit: Triton touto erhomai pros umas* epi stomatos dyo martyron kai trion stathisetai pan Rema.
verses.translation: This is the third time I am coming to you. In the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word be established.

verses.original: προείρηκα καὶ προλέγω ὡς παρὼν τὸ δεύτερον καὶ ἀπὼν ⸀νῦν, τοῖς προημαρτηκόσιν καὶ τοῖς λοιποῖς πᾶσιν, ὅτι ἐὰν ἔλθω εἰς τὸ πάλιν οὐ φείσομαι,
verses.translit: proeirika kai prolego os paron to deyteron kai apon nun, tois proimartikosin kai tois loipois pasin, oti ean eltho eis to palin ou feisomai,
verses.translation: I told you before, and foretell you, as if I were present, the second time; and being absent now I write to them which heretofore have sinned, and to all other, that, if I come again, I will not spare:

verses.original: ἐπεὶ δοκιμὴν ζητεῖτε τοῦ ἐν ἐμοὶ λαλοῦντος Χριστοῦ· ὃς εἰς ὑμᾶς οὐκ ἀσθενεῖ ἀλλὰ δυνατεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν,
verses.translit: epei dokimen ziteite tou en emoi lalountos Hristou* os eis umas ouk asthenei alla dynatei en umin,
verses.translation: Since ye seek a proof of Christ speaking in me, which to you-ward is not weak, but is mighty in you.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀γὰρ ἐσταυρώθη ἐξ ἀσθενείας, ἀλλὰ ζῇ ἐκ δυνάμεως θεοῦ. καὶ γὰρ ἡμεῖς ἀσθενοῦμεν ἐν αὐτῷ, ἀλλὰ ⸀ζήσομεν σὺν αὐτῷ ἐκ δυνάμεως θεοῦ εἰς ὑμᾶς.
verses.translit: kai gar estayrothi ex astheneias, alla ze ek dynameos theou. kai gar emeis asthenoumen en auto, alla zisomen sun auto ek dynameos theou eis umas.
verses.translation: For though he was crucified through weakness, yet he liveth by the power of God. For we also are weak in him, but we shall live with him by the power of God toward you.

verses.original: Ἑαυτοὺς πειράζετε εἰ ἐστὲ ἐν τῇ πίστει, ἑαυτοὺς δοκιμάζετε· ἢ οὐκ ἐπιγινώσκετε ἑαυτοὺς ὅτι ⸂Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς⸃ ἐν ⸀ὑμῖν; εἰ μήτι ἀδόκιμοί ἐστε.
verses.translit: Eaytous peirazete ei este en te pistei, eaytous dokimazete* e ouk epiginoskete eaytous oti Iisous Hristos en umin; ei miti adokimoi este.
verses.translation: Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves. Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates?

verses.original: ἐλπίζω δὲ ὅτι γνώσεσθε ὅτι ἡμεῖς οὐκ ἐσμὲν ἀδόκιμοι.
verses.translit: elpizo de oti gnosesthe oti emeis ouk esmen adokimoi.
verses.translation: But I trust that ye shall know that we are not reprobates.

verses.original: ⸀εὐχόμεθα δὲ πρὸς τὸν θεὸν μὴ ποιῆσαι ὑμᾶς κακὸν μηδέν, οὐχ ἵνα ἡμεῖς δόκιμοι φανῶμεν, ἀλλʼ ἵνα ὑμεῖς τὸ καλὸν ποιῆτε, ἡμεῖς δὲ ὡς ἀδόκιμοι ὦμεν.
verses.translit: euhometha de pros ton theon me poiesai umas kakon miden, ouh ina emeis dokimoi fanomen, all' ina umeis to kalon poiete, emeis de os adokimoi omen.
verses.translation: Now I pray to God that ye do no evil; not that we should appear approved, but that ye should do that which is honest, though we be as reprobates.

verses.original: οὐ γὰρ δυνάμεθά τι κατὰ τῆς ἀληθείας, ἀλλὰ ὑπὲρ τῆς ἀληθείας.
verses.translit: ou gar dynametha ti kata tes alitheias, alla uper tes alitheias.
verses.translation: For we can do nothing against the truth, but for the truth.

verses.original: χαίρομεν γὰρ ὅταν ἡμεῖς ἀσθενῶμεν, ὑμεῖς δὲ δυνατοὶ ἦτε· ⸀τοῦτο καὶ εὐχόμεθα, τὴν ὑμῶν κατάρτισιν.
verses.translit: hairomen gar otan emeis asthenomen, umeis de dynatoi ete* touto kai euhometha, ten umon katartisin.
verses.translation: For we are glad, when we are weak, and ye are strong: and this also we wish, even your perfection.

verses.original: διὰ τοῦτο ταῦτα ἀπὼν γράφω, ἵνα παρὼν μὴ ἀποτόμως χρήσωμαι κατὰ τὴν ἐξουσίαν ἣν ⸂ὁ κύριος ἔδωκέν μοι⸃, εἰς οἰκοδομὴν καὶ οὐκ εἰς καθαίρεσιν.
verses.translit: dia touto tauta apon grafo, ina paron me apotomos hrisomai kata ten exoysian en o kyrios edoken moi, eis oikodomen kai ouk eis kathairesin.
verses.translation: Therefore I write these things being absent, lest being present I should use sharpness, according to the power which the Lord hath given me to edification, and not to destruction.

verses.original: Λοιπόν, ἀδελφοί, χαίρετε, καταρτίζεσθε, παρακαλεῖσθε, τὸ αὐτὸ φρονεῖτε, εἰρηνεύετε, καὶ ὁ θεὸς τῆς ἀγάπης καὶ εἰρήνης ἔσται μεθʼ ὑμῶν.
verses.translit: Loipon, adelfoi, hairete, katartizesthe, parakaleisthe, to auto froneite, eirineyete, kai o theos tes agapis kai eirinis estai meth' umon.
verses.translation: Finally, brethren, farewell. Be perfect, be of good comfort, be of one mind, live in peace; and the God of love and peace shall be with you.

verses.original: ἀσπάσασθε ἀλλήλους ἐν ἁγίῳ φιλήματι. ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς οἱ ἅγιοι πάντες.
verses.translit: aspasasthe alliloys en agio filimati. aspazontai umas oi agioi pantes.
verses.translation: Greet one another with an holy kiss.

verses.original: ἡ χάρις τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἡ ἀγάπη τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἡ κοινωνία τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος μετὰ πάντων ⸀ὑμῶν.
verses.translit: e haris tou kyrioy Iisou Hristou kai e agapi tou theou kai e koinonia tou agioy pneymatos meta panton umon.
verses.translation: All the saints salute you.
The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Ghost, be with you all. Amen.

verses.original: Παῦλος ἀπόστολος, οὐκ ἀπʼ ἀνθρώπων οὐδὲ διʼ ἀνθρώπου ἀλλὰ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ θεοῦ πατρὸς τοῦ ἐγείραντος αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν,
verses.translit: Paulos apostolos, ouk ap' anthropon oude di' anthropoy alla dia Iisou Hristou kai theou patros tou egeirantos auton ek nekron,
verses.translation: Paul, an apostle, (not of men, neither by man, but by Jesus Christ, and God the Father, who raised him from the dead;)

verses.original: καὶ οἱ σὺν ἐμοὶ πάντες ἀδελφοί, ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τῆς Γαλατίας·
verses.translit: kai oi sun emoi pantes adelfoi, tais ekklisiais tes Galatias*
verses.translation: And all the brethren which are with me, unto the churches of Galatia:

verses.original: χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς ⸂καὶ κυρίου ἡμῶν⸃ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ,
verses.translit: haris umin kai eirini apo theou patros kai kyrioy emon Iisou Hristou,
verses.translation: Grace be to you and peace from God the Father, and from our Lord Jesus Christ,

verses.original: τοῦ δόντος ἑαυτὸν ⸀ὑπὲρ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν ὅπως ἐξέληται ἡμᾶς ἐκ τοῦ ⸂αἰῶνος τοῦ ἐνεστῶτος⸃ πονηροῦ κατὰ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ πατρὸς ἡμῶν,
verses.translit: tou dontos eayton uper ton amartion emon opos exelitai emas ek tou aionos tou enestotos ponirou kata to thelima tou theou kai patros emon,
verses.translation: Who gave himself for our sins, that he might deliver us from this present evil world, according to the will of God and our Father:

verses.original: ᾧ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων· ἀμήν.
verses.translit: o e doxa eis tous aionas ton aionon* amin.
verses.translation: To whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen.

verses.original: Θαυμάζω ὅτι οὕτως ταχέως μετατίθεσθε ἀπὸ τοῦ καλέσαντος ὑμᾶς ἐν χάριτι Χριστοῦ εἰς ἕτερον εὐαγγέλιον,
verses.translit: Thaymazo oti outos taheos metatithesthe apo tou kalesantos umas en hariti Hristou eis eteron euaggelion,
verses.translation: I marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel:

verses.original: ὃ οὐκ ἔστιν ἄλλο· εἰ μή τινές εἰσιν οἱ ταράσσοντες ὑμᾶς καὶ θέλοντες μεταστρέψαι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Χριστοῦ.
verses.translit: o ouk estin allo* ei mi tines eisin oi tarassontes umas kai thelontes metastrepsai to euaggelion tou Hristou.
verses.translation: Which is not another; but there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ.

verses.original: ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐὰν ἡμεῖς ἢ ἄγγελος ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ⸀εὐαγγελίζηται ⸀ὑμῖν παρʼ ὃ εὐηγγελισάμεθα ὑμῖν, ἀνάθεμα ἔστω.
verses.translit: alla kai ean emeis e aggelos ex ouranou euaggelizitai umin par' o euiggelisametha umin, anathema esto.
verses.translation: But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed.

verses.original: ὡς προειρήκαμεν, καὶ ἄρτι πάλιν λέγω, εἴ τις ὑμᾶς εὐαγγελίζεται παρʼ ὃ παρελάβετε, ἀνάθεμα ἔστω.
verses.translit: os proeirikamen, kai arti palin lego, ei tis umas euaggelizetai par' o parelavete, anathema esto.
verses.translation: As we said before, so say I now again, If any man preach any other gospel unto you than that ye have received, let him be accursed.

verses.original: Ἄρτι γὰρ ἀνθρώπους πείθω ἢ τὸν θεόν; ἢ ζητῶ ἀνθρώποις ἀρέσκειν; ⸀εἰ ἔτι ἀνθρώποις ἤρεσκον, Χριστοῦ δοῦλος οὐκ ἂν ἤμην.
verses.translit: Arti gar anthropoys peitho e ton theon; e zito anthropois areskein; ei eti anthropois ereskon, Hristou doulos ouk an emin.
verses.translation: For do I now persuade men, or God? or do I seek to please men? for if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ.

verses.original: Γνωρίζω ⸀γὰρ ὑμῖν, ἀδελφοί, τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τὸ εὐαγγελισθὲν ὑπʼ ἐμοῦ ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν κατὰ ἄνθρωπον·
verses.translit: Gnorizo gar umin, adelfoi, to euaggelion to euaggelisthen up' emou oti ouk estin kata anthropon*
verses.translation: But I certify you, brethren, that the gospel which was preached of me is not after man.

verses.original: οὐδὲ γὰρ ἐγὼ παρὰ ἀνθρώπου παρέλαβον αὐτό, ⸀οὔτε ἐδιδάχθην, ἀλλὰ διʼ ἀποκαλύψεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
verses.translit: oude gar ego para anthropoy parelavon auto, oute edidahthin, alla di' apokalypseos Iisou Hristou.
verses.translation: For I neither received it of man, neither was I taught it , but by the revelation of Jesus Christ.

verses.original: Ἠκούσατε γὰρ τὴν ἐμὴν ἀναστροφήν ποτε ἐν τῷ Ἰουδαϊσμῷ, ὅτι καθʼ ὑπερβολὴν ἐδίωκον τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἐπόρθουν αὐτήν,
verses.translit: Ekoysate gar ten emen anastrofin pote en to Ioydaismo, oti kath' upervolen ediokon ten ekklisian tou theou kai eporthoyn autin,
verses.translation: For ye have heard of my conversation in time past in the Jews’ religion, how that beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and wasted it:

verses.original: καὶ προέκοπτον ἐν τῷ Ἰουδαϊσμῷ ὑπὲρ πολλοὺς συνηλικιώτας ἐν τῷ γένει μου, περισσοτέρως ζηλωτὴς ὑπάρχων τῶν πατρικῶν μου παραδόσεων.
verses.translit: kai proekopton en to Ioydaismo uper pollous synilikiotas en to genei moy, perissoteros zilotes uparhon ton patrikon moy paradoseon.
verses.translation: And profited in the Jews’ religion above many my equals in mine own nation, being more exceedingly zealous of the traditions of my fathers.

verses.original: ὅτε δὲ ⸀εὐδόκησεν ὁ ἀφορίσας με ἐκ κοιλίας μητρός μου καὶ καλέσας διὰ τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ
verses.translit: ote de eudokisen o aforisas me ek koilias mitros moy kai kalesas dia tes haritos autou
verses.translation: But when it pleased God, who separated me from my mother’s womb, and called me by his grace,

verses.original: ἀποκαλύψαι τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ ἐν ἐμοὶ ἵνα εὐαγγελίζωμαι αὐτὸν ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, εὐθέως οὐ προσανεθέμην σαρκὶ καὶ αἵματι,
verses.translit: apokalypsai ton yion autou en emoi ina euaggelizomai auton en tois ethnesin, eutheos ou prosanethemin sarki kai aimati,
verses.translation: To reveal his Son in me, that I might preach him among the heathen; immediately I conferred not with flesh and blood:

verses.original: οὐδὲ ἀνῆλθον εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα πρὸς τοὺς πρὸ ἐμοῦ ἀποστόλους, ἀλλὰ ἀπῆλθον εἰς Ἀραβίαν, καὶ πάλιν ὑπέστρεψα εἰς Δαμασκόν.
verses.translit: oude anelthon eis Ierosolyma pros tous pro emou apostoloys, alla apelthon eis Aravian, kai palin upestrepsa eis Damaskon.
verses.translation: Neither went I up to Jerusalem to them which were apostles before me; but I went into Arabia, and returned again unto Damascus.

verses.original: Ἔπειτα μετὰ ⸂ἔτη τρία⸃ ἀνῆλθον εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἱστορῆσαι ⸀Κηφᾶν, καὶ ἐπέμεινα πρὸς αὐτὸν ἡμέρας δεκαπέντε·
verses.translit: Epeita meta eti tria anelthon eis Ierosolyma istoresai Kifan, kai epemeina pros auton emeras dekapente*
verses.translation: Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to see Peter, and abode with him fifteen days.

verses.original: ἕτερον δὲ τῶν ἀποστόλων οὐκ εἶδον, εἰ μὴ Ἰάκωβον τὸν ἀδελφὸν τοῦ κυρίου.
verses.translit: eteron de ton apostolon ouk eidon, ei me Iakovon ton adelfon tou kyrioy.
verses.translation: But other of the apostles saw I none, save James the Lord’s brother.

verses.original: ἃ δὲ γράφω ὑμῖν, ἰδοὺ ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ ὅτι οὐ ψεύδομαι.
verses.translit: a de grafo umin, idou enopion tou theou oti ou pseydomai.
verses.translation: Now the things which I write unto you, behold, before God, I lie not.

verses.original: ἔπειτα ἦλθον εἰς τὰ κλίματα τῆς Συρίας καὶ τῆς Κιλικίας.
verses.translit: epeita elthon eis ta klimata tes Syrias kai tes Kilikias.
verses.translation: Afterwards I came into the regions of Syria and Cilicia;

verses.original: ἤμην δὲ ἀγνοούμενος τῷ προσώπῳ ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τῆς Ἰουδαίας ταῖς ἐν Χριστῷ,
verses.translit: emin de agnooymenos to prosopo tais ekklisiais tes Ioydaias tais en Hristo,
verses.translation: And was unknown by face unto the churches of Judaea which were in Christ:

verses.original: μόνον δὲ ἀκούοντες ἦσαν ὅτι Ὁ διώκων ἡμᾶς ποτε νῦν εὐαγγελίζεται τὴν πίστιν ἥν ποτε ἐπόρθει,
verses.translit: monon de akoyontes esan oti O diokon emas pote nun euaggelizetai ten pistin en pote eporthei,
verses.translation: But they had heard only, That he which persecuted us in times past now preacheth the faith which once he destroyed.

verses.original: καὶ ἐδόξαζον ἐν ἐμοὶ τὸν θεόν.
verses.translit: kai edoxazon en emoi ton theon.
verses.translation: And they glorified God in me.

verses.original: Ἔπειτα διὰ δεκατεσσάρων ἐτῶν πάλιν ἀνέβην εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα μετὰ Βαρναβᾶ συμπαραλαβὼν καὶ Τίτον·
verses.translit: Epeita dia dekatessaron eton palin anevin eis Ierosolyma meta Varnava symparalavon kai Titon*
verses.translation: Then fourteen years after I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, and took Titus with me also.

verses.original: ἀνέβην δὲ κατὰ ἀποκάλυψιν· καὶ ἀνεθέμην αὐτοῖς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον ὃ κηρύσσω ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, κατʼ ἰδίαν δὲ τοῖς δοκοῦσιν, μή πως εἰς κενὸν τρέχω ἢ ἔδραμον.
verses.translit: anevin de kata apokalypsin* kai anethemin autois to euaggelion o kirysso en tois ethnesin, kat' idian de tois dokousin, mi pos eis kenon treho e edramon.
verses.translation: And I went up by revelation, and communicated unto them that gospel which I preach among the Gentiles, but privately to them which were of reputation, lest by any means I should run, or had run, in vain.

verses.original: ἀλλʼ οὐδὲ Τίτος ὁ σὺν ἐμοί, Ἕλλην ὤν, ἠναγκάσθη περιτμηθῆναι·
verses.translit: all' oude Titos o sun emoi, Ellin on, enagkasthi peritmithenai*
verses.translation: But neither Titus, who was with me, being a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised:

verses.original: διὰ δὲ τοὺς παρεισάκτους ψευδαδέλφους, οἵτινες παρεισῆλθον κατασκοπῆσαι τὴν ἐλευθερίαν ἡμῶν ἣν ἔχομεν ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, ἵνα ἡμᾶς ⸀καταδουλώσουσιν—
verses.translit: dia de tous pareisaktoys pseydadelfoys, oitines pareiselthon kataskopesai ten eleytherian emon en ehomen en Hristo Iisou, ina emas katadoylosoysin--
verses.translation: And that because of false brethren unawares brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage:

verses.original: οἷς οὐδὲ πρὸς ὥραν εἴξαμεν τῇ ὑποταγῇ, ἵνα ἡ ἀλήθεια τοῦ εὐαγγελίου διαμείνῃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς.
verses.translit: ois oude pros oran eixamen te upotage, ina e alitheia tou euaggelioy diameine pros umas.
verses.translation: To whom we gave place by subjection, no, not for an hour; that the truth of the gospel might continue with you.

verses.original: ἀπὸ δὲ τῶν δοκούντων εἶναί τι— ὁποῖοί ποτε ἦσαν οὐδέν μοι διαφέρει· πρόσωπον ⸀θεὸς ἀνθρώπου οὐ λαμβάνει— ἐμοὶ γὰρ οἱ δοκοῦντες οὐδὲν προσανέθεντο,
verses.translit: apo de ton dokoynton einai ti-- opoioi pote esan ouden moi diaferei* prosopon theos anthropoy ou lamvanei-- emoi gar oi dokountes ouden prosanethento,
verses.translation: But of these who seemed to be somewhat, (whatsoever they were, it maketh no matter to me: God accepteth no man’s person:) for they who seemed to be somewhat in conference added nothing to me:

verses.original: ἀλλὰ τοὐναντίον ἰδόντες ὅτι πεπίστευμαι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς ἀκροβυστίας καθὼς Πέτρος τῆς περιτομῆς,
verses.translit: alla tounantion idontes oti pepisteymai to euaggelion tes akrovystias kathos Petros tes peritomes,
verses.translation: But contrariwise, when they saw that the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed unto me, as the gospel of the circumcision was unto Peter;

verses.original: ὁ γὰρ ἐνεργήσας Πέτρῳ εἰς ἀποστολὴν τῆς περιτομῆς ἐνήργησεν καὶ ἐμοὶ εἰς τὰ ἔθνη,
verses.translit: o gar energisas Petro eis apostolen tes peritomes enirgisen kai emoi eis ta ethni,
verses.translation: (For he that wrought effectually in Peter to the apostleship of the circumcision, the same was mighty in me toward the Gentiles:)

verses.original: καὶ γνόντες τὴν χάριν τὴν δοθεῖσάν μοι, Ἰάκωβος καὶ Κηφᾶς καὶ Ἰωάννης, οἱ δοκοῦντες στῦλοι εἶναι, δεξιὰς ἔδωκαν ἐμοὶ καὶ Βαρναβᾷ κοινωνίας, ἵνα ⸀ἡμεῖς εἰς τὰ ἔθνη, αὐτοὶ δὲ εἰς τὴν περιτομήν·
verses.translit: kai gnontes ten harin ten dotheisan moi, Iakovos kai Kifas kai Ioannis, oi dokountes stuloi einai, dexias edokan emoi kai Varnava koinonias, ina emeis eis ta ethni, autoi de eis ten peritomin*
verses.translation: And when James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars, perceived the grace that was given unto me, they gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship; that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision.

verses.original: μόνον τῶν πτωχῶν ἵνα μνημονεύωμεν, ὃ καὶ ἐσπούδασα αὐτὸ τοῦτο ποιῆσαι.
verses.translit: monon ton ptohon ina mnimoneyomen, o kai espoydasa auto touto poiesai.
verses.translation: Only they would that we should remember the poor; the same which I also was forward to do.

verses.original: Ὅτε δὲ ἦλθεν ⸀Κηφᾶς εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν, κατὰ πρόσωπον αὐτῷ ἀντέστην, ὅτι κατεγνωσμένος ἦν·
verses.translit: Ote de elthen Kifas eis Antioheian, kata prosopon auto antestin, oti kategnosmenos en*
verses.translation: But when Peter was come to Antioch, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed.

verses.original: πρὸ τοῦ γὰρ ἐλθεῖν τινας ἀπὸ Ἰακώβου μετὰ τῶν ἐθνῶν συνήσθιεν· ὅτε δὲ ⸀ἦλθον, ὑπέστελλεν καὶ ἀφώριζεν ἑαυτόν, φοβούμενος τοὺς ἐκ περιτομῆς.
verses.translit: pro tou gar elthein tinas apo Iakovoy meta ton ethnon synisthien* ote de elthon, upestellen kai aforizen eayton, fovoymenos tous ek peritomes.
verses.translation: For before that certain came from James, he did eat with the Gentiles: but when they were come, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision.

verses.original: καὶ συνυπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ ⸀καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ Ἰουδαῖοι, ὥστε καὶ Βαρναβᾶς συναπήχθη αὐτῶν τῇ ὑποκρίσει.
verses.translit: kai synypekrithisan auto kai oi loipoi Ioydaioi, oste kai Varnavas synapihthi auton te upokrisei.
verses.translation: And the other Jews dissembled likewise with him; insomuch that Barnabas also was carried away with their dissimulation.

verses.original: ἀλλʼ ὅτε εἶδον ὅτι οὐκ ὀρθοποδοῦσιν πρὸς τὴν ἀλήθειαν τοῦ εὐαγγελίου, εἶπον τῷ ⸀Κηφᾷ ἔμπροσθεν πάντων· Εἰ σὺ Ἰουδαῖος ὑπάρχων ἐθνικῶς ⸂καὶ ⸀οὐκ Ἰουδαϊκῶς ζῇς⸃, ⸀πῶς τὰ ἔθνη ἀναγκάζεις Ἰουδαΐζειν;
verses.translit: all' ote eidon oti ouk orthopodousin pros ten alitheian tou euaggelioy, eipon to Kifa emprosthen panton* Ei su Ioydaios uparhon ethnikos kai ouk Ioydaikos zes, pos ta ethni anagkazeis IoydaIzein;
verses.translation: But when I saw that they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel, I said unto Peter before them all, If thou, being a Jew, livest after the manner of Gentiles, and not as do the Jews, why compellest thou the Gentiles to live as do the Jews?

verses.original: Ἡμεῖς φύσει Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ οὐκ ἐξ ἐθνῶν ἁμαρτωλοί,
verses.translit: Emeis fysei Ioydaioi kai ouk ex ethnon amartoloi,
verses.translation: We who are Jews by nature, and not sinners of the Gentiles,

verses.original: εἰδότες ⸀δὲ ὅτι οὐ δικαιοῦται ἄνθρωπος ἐξ ἔργων νόμου ἐὰν μὴ διὰ πίστεως ⸂Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ⸃, καὶ ἡμεῖς εἰς Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐπιστεύσαμεν, ἵνα δικαιωθῶμεν ἐκ πίστεως Χριστοῦ καὶ οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων νόμου, ⸂ὅτι ἐξ ἔργων νόμου οὐ δικαιωθήσεται⸃ πᾶσα σάρξ.
verses.translit: eidotes de oti ou dikaioutai anthropos ex ergon nomoy ean me dia pisteos Iisou Hristou, kai emeis eis Hriston Iisoun episteysamen, ina dikaiothomen ek pisteos Hristou kai ouk ex ergon nomoy, oti ex ergon nomoy ou dikaiothisetai pasa sarx.
verses.translation: Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified.

verses.original: εἰ δὲ ζητοῦντες δικαιωθῆναι ἐν Χριστῷ εὑρέθημεν καὶ αὐτοὶ ἁμαρτωλοί, ἆρα Χριστὸς ἁμαρτίας διάκονος; μὴ γένοιτο·
verses.translit: ei de zitountes dikaiothenai en Hristo eurethimen kai autoi amartoloi, ara Hristos amartias diakonos; me genoito*
verses.translation: But if, while we seek to be justified by Christ, we ourselves also are found sinners, is therefore Christ the minister of sin? God forbid.

verses.original: εἰ γὰρ ἃ κατέλυσα ταῦτα πάλιν οἰκοδομῶ, παραβάτην ἐμαυτὸν ⸀συνιστάνω.
verses.translit: ei gar a katelysa tauta palin oikodomo, paravatin emayton synistano.
verses.translation: For if I build again the things which I destroyed, I make myself a transgressor.

verses.original: ἐγὼ γὰρ διὰ νόμου νόμῳ ἀπέθανον ἵνα θεῷ ζήσω· Χριστῷ συνεσταύρωμαι·
verses.translit: ego gar dia nomoy nomo apethanon ina theo ziso* Hristo synestayromai*
verses.translation: For I through the law am dead to the law, that I might live unto God.

verses.original: ζῶ δὲ οὐκέτι ἐγώ, ζῇ δὲ ἐν ἐμοὶ Χριστός· ὃ δὲ νῦν ζῶ ἐν σαρκί, ἐν πίστει ζῶ τῇ τοῦ ⸂υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ⸃ τοῦ ἀγαπήσαντός με καὶ παραδόντος ἑαυτὸν ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ.
verses.translit: zo de ouketi ego, ze de en emoi Hristos* o de nun zo en sarki, en pistei zo te tou yiou tou theou tou agapisantos me kai paradontos eayton uper emou.
verses.translation: I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me.

verses.original: οὐκ ἀθετῶ τὴν χάριν τοῦ θεοῦ· εἰ γὰρ διὰ νόμου δικαιοσύνη, ἄρα Χριστὸς δωρεὰν ἀπέθανεν.
verses.translit: ouk atheto ten harin tou theou* ei gar dia nomoy dikaiosyni, ara Hristos dorean apethanen.
verses.translation: I do not frustrate the grace of God: for if righteousness come by the law, then Christ is dead in vain.

verses.original: Ὦ ἀνόητοι Γαλάται, τίς ὑμᾶς ⸀ἐβάσκανεν, οἷς κατʼ ὀφθαλμοὺς Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ⸀προεγράφη ἐσταυρωμένος;
verses.translit: O anoitoi Galatai, tis umas evaskanen, ois kat' ofthalmous Iisous Hristos proegrafi estayromenos;
verses.translation: O foolish Galatians, who hath bewitched you, that ye should not obey the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ hath been evidently set forth, crucified among you?

verses.original: τοῦτο μόνον θέλω μαθεῖν ἀφʼ ὑμῶν, ἐξ ἔργων νόμου τὸ πνεῦμα ἐλάβετε ἢ ἐξ ἀκοῆς πίστεως;
verses.translit: touto monon thelo mathein af' umon, ex ergon nomoy to pneuma elavete e ex akoes pisteos;
verses.translation: This only would I learn of you, Received ye the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?

verses.original: οὕτως ἀνόητοί ἐστε; ἐναρξάμενοι πνεύματι νῦν σαρκὶ ἐπιτελεῖσθε;
verses.translit: outos anoitoi este? enarxamenoi pneymati nun sarki epiteleisthe;
verses.translation: Are ye so foolish? having begun in the Spirit, are ye now made perfect by the flesh?

verses.original: τοσαῦτα ἐπάθετε εἰκῇ; εἴ γε καὶ εἰκῇ.
verses.translit: tosauta epathete eike; ei ge kai eike.
verses.translation: Have ye suffered so many things in vain? if it be yet in vain.

verses.original: ὁ οὖν ἐπιχορηγῶν ὑμῖν τὸ πνεῦμα καὶ ἐνεργῶν δυνάμεις ἐν ὑμῖν ἐξ ἔργων νόμου ἢ ἐξ ἀκοῆς πίστεως;
verses.translit: o oun epihorigon umin to pneuma kai energon dynameis en umin ex ergon nomoy e ex akoes pisteos;
verses.translation: He therefore that ministereth to you the Spirit, and worketh miracles among you, doeth he it by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?

verses.original: καθὼς Ἀβραὰμ ἐπίστευσεν τῷ θεῷ, καὶ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην.
verses.translit: kathos Avraam episteysen to theo, kai elogisthi auto eis dikaiosynin.
verses.translation: Even as Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness.

verses.original: Γινώσκετε ἄρα ὅτι οἱ ἐκ πίστεως, οὗτοι ⸂υἱοί εἰσιν⸃ Ἀβραάμ.
verses.translit: Ginoskete ara oti oi ek pisteos, outoi yioi eisin Avraam.
verses.translation: Know ye therefore that they which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham.

verses.original: προϊδοῦσα δὲ ἡ γραφὴ ὅτι ἐκ πίστεως δικαιοῖ τὰ ἔθνη ὁ θεὸς προευηγγελίσατο τῷ Ἀβραὰμ ὅτι Ἐνευλογηθήσονται ἐν σοὶ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη.
verses.translit: proidousa de e grafe oti ek pisteos dikaioi ta ethni o theos proeyiggelisato to Avraam oti Eneylogithisontai en soi panta ta ethni.
verses.translation: And the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham, saying , In thee shall all nations be blessed.

verses.original: ὥστε οἱ ἐκ πίστεως εὐλογοῦνται σὺν τῷ πιστῷ Ἀβραάμ.
verses.translit: oste oi ek pisteos eulogountai sun to pisto Avraam.
verses.translation: So then they which be of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham.

verses.original: Ὅσοι γὰρ ἐξ ἔργων νόμου εἰσὶν ὑπὸ κατάραν εἰσίν, γέγραπται γὰρ ⸀ὅτι Ἐπικατάρατος πᾶς ὃς οὐκ ⸀ἐμμένει πᾶσιν τοῖς γεγραμμένοις ἐν τῷ βιβλίῳ τοῦ νόμου τοῦ ποιῆσαι αὐτά.
verses.translit: Osoi gar ex ergon nomoy eisin upo kataran eisin, gegraptai gar oti Epikataratos pas os ouk emmenei pasin tois gegrammenois en to vivlio tou nomoy tou poiesai auta.
verses.translation: For as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse: for it is written, Cursed is every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them.

verses.original: ὅτι δὲ ἐν νόμῳ οὐδεὶς δικαιοῦται παρὰ τῷ θεῷ δῆλον, ὅτι Ὁ δίκαιος ἐκ πίστεως ζήσεται,
verses.translit: oti de en nomo oudeis dikaioutai para to theo delon, oti O dikaios ek pisteos zisetai,
verses.translation: But that no man is justified by the law in the sight of God, it is evident: for, The just shall live by faith.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ νόμος οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ πίστεως, ἀλλʼ· Ὁ ποιήσας ⸀αὐτὰ ζήσεται ἐν αὐτοῖς.
verses.translit: o de nomos ouk estin ek pisteos, all'* O poiisas auta zisetai en autois.
verses.translation: And the law is not of faith: but, The man that doeth them shall live in them.

verses.original: Χριστὸς ἡμᾶς ἐξηγόρασεν ἐκ τῆς κατάρας τοῦ νόμου γενόμενος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν κατάρα, ⸂ὅτι γέγραπται⸃· Ἐπικατάρατος πᾶς ὁ κρεμάμενος ἐπὶ ξύλου,
verses.translit: Hristos emas exigorasen ek tes kataras tou nomoy genomenos uper emon katara, oti gegraptai* Epikataratos pas o kremamenos epi xyloy,
verses.translation: Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree:

verses.original: ἵνα εἰς τὰ ἔθνη ἡ εὐλογία τοῦ Ἀβραὰμ γένηται ἐν ⸂Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ⸃, ἵνα τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ πνεύματος λάβωμεν διὰ τῆς πίστεως.
verses.translit: ina eis ta ethni e eulogia tou Avraam genitai en Hristo Iisou, ina ten epaggelian tou pneymatos lavomen dia tes pisteos.
verses.translation: That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ; that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.

verses.original: Ἀδελφοί, κατὰ ἄνθρωπον λέγω· ὅμως ἀνθρώπου κεκυρωμένην διαθήκην οὐδεὶς ἀθετεῖ ἢ ἐπιδιατάσσεται.
verses.translit: Adelfoi, kata anthropon lego* omos anthropoy kekyromenin diathikin oudeis athetei e epidiatassetai.
verses.translation: Brethren, I speak after the manner of men; Though it be but a man’s covenant, yet if it be confirmed, no man disannulleth, or addeth thereto.

verses.original: τῷ δὲ Ἀβραὰμ ἐρρέθησαν αἱ ἐπαγγελίαι καὶ τῷ σπέρματι αὐτοῦ· οὐ λέγει· Καὶ τοῖς σπέρμασιν, ὡς ἐπὶ πολλῶν, ἀλλʼ ὡς ἐφʼ ἑνός· Καὶ τῷ σπέρματί σου, ὅς ἐστιν Χριστός.
verses.translit: to de Avraam errethisan ai epaggeliai kai to spermati autou* ou legei* Kai tois spermasin, os epi pollon, all' os ef' enos* Kai to spermati soy, os estin Hristos.
verses.translation: Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ.

verses.original: τοῦτο δὲ λέγω· διαθήκην προκεκυρωμένην ὑπὸ τοῦ ⸀θεοῦ ὁ μετὰ ⸂τετρακόσια καὶ τριάκοντα ἔτη⸃ γεγονὼς νόμος οὐκ ἀκυροῖ, εἰς τὸ καταργῆσαι τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν.
verses.translit: touto de lego* diathikin prokekyromenin upo tou theou o meta tetrakosia kai triakonta eti gegonos nomos ouk akyroi, eis to katargesai ten epaggelian.
verses.translation: And this I say, that the covenant, that was confirmed before of God in Christ, the law, which was four hundred and thirty years after, cannot disannul, that it should make the promise of none effect.

verses.original: εἰ γὰρ ἐκ νόμου ἡ κληρονομία, οὐκέτι ἐξ ἐπαγγελίας· τῷ δὲ Ἀβραὰμ διʼ ἐπαγγελίας κεχάρισται ὁ θεός.
verses.translit: ei gar ek nomoy e klironomia, ouketi ex epaggelias* to de Avraam di' epaggelias keharistai o theos.
verses.translation: For if the inheritance be of the law, it is no more of promise: but God gave it to Abraham by promise.

verses.original: Τί οὖν ὁ νόμος; τῶν παραβάσεων χάριν προσετέθη, ἄχρις ⸀οὗ ἔλθῃ τὸ σπέρμα ᾧ ἐπήγγελται, διαταγεὶς διʼ ἀγγέλων ἐν χειρὶ μεσίτου·
verses.translit: Ti oun o nomos; ton paravaseon harin prosetethi, ahris ou elthe to sperma o epiggeltai, diatageis di' aggelon en heiri mesitoy*
verses.translation: Wherefore then serveth the law? It was added because of transgressions, till the seed should come to whom the promise was made; and it was ordained by angels in the hand of a mediator.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ μεσίτης ἑνὸς οὐκ ἔστιν, ὁ δὲ θεὸς εἷς ἐστιν.
verses.translit: o de mesitis enos ouk estin, o de theos eis estin.
verses.translation: Now a mediator is not a mediator of one, but God is one.

verses.original: Ὁ οὖν νόμος κατὰ τῶν ἐπαγγελιῶν τοῦ θεοῦ; μὴ γένοιτο· εἰ γὰρ ἐδόθη νόμος ὁ δυνάμενος ζῳοποιῆσαι, ὄντως ⸂ἐκ νόμου ἂν⸃ ἦν ἡ δικαιοσύνη.
verses.translit: O oun nomos kata ton epaggelion tou theou; me genoito* ei gar edothi nomos o dynamenos zoopoiesai, ontos ek nomoy an en e dikaiosyni.
verses.translation: Is the law then against the promises of God? God forbid: for if there had been a law given which could have given life, verily righteousness should have been by the law.

verses.original: ἀλλὰ συνέκλεισεν ἡ γραφὴ τὰ πάντα ὑπὸ ἁμαρτίαν ἵνα ἡ ἐπαγγελία ἐκ πίστεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ δοθῇ τοῖς πιστεύουσιν.
verses.translit: alla synekleisen e grafe ta panta upo amartian ina e epaggelia ek pisteos Iisou Hristou dothe tois pisteyoysin.
verses.translation: But the scripture hath concluded all under sin, that the promise by faith of Jesus Christ might be given to them that believe.

verses.original: Πρὸ τοῦ δὲ ἐλθεῖν τὴν πίστιν ὑπὸ νόμον ἐφρουρούμεθα ⸀συγκλειόμενοι εἰς τὴν μέλλουσαν πίστιν ἀποκαλυφθῆναι.
verses.translit: Pro tou de elthein ten pistin upo nomon efroyroymetha sygkleiomenoi eis ten melloysan pistin apokalyfthenai.
verses.translation: But before faith came, we were kept under the law, shut up unto the faith which should afterwards be revealed.

verses.original: ὥστε ὁ νόμος παιδαγωγὸς ἡμῶν γέγονεν εἰς Χριστόν, ἵνα ἐκ πίστεως δικαιωθῶμεν·
verses.translit: oste o nomos paidagogos emon gegonen eis Hriston, ina ek pisteos dikaiothomen*
verses.translation: Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith.

verses.original: ἐλθούσης δὲ τῆς πίστεως οὐκέτι ὑπὸ παιδαγωγόν ἐσμεν.
verses.translit: elthoysis de tes pisteos ouketi upo paidagogon esmen.
verses.translation: But after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster.

verses.original: πάντες γὰρ υἱοὶ θεοῦ ἐστε διὰ τῆς πίστεως ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.
verses.translit: pantes gar yioi theou este dia tes pisteos en Hristo Iisou.
verses.translation: For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus.

verses.original: ὅσοι γὰρ εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε, Χριστὸν ἐνεδύσασθε·
verses.translit: osoi gar eis Hriston evaptisthite, Hriston enedysasthe*
verses.translation: For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ.

verses.original: οὐκ ἔνι Ἰουδαῖος οὐδὲ Ἕλλην, οὐκ ἔνι δοῦλος οὐδὲ ἐλεύθερος, οὐκ ἔνι ἄρσεν καὶ θῆλυ· ⸀πάντες γὰρ ὑμεῖς εἷς ἐστε ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.
verses.translit: ouk eni Ioydaios oude Ellin, ouk eni doulos oude eleytheros, ouk eni arsen kai thely* pantes gar umeis eis este en Hristo Iisou.
verses.translation: There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus.

verses.original: εἰ δὲ ὑμεῖς Χριστοῦ, ἄρα τοῦ Ἀβραὰμ σπέρμα ἐστέ, ⸀κατʼ ἐπαγγελίαν κληρονόμοι.
verses.translit: ei de umeis Hristou, ara tou Avraam sperma este, kat' epaggelian klironomoi.
verses.translation: And if ye be Christ’s, then are ye Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise.

verses.original: Λέγω δέ, ἐφʼ ὅσον χρόνον ὁ κληρονόμος νήπιός ἐστιν, οὐδὲν διαφέρει δούλου κύριος πάντων ὤν,
verses.translit: Lego de, ef' oson hronon o klironomos nipios estin, ouden diaferei doyloy kyrios panton on,
verses.translation: Now I say, That the heir, as long as he is a child, differeth nothing from a servant, though he be lord of all;

verses.original: ἀλλὰ ὑπὸ ἐπιτρόπους ἐστὶ καὶ οἰκονόμους ἄχρι τῆς προθεσμίας τοῦ πατρός.
verses.translit: alla upo epitropoys esti kai oikonomoys ahri tes prothesmias tou patros.
verses.translation: But is under tutors and governors until the time appointed of the father.

verses.original: οὕτως καὶ ἡμεῖς, ὅτε ἦμεν νήπιοι, ὑπὸ τὰ στοιχεῖα τοῦ κόσμου ⸀ἤμεθα δεδουλωμένοι·
verses.translit: outos kai emeis, ote emen nipioi, upo ta stoiheia tou kosmoy emetha dedoylomenoi*
verses.translation: Even so we, when we were children, were in bondage under the elements of the world:

verses.original: ὅτε δὲ ἦλθεν τὸ πλήρωμα τοῦ χρόνου, ἐξαπέστειλεν ὁ θεὸς τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ, γενόμενον ἐκ γυναικός, γενόμενον ὑπὸ νόμον,
verses.translit: ote de elthen to pliroma tou hronoy, exapesteilen o theos ton yion autou, genomenon ek gynaikos, genomenon upo nomon,
verses.translation: But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law,

verses.original: ἵνα τοὺς ὑπὸ νόμον ἐξαγοράσῃ, ἵνα τὴν υἱοθεσίαν ἀπολάβωμεν.
verses.translit: ina tous upo nomon exagorase, ina ten yiothesian apolavomen.
verses.translation: To redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons.

verses.original: ὅτι δέ ἐστε υἱοί, ἐξαπέστειλεν ὁ θεὸς τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰς καρδίας ⸀ἡμῶν, κρᾶζον· Αββα ὁ πατήρ.
verses.translit: oti de este yioi, exapesteilen o theos to pneuma tou yiou autou eis tas kardias emon, krazon* Avva o patir.
verses.translation: And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father.

verses.original: ὥστε οὐκέτι εἶ δοῦλος ἀλλὰ υἱός· εἰ δὲ υἱός, καὶ κληρονόμος ⸂διὰ θεοῦ⸃.
verses.translit: oste ouketi ei doulos alla yios* ei de yios, kai klironomos dia theou.
verses.translation: Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ.

verses.original: Ἀλλὰ τότε μὲν οὐκ εἰδότες θεὸν ἐδουλεύσατε τοῖς ⸂φύσει μὴ⸃ οὖσι θεοῖς·
verses.translit: Alla tote men ouk eidotes theon edoyleysate tois fysei me ousi theois*
verses.translation: Howbeit then, when ye knew not God, ye did service unto them which by nature are no gods.

verses.original: νῦν δὲ γνόντες θεόν, μᾶλλον δὲ γνωσθέντες ὑπὸ θεοῦ, πῶς ἐπιστρέφετε πάλιν ἐπὶ τὰ ἀσθενῆ καὶ πτωχὰ στοιχεῖα, οἷς πάλιν ἄνωθεν ⸀δουλεύειν θέλετε;
verses.translit: nun de gnontes theon, mallon de gnosthentes upo theou, pos epistrefete palin epi ta asthene kai ptoha stoiheia, ois palin anothen doyleyein thelete;
verses.translation: But now, after that ye have known God, or rather are known of God, how turn ye again to the weak and beggarly elements, whereunto ye desire again to be in bondage?

verses.original: ἡμέρας παρατηρεῖσθε καὶ μῆνας καὶ καιροὺς καὶ ἐνιαυτούς.
verses.translit: emeras paratireisthe kai menas kai kairous kai eniaytoys.
