verses.translation: Seeing then that we have a great high priest, that is passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our profession.

verses.original: οὐ γὰρ ἔχομεν ἀρχιερέα μὴ δυνάμενον συμπαθῆσαι ταῖς ἀσθενείαις ἡμῶν, ⸀πεπειρασμένον δὲ κατὰ πάντα καθʼ ὁμοιότητα χωρὶς ἁμαρτίας.
verses.translit: ou gar ehomen arhierea me dynamenon sympathesai tais astheneiais emon, pepeirasmenon de kata panta kath' omoiotita horis amartias.
verses.translation: For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin.

verses.original: προσερχώμεθα οὖν μετὰ παρρησίας τῷ θρόνῳ τῆς χάριτος, ἵνα λάβωμεν ἔλεος καὶ χάριν εὕρωμεν εἰς εὔκαιρον βοήθειαν.
verses.translit: proserhometha oun meta parrisias to throno tes haritos, ina lavomen eleos kai harin euromen eis eukairon voitheian.
verses.translation: Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.

verses.original: Πᾶς γὰρ ἀρχιερεὺς ἐξ ἀνθρώπων λαμβανόμενος ὑπὲρ ἀνθρώπων καθίσταται τὰ πρὸς τὸν θεόν, ἵνα προσφέρῃ δῶρά τε καὶ θυσίας ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτιῶν,
verses.translit: Pas gar arhiereus ex anthropon lamvanomenos uper anthropon kathistatai ta pros ton theon, ina prosfere dora te kai thysias uper amartion,
verses.translation: For every high priest taken from among men is ordained for men in things pertaining to God, that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins:

verses.original: μετριοπαθεῖν δυνάμενος τοῖς ἀγνοοῦσι καὶ πλανωμένοις ἐπεὶ καὶ αὐτὸς περίκειται ἀσθένειαν,
verses.translit: metriopathein dynamenos tois agnoousi kai planomenois epei kai autos perikeitai astheneian,
verses.translation: Who can have compassion on the ignorant, and on them that are out of the way; for that he himself also is compassed with infirmity.

verses.original: καὶ ⸂διʼ αὐτὴν⸃ ὀφείλει, καθὼς περὶ τοῦ λαοῦ, οὕτως καὶ περὶ ⸀αὑτοῦ προσφέρειν ⸀περὶ ἁμαρτιῶν.
verses.translit: kai di' auten ofeilei, kathos peri tou laou, outos kai peri autou prosferein peri amartion.
verses.translation: And by reason hereof he ought, as for the people, so also for himself, to offer for sins.

verses.original: καὶ οὐχ ἑαυτῷ τις λαμβάνει τὴν τιμήν, ἀλλὰ καλούμενος ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ, ⸀καθώσπερ καὶ Ἀαρών.
verses.translit: kai ouh eayto tis lamvanei ten timin, alla kaloymenos upo tou theou, kathosper kai Aaron.
verses.translation: And no man taketh this honour unto himself, but he that is called of God, as was Aaron.

verses.original: Οὕτως καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς οὐχ ἑαυτὸν ἐδόξασεν γενηθῆναι ἀρχιερέα, ἀλλʼ ὁ λαλήσας πρὸς αὐτόν· Υἱός μου εἶ σύ, ἐγὼ σήμερον γεγέννηκά σε·
verses.translit: Outos kai o Hristos ouh eayton edoxasen genithenai arhierea, all' o lalisas pros auton* Yios moy ei sy, ego simeron gegennika se*
verses.translation: So also Christ glorified not himself to be made an high priest; but he that said unto him, Thou art my Son, to day have I begotten thee.

verses.original: καθὼς καὶ ἐν ἑτέρῳ λέγει· Σὺ ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισέδεκ,
verses.translit: kathos kai en etero legei* Su iereus eis ton aiona kata ten taxin Melhisedek,
verses.translation: As he saith also in another place , Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.

verses.original: ὃς ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τῆς σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ δεήσεις τε καὶ ἱκετηρίας πρὸς τὸν δυνάμενον σῴζειν αὐτὸν ἐκ θανάτου μετὰ κραυγῆς ἰσχυρᾶς καὶ δακρύων προσενέγκας καὶ εἰσακουσθεὶς ἀπὸ τῆς εὐλαβείας,
verses.translit: os en tais emerais tes sarkos autou deiseis te kai iketirias pros ton dynamenon sozein auton ek thanatoy meta krayges ishyras kai dakryon prosenegkas kai eisakoystheis apo tes eulaveias,
verses.translation: Who in the days of his flesh, when he had offered up prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears unto him that was able to save him from death, and was heard in that he feared;

verses.original: καίπερ ὢν υἱός, ἔμαθεν ἀφʼ ὧν ἔπαθεν τὴν ὑπακοήν,
verses.translit: kaiper on yios, emathen af' on epathen ten upakoin,
verses.translation: Though he were a Son, yet learned he obedience by the things which he suffered;

verses.original: καὶ τελειωθεὶς ἐγένετο ⸂πᾶσιν τοῖς ὑπακούουσιν αὐτῷ⸃ αἴτιος σωτηρίας αἰωνίου,
verses.translit: kai teleiotheis egeneto pasin tois upakoyoysin auto aitios sotirias aionioy,
verses.translation: And being made perfect, he became the author of eternal salvation unto all them that obey him;

verses.original: προσαγορευθεὶς ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ ἀρχιερεὺς κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισέδεκ.
verses.translit: prosagoreytheis upo tou theou arhiereus kata ten taxin Melhisedek.
verses.translation: Called of God an high priest after the order of Melchisedec.

verses.original: Περὶ οὗ πολὺς ἡμῖν ὁ λόγος καὶ δυσερμήνευτος λέγειν, ἐπεὶ νωθροὶ γεγόνατε ταῖς ἀκοαῖς·
verses.translit: Peri ou polus emin o logos kai dysermineytos legein, epei nothroi gegonate tais akoais*
verses.translation: Of whom we have many things to say, and hard to be uttered, seeing ye are dull of hearing.

verses.original: καὶ γὰρ ὀφείλοντες εἶναι διδάσκαλοι διὰ τὸν χρόνον, πάλιν χρείαν ἔχετε τοῦ διδάσκειν ὑμᾶς ⸀τινὰ τὰ στοιχεῖα τῆς ἀρχῆς τῶν λογίων τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ γεγόνατε χρείαν ἔχοντες γάλακτος, ⸀οὐ στερεᾶς τροφῆς.
verses.translit: kai gar ofeilontes einai didaskaloi dia ton hronon, palin hreian ehete tou didaskein umas tina ta stoiheia tes arhes ton logion tou theou, kai gegonate hreian ehontes galaktos, ou stereas trofes.
verses.translation: For when for the time ye ought to be teachers, ye have need that one teach you again which be the first principles of the oracles of God; and are become such as have need of milk, and not of strong meat.

verses.original: πᾶς γὰρ ὁ μετέχων γάλακτος ἄπειρος λόγου δικαιοσύνης, νήπιος γάρ ἐστιν·
verses.translit: pas gar o metehon galaktos apeiros logoy dikaiosynis, nipios gar estin*
verses.translation: For every one that useth milk is unskilful in the word of righteousness: for he is a babe.

verses.original: τελείων δέ ἐστιν ἡ στερεὰ τροφή, τῶν διὰ τὴν ἕξιν τὰ αἰσθητήρια γεγυμνασμένα ἐχόντων πρὸς διάκρισιν καλοῦ τε καὶ κακοῦ.
verses.translit: teleion de estin e sterea trofi, ton dia ten exin ta aisthitiria gegymnasmena ehonton pros diakrisin kalou te kai kakou.
verses.translation: But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.

verses.original: Διὸ ἀφέντες τὸν τῆς ἀρχῆς τοῦ Χριστοῦ λόγον ἐπὶ τὴν τελειότητα φερώμεθα, μὴ πάλιν θεμέλιον καταβαλλόμενοι μετανοίας ἀπὸ νεκρῶν ἔργων, καὶ πίστεως ἐπὶ θεόν,
verses.translit: Dio afentes ton tes arhes tou Hristou logon epi ten teleiotita ferometha, me palin themelion katavallomenoi metanoias apo nekron ergon, kai pisteos epi theon,
verses.translation: Therefore leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection; not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith toward God,

verses.original: βαπτισμῶν ⸀διδαχὴν ἐπιθέσεώς τε χειρῶν, ἀναστάσεώς ⸀τε νεκρῶν καὶ κρίματος αἰωνίου.
verses.translit: vaptismon didahen epitheseos te heiron, anastaseos te nekron kai krimatos aionioy.
verses.translation: Of the doctrine of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.

verses.original: καὶ τοῦτο ⸀ποιήσομεν ἐάνπερ ἐπιτρέπῃ ὁ θεός.
verses.translit: kai touto poiisomen eanper epitrepe o theos.
verses.translation: And this will we do, if God permit.

verses.original: Ἀδύνατον γὰρ τοὺς ἅπαξ φωτισθέντας γευσαμένους τε τῆς δωρεᾶς τῆς ἐπουρανίου καὶ μετόχους γενηθέντας πνεύματος ἁγίου
verses.translit: Adynaton gar tous apax fotisthentas geysamenoys te tes doreas tes epoyranioy kai metohoys genithentas pneymatos agioy
verses.translation: For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost,

verses.original: καὶ καλὸν γευσαμένους θεοῦ ῥῆμα δυνάμεις τε μέλλοντος αἰῶνος,
verses.translit: kai kalon geysamenoys theou Rema dynameis te mellontos aionos,
verses.translation: And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come,

verses.original: καὶ παραπεσόντας, πάλιν ἀνακαινίζειν εἰς μετάνοιαν, ἀνασταυροῦντας ἑαυτοῖς τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ παραδειγματίζοντας.
verses.translit: kai parapesontas, palin anakainizein eis metanoian, anastayrountas eaytois ton yion tou theou kai paradeigmatizontas.
verses.translation: If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame.

verses.original: γῆ γὰρ ἡ πιοῦσα τὸν ἐπʼ αὐτῆς ⸂ἐρχόμενον πολλάκις⸃ ὑετόν, καὶ τίκτουσα βοτάνην εὔθετον ἐκείνοις διʼ οὓς καὶ γεωργεῖται, μεταλαμβάνει εὐλογίας ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ·
verses.translit: ge gar e piousa ton ep' autes erhomenon pollakis ueton, kai tiktoysa votanin eutheton ekeinois di' ous kai georgeitai, metalamvanei eulogias apo tou theou*
verses.translation: For the earth which drinketh in the rain that cometh oft upon it, and bringeth forth herbs meet for them by whom it is dressed, receiveth blessing from God:

verses.original: ἐκφέρουσα δὲ ἀκάνθας καὶ τριβόλους ἀδόκιμος καὶ κατάρας ἐγγύς, ἧς τὸ τέλος εἰς καῦσιν.
verses.translit: ekferoysa de akanthas kai trivoloys adokimos kai kataras eggys, es to telos eis kausin.
verses.translation: But that which beareth thorns and briers is rejected, and is nigh unto cursing; whose end is to be burned.

verses.original: Πεπείσμεθα δὲ περὶ ὑμῶν, ἀγαπητοί, τὰ κρείσσονα καὶ ἐχόμενα σωτηρίας, εἰ καὶ οὕτως λαλοῦμεν·
verses.translit: Pepeismetha de peri umon, agapitoi, ta kreissona kai ehomena sotirias, ei kai outos laloumen*
verses.translation: But, beloved, we are persuaded better things of you, and things that accompany salvation, though we thus speak.

verses.original: οὐ γὰρ ἄδικος ὁ θεὸς ἐπιλαθέσθαι τοῦ ἔργου ὑμῶν ⸀καὶ τῆς ἀγάπης ἧς ἐνεδείξασθε εἰς τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ, διακονήσαντες τοῖς ἁγίοις καὶ διακονοῦντες.
verses.translit: ou gar adikos o theos epilathesthai tou ergoy umon kai tes agapis es enedeixasthe eis to onoma autou, diakonisantes tois agiois kai diakonountes.
verses.translation: For God is not unrighteous to forget your work and labour of love, which ye have shewed toward his name, in that ye have ministered to the saints, and do minister.

verses.original: ἐπιθυμοῦμεν δὲ ἕκαστον ὑμῶν τὴν αὐτὴν ἐνδείκνυσθαι σπουδὴν πρὸς τὴν πληροφορίαν τῆς ἐλπίδος ἄχρι τέλους,
verses.translit: epithymoumen de ekaston umon ten auten endeiknysthai spoyden pros ten pliroforian tes elpidos ahri teloys,
verses.translation: And we desire that every one of you do shew the same diligence to the full assurance of hope unto the end:

verses.original: ἵνα μὴ νωθροὶ γένησθε, μιμηταὶ δὲ τῶν διὰ πίστεως καὶ μακροθυμίας κληρονομούντων τὰς ἐπαγγελίας.
verses.translit: ina me nothroi genisthe, mimitai de ton dia pisteos kai makrothymias klironomoynton tas epaggelias.
verses.translation: That ye be not slothful, but followers of them who through faith and patience inherit the promises.

verses.original: Τῷ γὰρ Ἀβραὰμ ἐπαγγειλάμενος ὁ θεός, ἐπεὶ κατʼ οὐδενὸς εἶχεν μείζονος ὀμόσαι, ὤμοσεν καθʼ ἑαυτοῦ,
verses.translit: To gar Avraam epaggeilamenos o theos, epei kat' oudenos eihen meizonos omosai, omosen kath' eaytou,
verses.translation: For when God made promise to Abraham, because he could swear by no greater, he sware by himself,

verses.original: λέγων· ⸀Εἰ μὴν εὐλογῶν εὐλογήσω σε καὶ πληθύνων πληθυνῶ σε·
verses.translit: legon* Ei men eulogon eulogiso se kai plithynon plithyno se*
verses.translation: Saying, Surely blessing I will bless thee, and multiplying I will multiply thee.

verses.original: καὶ οὕτως μακροθυμήσας ἐπέτυχεν τῆς ἐπαγγελίας.
verses.translit: kai outos makrothymisas epetyhen tes epaggelias.
verses.translation: And so, after he had patiently endured, he obtained the promise.

verses.original: ⸀ἄνθρωποι γὰρ κατὰ τοῦ μείζονος ὀμνύουσιν, καὶ πάσης αὐτοῖς ἀντιλογίας πέρας εἰς βεβαίωσιν ὁ ὅρκος·
verses.translit: anthropoi gar kata tou meizonos omnyoysin, kai pasis autois antilogias peras eis vevaiosin o orkos*
verses.translation: For men verily swear by the greater: and an oath for confirmation is to them an end of all strife.

verses.original: ἐν ᾧ περισσότερον βουλόμενος ὁ θεὸς ἐπιδεῖξαι τοῖς κληρονόμοις τῆς ἐπαγγελίας τὸ ἀμετάθετον τῆς βουλῆς αὐτοῦ ἐμεσίτευσεν ὅρκῳ,
verses.translit: en o perissoteron voylomenos o theos epideixai tois klironomois tes epaggelias to ametatheton tes voyles autou emesiteysen orko,
verses.translation: Wherein God, willing more abundantly to shew unto the heirs of promise the immutability of his counsel, confirmed it by an oath:

verses.original: ἵνα διὰ δύο πραγμάτων ἀμεταθέτων, ἐν οἷς ἀδύνατον ψεύσασθαι ⸀θεόν, ἰσχυρὰν παράκλησιν ἔχωμεν οἱ καταφυγόντες κρατῆσαι τῆς προκειμένης ἐλπίδος·
verses.translit: ina dia dyo pragmaton ametatheton, en ois adynaton pseysasthai theon, ishyran paraklisin ehomen oi katafygontes kratesai tes prokeimenis elpidos*
verses.translation: That by two immutable things, in which it was impossible for God to lie, we might have a strong consolation, who have fled for refuge to lay hold upon the hope set before us:

verses.original: ἣν ὡς ἄγκυραν ἔχομεν τῆς ψυχῆς, ⸀ἀσφαλῆ τε καὶ βεβαίαν καὶ εἰσερχομένην εἰς τὸ ἐσώτερον τοῦ καταπετάσματος,
verses.translit: en os agkyran ehomen tes psyhes, asfale te kai vevaian kai eiserhomenin eis to esoteron tou katapetasmatos,
verses.translation: Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast, and which entereth into that within the veil;

verses.original: ὅπου πρόδρομος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν εἰσῆλθεν Ἰησοῦς, κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισέδεκ ἀρχιερεὺς γενόμενος εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.
verses.translit: opoy prodromos uper emon eiselthen Iisous, kata ten taxin Melhisedek arhiereus genomenos eis ton aiona.
verses.translation: Whither the forerunner is for us entered, even Jesus, made an high priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.

verses.original: Οὗτος γὰρ ὁ Μελχισέδεκ, βασιλεὺς Σαλήμ, ἱερεὺς τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ὑψίστου, ⸀ὁ συναντήσας Ἀβραὰμ ὑποστρέφοντι ἀπὸ τῆς κοπῆς τῶν βασιλέων καὶ εὐλογήσας αὐτόν,
verses.translit: Outos gar o Melhisedek, vasileus Salim, iereus tou theou tou upsistoy, o synantisas Avraam upostrefonti apo tes kopes ton vasileon kai eulogisas auton,
verses.translation: For this Melchisedec, king of Salem, priest of the most high God, who met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings, and blessed him;

verses.original: ᾧ καὶ δεκάτην ἀπὸ πάντων ἐμέρισεν Ἀβραάμ, πρῶτον μὲν ἑρμηνευόμενος βασιλεὺς δικαιοσύνης ἔπειτα δὲ καὶ βασιλεὺς Σαλήμ, ὅ ἐστιν βασιλεὺς εἰρήνης,
verses.translit: o kai dekatin apo panton emerisen Avraam, proton men ermineyomenos vasileus dikaiosynis epeita de kai vasileus Salim, o estin vasileus eirinis,
verses.translation: To whom also Abraham gave a tenth part of all; first being by interpretation King of righteousness, and after that also King of Salem, which is, King of peace;

verses.original: ἀπάτωρ, ἀμήτωρ, ἀγενεαλόγητος, μήτε ἀρχὴν ἡμερῶν μήτε ζωῆς τέλος ἔχων, ἀφωμοιωμένος δὲ τῷ υἱῷ τοῦ θεοῦ, μένει ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸ διηνεκές.
verses.translit: apator, amitor, agenealogitos, mite arhen emeron mite zoes telos ehon, afomoiomenos de to yio tou theou, menei iereus eis to diinekes.
verses.translation: Without father, without mother, without descent, having neither beginning of days, nor end of life; but made like unto the Son of God; abideth a priest continually.

verses.original: Θεωρεῖτε δὲ πηλίκος οὗτος ⸀ᾧ δεκάτην Ἀβραὰμ ἔδωκεν ἐκ τῶν ἀκροθινίων ὁ πατριάρχης.
verses.translit: Theoreite de pilikos outos o dekatin Avraam edoken ek ton akrothinion o patriarhis.
verses.translation: Now consider how great this man was , unto whom even the patriarch Abraham gave the tenth of the spoils.

verses.original: καὶ οἱ μὲν ἐκ τῶν υἱῶν Λευὶ τὴν ἱερατείαν λαμβάνοντες ἐντολὴν ἔχουσιν ἀποδεκατοῦν τὸν λαὸν κατὰ τὸν νόμον, τοῦτʼ ἔστιν τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτῶν, καίπερ ἐξεληλυθότας ἐκ τῆς ὀσφύος Ἀβραάμ·
verses.translit: kai oi men ek ton yion Leyi ten ierateian lamvanontes entolen ehoysin apodekatoun ton laon kata ton nomon, tout' estin tous adelfous auton, kaiper exelilythotas ek tes osfyos Avraam*
verses.translation: And verily they that are of the sons of Levi, who receive the office of the priesthood, have a commandment to take tithes of the people according to the law, that is, of their brethren, though they come out of the loins of Abraham:

verses.original: ὁ δὲ μὴ γενεαλογούμενος ἐξ αὐτῶν δεδεκάτωκεν ⸀Ἀβραάμ, καὶ τὸν ἔχοντα τὰς ἐπαγγελίας εὐλόγηκεν.
verses.translit: o de me genealogoymenos ex auton dedekatoken Avraam, kai ton ehonta tas epaggelias eulogiken.
verses.translation: But he whose descent is not counted from them received tithes of Abraham, and blessed him that had the promises.

verses.original: χωρὶς δὲ πάσης ἀντιλογίας τὸ ἔλαττον ὑπὸ τοῦ κρείττονος εὐλογεῖται.
verses.translit: horis de pasis antilogias to elatton upo tou kreittonos eulogeitai.
verses.translation: And without all contradiction the less is blessed of the better.

verses.original: καὶ ὧδε μὲν δεκάτας ἀποθνῄσκοντες ἄνθρωποι λαμβάνουσιν, ἐκεῖ δὲ μαρτυρούμενος ὅτι ζῇ.
verses.translit: kai ode men dekatas apothneskontes anthropoi lamvanoysin, ekei de martyroymenos oti ze.
verses.translation: And here men that die receive tithes; but there he receiveth them , of whom it is witnessed that he liveth.

verses.original: καὶ ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν, διʼ Ἀβραὰμ καὶ Λευὶ ὁ δεκάτας λαμβάνων δεδεκάτωται,
verses.translit: kai os epos eipein, di' Avraam kai Leyi o dekatas lamvanon dedekatotai,
verses.translation: And as I may so say, Levi also, who receiveth tithes, payed tithes in Abraham.

verses.original: ἔτι γὰρ ἐν τῇ ὀσφύϊ τοῦ πατρὸς ἦν ὅτε συνήντησεν αὐτῷ ⸀Μελχισέδεκ.
verses.translit: eti gar en te osfyi tou patros en ote synintisen auto Melhisedek.
verses.translation: For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him.

verses.original: Εἰ μὲν οὖν τελείωσις διὰ τῆς Λευιτικῆς ἱερωσύνης ἦν, ὁ λαὸς γὰρ ἐπʼ ⸀αὐτῆς ⸀νενομοθέτηται, τίς ἔτι χρεία κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισέδεκ ἕτερον ἀνίστασθαι ἱερέα καὶ οὐ κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Ἀαρὼν λέγεσθαι;
verses.translit: Ei men oun teleiosis dia tes Leyitikes ierosynis en, o laos gar ep' autes nenomothetitai, tis eti hreia kata ten taxin Melhisedek eteron anistasthai ierea kai ou kata ten taxin Aaron legesthai;
verses.translation: If therefore perfection were by the Levitical priesthood, (for under it the people received the law,) what further need was there that another priest should rise after the order of Melchisedec, and not be called after the order of Aaron?

verses.original: μετατιθεμένης γὰρ τῆς ἱερωσύνης ἐξ ἀνάγκης καὶ νόμου μετάθεσις γίνεται.
verses.translit: metatithemenis gar tes ierosynis ex anagkis kai nomoy metathesis ginetai.
verses.translation: For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law.

verses.original: ἐφʼ ὃν γὰρ λέγεται ταῦτα φυλῆς ἑτέρας μετέσχηκεν, ἀφʼ ἧς οὐδεὶς προσέσχηκεν τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ·
verses.translit: ef' on gar legetai tauta fyles eteras meteshiken, af' es oudeis proseshiken to thysiastirio*
verses.translation: For he of whom these things are spoken pertaineth to another tribe, of which no man gave attendance at the altar.

verses.original: πρόδηλον γὰρ ὅτι ἐξ Ἰούδα ἀνατέταλκεν ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν, εἰς ἣν φυλὴν ⸂περὶ ἱερέων οὐδὲν⸃ Μωϋσῆς ἐλάλησεν.
verses.translit: prodilon gar oti ex Ioyda anatetalken o kyrios emon, eis en fylen peri iereon ouden Moyses elalisen.
verses.translation: For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.

verses.original: Καὶ περισσότερον ἔτι κατάδηλόν ἐστιν, εἰ κατὰ τὴν ὁμοιότητα Μελχισέδεκ ἀνίσταται ἱερεὺς ἕτερος,
verses.translit: Kai perissoteron eti katadilon estin, ei kata ten omoiotita Melhisedek anistatai iereus eteros,
verses.translation: And it is yet far more evident: for that after the similitude of Melchisedec there ariseth another priest,

verses.original: ὃς οὐ κατὰ νόμον ἐντολῆς ⸀σαρκίνης γέγονεν ἀλλὰ κατὰ δύναμιν ζωῆς ἀκαταλύτου,
verses.translit: os ou kata nomon entoles sarkinis gegonen alla kata dynamin zoes akatalytoy,
verses.translation: Who is made, not after the law of a carnal commandment, but after the power of an endless life.

verses.original: ⸀μαρτυρεῖται γὰρ ὅτι Σὺ ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισέδεκ.
verses.translit: martyreitai gar oti Su iereus eis ton aiona kata ten taxin Melhisedek.
verses.translation: For he testifieth, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.

verses.original: ἀθέτησις μὲν γὰρ γίνεται προαγούσης ἐντολῆς διὰ τὸ αὐτῆς ἀσθενὲς καὶ ἀνωφελές,
verses.translit: athetisis men gar ginetai proagoysis entoles dia to autes asthenes kai anofeles,
verses.translation: For there is verily a disannulling of the commandment going before for the weakness and unprofitableness thereof.

verses.original: οὐδὲν γὰρ ἐτελείωσεν ὁ νόμος, ἐπεισαγωγὴ δὲ κρείττονος ἐλπίδος, διʼ ἧς ἐγγίζομεν τῷ θεῷ.
verses.translit: ouden gar eteleiosen o nomos, epeisagoge de kreittonos elpidos, di' es eggizomen to theo.
verses.translation: For the law made nothing perfect, but the bringing in of a better hope did ; by the which we draw nigh unto God.

verses.original: Καὶ καθʼ ὅσον οὐ χωρὶς ὁρκωμοσίας (οἱ μὲν γὰρ χωρὶς ὁρκωμοσίας εἰσὶν ἱερεῖς γεγονότες,
verses.translit: Kai kath' oson ou horis orkomosias (oi men gar horis orkomosias eisin iereis gegonotes,
verses.translation: And inasmuch as not without an oath he was made priest :

verses.original: ὁ δὲ μετὰ ὁρκωμοσίας διὰ τοῦ λέγοντος πρὸς αὐτόν· Ὤμοσεν κύριος, καὶ οὐ μεταμεληθήσεται, Σὺ ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸν ⸀αἰῶνα),
verses.translit: o de meta orkomosias dia tou legontos pros auton* Omosen kyrios, kai ou metamelithisetai, Su iereus eis ton aiona),
verses.translation: (For those priests were made without an oath; but this with an oath by him that said unto him, The Lord sware and will not repent, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec:)

verses.original: κατὰ ⸀τοσοῦτο ⸀κρείττονος διαθήκης γέγονεν ἔγγυος Ἰησοῦς.
verses.translit: kata tosouto kreittonos diathikis gegonen eggyos Iisous.
verses.translation: By so much was Jesus made a surety of a better testament.

verses.original: Καὶ οἱ μὲν πλείονές εἰσιν γεγονότες ἱερεῖς διὰ τὸ θανάτῳ κωλύεσθαι παραμένειν·
verses.translit: Kai oi men pleiones eisin gegonotes iereis dia to thanato kolyesthai paramenein*
verses.translation: And they truly were many priests, because they were not suffered to continue by reason of death:

verses.original: ὁ δὲ διὰ τὸ μένειν αὐτὸν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ἀπαράβατον ἔχει τὴν ἱερωσύνην·
verses.translit: o de dia to menein auton eis ton aiona aparavaton ehei ten ierosynin*
verses.translation: But this man , because he continueth ever, hath an unchangeable priesthood.

verses.original: ὅθεν καὶ σῴζειν εἰς τὸ παντελὲς δύναται τοὺς προσερχομένους διʼ αὐτοῦ τῷ θεῷ, πάντοτε ζῶν εἰς τὸ ἐντυγχάνειν ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: othen kai sozein eis to panteles dynatai tous proserhomenoys di' autou to theo, pantote zon eis to entyghanein uper auton.
verses.translation: Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them.

verses.original: Τοιοῦτος γὰρ ἡμῖν ⸀καὶ ἔπρεπεν ἀρχιερεύς, ὅσιος, ἄκακος, ἀμίαντος, κεχωρισμένος ἀπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν, καὶ ὑψηλότερος τῶν οὐρανῶν γενόμενος·
verses.translit: Toioutos gar emin kai eprepen arhiereys, osios, akakos, amiantos, kehorismenos apo ton amartolon, kai upsiloteros ton ouranon genomenos*
verses.translation: For such an high priest became us, who is holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners, and made higher than the heavens;

verses.original: ὃς οὐκ ἔχει καθʼ ἡμέραν ἀνάγκην, ὥσπερ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς, πρότερον ὑπὲρ τῶν ἰδίων ἁμαρτιῶν θυσίας ἀναφέρειν, ἔπειτα τῶν τοῦ λαοῦ (τοῦτο γὰρ ἐποίησεν ἐφάπαξ ἑαυτὸν ἀνενέγκας)·
verses.translit: os ouk ehei kath' emeran anagkin, osper oi arhiereis, proteron uper ton idion amartion thysias anaferein, epeita ton tou laou (touto gar epoiisen efapax eayton anenegkas)*
verses.translation: Who needeth not daily, as those high priests, to offer up sacrifice, first for his own sins, and then for the people’s: for this he did once, when he offered up himself.

verses.original: ὁ νόμος γὰρ ἀνθρώπους καθίστησιν ἀρχιερεῖς ἔχοντας ἀσθένειαν, ὁ λόγος δὲ τῆς ὁρκωμοσίας τῆς μετὰ τὸν νόμον υἱόν, εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τετελειωμένον.
verses.translit: o nomos gar anthropoys kathistisin arhiereis ehontas astheneian, o logos de tes orkomosias tes meta ton nomon yion, eis ton aiona teteleiomenon.
verses.translation: For the law maketh men high priests which have infirmity; but the word of the oath, which was since the law, maketh the Son, who is consecrated for evermore.

verses.original: Κεφάλαιον δὲ ἐπὶ τοῖς λεγομένοις, τοιοῦτον ἔχομεν ἀρχιερέα, ὃς ἐκάθισεν ἐν δεξιᾷ τοῦ θρόνου τῆς μεγαλωσύνης ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς,
verses.translit: Kefalaion de epi tois legomenois, toiouton ehomen arhierea, os ekathisen en dexia tou thronoy tes megalosynis en tois ouranois,
verses.translation: Now of the things which we have spoken this is the sum: We have such an high priest, who is set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens;

verses.original: τῶν ἁγίων λειτουργὸς καὶ τῆς σκηνῆς τῆς ἀληθινῆς, ἣν ἔπηξεν ὁ κύριος, ⸀οὐκ ἄνθρωπος.
verses.translit: ton agion leitoyrgos kai tes skines tes alithines, en epixen o kyrios, ouk anthropos.
verses.translation: A minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man.

verses.original: πᾶς γὰρ ἀρχιερεὺς εἰς τὸ προσφέρειν δῶρά τε καὶ θυσίας καθίσταται· ὅθεν ἀναγκαῖον ἔχειν τι καὶ τοῦτον ὃ προσενέγκῃ.
verses.translit: pas gar arhiereus eis to prosferein dora te kai thysias kathistatai* othen anagkaion ehein ti kai touton o prosenegke.
verses.translation: For every high priest is ordained to offer gifts and sacrifices: wherefore it is of necessity that this man have somewhat also to offer.

verses.original: εἰ μὲν ⸀οὖν ἦν ἐπὶ γῆς, οὐδʼ ἂν ἦν ἱερεύς, ⸀ὄντων τῶν προσφερόντων κατὰ ⸀νόμον τὰ δῶρα·
verses.translit: ei men oun en epi ges, oud' an en iereys, onton ton prosferonton kata nomon ta dora*
verses.translation: For if he were on earth, he should not be a priest, seeing that there are priests that offer gifts according to the law:

verses.original: (οἵτινες ὑποδείγματι καὶ σκιᾷ λατρεύουσιν τῶν ἐπουρανίων, καθὼς κεχρημάτισται Μωϋσῆς μέλλων ἐπιτελεῖν τὴν σκηνήν, Ὅρα γάρ, φησίν, ποιήσεις πάντα κατὰ τὸν τύπον τὸν δειχθέντα σοι ἐν τῷ ὄρει)·
verses.translit: (oitines upodeigmati kai skia latreyoysin ton epoyranion, kathos kehrimatistai Moyses mellon epitelein ten skinin, Ora gar, fisin, poiiseis panta kata ton typon ton deihthenta soi en to orei)*
verses.translation: Who serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: for, See, saith he, that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount.

verses.original: ⸀νυνὶ δὲ διαφορωτέρας τέτυχεν λειτουργίας, ὅσῳ καὶ κρείττονός ἐστιν διαθήκης μεσίτης, ἥτις ἐπὶ κρείττοσιν ἐπαγγελίαις νενομοθέτηται.
verses.translit: nyni de diaforoteras tetyhen leitoyrgias, oso kai kreittonos estin diathikis mesitis, etis epi kreittosin epaggeliais nenomothetitai.
verses.translation: But now hath he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises.

verses.original: Εἰ γὰρ ἡ πρώτη ἐκείνη ἦν ἄμεμπτος, οὐκ ἂν δευτέρας ἐζητεῖτο τόπος·
verses.translit: Ei gar e proti ekeini en amemptos, ouk an deyteras eziteito topos*
verses.translation: For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second.

verses.original: μεμφόμενος γὰρ ⸀αὐτοὺς λέγει· Ἰδοὺ ἡμέραι ἔρχονται, λέγει κύριος, καὶ συντελέσω ἐπὶ τὸν οἶκον Ἰσραὴλ καὶ ἐπὶ τὸν οἶκον Ἰούδα διαθήκην καινήν,
verses.translit: memfomenos gar autous legei* Idou emerai erhontai, legei kyrios, kai synteleso epi ton oikon Israel kai epi ton oikon Ioyda diathikin kainin,
verses.translation: For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah:

verses.original: οὐ κατὰ τὴν διαθήκην ἣν ἐποίησα τοῖς πατράσιν αὐτῶν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ἐπιλαβομένου μου τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῶν ἐξαγαγεῖν αὐτοὺς ἐκ γῆς Αἰγύπτου, ὅτι αὐτοὶ οὐκ ἐνέμειναν ἐν τῇ διαθήκῃ μου, κἀγὼ ἠμέλησα αὐτῶν, λέγει κύριος.
verses.translit: ou kata ten diathikin en epoiisa tois patrasin auton en emera epilavomenoy moy tes heiros auton exagagein autous ek ges Aigyptoy, oti autoi ouk enemeinan en te diathike moy, kago emelisa auton, legei kyrios.
verses.translation: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord.

verses.original: ὅτι αὕτη ἡ διαθήκη ἣν διαθήσομαι τῷ οἴκῳ Ἰσραὴλ μετὰ τὰς ἡμέρας ἐκείνας, λέγει κύριος, διδοὺς νόμους μου εἰς τὴν διάνοιαν αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐπὶ καρδίας αὐτῶν ἐπιγράψω αὐτούς, καὶ ἔσομαι αὐτοῖς εἰς θεόν καὶ αὐτοὶ ἔσονταί μοι εἰς λαόν.
verses.translit: oti auti e diathiki en diathisomai to oiko Israel meta tas emeras ekeinas, legei kyrios, didous nomoys moy eis ten dianoian auton, kai epi kardias auton epigrapso autoys, kai esomai autois eis theon kai autoi esontai moi eis laon.
verses.translation: For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people:

verses.original: καὶ οὐ μὴ διδάξωσιν ἕκαστος τὸν πολίτην αὐτοῦ καὶ ἕκαστος τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, λέγων· Γνῶθι τὸν κύριον, ὅτι πάντες εἰδήσουσίν με ἀπὸ ⸀μικροῦ ἕως μεγάλου αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: kai ou me didaxosin ekastos ton politin autou kai ekastos ton adelfon autou, legon* Gnothi ton kyrion, oti pantes eidisoysin me apo mikrou eos megaloy auton.
verses.translation: And they shall not teach every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for all shall know me, from the least to the greatest.

verses.original: ὅτι ἵλεως ἔσομαι ταῖς ἀδικίαις αὐτῶν, καὶ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ⸀αὐτῶν οὐ μὴ μνησθῶ ἔτι.
verses.translit: oti ileos esomai tais adikiais auton, kai ton amartion auton ou me mnistho eti.
verses.translation: For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more.

verses.original: ἐν τῷ λέγειν Καινὴν πεπαλαίωκεν τὴν πρώτην, τὸ δὲ παλαιούμενον καὶ γηράσκον ἐγγὺς ἀφανισμοῦ.
verses.translit: en to legein Kainen pepalaioken ten protin, to de palaioymenon kai giraskon eggus afanismou.
verses.translation: In that he saith, A new covenant , he hath made the first old. Now that which decayeth and waxeth old is ready to vanish away.

verses.original: Εἶχε μὲν ⸀οὖν ἡ πρώτη δικαιώματα λατρείας τό τε ἅγιον κοσμικόν.
verses.translit: Eihe men oun e proti dikaiomata latreias to te agion kosmikon.
verses.translation: Then verily the first covenant had also ordinances of divine service, and a worldly sanctuary.

verses.original: σκηνὴ γὰρ κατεσκευάσθη ἡ πρώτη ἐν ᾗ ἥ τε λυχνία καὶ ἡ τράπεζα καὶ ἡ πρόθεσις τῶν ἄρτων, ἥτις λέγεται Ἅγια·
verses.translit: skine gar kateskeyasthi e proti en e e te lyhnia kai e trapeza kai e prothesis ton arton, etis legetai Agia*
verses.translation: For there was a tabernacle made; the first, wherein was the candlestick, and the table, and the shewbread; which is called the sanctuary.

verses.original: μετὰ δὲ τὸ δεύτερον καταπέτασμα σκηνὴ ἡ λεγομένη ⸂Ἅγια Ἁγίων⸃,
verses.translit: meta de to deyteron katapetasma skine e legomeni Agia Agion,
verses.translation: And after the second veil, the tabernacle which is called the Holiest of all;

verses.original: χρυσοῦν ἔχουσα θυμιατήριον καὶ τὴν κιβωτὸν τῆς διαθήκης περικεκαλυμμένην πάντοθεν χρυσίῳ, ἐν ᾗ στάμνος χρυσῆ ἔχουσα τὸ μάννα καὶ ἡ ῥάβδος Ἀαρὼν ἡ βλαστήσασα καὶ αἱ πλάκες τῆς διαθήκης,
verses.translit: hrysoun ehoysa thymiatirion kai ten kivoton tes diathikis perikekalymmenin pantothen hrysio, en e stamnos hryse ehoysa to manna kai e Ravdos Aaron e vlastisasa kai ai plakes tes diathikis,
verses.translation: Which had the golden censer, and the ark of the covenant overlaid round about with gold, wherein was the golden pot that had manna, and Aaron’s rod that budded, and the tables of the covenant;

verses.original: ὑπεράνω δὲ αὐτῆς Χερουβὶν δόξης κατασκιάζοντα τὸ ἱλαστήριον· περὶ ὧν οὐκ ἔστιν νῦν λέγειν κατὰ μέρος.
verses.translit: uperano de autes Heroyvin doxis kataskiazonta to ilastirion* peri on ouk estin nun legein kata meros.
verses.translation: And over it the cherubims of glory shadowing the mercyseat; of which we cannot now speak particularly.

verses.original: Τούτων δὲ οὕτως κατεσκευασμένων, εἰς μὲν τὴν πρώτην σκηνὴν διὰ παντὸς εἰσίασιν οἱ ἱερεῖς τὰς λατρείας ἐπιτελοῦντες,
verses.translit: Toyton de outos kateskeyasmenon, eis men ten protin skinen dia pantos eisiasin oi iereis tas latreias epitelountes,
verses.translation: Now when these things were thus ordained, the priests went always into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the service of God .

verses.original: εἰς δὲ τὴν δευτέραν ἅπαξ τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ μόνος ὁ ἀρχιερεύς, οὐ χωρὶς αἵματος, ὃ προσφέρει ὑπὲρ ἑαυτοῦ καὶ τῶν τοῦ λαοῦ ἀγνοημάτων,
verses.translit: eis de ten deyteran apax tou eniaytou monos o arhiereys, ou horis aimatos, o prosferei uper eaytou kai ton tou laou agnoimaton,
verses.translation: But into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself, and for the errors of the people:

verses.original: τοῦτο δηλοῦντος τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου, μήπω πεφανερῶσθαι τὴν τῶν ἁγίων ὁδὸν ἔτι τῆς πρώτης σκηνῆς ἐχούσης στάσιν,
verses.translit: touto dilountos tou pneymatos tou agioy, mipo pefanerosthai ten ton agion odon eti tes protis skines ehoysis stasin,
verses.translation: The Holy Ghost this signifying, that the way into the holiest of all was not yet made manifest, while as the first tabernacle was yet standing:

verses.original: ἥτις παραβολὴ εἰς τὸν καιρὸν τὸν ἐνεστηκότα, καθʼ ⸀ἣν δῶρά τε καὶ θυσίαι προσφέρονται μὴ δυνάμεναι κατὰ συνείδησιν τελειῶσαι τὸν λατρεύοντα,
verses.translit: etis paravole eis ton kairon ton enestikota, kath' en dora te kai thysiai prosferontai me dynamenai kata syneidisin teleiosai ton latreyonta,
verses.translation: Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience;

verses.original: μόνον ἐπὶ βρώμασιν καὶ πόμασιν καὶ διαφόροις βαπτισμοῖς, ⸀δικαιώματα σαρκὸς μέχρι καιροῦ διορθώσεως ἐπικείμενα.
verses.translit: monon epi vromasin kai pomasin kai diaforois vaptismois, dikaiomata sarkos mehri kairou diorthoseos epikeimena.
verses.translation: Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation.

verses.original: Χριστὸς δὲ παραγενόμενος ἀρχιερεὺς τῶν ⸀γενομένων ἀγαθῶν διὰ τῆς μείζονος καὶ τελειοτέρας σκηνῆς οὐ χειροποιήτου, τοῦτʼ ἔστιν οὐ ταύτης τῆς κτίσεως,
verses.translit: Hristos de paragenomenos arhiereus ton genomenon agathon dia tes meizonos kai teleioteras skines ou heiropoiitoy, tout' estin ou taytis tes ktiseos,
verses.translation: But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building;

verses.original: οὐδὲ διʼ αἵματος τράγων καὶ μόσχων διὰ δὲ τοῦ ἰδίου αἵματος, εἰσῆλθεν ἐφάπαξ εἰς τὰ ἅγια, αἰωνίαν λύτρωσιν εὑράμενος.
verses.translit: oude di' aimatos tragon kai moshon dia de tou idioy aimatos, eiselthen efapax eis ta agia, aionian lytrosin euramenos.
verses.translation: Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us .

verses.original: εἰ γὰρ τὸ αἷμα ⸂τράγων καὶ ταύρων⸃ καὶ σποδὸς δαμάλεως ῥαντίζουσα τοὺς κεκοινωμένους ἁγιάζει πρὸς τὴν τῆς σαρκὸς καθαρότητα,
verses.translit: ei gar to aima tragon kai tayron kai spodos damaleos Rantizoysa tous kekoinomenoys agiazei pros ten tes sarkos katharotita,
verses.translation: For if the blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of an heifer sprinkling the unclean, sanctifieth to the purifying of the flesh:

verses.original: πόσῳ μᾶλλον τὸ αἷμα τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὃς διὰ πνεύματος αἰωνίου ἑαυτὸν προσήνεγκεν ἄμωμον τῷ θεῷ, καθαριεῖ τὴν συνείδησιν ⸀ἡμῶν ἀπὸ νεκρῶν ἔργων εἰς τὸ λατρεύειν θεῷ ζῶντι.
verses.translit: poso mallon to aima tou Hristou, os dia pneymatos aionioy eayton prosinegken amomon to theo, kathariei ten syneidisin emon apo nekron ergon eis to latreyein theo zonti.
verses.translation: How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?

verses.original: Καὶ διὰ τοῦτο διαθήκης καινῆς μεσίτης ἐστίν, ὅπως θανάτου γενομένου εἰς ἀπολύτρωσιν τῶν ἐπὶ τῇ πρώτῃ διαθήκῃ παραβάσεων τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν λάβωσιν οἱ κεκλημένοι τῆς αἰωνίου κληρονομίας.
verses.translit: Kai dia touto diathikis kaines mesitis estin, opos thanatoy genomenoy eis apolytrosin ton epi te prote diathike paravaseon ten epaggelian lavosin oi keklimenoi tes aionioy klironomias.
verses.translation: And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance.

verses.original: ὅπου γὰρ διαθήκη, θάνατον ἀνάγκη φέρεσθαι τοῦ διαθεμένου·
verses.translit: opoy gar diathiki, thanaton anagki feresthai tou diathemenoy*
verses.translation: For where a testament is , there must also of necessity be the death of the testator.

verses.original: διαθήκη γὰρ ἐπὶ νεκροῖς βεβαία, ἐπεὶ ⸀μήποτε ἰσχύει ὅτε ζῇ ὁ διαθέμενος.
verses.translit: diathiki gar epi nekrois vevaia, epei mipote ishyei ote ze o diathemenos.
verses.translation: For a testament is of force after men are dead: otherwise it is of no strength at all while the testator liveth.

verses.original: ὅθεν οὐδὲ ἡ πρώτη χωρὶς αἵματος ἐγκεκαίνισται·
verses.translit: othen oude e proti horis aimatos egkekainistai*
verses.translation: Whereupon neither the first testament was dedicated without blood.

verses.original: λαληθείσης γὰρ πάσης ἐντολῆς κατὰ ⸀τὸν νόμον ὑπὸ Μωϋσέως παντὶ τῷ λαῷ, λαβὼν τὸ αἷμα τῶν ⸀μόσχων μετὰ ὕδατος καὶ ἐρίου κοκκίνου καὶ ὑσσώπου αὐτό τε τὸ βιβλίον καὶ πάντα τὸν λαὸν ἐράντισεν,
verses.translit: lalitheisis gar pasis entoles kata ton nomon upo Moyseos panti to lao, lavon to aima ton moshon meta udatos kai erioy kokkinoy kai ussopoy auto te to vivlion kai panta ton laon erantisen,
verses.translation: For when Moses had spoken every precept to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of calves and of goats, with water, and scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book, and all the people,

verses.original: λέγων· Τοῦτο τὸ αἷμα τῆς διαθήκης ἧς ἐνετείλατο πρὸς ὑμᾶς ὁ θεός·
verses.translit: legon* Touto to aima tes diathikis es eneteilato pros umas o theos*
verses.translation: Saying, This is the blood of the testament which God hath enjoined unto you.

verses.original: καὶ τὴν σκηνὴν δὲ καὶ πάντα τὰ σκεύη τῆς λειτουργίας τῷ αἵματι ὁμοίως ἐράντισεν.
verses.translit: kai ten skinen de kai panta ta skeyi tes leitoyrgias to aimati omoios erantisen.
verses.translation: Moreover he sprinkled with blood both the tabernacle, and all the vessels of the ministry.

verses.original: καὶ σχεδὸν ἐν αἵματι πάντα καθαρίζεται κατὰ τὸν νόμον, καὶ χωρὶς αἱματεκχυσίας οὐ γίνεται ἄφεσις.
verses.translit: kai shedon en aimati panta katharizetai kata ton nomon, kai horis aimatekhysias ou ginetai afesis.
verses.translation: And almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission.

verses.original: Ἀνάγκη οὖν τὰ μὲν ὑποδείγματα τῶν ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς τούτοις καθαρίζεσθαι, αὐτὰ δὲ τὰ ἐπουράνια κρείττοσι θυσίαις παρὰ ταύτας.
verses.translit: Anagki oun ta men upodeigmata ton en tois ouranois toytois katharizesthai, auta de ta epoyrania kreittosi thysiais para taytas.
verses.translation: It was therefore necessary that the patterns of things in the heavens should be purified with these; but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.

verses.original: οὐ γὰρ εἰς χειροποίητα ⸂εἰσῆλθεν ἅγια⸃ Χριστός, ἀντίτυπα τῶν ἀληθινῶν, ἀλλʼ εἰς αὐτὸν τὸν οὐρανόν, νῦν ἐμφανισθῆναι τῷ προσώπῳ τοῦ θεοῦ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν·
verses.translit: ou gar eis heiropoiita eiselthen agia Hristos, antitypa ton alithinon, all' eis auton ton ouranon, nun emfanisthenai to prosopo tou theou uper emon*
verses.translation: For Christ is not entered into the holy places made with hands, which are the figures of the true; but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us:

verses.original: οὐδʼ ἵνα πολλάκις προσφέρῃ ἑαυτόν, ὥσπερ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς εἰσέρχεται εἰς τὰ ἅγια κατʼ ἐνιαυτὸν ἐν αἵματι ἀλλοτρίῳ,
verses.translit: oud' ina pollakis prosfere eayton, osper o arhiereus eiserhetai eis ta agia kat' eniayton en aimati allotrio,
verses.translation: Nor yet that he should offer himself often, as the high priest entereth into the holy place every year with blood of others;

verses.original: ἐπεὶ ἔδει αὐτὸν πολλάκις παθεῖν ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου· ⸀νυνὶ δὲ ἅπαξ ἐπὶ συντελείᾳ τῶν αἰώνων εἰς ἀθέτησιν ⸀ἁμαρτίας διὰ τῆς θυσίας αὐτοῦ πεφανέρωται.
verses.translit: epei edei auton pollakis pathein apo katavoles kosmoy* nyni de apax epi synteleia ton aionon eis athetisin amartias dia tes thysias autou pefanerotai.
verses.translation: For then must he often have suffered since the foundation of the world: but now once in the end of the world hath he appeared to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself.

verses.original: καὶ καθʼ ὅσον ἀπόκειται τοῖς ἀνθρώποις ἅπαξ ἀποθανεῖν, μετὰ δὲ τοῦτο κρίσις,
verses.translit: kai kath' oson apokeitai tois anthropois apax apothanein, meta de touto krisis,
verses.translation: And as it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment:

verses.original: οὕτως καὶ ὁ Χριστός, ἅπαξ προσενεχθεὶς εἰς τὸ πολλῶν ἀνενεγκεῖν ἁμαρτίας, ἐκ δευτέρου χωρὶς ἁμαρτίας ὀφθήσεται τοῖς αὐτὸν ἀπεκδεχομένοις εἰς σωτηρίαν.
verses.translit: outos kai o Hristos, apax prosenehtheis eis to pollon anenegkein amartias, ek deyteroy horis amartias ofthisetai tois auton apekdehomenois eis sotirian.
verses.translation: So Christ was once offered to bear the sins of many; and unto them that look for him shall he appear the second time without sin unto salvation.

verses.original: Σκιὰν γὰρ ἔχων ὁ νόμος τῶν μελλόντων ἀγαθῶν, οὐκ αὐτὴν τὴν εἰκόνα τῶν πραγμάτων, κατʼ ἐνιαυτὸν ταῖς αὐταῖς θυσίαις ἃς προσφέρουσιν εἰς τὸ διηνεκὲς οὐδέποτε ⸀δύναται τοὺς προσερχομένους τελειῶσαι·
verses.translit: Skian gar ehon o nomos ton mellonton agathon, ouk auten ten eikona ton pragmaton, kat' eniayton tais autais thysiais as prosferoysin eis to diinekes oudepote dynatai tous proserhomenoys teleiosai*
verses.translation: For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.

verses.original: ἐπεὶ οὐκ ἂν ἐπαύσαντο προσφερόμεναι, διὰ τὸ μηδεμίαν ἔχειν ἔτι συνείδησιν ἁμαρτιῶν τοὺς λατρεύοντας ἅπαξ ⸀κεκαθαρισμένους;
verses.translit: epei ouk an epaysanto prosferomenai, dia to midemian ehein eti syneidisin amartion tous latreyontas apax kekatharismenoys;
verses.translation: For then would they not have ceased to be offered? because that the worshippers once purged should have had no more conscience of sins.

verses.original: ἀλλʼ ἐν αὐταῖς ἀνάμνησις ἁμαρτιῶν κατʼ ἐνιαυτόν,
verses.translit: all' en autais anamnisis amartion kat' eniayton,
verses.translation: But in those sacrifices there is a remembrance again made of sins every year.

verses.original: ἀδύνατον γὰρ αἷμα ταύρων καὶ τράγων ἀφαιρεῖν ἁμαρτίας.
verses.translit: adynaton gar aima tayron kai tragon afairein amartias.
verses.translation: For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins.

verses.original: διὸ εἰσερχόμενος εἰς τὸν κόσμον λέγει· Θυσίαν καὶ προσφορὰν οὐκ ἠθέλησας, σῶμα δὲ κατηρτίσω μοι·
verses.translit: dio eiserhomenos eis ton kosmon legei* Thysian kai prosforan ouk ethelisas, soma de katirtiso moi*
verses.translation: Wherefore when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me:

verses.original: ὁλοκαυτώματα καὶ περὶ ἁμαρτίας οὐκ εὐδόκησας.
verses.translit: olokaytomata kai peri amartias ouk eudokisas.
verses.translation: In burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin thou hast had no pleasure.

verses.original: τότε εἶπον· Ἰδοὺ ἥκω, ἐν κεφαλίδι βιβλίου γέγραπται περὶ ἐμοῦ, τοῦ ποιῆσαι, ὁ θεός, τὸ θέλημά σου.
verses.translit: tote eipon* Idou eko, en kefalidi vivlioy gegraptai peri emou, tou poiesai, o theos, to thelima soy.
verses.translation: Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God.

verses.original: ἀνώτερον λέγων ὅτι ⸂Θυσίας καὶ προσφορὰς⸃ καὶ ὁλοκαυτώματα καὶ περὶ ἁμαρτίας οὐκ ἠθέλησας οὐδὲ εὐδόκησας, αἵτινες κατὰ ⸀νόμον προσφέρονται,
verses.translit: anoteron legon oti Thysias kai prosforas kai olokaytomata kai peri amartias ouk ethelisas oude eudokisas, aitines kata nomon prosferontai,
verses.translation: Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein ; which are offered by the law;

verses.original: τότε εἴρηκεν· Ἰδοὺ ἥκω τοῦ ⸀ποιῆσαι τὸ θέλημά σου· ἀναιρεῖ τὸ πρῶτον ἵνα τὸ δεύτερον στήσῃ.
verses.translit: tote eiriken* Idou eko tou poiesai to thelima soy* anairei to proton ina to deyteron stise.
verses.translation: Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second.

verses.original: ἐν ᾧ θελήματι ἡγιασμένοι ⸀ἐσμὲν διὰ τῆς προσφορᾶς τοῦ σώματος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐφάπαξ.
verses.translit: en o thelimati egiasmenoi esmen dia tes prosforas tou somatos Iisou Hristou efapax.
verses.translation: By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all .

verses.original: Καὶ πᾶς μὲν ἱερεὺς ἕστηκεν καθʼ ἡμέραν λειτουργῶν καὶ τὰς αὐτὰς πολλάκις προσφέρων θυσίας, αἵτινες οὐδέποτε δύνανται περιελεῖν ἁμαρτίας.
verses.translit: Kai pas men iereus estiken kath' emeran leitoyrgon kai tas autas pollakis prosferon thysias, aitines oudepote dynantai perielein amartias.
verses.translation: And every priest standeth daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins:

verses.original: ⸀οὗτος δὲ μίαν ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτιῶν προσενέγκας θυσίαν εἰς τὸ διηνεκὲς ἐκάθισεν ἐν δεξιᾷ τοῦ θεοῦ,
verses.translit: outos de mian uper amartion prosenegkas thysian eis to diinekes ekathisen en dexia tou theou,
verses.translation: But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God;

verses.original: τὸ λοιπὸν ἐκδεχόμενος ἕως τεθῶσιν οἱ ἐχθροὶ αὐτοῦ ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν αὐτοῦ,
verses.translit: to loipon ekdehomenos eos tethosin oi ehthroi autou upopodion ton podon autou,
verses.translation: From henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool.

verses.original: μιᾷ γὰρ προσφορᾷ τετελείωκεν εἰς τὸ διηνεκὲς τοὺς ἁγιαζομένους.
verses.translit: mia gar prosfora teteleioken eis to diinekes tous agiazomenoys.
verses.translation: For by one offering he hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified.

verses.original: μαρτυρεῖ δὲ ἡμῖν καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, μετὰ γὰρ τὸ ⸀εἰρηκέναι·
verses.translit: martyrei de emin kai to pneuma to agion, meta gar to eirikenai*
verses.translation: Whereof the Holy Ghost also is a witness to us: for after that he had said before,

verses.original: Αὕτη ἡ διαθήκη ἣν διαθήσομαι πρὸς αὐτοὺς μετὰ τὰς ἡμέρας ἐκείνας, λέγει κύριος, διδοὺς νόμους μου ἐπὶ καρδίας αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐπὶ ⸂τὴν διάνοιαν⸃ αὐτῶν ἐπιγράψω αὐτούς,
verses.translit: Auti e diathiki en diathisomai pros autous meta tas emeras ekeinas, legei kyrios, didous nomoys moy epi kardias auton, kai epi ten dianoian auton epigrapso autoys,
verses.translation: This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, saith the Lord, I will put my laws into their hearts, and in their minds will I write them;

verses.original: ⸀καὶ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν καὶ τῶν ἀνομιῶν αὐτῶν οὐ μὴ ⸀μνησθήσομαι ἔτι·
verses.translit: kai ton amartion auton kai ton anomion auton ou me mnisthisomai eti*
verses.translation: And their sins and iniquities will I remember no more.

verses.original: ὅπου δὲ ἄφεσις τούτων, οὐκέτι προσφορὰ περὶ ἁμαρτίας.
verses.translit: opoy de afesis toyton, ouketi prosfora peri amartias.
verses.translation: Now where remission of these is, there is no more offering for sin.

verses.original: Ἔχοντες οὖν, ἀδελφοί, παρρησίαν εἰς τὴν εἴσοδον τῶν ἁγίων ἐν τῷ αἵματι Ἰησοῦ,
verses.translit: Ehontes oun, adelfoi, parrisian eis ten eisodon ton agion en to aimati Iisou,
verses.translation: Having therefore, brethren, boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus,

verses.original: ἣν ἐνεκαίνισεν ἡμῖν ὁδὸν πρόσφατον καὶ ζῶσαν διὰ τοῦ καταπετάσματος, τοῦτʼ ἔστιν τῆς σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ,
verses.translit: en enekainisen emin odon prosfaton kai zosan dia tou katapetasmatos, tout' estin tes sarkos autou,
verses.translation: By a new and living way, which he hath consecrated for us, through the veil, that is to say, his flesh;

verses.original: καὶ ἱερέα μέγαν ἐπὶ τὸν οἶκον τοῦ θεοῦ,
verses.translit: kai ierea megan epi ton oikon tou theou,
verses.translation: And having an high priest over the house of God;

verses.original: προσερχώμεθα μετὰ ἀληθινῆς καρδίας ἐν πληροφορίᾳ πίστεως, ῥεραντισμένοι τὰς καρδίας ἀπὸ συνειδήσεως πονηρᾶς καὶ λελουσμένοι τὸ σῶμα ὕδατι καθαρῷ·
verses.translit: proserhometha meta alithines kardias en pliroforia pisteos, Rerantismenoi tas kardias apo syneidiseos poniras kai leloysmenoi to soma udati katharo*
verses.translation: Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water.

verses.original: κατέχωμεν τὴν ὁμολογίαν τῆς ἐλπίδος ἀκλινῆ, πιστὸς γὰρ ὁ ἐπαγγειλάμενος·
verses.translit: katehomen ten omologian tes elpidos akline, pistos gar o epaggeilamenos*
verses.translation: Let us hold fast the profession of our faith without wavering; (for he is faithful that promised;)

verses.original: καὶ κατανοῶμεν ἀλλήλους εἰς παροξυσμὸν ἀγάπης καὶ καλῶν ἔργων,
verses.translit: kai katanoomen alliloys eis paroxysmon agapis kai kalon ergon,
verses.translation: And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works:

verses.original: μὴ ἐγκαταλείποντες τὴν ἐπισυναγωγὴν ἑαυτῶν, καθὼς ἔθος τισίν, ἀλλὰ παρακαλοῦντες, καὶ τοσούτῳ μᾶλλον ὅσῳ βλέπετε ἐγγίζουσαν τὴν ἡμέραν.
verses.translit: me egkataleipontes ten episynagogen eayton, kathos ethos tisin, alla parakalountes, kai tosoyto mallon oso vlepete eggizoysan ten emeran.
verses.translation: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is ; but exhorting one another : and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.

verses.original: Ἑκουσίως γὰρ ἁμαρτανόντων ἡμῶν μετὰ τὸ λαβεῖν τὴν ἐπίγνωσιν τῆς ἀληθείας, οὐκέτι περὶ ἁμαρτιῶν ἀπολείπεται θυσία,
verses.translit: Ekoysios gar amartanonton emon meta to lavein ten epignosin tes alitheias, ouketi peri amartion apoleipetai thysia,
verses.translation: For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins,

verses.original: φοβερὰ δέ τις ἐκδοχὴ κρίσεως καὶ πυρὸς ζῆλος ἐσθίειν μέλλοντος τοὺς ὑπεναντίους.
verses.translit: fovera de tis ekdohe kriseos kai pyros zelos esthiein mellontos tous upenantioys.
verses.translation: But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries.

verses.original: ἀθετήσας τις νόμον Μωϋσέως χωρὶς οἰκτιρμῶν ἐπὶ δυσὶν ἢ τρισὶν μάρτυσιν ἀποθνῄσκει·
verses.translit: athetisas tis nomon Moyseos horis oiktirmon epi dysin e trisin martysin apothneskei*
verses.translation: He that despised Moses’ law died without mercy under two or three witnesses:

verses.original: πόσῳ δοκεῖτε χείρονος ἀξιωθήσεται τιμωρίας ὁ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ καταπατήσας, καὶ τὸ αἷμα τῆς διαθήκης κοινὸν ἡγησάμενος ἐν ᾧ ἡγιάσθη, καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς χάριτος ἐνυβρίσας.
verses.translit: poso dokeite heironos axiothisetai timorias o ton yion tou theou katapatisas, kai to aima tes diathikis koinon egisamenos en o egiasthi, kai to pneuma tes haritos enyvrisas.
verses.translation: Of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace?

verses.original: οἴδαμεν γὰρ τὸν εἰπόντα· Ἐμοὶ ἐκδίκησις, ἐγὼ ⸀ἀνταποδώσω· καὶ πάλιν· ⸂Κρινεῖ κύριος⸃ τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: oidamen gar ton eiponta* Emoi ekdikisis, ego antapodoso* kai palin* Krinei kyrios ton laon autou.
verses.translation: For we know him that hath said, Vengeance belongeth unto me, I will recompense, saith the Lord. And again, The Lord shall judge his people.

verses.original: φοβερὸν τὸ ἐμπεσεῖν εἰς χεῖρας θεοῦ ζῶντος.
verses.translit: foveron to empesein eis heiras theou zontos.
verses.translation: It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.

verses.original: Ἀναμιμνῄσκεσθε δὲ τὰς πρότερον ἡμέρας, ἐν αἷς φωτισθέντες πολλὴν ἄθλησιν ὑπεμείνατε παθημάτων,
verses.translit: Anamimneskesthe de tas proteron emeras, en ais fotisthentes pollen athlisin upemeinate pathimaton,
verses.translation: But call to remembrance the former days, in which, after ye were illuminated, ye endured a great fight of afflictions;

verses.original: τοῦτο μὲν ὀνειδισμοῖς τε καὶ θλίψεσιν θεατριζόμενοι, τοῦτο δὲ κοινωνοὶ τῶν οὕτως ἀναστρεφομένων γενηθέντες·
verses.translit: touto men oneidismois te kai thlipsesin theatrizomenoi, touto de koinonoi ton outos anastrefomenon genithentes*
verses.translation: Partly, whilst ye were made a gazingstock both by reproaches and afflictions; and partly, whilst ye became companions of them that were so used.

verses.original: καὶ γὰρ τοῖς ⸀δεσμίοις συνεπαθήσατε, καὶ τὴν ἁρπαγὴν τῶν ὑπαρχόντων ὑμῶν μετὰ χαρᾶς προσεδέξασθε, γινώσκοντες ἔχειν ⸀ἑαυτοὺς κρείττονα ⸀ὕπαρξιν καὶ μένουσαν.
verses.translit: kai gar tois desmiois synepathisate, kai ten arpagen ton uparhonton umon meta haras prosedexasthe, ginoskontes ehein eaytous kreittona uparxin kai menoysan.
verses.translation: For ye had compassion of me in my bonds, and took joyfully the spoiling of your goods, knowing in yourselves that ye have in heaven a better and an enduring substance.

verses.original: μὴ ἀποβάλητε οὖν τὴν παρρησίαν ὑμῶν, ἥτις ἔχει ⸂μεγάλην μισθαποδοσίαν⸃,
verses.translit: me apovalite oun ten parrisian umon, etis ehei megalin misthapodosian,
verses.translation: Cast not away therefore your confidence, which hath great recompence of reward.

verses.original: ὑπομονῆς γὰρ ἔχετε χρείαν ἵνα τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ ποιήσαντες κομίσησθε τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν·
verses.translit: upomones gar ehete hreian ina to thelima tou theou poiisantes komisisthe ten epaggelian*
verses.translation: For ye have need of patience, that, after ye have done the will of God, ye might receive the promise.

verses.original: ἔτι γὰρ μικρὸν ὅσον ὅσον, ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἥξει καὶ οὐ χρονίσει·
verses.translit: eti gar mikron oson oson, o erhomenos exei kai ou hronisei*
verses.translation: For yet a little while, and he that shall come will come, and will not tarry.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ δίκαιός ⸀μου ἐκ πίστεως ζήσεται, καὶ ἐὰν ὑποστείληται, οὐκ εὐδοκεῖ ἡ ψυχή μου ἐν αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: o de dikaios moy ek pisteos zisetai, kai ean uposteilitai, ouk eudokei e psyhi moy en auto.
verses.translation: Now the just shall live by faith: but if any man draw back, my soul shall have no pleasure in him.

verses.original: ἡμεῖς δὲ οὐκ ἐσμὲν ὑποστολῆς εἰς ἀπώλειαν, ἀλλὰ πίστεως εἰς περιποίησιν ψυχῆς.
verses.translit: emeis de ouk esmen upostoles eis apoleian, alla pisteos eis peripoiisin psyhes.
verses.translation: But we are not of them who draw back unto perdition; but of them that believe to the saving of the soul.

verses.original: Ἔστιν δὲ πίστις ἐλπιζομένων ὑπόστασις, πραγμάτων ἔλεγχος οὐ βλεπομένων·
verses.translit: Estin de pistis elpizomenon upostasis, pragmaton eleghos ou vlepomenon*
verses.translation: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.

verses.original: ἐν ταύτῃ γὰρ ἐμαρτυρήθησαν οἱ πρεσβύτεροι.
verses.translit: en tayte gar emartyrithisan oi presvyteroi.
verses.translation: For by it the elders obtained a good report.

verses.original: πίστει νοοῦμεν κατηρτίσθαι τοὺς αἰῶνας ῥήματι θεοῦ, εἰς τὸ μὴ ἐκ φαινομένων ⸂τὸ βλεπόμενον⸃ γεγονέναι.
verses.translit: pistei nooumen katirtisthai tous aionas Rimati theou, eis to me ek fainomenon to vlepomenon gegonenai.
verses.translation: Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God, so that things which are seen were not made of things which do appear.

verses.original: Πίστει πλείονα θυσίαν Ἅβελ παρὰ Κάϊν προσήνεγκεν τῷ θεῷ, διʼ ἧς ἐμαρτυρήθη εἶναι δίκαιος, μαρτυροῦντος ἐπὶ τοῖς δώροις αὐτοῦ ⸂τοῦ θεοῦ⸃, καὶ διʼ αὐτῆς ἀποθανὼν ἔτι ⸀λαλεῖ.
verses.translit: Pistei pleiona thysian Avel para Kain prosinegken to theo, di' es emartyrithi einai dikaios, martyrountos epi tois dorois autou tou theou, kai di' autes apothanon eti lalei.
verses.translation: By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh.

verses.original: Πίστει Ἑνὼχ μετετέθη τοῦ μὴ ἰδεῖν θάνατον, καὶ οὐχ ηὑρίσκετο διότι μετέθηκεν αὐτὸν ὁ θεός· πρὸ γὰρ τῆς ⸀μεταθέσεως μεμαρτύρηται εὐαρεστηκέναι τῷ θεῷ,
verses.translit: Pistei Enoh metetethi tou me idein thanaton, kai ouh iurisketo dioti metethiken auton o theos* pro gar tes metatheseos memartyritai euarestikenai to theo,
verses.translation: By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death; and was not found, because God had translated him: for before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased God.

verses.original: χωρὶς δὲ πίστεως ἀδύνατον εὐαρεστῆσαι, πιστεῦσαι γὰρ δεῖ τὸν προσερχόμενον τῷ θεῷ ὅτι ἔστιν καὶ τοῖς ἐκζητοῦσιν αὐτὸν μισθαποδότης γίνεται.
verses.translit: horis de pisteos adynaton euarestesai, pisteusai gar dei ton proserhomenon to theo oti estin kai tois ekzitousin auton misthapodotis ginetai.
verses.translation: But without faith it is impossible to please him : for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.

verses.original: πίστει χρηματισθεὶς Νῶε περὶ τῶν μηδέπω βλεπομένων εὐλαβηθεὶς κατεσκεύασεν κιβωτὸν εἰς σωτηρίαν τοῦ οἴκου αὐτοῦ, διʼ ἧς κατέκρινεν τὸν κόσμον, καὶ τῆς κατὰ πίστιν δικαιοσύνης ἐγένετο κληρονόμος.
verses.translit: pistei hrimatistheis Noe peri ton midepo vlepomenon eulavitheis kateskeyasen kivoton eis sotirian tou oikoy autou, di' es katekrinen ton kosmon, kai tes kata pistin dikaiosynis egeneto klironomos.
verses.translation: By faith Noah, being warned of God of things not seen as yet, moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house; by the which he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is by faith.

verses.original: ⸀Πίστει καλούμενος Ἀβραὰμ ὑπήκουσεν ἐξελθεῖν εἰς ⸀τόπον ὃν ἤμελλεν λαμβάνειν εἰς κληρονομίαν, καὶ ἐξῆλθεν μὴ ἐπιστάμενος ποῦ ἔρχεται.
verses.translit: Pistei kaloymenos Avraam upikoysen exelthein eis topon on emellen lamvanein eis klironomian, kai exelthen me epistamenos pou erhetai.
verses.translation: By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went.

verses.original: πίστει παρῴκησεν εἰς γῆν τῆς ἐπαγγελίας ὡς ἀλλοτρίαν, ἐν σκηναῖς κατοικήσας μετὰ Ἰσαὰκ καὶ Ἰακὼβ τῶν συγκληρονόμων τῆς ἐπαγγελίας τῆς αὐτῆς·
verses.translit: pistei parokisen eis gen tes epaggelias os allotrian, en skinais katoikisas meta Isaak kai Iakov ton sygklironomon tes epaggelias tes autes*
verses.translation: By faith he sojourned in the land of promise, as in a strange country, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise:

verses.original: ἐξεδέχετο γὰρ τὴν τοὺς θεμελίους ἔχουσαν πόλιν, ἧς τεχνίτης καὶ δημιουργὸς ὁ θεός.
verses.translit: exedeheto gar ten tous themelioys ehoysan polin, es tehnitis kai dimioyrgos o theos.
verses.translation: For he looked for a city which hath foundations, whose builder and maker is God.

verses.original: πίστει καὶ ⸂αὐτῇ Σάρρᾳ⸃ δύναμιν εἰς καταβολὴν σπέρματος ἔλαβεν καὶ παρὰ καιρὸν ⸀ἡλικίας, ἐπεὶ πιστὸν ἡγήσατο τὸν ἐπαγγειλάμενον·
verses.translit: pistei kai aute Sarra dynamin eis katavolen spermatos elaven kai para kairon elikias, epei piston egisato ton epaggeilamenon*
verses.translation: Through faith also Sara herself received strength to conceive seed, and was delivered of a child when she was past age, because she judged him faithful who had promised.

verses.original: διὸ καὶ ἀφʼ ἑνὸς ἐγεννήθησαν, καὶ ταῦτα νενεκρωμένου, καθὼς τὰ ἄστρα τοῦ οὐρανοῦ τῷ πλήθει καὶ ὡς ἡ ἄμμος ἡ παρὰ τὸ χεῖλος τῆς θαλάσσης ἡ ἀναρίθμητος.
verses.translit: dio kai af' enos egennithisan, kai tauta nenekromenoy, kathos ta astra tou ouranou to plithei kai os e ammos e para to heilos tes thalassis e anarithmitos.
verses.translation: Therefore sprang there even of one, and him as good as dead, so many as the stars of the sky in multitude, and as the sand which is by the sea shore innumerable.

verses.original: Κατὰ πίστιν ἀπέθανον οὗτοι πάντες, μὴ ⸀λαβόντες τὰς ἐπαγγελίας, ἀλλὰ πόρρωθεν αὐτὰς ἰδόντες καὶ ἀσπασάμενοι, καὶ ὁμολογήσαντες ὅτι ξένοι καὶ παρεπίδημοί εἰσιν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
verses.translit: Kata pistin apethanon outoi pantes, me lavontes tas epaggelias, alla porrothen autas idontes kai aspasamenoi, kai omologisantes oti xenoi kai parepidimoi eisin epi tes ges.
verses.translation: These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them afar off, and were persuaded of them , and embraced them , and confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.

verses.original: οἱ γὰρ τοιαῦτα λέγοντες ἐμφανίζουσιν ὅτι πατρίδα ἐπιζητοῦσιν.
verses.translit: oi gar toiauta legontes emfanizoysin oti patrida epizitousin.
verses.translation: For they that say such things declare plainly that they seek a country.

verses.original: καὶ εἰ μὲν ἐκείνης ⸀μνημονεύουσιν ἀφʼ ἧς ⸀ἐξέβησαν, εἶχον ἂν καιρὸν ἀνακάμψαι·
verses.translit: kai ei men ekeinis mnimoneyoysin af' es exevisan, eihon an kairon anakampsai*
verses.translation: And truly, if they had been mindful of that country from whence they came out, they might have had opportunity to have returned.

verses.original: νῦν δὲ κρείττονος ὀρέγονται, τοῦτʼ ἔστιν ἐπουρανίου. διὸ οὐκ ἐπαισχύνεται αὐτοὺς ὁ θεὸς θεὸς ἐπικαλεῖσθαι αὐτῶν, ἡτοίμασεν γὰρ αὐτοῖς πόλιν.
verses.translit: nun de kreittonos oregontai, tout' estin epoyranioy. dio ouk epaishynetai autous o theos theos epikaleisthai auton, etoimasen gar autois polin.
verses.translation: But now they desire a better country , that is, an heavenly: wherefore God is not ashamed to be called their God: for he hath prepared for them a city.

verses.original: Πίστει προσενήνοχεν Ἀβραὰμ τὸν Ἰσαὰκ πειραζόμενος, καὶ τὸν μονογενῆ προσέφερεν ὁ τὰς ἐπαγγελίας ἀναδεξάμενος,
verses.translit: Pistei proseninohen Avraam ton Isaak peirazomenos, kai ton monogene proseferen o tas epaggelias anadexamenos,
verses.translation: By faith Abraham, when he was tried, offered up Isaac: and he that had received the promises offered up his only begotten son ,

verses.original: πρὸς ὃν ἐλαλήθη ὅτι Ἐν Ἰσαὰκ κληθήσεταί σοι σπέρμα,
verses.translit: pros on elalithi oti En Isaak klithisetai soi sperma,
verses.translation: Of whom it was said, That in Isaac shall thy seed be called:

verses.original: λογισάμενος ὅτι καὶ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἐγείρειν δυνατὸς ὁ θεός· ὅθεν αὐτὸν καὶ ἐν παραβολῇ ἐκομίσατο.
verses.translit: logisamenos oti kai ek nekron egeirein dynatos o theos* othen auton kai en paravole ekomisato.
verses.translation: Accounting that God was able to raise him up, even from the dead; from whence also he received him in a figure.

verses.original: Πίστει ⸀καὶ περὶ μελλόντων εὐλόγησεν Ἰσαὰκ τὸν Ἰακὼβ καὶ τὸν Ἠσαῦ.
verses.translit: Pistei kai peri mellonton eulogisen Isaak ton Iakov kai ton Esau.
verses.translation: By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning things to come.

verses.original: πίστει Ἰακὼβ ἀποθνῄσκων ἕκαστον τῶν υἱῶν Ἰωσὴφ εὐλόγησεν, καὶ προσεκύνησεν ἐπὶ τὸ ἄκρον τῆς ῥάβδου αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: pistei Iakov apothneskon ekaston ton yion Iosef eulogisen, kai prosekynisen epi to akron tes Ravdoy autou.
verses.translation: By faith Jacob, when he was a dying, blessed both the sons of Joseph; and worshipped, leaning upon the top of his staff.

verses.original: πίστει Ἰωσὴφ τελευτῶν περὶ τῆς ἐξόδου τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ ἐμνημόνευσεν, καὶ περὶ τῶν ὀστέων αὐτοῦ ἐνετείλατο.
verses.translit: pistei Iosef teleyton peri tes exodoy ton yion Israel emnimoneysen, kai peri ton osteon autou eneteilato.
verses.translation: By faith Joseph, when he died, made mention of the departing of the children of Israel; and gave commandment concerning his bones.

verses.original: Πίστει Μωϋσῆς γεννηθεὶς ἐκρύβη τρίμηνον ὑπὸ τῶν πατέρων αὐτοῦ, διότι εἶδον ἀστεῖον τὸ παιδίον καὶ οὐκ ἐφοβήθησαν τὸ διάταγμα τοῦ βασιλέως.
verses.translit: Pistei Moyses gennitheis ekryvi triminon upo ton pateron autou, dioti eidon asteion to paidion kai ouk efovithisan to diatagma tou vasileos.
verses.translation: By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months of his parents, because they saw he was a proper child; and they were not afraid of the king’s commandment.

verses.original: πίστει Μωϋσῆς μέγας γενόμενος ἠρνήσατο λέγεσθαι υἱὸς θυγατρὸς Φαραώ,
verses.translit: pistei Moyses megas genomenos ernisato legesthai yios thygatros Farao,
verses.translation: By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter;

verses.original: μᾶλλον ἑλόμενος συγκακουχεῖσθαι τῷ λαῷ τοῦ θεοῦ ἢ πρόσκαιρον ἔχειν ἁμαρτίας ἀπόλαυσιν,
verses.translit: mallon elomenos sygkakoyheisthai to lao tou theou e proskairon ehein amartias apolaysin,
verses.translation: Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season;

verses.original: μείζονα πλοῦτον ἡγησάμενος τῶν Αἰγύπτου θησαυρῶν τὸν ὀνειδισμὸν τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἀπέβλεπεν γὰρ εἰς τὴν μισθαποδοσίαν.
verses.translit: meizona plouton egisamenos ton Aigyptoy thisayron ton oneidismon tou Hristou, apevlepen gar eis ten misthapodosian.
verses.translation: Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt: for he had respect unto the recompence of the reward.

verses.original: πίστει κατέλιπεν Αἴγυπτον, μὴ φοβηθεὶς τὸν θυμὸν τοῦ βασιλέως, τὸν γὰρ ἀόρατον ὡς ὁρῶν ἐκαρτέρησεν.
verses.translit: pistei katelipen Aigypton, me fovitheis ton thymon tou vasileos, ton gar aoraton os oron ekarterisen.
verses.translation: By faith he forsook Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king: for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible.

verses.original: πίστει πεποίηκεν τὸ πάσχα καὶ τὴν πρόσχυσιν τοῦ αἵματος, ἵνα μὴ ὁ ὀλοθρεύων τὰ πρωτότοκα θίγῃ αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: pistei pepoiiken to pasha kai ten proshysin tou aimatos, ina me o olothreyon ta prototoka thige auton.
verses.translation: Through faith he kept the passover, and the sprinkling of blood, lest he that destroyed the firstborn should touch them.

verses.original: Πίστει διέβησαν τὴν Ἐρυθρὰν Θάλασσαν ὡς διὰ ξηρᾶς ⸀γῆς, ἧς πεῖραν λαβόντες οἱ Αἰγύπτιοι κατεπόθησαν.
verses.translit: Pistei dievisan ten Erythran Thalassan os dia xiras ges, es peiran lavontes oi Aigyptioi katepothisan.
verses.translation: By faith they passed through the Red sea as by dry land : which the Egyptians assaying to do were drowned.

verses.original: πίστει τὰ τείχη Ἰεριχὼ ⸀ἔπεσαν κυκλωθέντα ἐπὶ ἑπτὰ ἡμέρας.
verses.translit: pistei ta teihi Ieriho epesan kyklothenta epi epta emeras.
verses.translation: By faith the walls of Jericho fell down, after they were compassed about seven days.

verses.original: πίστει Ῥαὰβ ἡ πόρνη οὐ συναπώλετο τοῖς ἀπειθήσασιν, δεξαμένη τοὺς κατασκόπους μετʼ εἰρήνης.
verses.translit: pistei Raav e porni ou synapoleto tois apeithisasin, dexameni tous kataskopoys met' eirinis.
verses.translation: By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace.

verses.original: Καὶ τί ἔτι λέγω; ἐπιλείψει ⸂με γὰρ⸃ διηγούμενον ὁ χρόνος περὶ Γεδεών, Βαράκ, ⸀Σαμψών, Ἰεφθάε, Δαυίδ τε καὶ Σαμουὴλ καὶ τῶν προφητῶν,
verses.translit: Kai ti eti lego; epileipsei me gar diigoymenon o hronos peri Gedeon, Varak, Sampson, Iefthae, Dayid te kai Samoyel kai ton profiton,
verses.translation: And what shall I more say? for the time would fail me to tell of Gedeon, and of Barak, and of Samson, and of Jephthae; of David also, and Samuel, and of the prophets:

verses.original: οἳ διὰ πίστεως κατηγωνίσαντο βασιλείας, εἰργάσαντο δικαιοσύνην, ἐπέτυχον ἐπαγγελιῶν, ἔφραξαν στόματα λεόντων,
verses.translit: oi dia pisteos katigonisanto vasileias, eirgasanto dikaiosynin, epetyhon epaggelion, efraxan stomata leonton,
verses.translation: Who through faith subdued kingdoms, wrought righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions,

verses.original: ἔσβεσαν δύναμιν πυρός, ἔφυγον στόματα ⸀μαχαίρης, ⸀ἐδυναμώθησαν ἀπὸ ἀσθενείας, ἐγενήθησαν ἰσχυροὶ ἐν πολέμῳ, παρεμβολὰς ἔκλιναν ἀλλοτρίων·
verses.translit: esvesan dynamin pyros, efygon stomata mahairis, edynamothisan apo astheneias, egenithisan ishyroi en polemo, paremvolas eklinan allotrion*
verses.translation: Quenched the violence of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, out of weakness were made strong, waxed valiant in fight, turned to flight the armies of the aliens.

verses.original: ἔλαβον γυναῖκες ἐξ ἀναστάσεως τοὺς νεκροὺς αὐτῶν· ἄλλοι δὲ ἐτυμπανίσθησαν, οὐ προσδεξάμενοι τὴν ἀπολύτρωσιν, ἵνα κρείττονος ἀναστάσεως τύχωσιν·
verses.translit: elavon gynaikes ex anastaseos tous nekrous auton* alloi de etympanisthisan, ou prosdexamenoi ten apolytrosin, ina kreittonos anastaseos tyhosin*
verses.translation: Women received their dead raised to life again: and others were tortured, not accepting deliverance; that they might obtain a better resurrection:

verses.original: ἕτεροι δὲ ἐμπαιγμῶν καὶ μαστίγων πεῖραν ἔλαβον, ἔτι δὲ δεσμῶν καὶ φυλακῆς·
verses.translit: eteroi de empaigmon kai mastigon peiran elavon, eti de desmon kai fylakes*
verses.translation: And others had trial of cruel mockings and scourgings, yea, moreover of bonds and imprisonment:

verses.original: ἐλιθάσθησαν, ⸀ἐπρίσθησαν, ἐν φόνῳ ⸀μαχαίρης ἀπέθανον, περιῆλθον ἐν μηλωταῖς, ἐν αἰγείοις δέρμασιν, ὑστερούμενοι, θλιβόμενοι, κακουχούμενοι,
verses.translit: elithasthisan, epristhisan, en fono mahairis apethanon, perielthon en milotais, en aigeiois dermasin, usteroymenoi, thlivomenoi, kakoyhoymenoi,
verses.translation: They were stoned, they were sawn asunder, were tempted, were slain with the sword: they wandered about in sheepskins and goatskins; being destitute, afflicted, tormented;

verses.original: ὧν οὐκ ἦν ἄξιος ὁ κόσμος ⸀ἐπὶ ἐρημίαις πλανώμενοι καὶ ὄρεσι καὶ σπηλαίοις καὶ ταῖς ὀπαῖς τῆς γῆς·
verses.translit: on ouk en axios o kosmos epi erimiais planomenoi kai oresi kai spilaiois kai tais opais tes ges*
verses.translation: (Of whom the world was not worthy:) they wandered in deserts, and in mountains, and in dens and caves of the earth.

verses.original: ⸀καὶ πάντες μαρτυρηθέντες διὰ τῆς πίστεως οὐκ ἐκομίσαντο τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν,
verses.translit: kai pantes martyrithentes dia tes pisteos ouk ekomisanto ten epaggelian,
verses.translation: And these all, having obtained a good report through faith, received not the promise:

verses.original: τοῦ θεοῦ περὶ ἡμῶν κρεῖττόν τι προβλεψαμένου, ἵνα μὴ χωρὶς ἡμῶν τελειωθῶσιν.
verses.translit: tou theou peri emon kreitton ti provlepsamenoy, ina me horis emon teleiothosin.
verses.translation: God having provided some better thing for us, that they without us should not be made perfect.

verses.original: Τοιγαροῦν καὶ ἡμεῖς, τοσοῦτον ἔχοντες περικείμενον ἡμῖν νέφος μαρτύρων, ὄγκον ἀποθέμενοι πάντα καὶ τὴν εὐπερίστατον ἁμαρτίαν, διʼ ὑπομονῆς τρέχωμεν τὸν προκείμενον ἡμῖν ἀγῶνα,
verses.translit: Toigaroun kai emeis, tosouton ehontes perikeimenon emin nefos martyron, ogkon apothemenoi panta kai ten euperistaton amartian, di' upomones trehomen ton prokeimenon emin agona,
verses.translation: Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us , and let us run with patience the race that is set before us,

verses.original: ἀφορῶντες εἰς τὸν τῆς πίστεως ἀρχηγὸν καὶ τελειωτὴν Ἰησοῦν, ὃς ἀντὶ τῆς προκειμένης αὐτῷ χαρᾶς ὑπέμεινεν σταυρὸν αἰσχύνης καταφρονήσας, ἐν δεξιᾷ τε τοῦ θρόνου τοῦ θεοῦ κεκάθικεν.
verses.translit: aforontes eis ton tes pisteos arhigon kai teleioten Iisoun, os anti tes prokeimenis auto haras upemeinen stayron aishynis katafronisas, en dexia te tou thronoy tou theou kekathiken.
verses.translation: Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God.

verses.original: Ἀναλογίσασθε γὰρ τὸν τοιαύτην ὑπομεμενηκότα ὑπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν εἰς ⸀ἑαυτοὺς ἀντιλογίαν, ἵνα μὴ κάμητε ταῖς ψυχαῖς ὑμῶν ἐκλυόμενοι.
verses.translit: Analogisasthe gar ton toiaytin upomemenikota upo ton amartolon eis eaytous antilogian, ina me kamite tais psyhais umon eklyomenoi.
verses.translation: For consider him that endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, lest ye be wearied and faint in your minds.

verses.original: οὔπω μέχρις αἵματος ἀντικατέστητε πρὸς τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ἀνταγωνιζόμενοι,
verses.translit: oupo mehris aimatos antikatestite pros ten amartian antagonizomenoi,
verses.translation: Ye have not yet resisted unto blood, striving against sin.

verses.original: καὶ ἐκλέλησθε τῆς παρακλήσεως, ἥτις ὑμῖν ὡς υἱοῖς διαλέγεται, Υἱέ μου, μὴ ὀλιγώρει παιδείας κυρίου, μηδὲ ἐκλύου ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ ἐλεγχόμενος·
verses.translit: kai eklelisthe tes parakliseos, etis umin os yiois dialegetai, Yie moy, me oligorei paideias kyrioy, mide eklyoy up' autou eleghomenos*
verses.translation: And ye have forgotten the exhortation which speaketh unto you as unto children, My son, despise not thou the chastening of the Lord, nor faint when thou art rebuked of him:

verses.original: ὃν γὰρ ἀγαπᾷ κύριος παιδεύει, μαστιγοῖ δὲ πάντα υἱὸν ὃν παραδέχεται.
verses.translit: on gar agapa kyrios paideyei, mastigoi de panta yion on paradehetai.
verses.translation: For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.

verses.original: εἰς παιδείαν ὑπομένετε· ὡς υἱοῖς ὑμῖν προσφέρεται ὁ θεός· τίς ⸀γὰρ υἱὸς ὃν οὐ παιδεύει πατήρ;
verses.translit: eis paideian upomenete* os yiois umin prosferetai o theos* tis gar yios on ou paideyei patir;
verses.translation: If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?

verses.original: εἰ δὲ χωρίς ἐστε παιδείας ἧς μέτοχοι γεγόνασι πάντες, ἄρα νόθοι ⸂καὶ οὐχ υἱοί ἐστε⸃.
verses.translit: ei de horis este paideias es metohoi gegonasi pantes, ara nothoi kai ouh yioi este.
verses.translation: But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.

verses.original: εἶτα τοὺς μὲν τῆς σαρκὸς ἡμῶν πατέρας εἴχομεν παιδευτὰς καὶ ἐνετρεπόμεθα· οὐ ⸀πολὺ μᾶλλον ὑποταγησόμεθα τῷ πατρὶ τῶν πνευμάτων καὶ ζήσομεν;
verses.translit: eita tous men tes sarkos emon pateras eihomen paideytas kai enetrepometha* ou polu mallon upotagisometha to patri ton pneymaton kai zisomen;
verses.translation: Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us , and we gave them reverence: shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live?

verses.original: οἱ μὲν γὰρ πρὸς ὀλίγας ἡμέρας κατὰ τὸ δοκοῦν αὐτοῖς ἐπαίδευον, ὁ δὲ ἐπὶ τὸ συμφέρον εἰς τὸ μεταλαβεῖν τῆς ἁγιότητος αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: oi men gar pros oligas emeras kata to dokoun autois epaideyon, o de epi to symferon eis to metalavein tes agiotitos autou.
verses.translation: For they verily for a few days chastened us after their own pleasure; but he for our profit, that we might be partakers of his holiness.

verses.original: πᾶσα ⸀δὲ παιδεία πρὸς μὲν τὸ παρὸν οὐ δοκεῖ χαρᾶς εἶναι ἀλλὰ λύπης, ὕστερον δὲ καρπὸν εἰρηνικὸν τοῖς διʼ αὐτῆς γεγυμνασμένοις ἀποδίδωσιν δικαιοσύνης.
verses.translit: pasa de paideia pros men to paron ou dokei haras einai alla lypis, usteron de karpon eirinikon tois di' autes gegymnasmenois apodidosin dikaiosynis.
verses.translation: Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby.

verses.original: Διὸ τὰς παρειμένας χεῖρας καὶ τὰ παραλελυμένα γόνατα ἀνορθώσατε,
verses.translit: Dio tas pareimenas heiras kai ta paralelymena gonata anorthosate,
verses.translation: Wherefore lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees;

verses.original: καὶ τροχιὰς ὀρθὰς ⸀ποιεῖτε τοῖς ποσὶν ὑμῶν, ἵνα μὴ τὸ χωλὸν ἐκτραπῇ, ἰαθῇ δὲ μᾶλλον.
verses.translit: kai trohias orthas poieite tois posin umon, ina me to holon ektrape, iathe de mallon.
verses.translation: And make straight paths for your feet, lest that which is lame be turned out of the way; but let it rather be healed.

verses.original: Εἰρήνην διώκετε μετὰ πάντων, καὶ τὸν ἁγιασμόν, οὗ χωρὶς οὐδεὶς ὄψεται τὸν κύριον,
verses.translit: Eirinin diokete meta panton, kai ton agiasmon, ou horis oudeis opsetai ton kyrion,
verses.translation: Follow peace with all men , and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord:

verses.original: ἐπισκοποῦντες μή τις ὑστερῶν ἀπὸ τῆς χάριτος τοῦ θεοῦ, μή τις ῥίζα πικρίας ἄνω φύουσα ἐνοχλῇ καὶ ⸂διʼ αὐτῆς⸃ μιανθῶσιν ⸀πολλοί,
verses.translit: episkopountes mi tis usteron apo tes haritos tou theou, mi tis Riza pikrias ano fyoysa enohle kai di' autes mianthosin polloi,
verses.translation: Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you , and thereby many be defiled;

verses.original: μή τις πόρνος ἢ βέβηλος ὡς Ἠσαῦ, ὃς ἀντὶ βρώσεως μιᾶς ἀπέδετο τὰ πρωτοτόκια ⸀ἑαυτοῦ.
verses.translit: mi tis pornos e vevilos os Esau, os anti vroseos mias apedeto ta prototokia eaytou.
verses.translation: Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright.

verses.original: ἴστε γὰρ ὅτι καὶ μετέπειτα θέλων κληρονομῆσαι τὴν εὐλογίαν ἀπεδοκιμάσθη, μετανοίας γὰρ τόπον οὐχ εὗρεν, καίπερ μετὰ δακρύων ἐκζητήσας αὐτήν.
verses.translit: iste gar oti kai metepeita thelon klironomesai ten eulogian apedokimasthi, metanoias gar topon ouh euren, kaiper meta dakryon ekzitisas autin.
verses.translation: For ye know how that afterward, when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected: for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears.

verses.original: Οὐ γὰρ προσεληλύθατε ⸀ψηλαφωμένῳ καὶ κεκαυμένῳ πυρὶ καὶ γνόφῳ καὶ ⸀ζόφῳ καὶ θυέλλῃ
verses.translit: Ou gar proselilythate psilafomeno kai kekaymeno pyri kai gnofo kai zofo kai thyelle
