verses.translation: For ye are not come unto the mount that might be touched, and that burned with fire, nor unto blackness, and darkness, and tempest,

verses.original: καὶ σάλπιγγος ἤχῳ καὶ φωνῇ ῥημάτων, ἧς οἱ ἀκούσαντες παρῃτήσαντο ⸀μὴ προστεθῆναι αὐτοῖς λόγον·
verses.translit: kai salpiggos eho kai fone Rimaton, es oi akoysantes paretisanto me prostethenai autois logon*
verses.translation: And the sound of a trumpet, and the voice of words; which voice they that heard intreated that the word should not be spoken to them any more:

verses.original: οὐκ ἔφερον γὰρ τὸ διαστελλόμενον· Κἂν θηρίον θίγῃ τοῦ ὄρους, λιθοβοληθήσεται·
verses.translit: ouk eferon gar to diastellomenon* Kan thirion thige tou oroys, lithovolithisetai*
verses.translation: (For they could not endure that which was commanded, And if so much as a beast touch the mountain, it shall be stoned, or thrust through with a dart:

verses.original: καί, οὕτω φοβερὸν ἦν τὸ φανταζόμενον, Μωϋσῆς εἶπεν· Ἔκφοβός εἰμι καὶ ἔντρομος.
verses.translit: kai, outo foveron en to fantazomenon, Moyses eipen* Ekfovos eimi kai entromos.
verses.translation: And so terrible was the sight, that Moses said, I exceedingly fear and quake:)

verses.original: ἀλλὰ προσεληλύθατε Σιὼν ὄρει καὶ πόλει θεοῦ ζῶντος, Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἐπουρανίῳ, καὶ μυριάσιν ἀγγέλων, πανηγύρει
verses.translit: alla proselilythate Sion orei kai polei theou zontos, Ieroysalem epoyranio, kai myriasin aggelon, panigyrei
verses.translation: But ye are come unto mount Sion, and unto the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to an innumerable company of angels,

verses.original: καὶ ἐκκλησίᾳ πρωτοτόκων ⸂ἀπογεγραμμένων ἐν οὐρανοῖς⸃, καὶ κριτῇ θεῷ πάντων, καὶ πνεύμασι δικαίων τετελειωμένων,
verses.translit: kai ekklisia prototokon apogegrammenon en ouranois, kai krite theo panton, kai pneymasi dikaion teteleiomenon,
verses.translation: To the general assembly and church of the firstborn, which are written in heaven, and to God the Judge of all, and to the spirits of just men made perfect,

verses.original: καὶ διαθήκης νέας μεσίτῃ Ἰησοῦ, καὶ αἵματι ῥαντισμοῦ κρεῖττον λαλοῦντι παρὰ τὸν Ἅβελ.
verses.translit: kai diathikis neas mesite Iisou, kai aimati Rantismou kreitton lalounti para ton Avel.
verses.translation: And to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling, that speaketh better things than that of Abel.

verses.original: Βλέπετε μὴ παραιτήσησθε τὸν λαλοῦντα· εἰ γὰρ ἐκεῖνοι οὐκ ⸀ἐξέφυγον ⸂ἐπὶ γῆς παραιτησάμενοι τὸν⸃ χρηματίζοντα, ⸀πολὺ μᾶλλον ἡμεῖς οἱ τὸν ἀπʼ οὐρανῶν ἀποστρεφόμενοι·
verses.translit: Vlepete me paraitisisthe ton lalounta* ei gar ekeinoi ouk exefygon epi ges paraitisamenoi ton hrimatizonta, polu mallon emeis oi ton ap' ouranon apostrefomenoi*
verses.translation: See that ye refuse not him that speaketh. For if they escaped not who refused him that spake on earth, much more shall not we escape , if we turn away from him that speaketh from heaven:

verses.original: οὗ ἡ φωνὴ τὴν γῆν ἐσάλευσεν τότε, νῦν δὲ ἐπήγγελται λέγων· Ἔτι ἅπαξ ἐγὼ ⸀σείσω οὐ μόνον τὴν γῆν ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸν οὐρανόν.
verses.translit: ou e fone ten gen esaleysen tote, nun de epiggeltai legon* Eti apax ego seiso ou monon ten gen alla kai ton ouranon.
verses.translation: Whose voice then shook the earth: but now he hath promised, saying, Yet once more I shake not the earth only, but also heaven.

verses.original: τὸ δὲ Ἔτι ἅπαξ δηλοῖ ⸂τῶν σαλευομένων⸃ μετάθεσιν ὡς πεποιημένων, ἵνα μείνῃ τὰ μὴ σαλευόμενα.
verses.translit: to de Eti apax diloi ton saleyomenon metathesin os pepoiimenon, ina meine ta me saleyomena.
verses.translation: And this word , Yet once more, signifieth the removing of those things that are shaken, as of things that are made, that those things which cannot be shaken may remain.

verses.original: διὸ βασιλείαν ἀσάλευτον παραλαμβάνοντες ἔχωμεν χάριν, διʼ ἧς ⸀λατρεύωμεν εὐαρέστως τῷ θεῷ μετὰ ⸂εὐλαβείας καὶ δέους⸃,
verses.translit: dio vasileian asaleyton paralamvanontes ehomen harin, di' es latreyomen euarestos to theo meta eulaveias kai deoys,
verses.translation: Wherefore we receiving a kingdom which cannot be moved, let us have grace, whereby we may serve God acceptably with reverence and godly fear:

verses.original: καὶ γὰρ ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν πῦρ καταναλίσκον.
verses.translit: kai gar o theos emon pur katanaliskon.
verses.translation: For our God is a consuming fire.

verses.original: Ἡ φιλαδελφία μενέτω.
verses.translit: E filadelfia meneto.
verses.translation: Let brotherly love continue.

verses.original: τῆς φιλοξενίας μὴ ἐπιλανθάνεσθε, διὰ ταύτης γὰρ ἔλαθόν τινες ξενίσαντες ἀγγέλους.
verses.translit: tes filoxenias me epilanthanesthe, dia taytis gar elathon tines xenisantes aggeloys.
verses.translation: Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.

verses.original: μιμνῄσκεσθε τῶν δεσμίων ὡς συνδεδεμένοι, τῶν κακουχουμένων ὡς καὶ αὐτοὶ ὄντες ἐν σώματι.
verses.translit: mimneskesthe ton desmion os syndedemenoi, ton kakoyhoymenon os kai autoi ontes en somati.
verses.translation: Remember them that are in bonds, as bound with them; and them which suffer adversity, as being yourselves also in the body.

verses.original: τίμιος ὁ γάμος ἐν πᾶσιν καὶ ἡ κοίτη ἀμίαντος, πόρνους ⸀γὰρ καὶ μοιχοὺς κρινεῖ ὁ θεός.
verses.translit: timios o gamos en pasin kai e koiti amiantos, pornoys gar kai moihous krinei o theos.
verses.translation: Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled: but whoremongers and adulterers God will judge.

verses.original: ἀφιλάργυρος ὁ τρόπος· ἀρκούμενοι τοῖς παροῦσιν· αὐτὸς γὰρ εἴρηκεν· Οὐ μή σε ἀνῶ οὐδʼ οὐ μή σε ⸀ἐγκαταλίπω·
verses.translit: afilargyros o tropos* arkoymenoi tois parousin* autos gar eiriken* Ou mi se ano oud' ou mi se egkatalipo*
verses.translation: Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.

verses.original: ὥστε θαρροῦντας ἡμᾶς λέγειν· Κύριος ἐμοὶ βοηθός, ⸀οὐ φοβηθήσομαι· τί ποιήσει μοι ἄνθρωπος;
verses.translit: oste tharrountas emas legein* Kyrios emoi voithos, ou fovithisomai* ti poiisei moi anthropos;
verses.translation: So that we may boldly say, The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me.

verses.original: Μνημονεύετε τῶν ἡγουμένων ὑμῶν, οἵτινες ἐλάλησαν ὑμῖν τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ, ὧν ἀναθεωροῦντες τὴν ἔκβασιν τῆς ἀναστροφῆς μιμεῖσθε τὴν πίστιν.
verses.translit: Mnimoneyete ton egoymenon umon, oitines elalisan umin ton logon tou theou, on anatheorountes ten ekvasin tes anastrofes mimeisthe ten pistin.
verses.translation: Remember them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of God: whose faith follow, considering the end of their conversation.

verses.original: Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ἐχθὲς καὶ σήμερον ὁ αὐτός, καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας.
verses.translit: Iisous Hristos ehthes kai simeron o autos, kai eis tous aionas.
verses.translation: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever.

verses.original: διδαχαῖς ποικίλαις καὶ ξέναις μὴ παραφέρεσθε· καλὸν γὰρ χάριτι βεβαιοῦσθαι τὴν καρδίαν, οὐ βρώμασιν, ἐν οἷς οὐκ ὠφελήθησαν οἱ ⸀περιπατοῦντες.
verses.translit: didahais poikilais kai xenais me paraferesthe* kalon gar hariti vevaiousthai ten kardian, ou vromasin, en ois ouk ofelithisan oi peripatountes.
verses.translation: Be not carried about with divers and strange doctrines. For it is a good thing that the heart be established with grace; not with meats, which have not profited them that have been occupied therein.

verses.original: ἔχομεν θυσιαστήριον ἐξ οὗ φαγεῖν οὐκ ἔχουσιν ἐξουσίαν οἱ τῇ σκηνῇ λατρεύοντες.
verses.translit: ehomen thysiastirion ex ou fagein ouk ehoysin exoysian oi te skine latreyontes.
verses.translation: We have an altar, whereof they have no right to eat which serve the tabernacle.

verses.original: ὧν γὰρ εἰσφέρεται ζῴων τὸ αἷμα περὶ ἁμαρτίας εἰς τὰ ἅγια διὰ τοῦ ἀρχιερέως, τούτων τὰ σώματα κατακαίεται ἔξω τῆς παρεμβολῆς·
verses.translit: on gar eisferetai zoon to aima peri amartias eis ta agia dia tou arhiereos, toyton ta somata katakaietai exo tes paremvoles*
verses.translation: For the bodies of those beasts, whose blood is brought into the sanctuary by the high priest for sin, are burned without the camp.

verses.original: διὸ καὶ Ἰησοῦς, ἵνα ἁγιάσῃ διὰ τοῦ ἰδίου αἵματος τὸν λαόν, ἔξω τῆς πύλης ἔπαθεν.
verses.translit: dio kai Iisous, ina agiase dia tou idioy aimatos ton laon, exo tes pylis epathen.
verses.translation: Wherefore Jesus also, that he might sanctify the people with his own blood, suffered without the gate.

verses.original: τοίνυν ἐξερχώμεθα πρὸς αὐτὸν ἔξω τῆς παρεμβολῆς, τὸν ὀνειδισμὸν αὐτοῦ φέροντες.
verses.translit: toinyn exerhometha pros auton exo tes paremvoles, ton oneidismon autou ferontes.
verses.translation: Let us go forth therefore unto him without the camp, bearing his reproach.

verses.original: οὐ γὰρ ἔχομεν ὧδε μένουσαν πόλιν, ἀλλὰ τὴν μέλλουσαν ἐπιζητοῦμεν·
verses.translit: ou gar ehomen ode menoysan polin, alla ten melloysan epizitoumen*
verses.translation: For here have we no continuing city, but we seek one to come.

verses.original: διʼ αὐτοῦ ⸀οὖν ἀναφέρωμεν θυσίαν αἰνέσεως διὰ παντὸς τῷ θεῷ, τοῦτʼ ἔστιν καρπὸν χειλέων ὁμολογούντων τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: di' autou oun anaferomen thysian aineseos dia pantos to theo, tout' estin karpon heileon omologoynton to onomati autou.
verses.translation: By him therefore let us offer the sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of our lips giving thanks to his name.

verses.original: τῆς δὲ εὐποιΐας καὶ κοινωνίας μὴ ἐπιλανθάνεσθε, τοιαύταις γὰρ θυσίαις εὐαρεστεῖται ὁ θεός.
verses.translit: tes de eupoiIas kai koinonias me epilanthanesthe, toiaytais gar thysiais euaresteitai o theos.
verses.translation: But to do good and to communicate forget not: for with such sacrifices God is well pleased.

verses.original: Πείθεσθε τοῖς ἡγουμένοις ὑμῶν καὶ ὑπείκετε, αὐτοὶ γὰρ ἀγρυπνοῦσιν ὑπὲρ τῶν ψυχῶν ὑμῶν ὡς λόγον ἀποδώσοντες, ἵνα μετὰ χαρᾶς τοῦτο ποιῶσιν καὶ μὴ στενάζοντες, ἀλυσιτελὲς γὰρ ὑμῖν τοῦτο.
verses.translit: Peithesthe tois egoymenois umon kai upeikete, autoi gar agrypnousin uper ton psyhon umon os logon apodosontes, ina meta haras touto poiosin kai me stenazontes, alysiteles gar umin touto.
verses.translation: Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account, that they may do it with joy, and not with grief: for that is unprofitable for you.

verses.original: Προσεύχεσθε περὶ ἡμῶν, ⸀πειθόμεθα γὰρ ὅτι καλὴν συνείδησιν ἔχομεν, ἐν πᾶσιν καλῶς θέλοντες ἀναστρέφεσθαι.
verses.translit: Proseyhesthe peri emon, peithometha gar oti kalen syneidisin ehomen, en pasin kalos thelontes anastrefesthai.
verses.translation: Pray for us: for we trust we have a good conscience, in all things willing to live honestly.

verses.original: περισσοτέρως δὲ παρακαλῶ τοῦτο ποιῆσαι ἵνα τάχιον ἀποκατασταθῶ ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: perissoteros de parakalo touto poiesai ina tahion apokatastatho umin.
verses.translation: But I beseech you the rather to do this, that I may be restored to you the sooner.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ θεὸς τῆς εἰρήνης, ὁ ἀναγαγὼν ἐκ νεκρῶν τὸν ποιμένα τῶν προβάτων τὸν μέγαν ἐν αἵματι διαθήκης αἰωνίου, τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν,
verses.translit: O de theos tes eirinis, o anagagon ek nekron ton poimena ton provaton ton megan en aimati diathikis aionioy, ton kyrion emon Iisoun,
verses.translation: Now the God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant,

verses.original: καταρτίσαι ὑμᾶς ἐν ⸀παντὶ ἀγαθῷ εἰς τὸ ποιῆσαι τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ, ποιῶν ἐν ⸀ἡμῖν τὸ εὐάρεστον ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ᾧ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς ⸀αἰῶνας· ἀμήν.
verses.translit: katartisai umas en panti agatho eis to poiesai to thelima autou, poion en emin to euareston enopion autou dia Iisou Hristou, o e doxa eis tous aionas* amin.
verses.translation: Make you perfect in every good work to do his will, working in you that which is wellpleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ; to whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen.

verses.original: Παρακαλῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί, ἀνέχεσθε τοῦ λόγου τῆς παρακλήσεως, καὶ γὰρ διὰ βραχέων ἐπέστειλα ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: Parakalo de umas, adelfoi, anehesthe tou logoy tes parakliseos, kai gar dia vraheon epesteila umin.
verses.translation: And I beseech you, brethren, suffer the word of exhortation: for I have written a letter unto you in few words.

verses.original: γινώσκετε τὸν ἀδελφὸν ⸀ἡμῶν Τιμόθεον ἀπολελυμένον, μεθʼ οὗ ἐὰν τάχιον ἔρχηται ὄψομαι ὑμᾶς.
verses.translit: ginoskete ton adelfon emon Timotheon apolelymenon, meth' ou ean tahion erhitai opsomai umas.
verses.translation: Know ye that our brother Timothy is set at liberty; with whom, if he come shortly, I will see you.

verses.original: ἀσπάσασθε πάντας τοὺς ἡγουμένους ὑμῶν καὶ πάντας τοὺς ἁγίους. ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς οἱ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰταλίας.
verses.translit: aspasasthe pantas tous egoymenoys umon kai pantas tous agioys. aspazontai umas oi apo tes Italias.
verses.translation: Salute all them that have the rule over you, and all the saints. They of Italy salute you.

verses.original: ἡ χάρις μετὰ πάντων ⸀ὑμῶν.
verses.translit: e haris meta panton umon.
verses.translation: Grace be with you all. Amen.

verses.original: Ἰάκωβος θεοῦ καὶ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ δοῦλος ταῖς δώδεκα φυλαῖς ταῖς ἐν τῇ διασπορᾷ χαίρειν.
verses.translit: Iakovos theou kai kyrioy Iisou Hristou doulos tais dodeka fylais tais en te diaspora hairein.
verses.translation: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.

verses.original: Πᾶσαν χαρὰν ἡγήσασθε, ἀδελφοί μου, ὅταν πειρασμοῖς περιπέσητε ποικίλοις,
verses.translit: Pasan haran egisasthe, adelfoi moy, otan peirasmois peripesite poikilois,
verses.translation: My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations;

verses.original: γινώσκοντες ὅτι τὸ δοκίμιον ὑμῶν τῆς πίστεως κατεργάζεται ὑπομονήν·
verses.translit: ginoskontes oti to dokimion umon tes pisteos katergazetai upomonin*
verses.translation: Knowing this , that the trying of your faith worketh patience.

verses.original: ἡ δὲ ὑπομονὴ ἔργον τέλειον ἐχέτω, ἵνα ἦτε τέλειοι καὶ ὁλόκληροι, ἐν μηδενὶ λειπόμενοι.
verses.translit: e de upomone ergon teleion eheto, ina ete teleioi kai olokliroi, en mideni leipomenoi.
verses.translation: But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.

verses.original: Εἰ δέ τις ὑμῶν λείπεται σοφίας, αἰτείτω παρὰ τοῦ διδόντος θεοῦ πᾶσιν ἁπλῶς καὶ ⸀μὴ ὀνειδίζοντος, καὶ δοθήσεται αὐτῷ·
verses.translit: Ei de tis umon leipetai sofias, aiteito para tou didontos theou pasin aplos kai me oneidizontos, kai dothisetai auto*
verses.translation: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.

verses.original: αἰτείτω δὲ ἐν πίστει, μηδὲν διακρινόμενος, ὁ γὰρ διακρινόμενος ἔοικεν κλύδωνι θαλάσσης ἀνεμιζομένῳ καὶ ῥιπιζομένῳ·
verses.translit: aiteito de en pistei, miden diakrinomenos, o gar diakrinomenos eoiken klydoni thalassis anemizomeno kai Ripizomeno*
verses.translation: But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.

verses.original: μὴ γὰρ οἰέσθω ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος ὅτι λήμψεταί τι παρὰ τοῦ κυρίου
verses.translit: me gar oiestho o anthropos ekeinos oti limpsetai ti para tou kyrioy
verses.translation: For let not that man think that he shall receive any thing of the Lord.

verses.original: ἀνὴρ δίψυχος, ἀκατάστατος ἐν πάσαις ταῖς ὁδοῖς αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: aner dipsyhos, akatastatos en pasais tais odois autou.
verses.translation: A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.

verses.original: Καυχάσθω δὲ ὁ ἀδελφὸς ὁ ταπεινὸς ἐν τῷ ὕψει αὐτοῦ,
verses.translit: Kayhastho de o adelfos o tapeinos en to upsei autou,
verses.translation: Let the brother of low degree rejoice in that he is exalted:

verses.original: ὁ δὲ πλούσιος ἐν τῇ ταπεινώσει αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ὡς ἄνθος χόρτου παρελεύσεται.
verses.translit: o de ploysios en te tapeinosei autou, oti os anthos hortoy pareleysetai.
verses.translation: But the rich, in that he is made low: because as the flower of the grass he shall pass away.

verses.original: ἀνέτειλεν γὰρ ὁ ἥλιος σὺν τῷ καύσωνι καὶ ἐξήρανεν τὸν χόρτον, καὶ τὸ ἄνθος αὐτοῦ ἐξέπεσεν καὶ ἡ εὐπρέπεια τοῦ προσώπου αὐτοῦ ἀπώλετο· οὕτως καὶ ὁ πλούσιος ἐν ταῖς πορείαις αὐτοῦ μαρανθήσεται.
verses.translit: aneteilen gar o elios sun to kaysoni kai exiranen ton horton, kai to anthos autou exepesen kai e euprepeia tou prosopoy autou apoleto* outos kai o ploysios en tais poreiais autou maranthisetai.
verses.translation: For the sun is no sooner risen with a burning heat, but it withereth the grass, and the flower thereof falleth, and the grace of the fashion of it perisheth: so also shall the rich man fade away in his ways.

verses.original: Μακάριος ἀνὴρ ὃς ὑπομένει πειρασμόν, ὅτι δόκιμος γενόμενος λήμψεται τὸν στέφανον τῆς ζωῆς, ὃν ⸀ἐπηγγείλατο τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν αὐτόν.
verses.translit: Makarios aner os upomenei peirasmon, oti dokimos genomenos limpsetai ton stefanon tes zoes, on epiggeilato tois agaposin auton.
verses.translation: Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord hath promised to them that love him.

verses.original: μηδεὶς πειραζόμενος λεγέτω ὅτι Ἀπὸ θεοῦ πειράζομαι· ὁ γὰρ θεὸς ἀπείραστός ἐστιν κακῶν, πειράζει δὲ αὐτὸς οὐδένα.
verses.translit: mideis peirazomenos legeto oti Apo theou peirazomai* o gar theos apeirastos estin kakon, peirazei de autos oudena.
verses.translation: Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God: for God cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man:

verses.original: ἕκαστος δὲ πειράζεται ὑπὸ τῆς ἰδίας ἐπιθυμίας ἐξελκόμενος καὶ δελεαζόμενος·
verses.translit: ekastos de peirazetai upo tes idias epithymias exelkomenos kai deleazomenos*
verses.translation: But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.

verses.original: εἶτα ἡ ἐπιθυμία συλλαβοῦσα τίκτει ἁμαρτίαν, ἡ δὲ ἁμαρτία ἀποτελεσθεῖσα ἀποκύει θάνατον.
verses.translit: eita e epithymia syllavousa tiktei amartian, e de amartia apotelestheisa apokyei thanaton.
verses.translation: Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.

verses.original: μὴ πλανᾶσθε, ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί.
verses.translit: me planasthe, adelfoi moy agapitoi.
verses.translation: Do not err, my beloved brethren.

verses.original: Πᾶσα δόσις ἀγαθὴ καὶ πᾶν δώρημα τέλειον ἄνωθέν ἐστιν, καταβαῖνον ἀπὸ τοῦ πατρὸς τῶν φώτων, παρʼ ᾧ οὐκ ἔνι παραλλαγὴ ἢ τροπῆς ἀποσκίασμα.
verses.translit: Pasa dosis agathe kai pan dorima teleion anothen estin, katavainon apo tou patros ton foton, par' o ouk eni parallage e tropes aposkiasma.
verses.translation: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning.

verses.original: βουληθεὶς ἀπεκύησεν ἡμᾶς λόγῳ ἀληθείας, εἰς τὸ εἶναι ἡμᾶς ἀπαρχήν τινα τῶν αὐτοῦ κτισμάτων.
verses.translit: voylitheis apekyisen emas logo alitheias, eis to einai emas aparhin tina ton autou ktismaton.
verses.translation: Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.

verses.original: ⸀Ἴστε, ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί. ἔστω ⸀δὲ πᾶς ἄνθρωπος ταχὺς εἰς τὸ ἀκοῦσαι, βραδὺς εἰς τὸ λαλῆσαι, βραδὺς εἰς ὀργήν,
verses.translit: Iste, adelfoi moy agapitoi. esto de pas anthropos tahus eis to akousai, vradus eis to lalesai, vradus eis orgin,
verses.translation: Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath:

verses.original: ὀργὴ γὰρ ἀνδρὸς δικαιοσύνην θεοῦ ⸂οὐκ ἐργάζεται⸃.
verses.translit: orge gar andros dikaiosynin theou ouk ergazetai.
verses.translation: For the wrath of man worketh not the righteousness of God.

verses.original: διὸ ἀποθέμενοι πᾶσαν ῥυπαρίαν καὶ περισσείαν κακίας ἐν πραΰτητι δέξασθε τὸν ἔμφυτον λόγον τὸν δυνάμενον σῶσαι τὰς ψυχὰς ὑμῶν.
verses.translit: dio apothemenoi pasan Ryparian kai perisseian kakias en praytiti dexasthe ton emfyton logon ton dynamenon sosai tas psyhas umon.
verses.translation: Wherefore lay apart all filthiness and superfluity of naughtiness, and receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls.

verses.original: Γίνεσθε δὲ ποιηταὶ λόγου καὶ μὴ ⸂ἀκροαταὶ μόνον⸃ παραλογιζόμενοι ἑαυτούς.
verses.translit: Ginesthe de poiitai logoy kai me akroatai monon paralogizomenoi eaytoys.
verses.translation: But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.

verses.original: ὅτι εἴ τις ἀκροατὴς λόγου ἐστὶν καὶ οὐ ποιητής, οὗτος ἔοικεν ἀνδρὶ κατανοοῦντι τὸ πρόσωπον τῆς γενέσεως αὐτοῦ ἐν ἐσόπτρῳ,
verses.translit: oti ei tis akroates logoy estin kai ou poiitis, outos eoiken andri katanoounti to prosopon tes geneseos autou en esoptro,
verses.translation: For if any be a hearer of the word, and not a doer, he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a glass:

verses.original: κατενόησεν γὰρ ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἀπελήλυθεν καὶ εὐθέως ἐπελάθετο ὁποῖος ἦν.
verses.translit: katenoisen gar eayton kai apelilythen kai eutheos epelatheto opoios en.
verses.translation: For he beholdeth himself, and goeth his way, and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ παρακύψας εἰς νόμον τέλειον τὸν τῆς ἐλευθερίας καὶ παραμείνας, ⸀οὐκ ἀκροατὴς ἐπιλησμονῆς γενόμενος ἀλλὰ ποιητὴς ἔργου, οὗτος μακάριος ἐν τῇ ποιήσει αὐτοῦ ἔσται.
verses.translit: o de parakypsas eis nomon teleion ton tes eleytherias kai parameinas, ouk akroates epilismones genomenos alla poiites ergoy, outos makarios en te poiisei autou estai.
verses.translation: But whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty, and continueth therein , he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed.

verses.original: Εἴ τις δοκεῖ θρησκὸς ⸀εἶναι μὴ χαλιναγωγῶν γλῶσσαν ⸀αὐτοῦ ἀλλὰ ἀπατῶν καρδίαν ⸀αὐτοῦ, τούτου μάταιος ἡ θρησκεία.
verses.translit: Ei tis dokei thriskos einai me halinagogon glossan autou alla apaton kardian autou, toytoy mataios e thriskeia.
verses.translation: If any man among you seem to be religious, and bridleth not his tongue, but deceiveth his own heart, this man’s religion is vain.

verses.original: θρησκεία καθαρὰ καὶ ἀμίαντος παρὰ ⸀τῷ θεῷ καὶ πατρὶ αὕτη ἐστίν, ἐπισκέπτεσθαι ὀρφανοὺς καὶ χήρας ἐν τῇ θλίψει αὐτῶν, ἄσπιλον ἑαυτὸν τηρεῖν ἀπὸ τοῦ κόσμου.
verses.translit: thriskeia kathara kai amiantos para to theo kai patri auti estin, episkeptesthai orfanous kai hiras en te thlipsei auton, aspilon eayton tirein apo tou kosmoy.
verses.translation: Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.

verses.original: Ἀδελφοί μου, μὴ ἐν προσωπολημψίαις ἔχετε τὴν πίστιν τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τῆς δόξης;
verses.translit: Adelfoi moy, me en prosopolimpsiais ehete ten pistin tou kyrioy emon Iisou Hristou tes doxis?
verses.translation: My brethren, have not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons.

verses.original: ἐὰν γὰρ εἰσέλθῃ ⸀εἰς συναγωγὴν ὑμῶν ἀνὴρ χρυσοδακτύλιος ἐν ἐσθῆτι λαμπρᾷ, εἰσέλθῃ δὲ καὶ πτωχὸς ἐν ῥυπαρᾷ ἐσθῆτι,
verses.translit: ean gar eiselthe eis synagogen umon aner hrysodaktylios en estheti lampra, eiselthe de kai ptohos en Rypara estheti,
verses.translation: For if there come unto your assembly a man with a gold ring, in goodly apparel, and there come in also a poor man in vile raiment;

verses.original: ⸂ἐπιβλέψητε δὲ⸃ ἐπὶ τὸν φοροῦντα τὴν ἐσθῆτα τὴν λαμπρὰν καὶ ⸀εἴπητε· Σὺ κάθου ὧδε καλῶς, καὶ τῷ πτωχῷ εἴπητε· Σὺ στῆθι ⸂ἢ κάθου ἐκεῖ⸃ ὑπὸ τὸ ὑποπόδιόν μου,
verses.translit: epivlepsite de epi ton forounta ten estheta ten lampran kai eipite* Su kathoy ode kalos, kai to ptoho eipite* Su stethi e kathoy ekei upo to upopodion moy,
verses.translation: And ye have respect to him that weareth the gay clothing, and say unto him, Sit thou here in a good place; and say to the poor, Stand thou there, or sit here under my footstool:

verses.original: ⸀οὐ διεκρίθητε ἐν ἑαυτοῖς καὶ ἐγένεσθε κριταὶ διαλογισμῶν πονηρῶν;
verses.translit: ou diekrithite en eaytois kai egenesthe kritai dialogismon poniron;
verses.translation: Are ye not then partial in yourselves, and are become judges of evil thoughts?

verses.original: ἀκούσατε, ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί. οὐχ ὁ θεὸς ἐξελέξατο τοὺς πτωχοὺς ⸂τῷ κόσμῳ⸃ πλουσίους ἐν πίστει καὶ κληρονόμους τῆς βασιλείας ἧς ἐπηγγείλατο τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν αὐτόν;
verses.translit: akoysate, adelfoi moy agapitoi. ouh o theos exelexato tous ptohous to kosmo ploysioys en pistei kai klironomoys tes vasileias es epiggeilato tois agaposin auton;
verses.translation: Hearken, my beloved brethren, Hath not God chosen the poor of this world rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom which he hath promised to them that love him?

verses.original: ὑμεῖς δὲ ἠτιμάσατε τὸν πτωχόν. οὐχ οἱ πλούσιοι καταδυναστεύουσιν ὑμῶν, καὶ αὐτοὶ ἕλκουσιν ὑμᾶς εἰς κριτήρια;
verses.translit: umeis de etimasate ton ptohon. ouh oi ploysioi katadynasteyoysin umon, kai autoi elkoysin umas eis kritiria;
verses.translation: But ye have despised the poor. Do not rich men oppress you, and draw you before the judgment seats?

verses.original: οὐκ αὐτοὶ βλασφημοῦσιν τὸ καλὸν ὄνομα τὸ ἐπικληθὲν ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς;
verses.translit: ouk autoi vlasfimousin to kalon onoma to epiklithen ef' umas;
verses.translation: Do not they blaspheme that worthy name by the which ye are called?

verses.original: Εἰ μέντοι νόμον τελεῖτε βασιλικὸν κατὰ τὴν γραφήν Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν, καλῶς ποιεῖτε·
verses.translit: Ei mentoi nomon teleite vasilikon kata ten grafin Agapiseis ton plision soy os seayton, kalos poieite*
verses.translation: If ye fulfil the royal law according to the scripture, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself, ye do well:

verses.original: εἰ δὲ προσωπολημπτεῖτε, ἁμαρτίαν ἐργάζεσθε, ἐλεγχόμενοι ὑπὸ τοῦ νόμου ὡς παραβάται.
verses.translit: ei de prosopolimpteite, amartian ergazesthe, eleghomenoi upo tou nomoy os paravatai.
verses.translation: But if ye have respect to persons, ye commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors.

verses.original: ὅστις γὰρ ὅλον τὸν νόμον ⸂τηρήσῃ, πταίσῃ⸃ δὲ ἐν ἑνί, γέγονεν πάντων ἔνοχος.
verses.translit: ostis gar olon ton nomon tirise, ptaise de en eni, gegonen panton enohos.
verses.translation: For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point , he is guilty of all.

verses.original: ὁ γὰρ εἰπών· Μὴ ⸀μοιχεύσῃς εἶπεν καί· Μὴ ⸀φονεύσῃς· εἰ δὲ οὐ ⸂μοιχεύεις φονεύεις⸃ δέ, γέγονας παραβάτης νόμου.
verses.translit: o gar eipon; Me moiheyses eipen kai; Me foneyses* ei de ou moiheyeis foneyeis de, gegonas paravatis nomoy.
verses.translation: For he that said, Do not commit adultery, said also, Do not kill. Now if thou commit no adultery, yet if thou kill, thou art become a transgressor of the law.

verses.original: οὕτως λαλεῖτε καὶ οὕτως ποιεῖτε ὡς διὰ νόμου ἐλευθερίας μέλλοντες κρίνεσθαι.
verses.translit: outos laleite kai outos poieite os dia nomoy eleytherias mellontes krinesthai.
verses.translation: So speak ye, and so do, as they that shall be judged by the law of liberty.

verses.original: ἡ γὰρ κρίσις ἀνέλεος τῷ μὴ ποιήσαντι ἔλεος· κατακαυχᾶται ⸀ἔλεος κρίσεως.
verses.translit: e gar krisis aneleos to me poiisanti eleos* katakayhatai eleos kriseos.
verses.translation: For he shall have judgment without mercy, that hath shewed no mercy; and mercy rejoiceth against judgment.

verses.original: ⸀Τί ὄφελος, ἀδελφοί μου, ἐὰν πίστιν λέγῃ τις ἔχειν ἔργα δὲ μὴ ἔχῃ; μὴ δύναται ἡ πίστις σῶσαι αὐτόν;
verses.translit: Ti ofelos, adelfoi moy, ean pistin lege tis ehein erga de me ehe; me dynatai e pistis sosai auton;
verses.translation: What doth it profit, my brethren, though a man say he hath faith, and have not works? can faith save him?

verses.original: ⸀ἐὰν ἀδελφὸς ἢ ἀδελφὴ γυμνοὶ ὑπάρχωσιν καὶ ⸀λειπόμενοι τῆς ἐφημέρου τροφῆς,
verses.translit: ean adelfos e adelfe gymnoi uparhosin kai leipomenoi tes efimeroy trofes,
verses.translation: If a brother or sister be naked, and destitute of daily food,

verses.original: εἴπῃ δέ τις αὐτοῖς ἐξ ὑμῶν· Ὑπάγετε ἐν εἰρήνῃ, θερμαίνεσθε καὶ χορτάζεσθε, μὴ δῶτε δὲ αὐτοῖς τὰ ἐπιτήδεια τοῦ σώματος, ⸀τί ὄφελος;
verses.translit: eipe de tis autois ex umon* Upagete en eirine, thermainesthe kai hortazesthe, me dote de autois ta epitideia tou somatos, ti ofelos;
verses.translation: And one of you say unto them, Depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled; notwithstanding ye give them not those things which are needful to the body; what doth it profit?

verses.original: οὕτως καὶ ἡ πίστις, ἐὰν μὴ ⸂ἔχῃ ἔργα⸃, νεκρά ἐστιν καθʼ ἑαυτήν.
verses.translit: outos kai e pistis, ean me ehe erga, nekra estin kath' eaytin.
verses.translation: Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.

verses.original: Ἀλλʼ ἐρεῖ τις· Σὺ πίστιν ἔχεις κἀγὼ ἔργα ἔχω. δεῖξόν μοι τὴν πίστιν σου ⸀χωρὶς τῶν ⸀ἔργων, κἀγώ ⸂σοι δείξω⸃ ἐκ τῶν ἔργων μου τὴν ⸀πίστιν.
verses.translit: All' erei tis* Su pistin eheis kago erga eho. deixon moi ten pistin soy horis ton ergon, kago soi deixo ek ton ergon moy ten pistin.
verses.translation: Yea, a man may say, Thou hast faith, and I have works: shew me thy faith without thy works, and I will shew thee my faith by my works.

verses.original: σὺ πιστεύεις ὅτι ⸂εἷς ἐστιν ὁ θεός⸃; καλῶς ποιεῖς· καὶ τὰ δαιμόνια πιστεύουσιν καὶ φρίσσουσιν.
verses.translit: su pisteyeis oti eis estin o theos? kalos poieis* kai ta daimonia pisteyoysin kai frissoysin.
verses.translation: Thou believest that there is one God; thou doest well: the devils also believe, and tremble.

verses.original: θέλεις δὲ γνῶναι, ὦ ἄνθρωπε κενέ, ὅτι ἡ πίστις χωρὶς τῶν ἔργων ⸀ἀργή ἐστιν;
verses.translit: theleis de gnonai, o anthrope kene, oti e pistis horis ton ergon argi estin;
verses.translation: But wilt thou know, O vain man, that faith without works is dead?

verses.original: Ἀβραὰμ ὁ πατὴρ ἡμῶν οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων ἐδικαιώθη, ἀνενέγκας Ἰσαὰκ τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον;
verses.translit: Avraam o pater emon ouk ex ergon edikaiothi, anenegkas Isaak ton yion autou epi to thysiastirion;
verses.translation: Was not Abraham our father justified by works, when he had offered Isaac his son upon the altar?

verses.original: βλέπεις ὅτι ἡ πίστις συνήργει τοῖς ἔργοις αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἔργων ἡ πίστις ἐτελειώθη,
verses.translit: vlepeis oti e pistis synirgei tois ergois autou kai ek ton ergon e pistis eteleiothi,
verses.translation: Seest thou how faith wrought with his works, and by works was faith made perfect?

verses.original: καὶ ἐπληρώθη ἡ γραφὴ ἡ λέγουσα· Ἐπίστευσεν δὲ Ἀβραὰμ τῷ θεῷ, καὶ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην, καὶ φίλος θεοῦ ἐκλήθη.
verses.translit: kai eplirothi e grafe e legoysa* Episteysen de Avraam to theo, kai elogisthi auto eis dikaiosynin, kai filos theou eklithi.
verses.translation: And the scripture was fulfilled which saith, Abraham believed God, and it was imputed unto him for righteousness: and he was called the Friend of God.

verses.original: ⸀ὁρᾶτε ὅτι ἐξ ἔργων δικαιοῦται ἄνθρωπος καὶ οὐκ ἐκ πίστεως μόνον.
verses.translit: orate oti ex ergon dikaioutai anthropos kai ouk ek pisteos monon.
verses.translation: Ye see then how that by works a man is justified, and not by faith only.

verses.original: ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ Ῥαὰβ ἡ πόρνη οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων ἐδικαιώθη, ὑποδεξαμένη τοὺς ἀγγέλους καὶ ἑτέρᾳ ὁδῷ ἐκβαλοῦσα;
verses.translit: omoios de kai Raav e porni ouk ex ergon edikaiothi, upodexameni tous aggeloys kai etera odo ekvalousa;
verses.translation: Likewise also was not Rahab the harlot justified by works, when she had received the messengers, and had sent them out another way?

verses.original: ὥσπερ ⸀γὰρ τὸ σῶμα χωρὶς πνεύματος νεκρόν ἐστιν, οὕτως καὶ ἡ πίστις ⸀χωρὶς ἔργων νεκρά ἐστιν.
verses.translit: osper gar to soma horis pneymatos nekron estin, outos kai e pistis horis ergon nekra estin.
verses.translation: For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.

verses.original: Μὴ πολλοὶ διδάσκαλοι γίνεσθε, ἀδελφοί μου, εἰδότες ὅτι μεῖζον κρίμα λημψόμεθα·
verses.translit: Me polloi didaskaloi ginesthe, adelfoi moy, eidotes oti meizon krima limpsometha*
verses.translation: My brethren, be not many masters, knowing that we shall receive the greater condemnation.

verses.original: πολλὰ γὰρ πταίομεν ἅπαντες. εἴ τις ἐν λόγῳ οὐ πταίει, οὗτος τέλειος ἀνήρ, δυνατὸς χαλιναγωγῆσαι καὶ ὅλον τὸ σῶμα.
verses.translit: polla gar ptaiomen apantes. ei tis en logo ou ptaiei, outos teleios anir, dynatos halinagogesai kai olon to soma.
verses.translation: For in many things we offend all. If any man offend not in word, the same is a perfect man, and able also to bridle the whole body.

verses.original: ⸂εἰ δὲ⸃ τῶν ἵππων τοὺς χαλινοὺς εἰς τὰ στόματα βάλλομεν ⸀εἰς τὸ πείθεσθαι αὐτοὺς ἡμῖν, καὶ ὅλον τὸ σῶμα αὐτῶν μετάγομεν.
verses.translit: ei de ton ippon tous halinous eis ta stomata vallomen eis to peithesthai autous emin, kai olon to soma auton metagomen.
verses.translation: Behold, we put bits in the horses’ mouths, that they may obey us; and we turn about their whole body.

verses.original: ἰδοὺ καὶ τὰ πλοῖα, τηλικαῦτα ὄντα καὶ ὑπὸ ⸂ἀνέμων σκληρῶν⸃ ἐλαυνόμενα, μετάγεται ὑπὸ ἐλαχίστου πηδαλίου ὅπου ⸂ἡ ὁρμὴ τοῦ εὐθύνοντος βούλεται⸃·
verses.translit: idou kai ta ploia, tilikauta onta kai upo anemon skliron elaynomena, metagetai upo elahistoy pidalioy opoy e orme tou euthynontos voyletai*
verses.translation: Behold also the ships, which though they be so great, and are driven of fierce winds, yet are they turned about with a very small helm, whithersoever the governor listeth.

verses.original: οὕτως καὶ ἡ γλῶσσα μικρὸν μέλος ἐστὶν καὶ ⸂μεγάλα αὐχεῖ⸃. Ἰδοὺ ⸀ἡλίκον πῦρ ἡλίκην ὕλην ἀνάπτει·
verses.translit: outos kai e glossa mikron melos estin kai megala auhei. Idou elikon pur elikin ulin anaptei*
verses.translation: Even so the tongue is a little member, and boasteth great things. Behold, how great a matter a little fire kindleth!

verses.original: καὶ ἡ γλῶσσα πῦρ, ὁ κόσμος τῆς ⸀ἀδικίας ἡ γλῶσσα καθίσταται ἐν τοῖς μέλεσιν ἡμῶν, ἡ σπιλοῦσα ὅλον τὸ σῶμα καὶ φλογίζουσα τὸν τροχὸν τῆς γενέσεως καὶ φλογιζομένη ὑπὸ τῆς γεέννης.
verses.translit: kai e glossa pur, o kosmos tes adikias e glossa kathistatai en tois melesin emon, e spilousa olon to soma kai flogizoysa ton trohon tes geneseos kai flogizomeni upo tes geennis.
verses.translation: And the tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity: so is the tongue among our members, that it defileth the whole body, and setteth on fire the course of nature; and it is set on fire of hell.

verses.original: πᾶσα γὰρ φύσις θηρίων τε καὶ πετεινῶν ἑρπετῶν τε καὶ ἐναλίων δαμάζεται καὶ δεδάμασται τῇ φύσει τῇ ἀνθρωπίνῃ·
verses.translit: pasa gar fysis thirion te kai peteinon erpeton te kai enalion damazetai kai dedamastai te fysei te anthropine*
verses.translation: For every kind of beasts, and of birds, and of serpents, and of things in the sea, is tamed, and hath been tamed of mankind:

verses.original: τὴν δὲ γλῶσσαν οὐδεὶς ⸂δαμάσαι δύναται ἀνθρώπων⸃· ⸀ἀκατάστατον κακόν, μεστὴ ἰοῦ θανατηφόρου.
verses.translit: ten de glossan oudeis damasai dynatai anthropon* akatastaton kakon, meste iou thanatiforoy.
verses.translation: But the tongue can no man tame; it is an unruly evil, full of deadly poison.

verses.original: ἐν αὐτῇ εὐλογοῦμεν τὸν ⸀κύριον καὶ πατέρα, καὶ ἐν αὐτῇ καταρώμεθα τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τοὺς καθʼ ὁμοίωσιν θεοῦ γεγονότας·
verses.translit: en aute eulogoumen ton kyrion kai patera, kai en aute katarometha tous anthropoys tous kath' omoiosin theou gegonotas*
verses.translation: Therewith bless we God, even the Father; and therewith curse we men, which are made after the similitude of God.

verses.original: ἐκ τοῦ αὐτοῦ στόματος ἐξέρχεται εὐλογία καὶ κατάρα. οὐ χρή, ἀδελφοί μου, ταῦτα οὕτως γίνεσθαι.
verses.translit: ek tou autou stomatos exerhetai eulogia kai katara. ou hri, adelfoi moy, tauta outos ginesthai.
verses.translation: Out of the same mouth proceedeth blessing and cursing. My brethren, these things ought not so to be.

verses.original: μήτι ἡ πηγὴ ἐκ τῆς αὐτῆς ὀπῆς βρύει τὸ γλυκὺ καὶ τὸ πικρόν;
verses.translit: miti e pige ek tes autes opes vryei to glyku kai to pikron;
verses.translation: Doth a fountain send forth at the same place sweet water and bitter?

verses.original: μὴ δύναται, ἀδελφοί μου, συκῆ ἐλαίας ποιῆσαι ἢ ἄμπελος σῦκα; ⸂οὔτε ἁλυκὸν⸃ γλυκὺ ποιῆσαι ὕδωρ.
verses.translit: me dynatai, adelfoi moy, syke elaias poiesai e ampelos suka; oute alykon glyku poiesai udor.
verses.translation: Can the fig tree, my brethren, bear olive berries? either a vine, figs? so can no fountain both yield salt water and fresh.

verses.original: Τίς σοφὸς καὶ ἐπιστήμων ἐν ὑμῖν; δειξάτω ἐκ τῆς καλῆς ἀναστροφῆς τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ ἐν πραΰτητι σοφίας.
verses.translit: Tis sofos kai epistimon en umin; deixato ek tes kales anastrofes ta erga autou en praytiti sofias.
verses.translation: Who is a wise man and endued with knowledge among you? let him shew out of a good conversation his works with meekness of wisdom.

verses.original: εἰ δὲ ζῆλον πικρὸν ἔχετε καὶ ἐριθείαν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ ὑμῶν, μὴ κατακαυχᾶσθε καὶ ψεύδεσθε κατὰ τῆς ἀληθείας.
verses.translit: ei de zelon pikron ehete kai eritheian en te kardia umon, me katakayhasthe kai pseydesthe kata tes alitheias.
verses.translation: But if ye have bitter envying and strife in your hearts, glory not, and lie not against the truth.

verses.original: οὐκ ἔστιν αὕτη ἡ σοφία ἄνωθεν κατερχομένη, ἀλλὰ ἐπίγειος, ψυχική, δαιμονιώδης·
verses.translit: ouk estin auti e sofia anothen katerhomeni, alla epigeios, psyhiki, daimoniodis*
verses.translation: This wisdom descendeth not from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish.

verses.original: ὅπου γὰρ ζῆλος καὶ ἐριθεία, ἐκεῖ ἀκαταστασία καὶ πᾶν φαῦλον πρᾶγμα.
verses.translit: opoy gar zelos kai eritheia, ekei akatastasia kai pan faulon pragma.
verses.translation: For where envying and strife is , there is confusion and every evil work.

verses.original: ἡ δὲ ἄνωθεν σοφία πρῶτον μὲν ἁγνή ἐστιν, ἔπειτα εἰρηνική, ἐπιεικής, εὐπειθής, μεστὴ ἐλέους καὶ καρπῶν ἀγαθῶν, ⸀ἀδιάκριτος, ἀνυπόκριτος·
verses.translit: e de anothen sofia proton men agni estin, epeita eiriniki, epieikis, eupeithis, meste eleoys kai karpon agathon, adiakritos, anypokritos*
verses.translation: But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, and easy to be intreated, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy.

verses.original: καρπὸς ⸀δὲ δικαιοσύνης ἐν εἰρήνῃ σπείρεται τοῖς ποιοῦσιν εἰρήνην.
verses.translit: karpos de dikaiosynis en eirine speiretai tois poiousin eirinin.
verses.translation: And the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace of them that make peace.

verses.original: Πόθεν πόλεμοι καὶ ⸀πόθεν μάχαι ἐν ὑμῖν; οὐκ ἐντεῦθεν, ἐκ τῶν ἡδονῶν ὑμῶν τῶν στρατευομένων ἐν τοῖς μέλεσιν ὑμῶν;
verses.translit: Pothen polemoi kai pothen mahai en umin; ouk enteuthen, ek ton edonon umon ton strateyomenon en tois melesin umon;
verses.translation: From whence come wars and fightings among you? come they not hence, even of your lusts that war in your members?

verses.original: ἐπιθυμεῖτε, καὶ οὐκ ἔχετε· φονεύετε καὶ ζηλοῦτε, καὶ οὐ δύνασθε ἐπιτυχεῖν· μάχεσθε καὶ πολεμεῖτε. οὐκ ἔχετε διὰ τὸ μὴ αἰτεῖσθαι ὑμᾶς·
verses.translit: epithymeite, kai ouk ehete* foneyete kai ziloute, kai ou dynasthe epityhein* mahesthe kai polemeite. ouk ehete dia to me aiteisthai umas*
verses.translation: Ye lust, and have not: ye kill, and desire to have, and cannot obtain: ye fight and war, yet ye have not, because ye ask not.

verses.original: αἰτεῖτε καὶ οὐ λαμβάνετε, διότι κακῶς αἰτεῖσθε, ἵνα ἐν ταῖς ἡδοναῖς ὑμῶν δαπανήσητε.
verses.translit: aiteite kai ou lamvanete, dioti kakos aiteisthe, ina en tais edonais umon dapanisite.
verses.translation: Ye ask, and receive not, because ye ask amiss, that ye may consume it upon your lusts.

verses.original: ⸀μοιχαλίδες, οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ἡ φιλία τοῦ κόσμου ἔχθρα τοῦ θεοῦ ἐστιν; ὃς ⸀ἐὰν οὖν βουληθῇ φίλος εἶναι τοῦ κόσμου, ἐχθρὸς τοῦ θεοῦ καθίσταται.
verses.translit: moihalides, ouk oidate oti e filia tou kosmoy ehthra tou theou estin; os ean oun voylithe filos einai tou kosmoy, ehthros tou theou kathistatai.
verses.translation: Ye adulterers and adulteresses, know ye not that the friendship of the world is enmity with God? whosoever therefore will be a friend of the world is the enemy of God.

verses.original: ἢ δοκεῖτε ὅτι κενῶς ἡ γραφὴ λέγει· Πρὸς φθόνον ἐπιποθεῖ τὸ πνεῦμα ὃ ⸀κατῴκισεν ἐν ἡμῖν;
verses.translit: e dokeite oti kenos e grafe legei* Pros fthonon epipothei to pneuma o katokisen en emin?
verses.translation: Do ye think that the scripture saith in vain, The spirit that dwelleth in us lusteth to envy?

verses.original: μείζονα δὲ δίδωσιν χάριν· διὸ λέγει· Ὁ θεὸς ὑπερηφάνοις ἀντιτάσσεται ταπεινοῖς δὲ δίδωσιν χάριν.
verses.translit: meizona de didosin harin* dio legei* O theos uperifanois antitassetai tapeinois de didosin harin.
verses.translation: But he giveth more grace. Wherefore he saith, God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble.

verses.original: ὑποτάγητε οὖν τῷ θεῷ· ἀντίστητε δὲ τῷ διαβόλῳ, καὶ φεύξεται ἀφʼ ὑμῶν·
verses.translit: upotagite oun to theo* antistite de to diavolo, kai feyxetai af' umon*
verses.translation: Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.

verses.original: ἐγγίσατε τῷ θεῷ, καὶ ⸀ἐγγιεῖ ὑμῖν. καθαρίσατε χεῖρας, ἁμαρτωλοί, καὶ ἁγνίσατε καρδίας, δίψυχοι.
verses.translit: eggisate to theo, kai eggiei umin. katharisate heiras, amartoloi, kai agnisate kardias, dipsyhoi.
verses.translation: Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.

verses.original: ταλαιπωρήσατε καὶ πενθήσατε καὶ κλαύσατε· ὁ γέλως ὑμῶν εἰς πένθος ⸀μετατραπήτω καὶ ἡ χαρὰ εἰς κατήφειαν·
verses.translit: talaiporisate kai penthisate kai klaysate* o gelos umon eis penthos metatrapito kai e hara eis katifeian*
verses.translation: Be afflicted, and mourn, and weep: let your laughter be turned to mourning, and your joy to heaviness.

verses.original: ταπεινώθητε ἐνώπιον ⸀κυρίου, καὶ ὑψώσει ὑμᾶς.
verses.translit: tapeinothite enopion kyrioy, kai upsosei umas.
verses.translation: Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he shall lift you up.

verses.original: Μὴ καταλαλεῖτε ἀλλήλων, ἀδελφοί· ὁ καταλαλῶν ἀδελφοῦ ⸀ἢ κρίνων τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ καταλαλεῖ νόμου καὶ κρίνει νόμον· εἰ δὲ νόμον κρίνεις, οὐκ εἶ ποιητὴς νόμου ἀλλὰ κριτής.
verses.translit: Me katalaleite allilon, adelfoi* o katalalon adelfou e krinon ton adelfon autou katalalei nomoy kai krinei nomon* ei de nomon krineis, ouk ei poiites nomoy alla kritis.
verses.translation: Speak not evil one of another, brethren. He that speaketh evil of his brother, and judgeth his brother, speaketh evil of the law, and judgeth the law: but if thou judge the law, thou art not a doer of the law, but a judge.

verses.original: εἷς ⸀ἐστιν νομοθέτης ⸂καὶ κριτής⸃, ὁ δυνάμενος σῶσαι καὶ ἀπολέσαι· σὺ δὲ τίς εἶ, ⸂ὁ κρίνων⸃ τὸν ⸀πλησίον;
verses.translit: eis estin nomothetis kai kritis, o dynamenos sosai kai apolesai* su de tis ei, o krinon ton plision;
verses.translation: There is one lawgiver, who is able to save and to destroy: who art thou that judgest another?

verses.original: Ἄγε νῦν οἱ λέγοντες· Σήμερον ⸀ἢ αὔριον ⸀πορευσόμεθα εἰς τήνδε τὴν πόλιν καὶ ⸀ποιήσομεν ἐκεῖ ⸀ἐνιαυτὸν καὶ ⸀ἐμπορευσόμεθα καὶ ⸀κερδήσομεν·
verses.translit: Age nun oi legontes* Simeron e aurion poreysometha eis tinde ten polin kai poiisomen ekei eniayton kai emporeysometha kai kerdisomen*
verses.translation: Go to now, ye that say, To day or to morrow we will go into such a city, and continue there a year, and buy and sell, and get gain:

verses.original: οἵτινες οὐκ ἐπίστασθε ⸀τὸ τῆς αὔριον ⸀ποία ἡ ζωὴ ὑμῶν· ἀτμὶς γάρ ⸀ἐστε ⸀ἡ πρὸς ὀλίγον φαινομένη, ⸀ἔπειτα καὶ ἀφανιζομένη·
verses.translit: oitines ouk epistasthe to tes aurion poia e zoe umon* atmis gar este e pros oligon fainomeni, epeita kai afanizomeni*
verses.translation: Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away.

verses.original: ἀντὶ τοῦ λέγειν ὑμᾶς· Ἐὰν ὁ κύριος ⸀θελήσῃ, καὶ ⸀ζήσομεν καὶ ⸀ποιήσομεν τοῦτο ἢ ἐκεῖνο.
verses.translit: anti tou legein umas* Ean o kyrios thelise, kai zisomen kai poiisomen touto e ekeino.
verses.translation: For that ye ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall live, and do this, or that.

verses.original: νῦν δὲ καυχᾶσθε ἐν ταῖς ἀλαζονείαις ὑμῶν· πᾶσα καύχησις τοιαύτη πονηρά ἐστιν.
verses.translit: nun de kayhasthe en tais alazoneiais umon* pasa kayhisis toiayti ponira estin.
verses.translation: But now ye rejoice in your boastings: all such rejoicing is evil.

verses.original: εἰδότι οὖν καλὸν ποιεῖν καὶ μὴ ποιοῦντι, ἁμαρτία αὐτῷ ἐστιν.
verses.translit: eidoti oun kalon poiein kai me poiounti, amartia auto estin.
verses.translation: Therefore to him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin.

verses.original: Ἄγε νῦν οἱ πλούσιοι, κλαύσατε ὀλολύζοντες ἐπὶ ταῖς ταλαιπωρίαις ὑμῶν ταῖς ἐπερχομέναις.
verses.translit: Age nun oi ploysioi, klaysate ololyzontes epi tais talaiporiais umon tais eperhomenais.
verses.translation: Go to now, ye rich men, weep and howl for your miseries that shall come upon you .

verses.original: ὁ πλοῦτος ὑμῶν σέσηπεν, καὶ τὰ ἱμάτια ὑμῶν σητόβρωτα γέγονεν,
verses.translit: o ploutos umon sesipen, kai ta imatia umon sitovrota gegonen,
verses.translation: Your riches are corrupted, and your garments are motheaten.

verses.original: ὁ χρυσὸς ὑμῶν καὶ ὁ ἄργυρος κατίωται, καὶ ὁ ἰὸς αὐτῶν εἰς μαρτύριον ὑμῖν ἔσται καὶ φάγεται τὰς σάρκας ὑμῶν· ὡς πῦρ ἐθησαυρίσατε ἐν ἐσχάταις ἡμέραις.
verses.translit: o hrysos umon kai o argyros katiotai, kai o ios auton eis martyrion umin estai kai fagetai tas sarkas umon* os pur ethisayrisate en eshatais emerais.
verses.translation: Your gold and silver is cankered; and the rust of them shall be a witness against you, and shall eat your flesh as it were fire. Ye have heaped treasure together for the last days.

verses.original: ἰδοὺ ὁ μισθὸς τῶν ἐργατῶν τῶν ἀμησάντων τὰς χώρας ὑμῶν ὁ ⸀ἀφυστερημένος ἀφʼ ὑμῶν κράζει, καὶ αἱ βοαὶ τῶν θερισάντων εἰς τὰ ὦτα Κυρίου Σαβαὼθ ⸀εἰσεληλύθασιν·
verses.translit: idou o misthos ton ergaton ton amisanton tas horas umon o afysterimenos af' umon krazei, kai ai voai ton therisanton eis ta ota Kyrioy Savaoth eiselilythasin*
verses.translation: Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of the Lord of sabaoth.

verses.original: ἐτρυφήσατε ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ἐσπαταλήσατε, ἐθρέψατε τὰς καρδίας ⸀ὑμῶν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ σφαγῆς.
verses.translit: etryfisate epi tes ges kai espatalisate, ethrepsate tas kardias umon en emera sfages.
verses.translation: Ye have lived in pleasure on the earth, and been wanton; ye have nourished your hearts, as in a day of slaughter.

verses.original: κατεδικάσατε, ἐφονεύσατε τὸν δίκαιον. οὐκ ἀντιτάσσεται ὑμῖν;
verses.translit: katedikasate, efoneysate ton dikaion. ouk antitassetai umin?
verses.translation: Ye have condemned and killed the just; and he doth not resist you.

verses.original: Μακροθυμήσατε οὖν, ἀδελφοί, ἕως τῆς παρουσίας τοῦ κυρίου. ἰδοὺ ὁ γεωργὸς ἐκδέχεται τὸν τίμιον καρπὸν τῆς γῆς, μακροθυμῶν ἐπʼ ⸀αὐτῷ ἕως ⸀λάβῃ πρόϊμον καὶ ὄψιμον.
verses.translit: Makrothymisate oun, adelfoi, eos tes paroysias tou kyrioy. idou o georgos ekdehetai ton timion karpon tes ges, makrothymon ep' auto eos lave proimon kai opsimon.
verses.translation: Be patient therefore, brethren, unto the coming of the Lord. Behold, the husbandman waiteth for the precious fruit of the earth, and hath long patience for it, until he receive the early and latter rain.

verses.original: μακροθυμήσατε καὶ ὑμεῖς, στηρίξατε τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν, ὅτι ἡ παρουσία τοῦ κυρίου ἤγγικεν.
verses.translit: makrothymisate kai umeis, stirixate tas kardias umon, oti e paroysia tou kyrioy eggiken.
verses.translation: Be ye also patient; stablish your hearts: for the coming of the Lord draweth nigh.

verses.original: μὴ στενάζετε, ⸂ἀδελφοί, κατʼ ἀλλήλων⸃, ἵνα μὴ κριθῆτε· ἰδοὺ ὁ κριτὴς πρὸ τῶν θυρῶν ἕστηκεν.
verses.translit: me stenazete, adelfoi, kat' allilon, ina me krithete* idou o krites pro ton thyron estiken.
verses.translation: Grudge not one against another, brethren, lest ye be condemned: behold, the judge standeth before the door.

verses.original: ὑπόδειγμα λάβετε, ⸀ἀδελφοί, τῆς κακοπαθίας καὶ τῆς μακροθυμίας τοὺς προφήτας, οἳ ἐλάλησαν ⸀ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι κυρίου.
verses.translit: upodeigma lavete, adelfoi, tes kakopathias kai tes makrothymias tous profitas, oi elalisan en to onomati kyrioy.
verses.translation: Take, my brethren, the prophets, who have spoken in the name of the Lord, for an example of suffering affliction, and of patience.

verses.original: ἰδοὺ μακαρίζομεν τοὺς ⸀ὑπομείναντας· τὴν ὑπομονὴν Ἰὼβ ἠκούσατε, καὶ τὸ τέλος κυρίου ⸀εἴδετε, ὅτι πολύσπλαγχνός ἐστιν ⸂ὁ κύριος⸃ καὶ οἰκτίρμων.
verses.translit: idou makarizomen tous upomeinantas* ten upomonen Iov ekoysate, kai to telos kyrioy eidete, oti polysplaghnos estin o kyrios kai oiktirmon.
verses.translation: Behold, we count them happy which endure. Ye have heard of the patience of Job, and have seen the end of the Lord; that the Lord is very pitiful, and of tender mercy.

verses.original: Πρὸ πάντων δέ, ἀδελφοί μου, μὴ ὀμνύετε, μήτε τὸν οὐρανὸν μήτε τὴν γῆν μήτε ἄλλον τινὰ ὅρκον· ἤτω δὲ ὑμῶν τὸ Ναὶ ναὶ καὶ τὸ Οὒ οὔ, ἵνα μὴ ⸂ὑπὸ κρίσιν⸃ πέσητε.
verses.translit: Pro panton de, adelfoi moy, me omnyete, mite ton ouranon mite ten gen mite allon tina orkon* eto de umon to Nai nai kai to Ou ou, ina me upo krisin pesite.
verses.translation: But above all things, my brethren, swear not, neither by heaven, neither by the earth, neither by any other oath: but let your yea be yea; and your nay, nay; lest ye fall into condemnation.

verses.original: Κακοπαθεῖ τις ἐν ὑμῖν; προσευχέσθω· εὐθυμεῖ τις; ψαλλέτω.
verses.translit: Kakopathei tis en umin? proseyhestho* euthymei tis? psalleto.
verses.translation: Is any among you afflicted? let him pray. Is any merry? let him sing psalms.

verses.original: ἀσθενεῖ τις ἐν ὑμῖν; προσκαλεσάσθω τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους τῆς ἐκκλησίας, καὶ προσευξάσθωσαν ἐπʼ αὐτὸν ἀλείψαντες ⸀αὐτὸν ἐλαίῳ ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ κυρίου·
verses.translit: asthenei tis en umin? proskalesastho tous presvyteroys tes ekklisias, kai proseyxasthosan ep' auton aleipsantes auton elaio en to onomati tou kyrioy*
verses.translation: Is any sick among you? let him call for the elders of the church; and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord:

verses.original: καὶ ἡ εὐχὴ τῆς πίστεως σώσει τὸν κάμνοντα, καὶ ἐγερεῖ αὐτὸν ὁ κύριος· κἂν ἁμαρτίας ᾖ πεποιηκώς, ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: kai e euhe tes pisteos sosei ton kamnonta, kai egerei auton o kyrios* kan amartias e pepoiikos, afethisetai auto.
verses.translation: And the prayer of faith shall save the sick, and the Lord shall raise him up; and if he have committed sins, they shall be forgiven him.

verses.original: ἐξομολογεῖσθε ⸀οὖν ἀλλήλοις ⸂τὰς ἁμαρτίας⸃ καὶ ⸀εὔχεσθε ὑπὲρ ἀλλήλων, ὅπως ἰαθῆτε. πολὺ ἰσχύει δέησις δικαίου ἐνεργουμένη.
verses.translit: exomologeisthe oun allilois tas amartias kai euhesthe uper allilon, opos iathete. polu ishyei deisis dikaioy energoymeni.
verses.translation: Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.

verses.original: Ἠλίας ἄνθρωπος ἦν ὁμοιοπαθὴς ἡμῖν, καὶ προσευχῇ προσηύξατο τοῦ μὴ βρέξαι, καὶ οὐκ ἔβρεξεν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἐνιαυτοὺς τρεῖς καὶ μῆνας ἕξ·
verses.translit: Elias anthropos en omoiopathes emin, kai proseyhe prosiyxato tou me vrexai, kai ouk evrexen epi tes ges eniaytous treis kai menas ex*
verses.translation: Elias was a man subject to like passions as we are, and he prayed earnestly that it might not rain: and it rained not on the earth by the space of three years and six months.

verses.original: καὶ πάλιν προσηύξατο, καὶ ὁ οὐρανὸς ⸂ὑετὸν ἔδωκεν⸃ καὶ ἡ γῆ ἐβλάστησεν τὸν καρπὸν αὐτῆς.
verses.translit: kai palin prosiyxato, kai o ouranos ueton edoken kai e ge evlastisen ton karpon autes.
verses.translation: And he prayed again, and the heaven gave rain, and the earth brought forth her fruit.

verses.original: Ἀδελφοί ⸀μου, ἐάν τις ἐν ὑμῖν πλανηθῇ ἀπὸ τῆς ἀληθείας καὶ ἐπιστρέψῃ τις αὐτόν,
verses.translit: Adelfoi moy, ean tis en umin planithe apo tes alitheias kai epistrepse tis auton,
verses.translation: Brethren, if any of you do err from the truth, and one convert him;

verses.original: ⸀γινωσκέτω ὅτι ὁ ἐπιστρέψας ἁμαρτωλὸν ἐκ πλάνης ὁδοῦ αὐτοῦ σώσει ψυχὴν ⸀αὐτοῦ ἐκ θανάτου καὶ καλύψει πλῆθος ἁμαρτιῶν.
verses.translit: ginosketo oti o epistrepsas amartolon ek planis odou autou sosei psyhen autou ek thanatoy kai kalypsei plethos amartion.
verses.translation: Let him know, that he which converteth the sinner from the error of his way shall save a soul from death, and shall hide a multitude of sins.

verses.original: Πέτρος ἀπόστολος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐκλεκτοῖς παρεπιδήμοις διασπορᾶς Πόντου, Γαλατίας, Καππαδοκίας, Ἀσίας, καὶ Βιθυνίας,
verses.translit: Petros apostolos Iisou Hristou eklektois parepidimois diasporas Pontoy, Galatias, Kappadokias, Asias, kai Vithynias,
verses.translation: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,

verses.original: κατὰ πρόγνωσιν θεοῦ πατρός, ἐν ἁγιασμῷ πνεύματος, εἰς ὑπακοὴν καὶ ῥαντισμὸν αἵματος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ· χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη πληθυνθείη.
verses.translit: kata prognosin theou patros, en agiasmo pneymatos, eis upakoen kai Rantismon aimatos Iisou Hristou* haris umin kai eirini plithyntheii.
verses.translation: Elect according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, through sanctification of the Spirit, unto obedience and sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ: Grace unto you, and peace, be multiplied.

verses.original: Εὐλογητὸς ὁ θεὸς καὶ πατὴρ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὁ κατὰ τὸ πολὺ αὐτοῦ ἔλεος ἀναγεννήσας ἡμᾶς εἰς ἐλπίδα ζῶσαν διʼ ἀναστάσεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐκ νεκρῶν,
verses.translit: Eulogitos o theos kai pater tou kyrioy emon Iisou Hristou, o kata to polu autou eleos anagennisas emas eis elpida zosan di' anastaseos Iisou Hristou ek nekron,
verses.translation: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, which according to his abundant mercy hath begotten us again unto a lively hope by the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,

verses.original: εἰς κληρονομίαν ἄφθαρτον καὶ ἀμίαντον καὶ ἀμάραντον, τετηρημένην ἐν οὐρανοῖς εἰς ὑμᾶς
verses.translit: eis klironomian aftharton kai amianton kai amaranton, tetirimenin en ouranois eis umas
verses.translation: To an inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and that fadeth not away, reserved in heaven for you,

verses.original: τοὺς ἐν δυνάμει θεοῦ φρουρουμένους διὰ πίστεως εἰς σωτηρίαν ἑτοίμην ἀποκαλυφθῆναι ἐν καιρῷ ἐσχάτῳ.
verses.translit: tous en dynamei theou froyroymenoys dia pisteos eis sotirian etoimin apokalyfthenai en kairo eshato.
verses.translation: Who are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.

verses.original: ἐν ᾧ ἀγαλλιᾶσθε, ὀλίγον ἄρτι εἰ ⸀δέον ⸀λυπηθέντες ἐν ποικίλοις πειρασμοῖς,
verses.translit: en o agalliasthe, oligon arti ei deon lypithentes en poikilois peirasmois,
verses.translation: Wherein ye greatly rejoice, though now for a season, if need be, ye are in heaviness through manifold temptations:

verses.original: ἵνα τὸ δοκίμιον ὑμῶν τῆς πίστεως ⸀πολυτιμότερον χρυσίου τοῦ ἀπολλυμένου διὰ πυρὸς δὲ δοκιμαζομένου εὑρεθῇ εἰς ἔπαινον καὶ ⸂δόξαν καὶ τιμὴν⸃ ἐν ἀποκαλύψει Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
verses.translit: ina to dokimion umon tes pisteos polytimoteron hrysioy tou apollymenoy dia pyros de dokimazomenoy eurethe eis epainon kai doxan kai timen en apokalypsei Iisou Hristou.
verses.translation: That the trial of your faith, being much more precious than of gold that perisheth, though it be tried with fire, might be found unto praise and honour and glory at the appearing of Jesus Christ:

verses.original: ὃν οὐκ ⸀ἰδόντες ἀγαπᾶτε, εἰς ὃν ἄρτι μὴ ὁρῶντες πιστεύοντες δὲ ⸀ἀγαλλιᾶσθε χαρᾷ ἀνεκλαλήτῳ καὶ δεδοξασμένῃ,
verses.translit: on ouk idontes agapate, eis on arti me orontes pisteyontes de agalliasthe hara aneklalito kai dedoxasmene,
verses.translation: Whom having not seen, ye love; in whom, though now ye see him not, yet believing, ye rejoice with joy unspeakable and full of glory:

verses.original: κομιζόμενοι τὸ τέλος τῆς πίστεως ⸀ὑμῶν σωτηρίαν ψυχῶν.
verses.translit: komizomenoi to telos tes pisteos umon sotirian psyhon.
verses.translation: Receiving the end of your faith, even the salvation of your souls.

verses.original: Περὶ ἧς σωτηρίας ἐξεζήτησαν καὶ ἐξηραύνησαν προφῆται οἱ περὶ τῆς εἰς ὑμᾶς χάριτος προφητεύσαντες,
verses.translit: Peri es sotirias exezitisan kai exiraynisan profetai oi peri tes eis umas haritos profiteysantes,
verses.translation: Of which salvation the prophets have enquired and searched diligently, who prophesied of the grace that should come unto you:

verses.original: ἐραυνῶντες εἰς τίνα ἢ ποῖον καιρὸν ἐδήλου τὸ ἐν αὐτοῖς πνεῦμα Χριστοῦ προμαρτυρόμενον τὰ εἰς Χριστὸν παθήματα καὶ τὰς μετὰ ταῦτα δόξας·
verses.translit: eraynontes eis tina e poion kairon ediloy to en autois pneuma Hristou promartyromenon ta eis Hriston pathimata kai tas meta tauta doxas*
verses.translation: Searching what, or what manner of time the Spirit of Christ which was in them did signify, when it testified beforehand the sufferings of Christ, and the glory that should follow.

verses.original: οἷς ἀπεκαλύφθη ὅτι οὐχ ἑαυτοῖς ὑμῖν δὲ διηκόνουν αὐτά, ἃ νῦν ἀνηγγέλη ὑμῖν διὰ τῶν εὐαγγελισαμένων ⸀ὑμᾶς πνεύματι ἁγίῳ ἀποσταλέντι ἀπʼ οὐρανοῦ, εἰς ἃ ἐπιθυμοῦσιν ἄγγελοι παρακύψαι.
verses.translit: ois apekalyfthi oti ouh eaytois umin de diikonoyn auta, a nun aniggeli umin dia ton euaggelisamenon umas pneymati agio apostalenti ap' ouranou, eis a epithymousin aggeloi parakypsai.
verses.translation: Unto whom it was revealed, that not unto themselves, but unto us they did minister the things, which are now reported unto you by them that have preached the gospel unto you with the Holy Ghost sent down from heaven; which things the angels desire to look into.

verses.original: Διὸ ἀναζωσάμενοι τὰς ὀσφύας τῆς διανοίας ὑμῶν, νήφοντες τελείως, ἐλπίσατε ἐπὶ τὴν φερομένην ὑμῖν χάριν ἐν ἀποκαλύψει Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
verses.translit: Dio anazosamenoi tas osfyas tes dianoias umon, nifontes teleios, elpisate epi ten feromenin umin harin en apokalypsei Iisou Hristou.
verses.translation: Wherefore gird up the loins of your mind, be sober, and hope to the end for the grace that is to be brought unto you at the revelation of Jesus Christ;

verses.original: ὡς τέκνα ὑπακοῆς, μὴ συσχηματιζόμενοι ταῖς πρότερον ἐν τῇ ἀγνοίᾳ ὑμῶν ἐπιθυμίαις,
verses.translit: os tekna upakoes, me syshimatizomenoi tais proteron en te agnoia umon epithymiais,
verses.translation: As obedient children, not fashioning yourselves according to the former lusts in your ignorance:

verses.original: ἀλλὰ κατὰ τὸν καλέσαντα ὑμᾶς ἅγιον καὶ αὐτοὶ ἅγιοι ἐν πάσῃ ἀναστροφῇ γενήθητε,
verses.translit: alla kata ton kalesanta umas agion kai autoi agioi en pase anastrofe genithite,
verses.translation: But as he which hath called you is holy, so be ye holy in all manner of conversation;

verses.original: διότι γέγραπται ⸀ὅτι Ἅγιοι ⸀ἔσεσθε, ὅτι ἐγὼ ⸀ἅγιος.
verses.translit: dioti gegraptai oti Agioi esesthe, oti ego agios.
verses.translation: Because it is written, Be ye holy; for I am holy.

verses.original: Καὶ εἰ πατέρα ἐπικαλεῖσθε τὸν ἀπροσωπολήμπτως κρίνοντα κατὰ τὸ ἑκάστου ἔργον, ἐν φόβῳ τὸν τῆς παροικίας ὑμῶν χρόνον ἀναστράφητε·
verses.translit: Kai ei patera epikaleisthe ton aprosopolimptos krinonta kata to ekastoy ergon, en fovo ton tes paroikias umon hronon anastrafite*
verses.translation: And if ye call on the Father, who without respect of persons judgeth according to every man’s work, pass the time of your sojourning here in fear:

verses.original: εἰδότες ὅτι οὐ φθαρτοῖς, ἀργυρίῳ ἢ χρυσίῳ, ἐλυτρώθητε ἐκ τῆς ματαίας ὑμῶν ἀναστροφῆς πατροπαραδότου,
verses.translit: eidotes oti ou fthartois, argyrio e hrysio, elytrothite ek tes mataias umon anastrofes patroparadotoy,
verses.translation: Forasmuch as ye know that ye were not redeemed with corruptible things, as silver and gold, from your vain conversation received by tradition from your fathers;

verses.original: ἀλλὰ τιμίῳ αἵματι ὡς ἀμνοῦ ἀμώμου καὶ ἀσπίλου Χριστοῦ,
verses.translit: alla timio aimati os amnou amomoy kai aspiloy Hristou,
verses.translation: But with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot:

verses.original: προεγνωσμένου μὲν πρὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου, φανερωθέντος δὲ ἐπʼ ⸀ἐσχάτου τῶν χρόνων διʼ ὑμᾶς
verses.translit: proegnosmenoy men pro katavoles kosmoy, fanerothentos de ep' eshatoy ton hronon di' umas
verses.translation: Who verily was foreordained before the foundation of the world, but was manifest in these last times for you,

verses.original: τοὺς διʼ αὐτοῦ ⸀πιστοὺς εἰς θεὸν τὸν ἐγείραντα αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν καὶ δόξαν αὐτῷ δόντα, ὥστε τὴν πίστιν ὑμῶν καὶ ἐλπίδα εἶναι εἰς θεόν.
verses.translit: tous di' autou pistous eis theon ton egeiranta auton ek nekron kai doxan auto donta, oste ten pistin umon kai elpida einai eis theon.
verses.translation: Who by him do believe in God, that raised him up from the dead, and gave him glory; that your faith and hope might be in God.

verses.original: Τὰς ψυχὰς ὑμῶν ἡγνικότες ἐν τῇ ὑπακοῇ τῆς ⸀ἀληθείας εἰς φιλαδελφίαν ἀνυπόκριτον ⸀ἐκ καρδίας ἀλλήλους ἀγαπήσατε ἐκτενῶς,
verses.translit: Tas psyhas umon egnikotes en te upakoe tes alitheias eis filadelfian anypokriton ek kardias alliloys agapisate ektenos,
verses.translation: Seeing ye have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit unto unfeigned love of the brethren, see that ye love one another with a pure heart fervently:

verses.original: ἀναγεγεννημένοι οὐκ ἐκ σπορᾶς φθαρτῆς ἀλλὰ ἀφθάρτου, διὰ λόγου ζῶντος θεοῦ καὶ ⸀μένοντος·
verses.translit: anagegennimenoi ouk ek sporas fthartes alla afthartoy, dia logoy zontos theou kai menontos*
verses.translation: Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever.

verses.original: διότι πᾶσα σὰρξ ὡς χόρτος, καὶ πᾶσα δόξα ⸀αὐτῆς ὡς ἄνθος χόρτου· ἐξηράνθη ὁ χόρτος, καὶ τὸ ⸀ἄνθος ἐξέπεσεν·
verses.translit: dioti pasa sarx os hortos, kai pasa doxa autes os anthos hortoy* exiranthi o hortos, kai to anthos exepesen*
verses.translation: For all flesh is as grass, and all the glory of man as the flower of grass. The grass withereth, and the flower thereof falleth away:

verses.original: τὸ δὲ ῥῆμα κυρίου μένει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα. τοῦτο δέ ἐστιν τὸ ῥῆμα τὸ εὐαγγελισθὲν εἰς ὑμᾶς.
verses.translit: to de Rema kyrioy menei eis ton aiona. touto de estin to Rema to euaggelisthen eis umas.
verses.translation: But the word of the Lord endureth for ever. And this is the word which by the gospel is preached unto you.

verses.original: Ἀποθέμενοι οὖν πᾶσαν κακίαν καὶ πάντα δόλον καὶ ⸀ὑποκρίσεις καὶ φθόνους καὶ πάσας καταλαλιάς,
verses.translit: Apothemenoi oun pasan kakian kai panta dolon kai upokriseis kai fthonoys kai pasas katalalias,
verses.translation: Wherefore laying aside all malice, and all guile, and hypocrisies, and envies, and all evil speakings,

verses.original: ὡς ἀρτιγέννητα βρέφη τὸ λογικὸν ἄδολον γάλα ἐπιποθήσατε, ἵνα ἐν αὐτῷ αὐξηθῆτε ⸂εἰς σωτηρίαν⸃,
verses.translit: os artigennita vrefi to logikon adolon gala epipothisate, ina en auto auxithete eis sotirian,
verses.translation: As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby:

verses.original: ⸀εἰ ἐγεύσασθε ὅτι χρηστὸς ὁ κύριος.
verses.translit: ei egeysasthe oti hristos o kyrios.
verses.translation: If so be ye have tasted that the Lord is gracious.

verses.original: Πρὸς ὃν προσερχόμενοι, λίθον ζῶντα, ὑπὸ ἀνθρώπων μὲν ἀποδεδοκιμασμένον παρὰ δὲ θεῷ ἐκλεκτὸν ἔντιμον
verses.translit: Pros on proserhomenoi, lithon zonta, upo anthropon men apodedokimasmenon para de theo eklekton entimon
verses.translation: To whom coming, as unto a living stone, disallowed indeed of men, but chosen of God, and precious,

verses.original: καὶ αὐτοὶ ὡς λίθοι ζῶντες οἰκοδομεῖσθε οἶκος πνευματικὸς ⸀εἰς ἱεράτευμα ἅγιον, ἀνενέγκαι πνευματικὰς θυσίας ⸀εὐπροσδέκτους θεῷ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ·
verses.translit: kai autoi os lithoi zontes oikodomeisthe oikos pneymatikos eis ierateyma agion, anenegkai pneymatikas thysias euprosdektoys theo dia Iisou Hristou*
verses.translation: Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ.

verses.original: διότι περιέχει ⸀ἐν γραφῇ· Ἰδοὺ τίθημι ἐν Σιὼν λίθον ⸂ἀκρογωνιαῖον ἐκλεκτὸν⸃ ἔντιμον, καὶ ὁ πιστεύων ἐπʼ αὐτῷ οὐ μὴ καταισχυνθῇ.
verses.translit: dioti periehei en grafe* Idou tithimi en Sion lithon akrogoniaion eklekton entimon, kai o pisteyon ep' auto ou me kataishynthe.
verses.translation: Wherefore also it is contained in the scripture, Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone, elect, precious: and he that believeth on him shall not be confounded.

verses.original: ὑμῖν οὖν ἡ τιμὴ τοῖς πιστεύουσιν· ⸀ἀπιστοῦσιν δὲ ⸀λίθος ὃν ἀπεδοκίμασαν οἱ οἰκοδομοῦντες οὗτος ἐγενήθη εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας
verses.translit: umin oun e time tois pisteyoysin* apistousin de lithos on apedokimasan oi oikodomountes outos egenithi eis kefalen gonias
verses.translation: Unto you therefore which believe he is precious: but unto them which be disobedient, the stone which the builders disallowed, the same is made the head of the corner,

verses.original: καὶ λίθος προσκόμματος καὶ πέτρα σκανδάλου· οἳ προσκόπτουσιν τῷ λόγῳ ἀπειθοῦντες· εἰς ὃ καὶ ἐτέθησαν.
verses.translit: kai lithos proskommatos kai petra skandaloy* oi proskoptoysin to logo apeithountes* eis o kai etethisan.
verses.translation: And a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offence, even to them which stumble at the word, being disobedient: whereunto also they were appointed.

verses.original: Ὑμεῖς δὲ γένος ἐκλεκτόν, βασίλειον ἱεράτευμα, ἔθνος ἅγιον, λαὸς εἰς περιποίησιν, ὅπως τὰς ἀρετὰς ἐξαγγείλητε τοῦ ἐκ σκότους ὑμᾶς καλέσαντος εἰς τὸ θαυμαστὸν αὐτοῦ φῶς·
verses.translit: Umeis de genos eklekton, vasileion ierateyma, ethnos agion, laos eis peripoiisin, opos tas aretas exaggeilite tou ek skotoys umas kalesantos eis to thaymaston autou fos*
verses.translation: But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light:

verses.original: οἵ ποτε οὐ λαὸς νῦν δὲ λαὸς θεοῦ, οἱ οὐκ ἠλεημένοι νῦν δὲ ἐλεηθέντες.
verses.translit: oi pote ou laos nun de laos theou, oi ouk eleimenoi nun de eleithentes.
verses.translation: Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: which had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy.

verses.original: Ἀγαπητοί, παρακαλῶ ὡς παροίκους καὶ παρεπιδήμους ἀπέχεσθαι τῶν σαρκικῶν ἐπιθυμιῶν, αἵτινες στρατεύονται κατὰ τῆς ψυχῆς·
verses.translit: Agapitoi, parakalo os paroikoys kai parepidimoys apehesthai ton sarkikon epithymion, aitines strateyontai kata tes psyhes*
verses.translation: Dearly beloved, I beseech you as strangers and pilgrims, abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul;

verses.original: τὴν ἀναστροφὴν ὑμῶν ⸂ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ἔχοντες καλήν⸃, ἵνα, ἐν ᾧ καταλαλοῦσιν ὑμῶν ὡς κακοποιῶν, ἐκ τῶν καλῶν ἔργων ⸀ἐποπτεύοντες δοξάσωσι τὸν θεὸν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ἐπισκοπῆς.
verses.translit: ten anastrofen umon en tois ethnesin ehontes kalin, ina, en o katalalousin umon os kakopoion, ek ton kalon ergon epopteyontes doxasosi ton theon en emera episkopes.
verses.translation: Having your conversation honest among the Gentiles: that, whereas they speak against you as evildoers, they may by your good works, which they shall behold, glorify God in the day of visitation.

verses.original: ⸀Ὑποτάγητε πάσῃ ἀνθρωπίνῃ κτίσει διὰ τὸν κύριον· εἴτε βασιλεῖ ὡς ὑπερέχοντι,
verses.translit: Upotagite pase anthropine ktisei dia ton kyrion* eite vasilei os uperehonti,
verses.translation: Submit yourselves to every ordinance of man for the Lord’s sake: whether it be to the king, as supreme;

verses.original: εἴτε ἡγεμόσιν ὡς διʼ αὐτοῦ πεμπομένοις εἰς ἐκδίκησιν κακοποιῶν ἔπαινον δὲ ἀγαθοποιῶν
verses.translit: eite egemosin os di' autou pempomenois eis ekdikisin kakopoion epainon de agathopoion
verses.translation: Or unto governors, as unto them that are sent by him for the punishment of evildoers, and for the praise of them that do well.

verses.original: (ὅτι οὕτως ἐστὶν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ, ἀγαθοποιοῦντας φιμοῦν τὴν τῶν ἀφρόνων ἀνθρώπων ἀγνωσίαν)·
verses.translit: (oti outos estin to thelima tou theou, agathopoiountas fimoun ten ton afronon anthropon agnosian)*
verses.translation: For so is the will of God, that with well doing ye may put to silence the ignorance of foolish men:

verses.original: ὡς ἐλεύθεροι, καὶ μὴ ὡς ἐπικάλυμμα ἔχοντες τῆς κακίας τὴν ἐλευθερίαν, ἀλλʼ ὡς ⸂θεοῦ δοῦλοι⸃.
verses.translit: os eleytheroi, kai me os epikalymma ehontes tes kakias ten eleytherian, all' os theou douloi.
verses.translation: As free, and not using your liberty for a cloke of maliciousness, but as the servants of God.

verses.original: πάντας τιμήσατε, τὴν ἀδελφότητα ⸀ἀγαπᾶτε, τὸν θεὸν φοβεῖσθε, τὸν βασιλέα τιμᾶτε.
verses.translit: pantas timisate, ten adelfotita agapate, ton theon foveisthe, ton vasilea timate.
verses.translation: Honour all men . Love the brotherhood. Fear God. Honour the king.

verses.original: Οἱ οἰκέται ὑποτασσόμενοι ἐν παντὶ φόβῳ τοῖς δεσπόταις, οὐ μόνον τοῖς ἀγαθοῖς καὶ ἐπιεικέσιν ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῖς σκολιοῖς.
verses.translit: Oi oiketai upotassomenoi en panti fovo tois despotais, ou monon tois agathois kai epieikesin alla kai tois skoliois.
verses.translation: Servants, be subject to your masters with all fear; not only to the good and gentle, but also to the froward.

verses.original: τοῦτο γὰρ χάρις εἰ διὰ συνείδησιν θεοῦ ὑποφέρει τις λύπας πάσχων ἀδίκως·
verses.translit: touto gar haris ei dia syneidisin theou upoferei tis lypas pashon adikos*
verses.translation: For this is thankworthy, if a man for conscience toward God endure grief, suffering wrongfully.

verses.original: ποῖον γὰρ κλέος εἰ ἁμαρτάνοντες καὶ κολαφιζόμενοι ὑπομενεῖτε; ἀλλʼ εἰ ἀγαθοποιοῦντες καὶ πάσχοντες ὑπομενεῖτε, τοῦτο χάρις παρὰ θεῷ.
verses.translit: poion gar kleos ei amartanontes kai kolafizomenoi upomeneite; all' ei agathopoiountes kai pashontes upomeneite, touto haris para theo.
verses.translation: For what glory is it , if, when ye be buffeted for your faults, ye shall take it patiently? but if, when ye do well, and suffer for it , ye take it patiently, this is acceptable with God.

verses.original: εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ ἐκλήθητε, ὅτι καὶ Χριστὸς ἔπαθεν ὑπὲρ ⸀ὑμῶν, ὑμῖν ὑπολιμπάνων ὑπογραμμὸν ἵνα ἐπακολουθήσητε τοῖς ἴχνεσιν αὐτοῦ·
verses.translit: eis touto gar eklithite, oti kai Hristos epathen uper umon, umin upolimpanon upogrammon ina epakoloythisite tois ihnesin autou*
verses.translation: For even hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps:

verses.original: ὃς ἁμαρτίαν οὐκ ἐποίησεν οὐδὲ εὑρέθη δόλος ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐτοῦ·
verses.translit: os amartian ouk epoiisen oude eurethi dolos en to stomati autou*
verses.translation: Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth:

verses.original: ὃς λοιδορούμενος οὐκ ἀντελοιδόρει, πάσχων οὐκ ἠπείλει, παρεδίδου δὲ τῷ κρίνοντι δικαίως·
verses.translit: os loidoroymenos ouk anteloidorei, pashon ouk epeilei, paredidoy de to krinonti dikaios*
verses.translation: Who, when he was reviled, reviled not again; when he suffered, he threatened not; but committed himself to him that judgeth righteously:

verses.original: ὃς τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν αὐτὸς ἀνήνεγκεν ἐν τῷ σώματι αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸ ξύλον, ἵνα ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις ἀπογενόμενοι τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ ζήσωμεν· οὗ τῷ ⸀μώλωπι ἰάθητε.
verses.translit: os tas amartias emon autos aninegken en to somati autou epi to xylon, ina tais amartiais apogenomenoi te dikaiosyne zisomen* ou to molopi iathite.
verses.translation: Who his own self bare our sins in his own body on the tree, that we, being dead to sins, should live unto righteousness: by whose stripes ye were healed.

verses.original: ἦτε γὰρ ὡς πρόβατα ⸀πλανώμενοι, ἀλλὰ ἐπεστράφητε νῦν ἐπὶ τὸν ποιμένα καὶ ἐπίσκοπον τῶν ψυχῶν ὑμῶν.
verses.translit: ete gar os provata planomenoi, alla epestrafite nun epi ton poimena kai episkopon ton psyhon umon.
verses.translation: For ye were as sheep going astray; but are now returned unto the Shepherd and Bishop of your souls.

verses.original: ⸀Ὁμοίως γυναῖκες ὑποτασσόμεναι τοῖς ἰδίοις ἀνδράσιν, ἵνα ⸀καὶ εἴ τινες ἀπειθοῦσιν τῷ λόγῳ διὰ τῆς τῶν γυναικῶν ἀναστροφῆς ἄνευ λόγου κερδηθήσονται
verses.translit: Omoios gynaikes upotassomenai tois idiois andrasin, ina kai ei tines apeithousin to logo dia tes ton gynaikon anastrofes aney logoy kerdithisontai
verses.translation: Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives;

verses.original: ἐποπτεύσαντες τὴν ἐν φόβῳ ἁγνὴν ἀναστροφὴν ὑμῶν.
verses.translit: epopteysantes ten en fovo agnen anastrofen umon.
verses.translation: While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear.

verses.original: ὧν ἔστω οὐχ ὁ ἔξωθεν ἐμπλοκῆς τριχῶν καὶ περιθέσεως χρυσίων ἢ ἐνδύσεως ἱματίων κόσμος,
verses.translit: on esto ouh o exothen emplokes trihon kai peritheseos hrysion e endyseos imation kosmos,
verses.translation: Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel;

verses.original: ἀλλʼ ὁ κρυπτὸς τῆς καρδίας ἄνθρωπος ἐν τῷ ἀφθάρτῳ τοῦ ⸂πραέως καὶ ἡσυχίου⸃ πνεύματος, ὅ ἐστιν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ πολυτελές.
verses.translit: all' o kryptos tes kardias anthropos en to aftharto tou praeos kai esyhioy pneymatos, o estin enopion tou theou polyteles.
verses.translation: But let it be the hidden man of the heart, in that which is not corruptible, even the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price.

verses.original: οὕτως γάρ ποτε καὶ αἱ ἅγιαι γυναῖκες αἱ ἐλπίζουσαι ⸀εἰς θεὸν ἐκόσμουν ἑαυτάς, ὑποτασσόμεναι τοῖς ἰδίοις ἀνδράσιν,
verses.translit: outos gar pote kai ai agiai gynaikes ai elpizoysai eis theon ekosmoyn eaytas, upotassomenai tois idiois andrasin,
verses.translation: For after this manner in the old time the holy women also, who trusted in God, adorned themselves, being in subjection unto their own husbands:

verses.original: ὡς Σάρρα ⸀ὑπήκουσεν τῷ Ἀβραάμ, κύριον αὐτὸν καλοῦσα· ἧς ἐγενήθητε τέκνα ἀγαθοποιοῦσαι καὶ μὴ φοβούμεναι μηδεμίαν πτόησιν.
verses.translit: os Sarra upikoysen to Avraam, kyrion auton kalousa* es egenithite tekna agathopoiousai kai me fovoymenai midemian ptoisin.
verses.translation: Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement.

verses.original: Οἱ ἄνδρες ὁμοίως συνοικοῦντες κατὰ γνῶσιν, ὡς ἀσθενεστέρῳ σκεύει τῷ γυναικείῳ ἀπονέμοντες τιμήν, ὡς καὶ ⸀συγκληρονόμοις χάριτος ζωῆς, εἰς τὸ μὴ ἐγκόπτεσθαι τὰς προσευχὰς ὑμῶν.
verses.translit: Oi andres omoios synoikountes kata gnosin, os asthenestero skeyei to gynaikeio aponemontes timin, os kai sygklironomois haritos zoes, eis to me egkoptesthai tas proseyhas umon.
verses.translation: Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered.

verses.original: Τὸ δὲ τέλος πάντες ὁμόφρονες, συμπαθεῖς, φιλάδελφοι, εὔσπλαγχνοι, ⸀ταπεινόφρονες,
verses.translit: To de telos pantes omofrones, sympatheis, filadelfoi, eusplaghnoi, tapeinofrones,
verses.translation: Finally, be ye all of one mind, having compassion one of another, love as brethren, be pitiful, be courteous:

verses.original: μὴ ἀποδιδόντες κακὸν ἀντὶ κακοῦ ἢ λοιδορίαν ἀντὶ λοιδορίας τοὐναντίον δὲ ⸀εὐλογοῦντες, ὅτι εἰς τοῦτο ἐκλήθητε ἵνα εὐλογίαν κληρονομήσητε.
verses.translit: me apodidontes kakon anti kakou e loidorian anti loidorias tounantion de eulogountes, oti eis touto eklithite ina eulogian klironomisite.
verses.translation: Not rendering evil for evil, or railing for railing: but contrariwise blessing; knowing that ye are thereunto called, that ye should inherit a blessing.

verses.original: ὁ γὰρ θέλων ζωὴν ἀγαπᾶν καὶ ἰδεῖν ἡμέρας ἀγαθὰς παυσάτω τὴν ⸀γλῶσσαν ἀπὸ κακοῦ καὶ ⸀χείλη τοῦ μὴ λαλῆσαι δόλον,
verses.translit: o gar thelon zoen agapan kai idein emeras agathas paysato ten glossan apo kakou kai heili tou me lalesai dolon,
verses.translation: For he that will love life, and see good days, let him refrain his tongue from evil, and his lips that they speak no guile:

verses.original: ἐκκλινάτω ⸀δὲ ἀπὸ κακοῦ καὶ ποιησάτω ἀγαθόν, ζητησάτω εἰρήνην καὶ διωξάτω αὐτήν·
verses.translit: ekklinato de apo kakou kai poiisato agathon, zitisato eirinin kai dioxato autin*
verses.translation: Let him eschew evil, and do good; let him seek peace, and ensue it.

verses.original: ὅτι ὀφθαλμοὶ κυρίου ἐπὶ δικαίους καὶ ὦτα αὐτοῦ εἰς δέησιν αὐτῶν, πρόσωπον δὲ κυρίου ἐπὶ ποιοῦντας κακά.
verses.translit: oti ofthalmoi kyrioy epi dikaioys kai ota autou eis deisin auton, prosopon de kyrioy epi poiountas kaka.
verses.translation: For the eyes of the Lord are over the righteous, and his ears are open unto their prayers: but the face of the Lord is against them that do evil.

verses.original: Καὶ τίς ὁ κακώσων ὑμᾶς ἐὰν τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ ⸀ζηλωταὶ γένησθε;
verses.translit: Kai tis o kakoson umas ean tou agathou zilotai genisthe;
verses.translation: And who is he that will harm you, if ye be followers of that which is good?

verses.original: ἀλλʼ εἰ καὶ πάσχοιτε διὰ δικαιοσύνην, μακάριοι. τὸν δὲ φόβον αὐτῶν μὴ φοβηθῆτε μηδὲ ταραχθῆτε,
verses.translit: all' ei kai pashoite dia dikaiosynin, makarioi. ton de fovon auton me fovithete mide tarahthete,
verses.translation: But and if ye suffer for righteousness’ sake, happy are ye : and be not afraid of their terror, neither be troubled;

verses.original: κύριον δὲ τὸν ⸀Χριστὸν ἁγιάσατε ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν, ⸀ἕτοιμοι ἀεὶ πρὸς ἀπολογίαν παντὶ τῷ αἰτοῦντι ὑμᾶς λόγον περὶ τῆς ἐν ὑμῖν ἐλπίδος,
verses.translit: kyrion de ton Hriston agiasate en tais kardiais umon, etoimoi aei pros apologian panti to aitounti umas logon peri tes en umin elpidos,
verses.translation: But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear:

verses.original: ⸀ἀλλὰ μετὰ πραΰτητος καὶ φόβου, συνείδησιν ἔχοντες ἀγαθήν, ἵνα ἐν ᾧ ⸀καταλαλεῖσθε καταισχυνθῶσιν οἱ ἐπηρεάζοντες ὑμῶν τὴν ἀγαθὴν ἐν Χριστῷ ἀναστροφήν.
verses.translit: alla meta praytitos kai fovoy, syneidisin ehontes agathin, ina en o katalaleisthe kataishynthosin oi epireazontes umon ten agathen en Hristo anastrofin.
verses.translation: Having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ.

verses.original: κρεῖττον γὰρ ἀγαθοποιοῦντας, εἰ θέλοι τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ, πάσχειν ἢ κακοποιοῦντας.
verses.translit: kreitton gar agathopoiountas, ei theloi to thelima tou theou, pashein e kakopoiountas.
